claims.t: Collins on this line is the anglicization of Ó Coileáin, a Munster sept driven from north Munster (Connello, Co. Limerick) into West Cork by the Geraldines in the 13th c. — matching the Munster-weighted DNA.
The Cromwellian conquest and 1652 Settlement Act drove Catholic landownership from ~60% (pre-1641) to ~8% under the Commonwealth.
The Penal Laws (from 1695), including gavelkind inheritance, drove Catholic landownership to ~5% by the 1770s.

The Great Famine (1845–1852) killed ~1–1.5m and forced ~1–1.5m to emigrate, cutting the population from ~8.2m (1841) to ~6.55m (1851); it fell hardest on the Irish-speaking southwest including West Cork. [Population endpoints corrected in Round 2.]
Post-Famine depopulation cut the population from >8m to ~4m by 1911 via emigration, late marriage, and high celibacy; 'less than half' was attributable to the Famine itself.
The Slavic expansion (c.500–1000 AD) produced the West/East Slav split; Balts are a separate IE branch and Estonians are Finnic (Uralic), not IE.
Balts, East Slavs, and Estonians form one tight autosomal cluster, so the NE-European DNA labels overstate sharpness and should be read as one signal.
Pokorný is overwhelmingly a Czech/Moravian surname meaning 'humble/meek', with Polish/Galician/Jewish offshoots; a Czech patriline is the strongest single hypothesis.
The three Partitions (1772/1793/1795) erased Poland and split these ancestors among empires for 123 years, governing almost the whole Parent-1 profile.
Austrian Galicia was the poorest province in Europe (mixed Polish/Ukrainian/Jewish population) — the likely heart of the Southern Poland + Western Ukraine signal.
The Baltic governorates split Lutheran Estonia/Latvia (Baltic-German elite, early serfdom abolition) from Catholic Lithuania (post-1863 Russification) — mapping Estonia & Latvia 9% + Lithuania 3%.
The 1880–1924 wave was driven by Galician land hunger/famine, conscription, Russification, and pogroms, and was cut off by the 1924 Johnson–Reed Act.
The percentages are an HMM/Viterbi comparison of ~300,000 SNPs against 146 reference populations across 1,001 genome windows.
By parent' is SideView — real IBD-based parental phasing (not a guess) using DNA shared with distant cousins — which reduces cross-parent bleed.
SideView is reliable for most testers but degrades with endogamy and does NOT say which parent is mother vs. father; the clean ~50/50 Irish-vs-Central-European split is the easy case.
Ireland's genome was largely set by a Bronze-Age Steppe/Bell-Beaker turnover (~32% Yamnaya) on Neolithic-farmer and Mesolithic HG layers, with ~4,000 years of continuity since.
Fine-scale Irish genetics resolves real Munster/Connacht/Ulster clusters, so a Munster-weighted all-Ireland spread is the textbook signature of one southwestern Gaelic line, not four origins.
Poles, Balts, East Slavs, and Estonians form one tight cluster (geography > language), so Southern Poland + Estonia/Latvia + Lithuania + NE Poland + W. Ukraine are one signal across adjacent labels.
The 1% tags (Northwestern Balkans, Germans in Russia) are most likely shared-haplotype noise; the 3–4% Germanic/British traces are real-but-unresolved (Ostsiedlung, Baltic-German, or bleed).
Estimates change between updates because the reference panel and algorithm change, not the DNA; the 2024–25 update split broad Eastern-European/Baltic labels into eight finer regions.

A Czech Pokorný reading 'Southern Poland' rather than 'Eastern Czechia' is consistent, not contradictory — explained by the porous Moravian–Silesian–Galician borderland and surname-vs-autosomal-average logic.

Irish emigration was financed from America via 'America letters', remittances, and prepaid tickets (>40% of remittances; ~75% of emigration paid by 'American money'; >$260m sent home) — classic chain migration.

claims.t: The Central-European/Baltic line came in the 1880–1924 wave and was recorded at Ellis Island by EMPIRE ('Austria'/'Russia'), not ethnicity — the single biggest genealogical complication for this line.
Czech (Bohemian/Moravian) emigrants tended to come as families intending to stay and clustered in the Midwest and Texas (Moravians often via Galveston).
Polish/Galician emigrants came disproportionately as young men 'for bread' (za chlebem) into heavy industry, with high return migration ('birds of passage'; ~1/3 of Poles returned).

The 1924 Johnson–Reed Act was the hard cutoff for the Eastern-European wave (Irish Free State 28,567 vs. Poland 6,524); 'before WWII' means 'before 1924' for the Pokorný line, with no comparable wall for the Collins line.
The two lines most plausibly met in an American industrial Catholic city via parish, neighborhood, school, and workplace — the strongest single inference in the corpus, explicitly flagged.
s: S9

claims.t: Intermarriage across white-ethnic Catholic groups became common by mid-century (the 'triple melting pot'), making an Irish–Czech/Polish union expected, not exceptional.
On a Munster-weighted line, Collins is best read as Gaelic Ó Coileáin (north-Munster origin, pushed into West Cork by the Geraldines).
Collins is ALSO a common English patronymic (from Colin, a diminutive of Nicholas), so the surname alone proves nothing — distribution and DNA disambiguate.
In Ireland, Collins is concentrated in Munster/Cork (Matheson 1890: 30th surname, ~15,700; Forebears: 17,231, highest density of any country).
Pokorný is overwhelmingly Czech (~20th–24th commonest surname, ~11,000 bearers, ~96% of accented-spelling bearers worldwide), concentrated in Central Bohemia, South Moravia, and Prague.

A Czech surname is fully reconcilable with a 'Southern Poland' DNA region: it is a broad Habsburg-borderland cluster spanning Moravia, Silesia, and Galicia; region labels are population clusters, not borders.
Methodological anchor: a surname is one patrilineal thread while the DNA estimate blends all lines — Collins and Pokorný cannot account for the Baltic, Ukrainian, Donegal, or Connacht signals.
Irish Catholicism reached its modern intensity through a post-Famine 'devotional revolution' (1850–75, Larkin); this Tridentine, parish-centered form is what the Collins line carried to America.
The Czech strand is the great secular exception: ≥half of pre-1914 Czech immigrants were 'free-thinkers' (svobodomyslní) organized around the anticlerical Sokol rather than the Church.
Polish Catholicism is intensely national, producing the national parish and the PNCC schism (Scranton 1897, Hodur) — the only enduring American-born Catholic schism.

The Baltic strand introduces a Protestant seam: Lithuania Catholic, but Estonia and Latvia historically Lutheran — though the small DNA percentages make lived Baltic religion in this family uncertain.
The languages die in one to three generations (Irish was dying before emigration), leaving the surname as the durable linguistic relic — Collins and Pokorný themselves.

By the 3rd–4th generation the heritage becomes symbolic ethnicity (Gans) / an ethnic option (Waters) — voluntary, intermittent, low-cost — and this costless optionality is itself a privilege of whiteness.

Within the menu of options the Irish strand reliably dominates (institutions, prestige, St. Patrick's Day, the 'exile' narrative) while the Czech/Polish/Baltic strands submerge — and DNA testing now revives them.

The highest-yield first move is testing a parent or older relative, which converts SideView's arbitrary Parent 1/Parent 2 into a real maternal/paternal anchor (and future-proofs against losing elder DNA).

claims.t: The 'illiterate maid burned it' account derives from Mill's confession and Carlyle's circle, not an independent witness; report as traditional, not verified.
Completed 12 Jan 1837; published ~May 1837 (corrects an earlier 'January 1837 publication' conflation).
Superseded as analysis but broadly faithful to the documented record; 'poetry scrupulously rooted in historical fact' (Rosenberg); 'the truest of histories' (Mill).
Conceived as a prose-epic; the double verdict (Mill 'epic poem… truest of histories' vs. Thackeray 'prose run mad') is permanent.
Epic intent is documented (Iliad in Greek, 1834; 'the grand Poem of our Time'), not inferred from style.
Dante's Inferno is invoked explicitly at Marie-Antoinette's trial ('the pale kingdoms of Dis… Styx and Lethe… Fire-Phlegethon and Cocytus') — among the most textually secure allusions.
Whether the borrowed scriptural-epic grandeur net-illuminates or net-distorts the history is a live, unsettled critical question.
Central thesis: revolution is the violent return of Reality after an age of Shams.
Embryonic 'great-man' reading (Mirabeau, Danton, Napoleon's 'whiff of grapeshot'), present in seed but checked by the impersonal force of Sansculottism.
The proto-fascist reading is a defensible reading of the doctrine's tendency and the later Carlyle, but an overreading of the 1837 text.
Mill's July 1837 review ('not so much a history, as an epic poem… the truest of histories') made the book; Carlyle replied 'You have said openly of my poor Book what I durst not myself dream of it.
Dickens's 'read it 500 times' is his own jocular hyperbole (traced to Edgar Johnson 1952), not a measured fact.
Dickens absorbs Carlyle's providential grammar but reverses his theodicy of violence, displacing redemption onto the private/Christian plane.
Michelet dismissed Carlyle's book in 1868 as 'a wretched work… devoid of study… full of false flights.
Modern consensus: unreliable as analysis, valuable as narrative art and as evocation; still in print and taught nearly 200 years on.
Cassirer names Carlyle 'father of the modern myth of the hero' but declines to charge him with 'all the consequences… drawn from his theory.
The first comprehensive scholarly edition appeared only in 2019 (Oxford), 182 years after publication.
Friedrich is Carlyle's last major work, six volumes 1858-1865, a ~13-year labour
Over thirteen years 'fewer and fewer traces of a hero' revealed themselves
Poor Imperial Majesty; a human creature doing Play-actorisms of too high a flight' fuses mock-pity, coinage, and Sham-vs-Reality polemic in one sentence
Thackeray (1837) supplied both the indictment and the defense of Carlylese; modern criticism restates his 'method in it
Dryasdust' is a recurring device and personification, not an ensemble character
The device anchors apRoberts's 'remarkable three-way relationship' among narrator, Frederick, and reader
The asyndetic sensory catalogue is Carlyle's primary battle-sublime instrument; its locus classicus is Prague, not Leuthen
The Leuthen Te-Deum converts the noise of battle into liturgy ('five-and-twenty thousand other voices')
The hero-figure migrates from literary prophet to 'the political despot who compels rather than persuades
Nation-building rendered as Genesis-like world-making; the Hohenzollerns named 'the Authors of Prussia
Carlyle's defining judgment: Friedrich 'managed not to be a Liar and Charlatan as his Century was
The Proem dismisses the 18th c. as a 'swindler-century' with 'nothing grand in it, except that grand universal Suicide, named French Revolution
Lord Acton called Carlyle 'the most detestable of historians' and the great-man creed an 'atrocity
Emerson's 'Judgment Day' and 'wittiest book that ever was written' praise is documented and verbatim
British periodical reviews of Vols I-II (1858) were predominantly negative; 'universal acclaim' is a myth
Nietzsche held Carlyle in documented contempt, complicating the Carlyle-to-fascism lineage
The famous bunker quotation ('Brave king! wait yet a little while') is not in Carlyle's text and is misdated
The claim that the bunker reading 'lastingly damaged the book's reputation' outruns the evidence; contested
Carlyle's mature thought is best read as a Scottish Calvinism that has lost its confession and kept its grammar — the load-bearing thesis of the corpus.

claims.t: The 32-bit IPv4 address length was fixed by Vint Cerf as DARPA program manager around 1977, after debate including 128-bit and variable-length proposals, on the assumption the protocol was an experiment to be replaced by a production version; Cerf has repeatedly confirmed this on the record.
s: RFC 791 [1]; Computerworld Australia 2018 [12]; Network World 2011 [13]; Engadget 2011 [14]

claims.t: At IETF 18 (August 1990), Frank Solensky — with Phill Gross and Sue Hares — presented projections that Class B address space would exhaust by ~March 1994 at then-current rates; this first formal IETF exhaustion forecast directly motivated the ROAD group, CIDR, and the IPng process.
s: Huston ISP Column Oct 2008 [10]; Huston IPv4 Address Report [11]; RFC 1752 [8]

claims.t: The classful A/B/C structure of RFC 791 forced allocations in blocks of 16.7M, 65,536, or 256 addresses, guaranteeing massive waste; CIDR (RFC 1338, 1992; RFC 1519, 1993) replaced classes with variable-length prefixes explicitly as a stopgap to buy time for a successor protocol.

NAT entered the standards record as RFC 1631 (May 1994, Egevang & Francis), building on Tsuchiya/Francis's January 1993 address-reuse paper; RFC 1631's own abstract describes NAT as a "short-term solution" with IPv6-class re-addressing as the long-term solution.
s: RFC 1631 [5]; Tsuchiya & Eng 1993 [6]; RFC 1918 [7]

claims.t: NAT destroyed the architectural assumption (Saltzer/Reed/Clark 1984) that an IP address uniquely and globally identifies an endpoint; the IETF catalogued these costs contemporaneously in RFC 2993 (Nov 2000) and RFC 2775 (Feb 2000).
s: Saltzer/Reed/Clark 1984 [15]; RFC 2993 [16]; RFC 2775 [17]

claims.t: After the IAB's mid-1992 CLNP-as-IPv7 plan was rejected by the IETF (the "Kobe affair"), the formal IPng process evaluated TUBA, CATNIP, and SIPP; RFC 1752 (January 1995) recommended SIPP revised to 128-bit fixed addresses, which became IPv6.
IPv6 was specified in RFC 1883 (December 1995), revised as RFC 2460 (December 1998), and only became full Internet Standard (STD 86) with RFC 8200 in July 2017.

The IETF's dual-stack/tunneling transition plan (RFC 1933, 1996; succeeded by RFC 2893/4213) assumed networks would retire IPv4 before the free pool emptied; instead IPv6 offered no unilateral economic benefit to early movers, deployment stayed below ~1% through 2010, and exhaustion arrived with the transition barely begun — making CGNAT, address markets, and IP-layer ambiguity permanent features.
IANA allocated its last five /8 blocks (one per RIR under the "final /8" policy) in a ceremony on 3 February 2011, triggered by APNIC's 31 January 2011 request that drained the unallocated pool.
s: NRO/ICANN/ISOC joint announcement [29]; Huston [11]

claims.t: APNIC reached its last-/8 austerity phase on 15 April 2011; RIPE NCC reached its last /8 on 14 September 2012 and full exhaustion on 25 November 2019; LACNIC entered exhaustion on 10 June 2014; ARIN's free pool hit zero on 24 September 2015; AFRINIC entered IPv4 Exhaustion (Soft Landing) Phase 1 on 31 March 2017 (announced 2 April 2017), with Phase 2 following on 13 January 2020.
s: APNIC [30]; RIPE NCC [31]; ARIN [32]; LACNIC/AFRINIC [33]; Huston [11]; Richter et al. [9]

claims.t: In March 2011, weeks after IANA exhaustion, Microsoft paid $7.5 million for 666,624 legacy IPv4 addresses ($11.25 each) from bankrupt Nortel Networks, approved by the Delaware bankruptcy court in April 2011 — the first large publicly disclosed IPv4 sale, establishing addresses as priced, transferable assets.
s: Network World [34]; Mueller/IGP [35]; CircleID [36]

claims.t: RFC 6598 (April 2012, BCP 153) reserved 100.64.0.0/10 as "Shared Address Space" specifically so ISPs could deploy carrier-grade NAT between customers and the public internet — the formal admission that many subscribers would share single public IPv4 addresses indefinitely.

Following the one-day World IPv6 Day test (8 June 2011), the Internet Society's World IPv6 Launch on 6 June 2012 had major operators (Google, Facebook, Yahoo!, Comcast, AT&T) permanently enable IPv6; global user adoption at the time was on the order of 1%, underscoring how late the transition started relative to exhaustion.
s: Internet Society [39]; Google IPv6 statistics [40]; Richter et al. [9]

claims.t: Digital Envoy (founded 1999; Digital Element division spun out 2005) and Quova (founded ~1999-2000, acquired by Neustar 27 October 2010) pioneered and patented IP-based geotargeting, selling primarily to ad networks, publishers, and websites — establishing the IP address as a commercial targeting signal a decade and a half before CTV.
s: Digital Envoy [26]; Neustar 8-K [27]; Arma Partners [41]; Goldsmith & Wu [42]

claims.t: In LICRA v. Yahoo! (Paris, 2000), a court-appointed expert panel including Vint Cerf concluded roughly 70-90% of French users could be identified by IP geolocation, and Judge Gomez ordered Yahoo! to filter accordingly — the first high-profile legal endorsement that an IP address maps usefully to real-world location, which legitimized the nascent geo-IP industry.
s: Goldsmith & Wu, Who Controls the Internet?, ch. 1 and 5 (Oxford UP, 2006) [42]

claims.t: CTV advertising (emerging with Roku's 2008 Netflix player, maturing programmatically ~2015-2019) runs in native, cookieless app environments; the IP address — in every OpenRTB bid request via device.ip/device.ipv6 — was the only universally present, household-stable signal, so household graphs, frequency capping, and cross-device attribution were built on it by default, while the designed alternative (platform IFAs: Roku RIDA, Amazon AFAI, etc.) remained fragmented.
s: OpenRTB 2.x spec [43]; IAB OTT IFA guidelines [44][45]; Digiday/trade press [33]

claims.t: IAB Tech Lab published "Guidelines for Identifier for Advertising (IFA) on OTT Platforms" (draft April 2018, final December 2018), requiring a resettable, hardware-disconnected IFA plus Limit Ad Tracking flag; the guidelines were deprecated in 2023, and the IP address remained the de facto cross-platform household key throughout.
s: IAB Tech Lab OTT IFA guidelines [44]; IAB press release [45]; trade analysis [33]

claims.t: Because IPv6's original SLAAC embedded the device MAC address in the interface identifier (EUI-64), the IETF created privacy extensions — RFC 3041 (2001), RFC 4941 (2007), RFC 8981 (2021) — generating short-lived randomized addresses precisely to prevent cross-session tracking of devices by address; the address layer's stewards have thus engineered against address-based identification for 25 years, in direct tension with advertising's use of addresses as stable identifiers.

Legacy (pre-RIR) allocations total roughly 82 /8-equivalents — about 37% of routable IPv4 space (Richter et al. 2015) — including the 40–49 single-organization Class A /8s of the classful era (RFC 1466 records 49 by May 1992), free, contract-less, and overwhelmingly to US institutions; the legacy space then became the principal supply side of the transfer market (e.g., MIT's reported 2017 sale of ~8 million addresses from 18.0.0.0/8 to Amazon).
s: Richter et al. 2015 [9]; Huston [10][11]; RFC 1366/1466 [52]; MIT-Amazon public record [53]

claims.t: The OpenRTB specification — OpenRTB Mobile 1.0 (Feb 2011), OpenRTB 2.0 unified and IAB-adopted by Jan 2012 — defines device.ip ("IPv4 address closest to device") and device.ipv6 as core Device-object fields in every bid request, with IP noted as among the most essential fields because it enables geo-lookup by the bidder.
s: [1] IAB OpenRTB 2.0 spec (Jan 2012); [2] IAB Tech Lab OpenRTB 2.6 GitHub

claims.t: RTB became commercially significant around 2009 (Google's DoubleClick Ad Exchange relaunch among catalysts), and the OpenRTB consortium project — begun by DSPs/SSPs in Nov 2010 and adopted by the IAB — standardized the bid-request/response protocol across the industry by Jan 2012.
s: [1][2] IAB OpenRTB specifications

claims.t: CTV apps run in walled environments without a shared third-party-cookie mechanism, so CTV identity has relied on platform device IDs, logged-in account data, and the household IP — the only signal shared across all apps and devices on a home network — making IP the probabilistic 'glue' of household graphs.

claims.t: The Trade Desk announced Unified ID 2.0 in 2020 as an email-derived, opt-in deterministic identifier (EUID as GDPR-adapted European variant), accumulating CTV adopters (Disney, NBCU, Paramount, Dish/Sling, LG Ad Solutions, TF1/M6 on EUID) — but because authenticated coverage never approached universality, IP-based probabilistic matching remained the connective tissue filling the gaps.
s: [18] The Trade Desk 8-K (SEC); [19] StreamTV Insider; [5] FreeWheel

claims.t: Chrome announced on Jan 14, 2020 it would phase out third-party cookies 'within two years'; after three delays (2021, 2022, 2024), Google announced July 22, 2024 it would not deprecate them, proposing a user-choice prompt; in April 2025 it abandoned even the prompt, leaving cookies operating as before and dramatically scaling back Privacy Sandbox.
s: [20] CNBC; [21] TechCrunch; [22] IAPP; [23] OneTrust; [24] The Register; [25] Clifford Chance

claims.t: During 2020-24, the expected death of the cookie pushed budgets, vendor roadmaps, and identity-graph construction toward non-Chrome signals — hashed emails, platform IDs, IP addresses — with cookieless CTV marketed as 'future-proof'; the 2024-25 reversal did not unwind this build-out, leaving IP more deeply embedded in identity infrastructure than in 2019.
s: [18][16][17][26] synthesized

claims.t: The Nov 2025 CIMM/Go Addressable/Truthset study — benchmarking ~1B IP records from six major data providers against ground-truth assignments from two ISPs and one MVPD — found IP-to-postal linkages accurate on average 13%, IP-to-email 16%, inter-provider agreement of only 6.4% (postal) and 2.8% (email), and ~3.2 IPs per postal address vs ~1.2 in ISP records.
s: [3] CIMM/Truthset report PDF; [4] CIMM release; [27] Adweek; [28] ppc.land

claims.t: FreeWheel (Comcast-owned) published guidance warning that IP-based household targeting executed against stale or third-party IP-to-household linkages can miss up to 87% of intended households, arguing for first-party/ISP-verified linkages; vendors responded that the failure is linkage hygiene and recency, not the IP signal itself, and Truthset reported working with providers to improve linkages rather than calling for abandonment of IP.
s: [5] FreeWheel; [28] ppc.land; [6] AdExchanger; [29] Truthset

claims.t: White Ops (later HUMAN) disclosed in April 2020 the ICEBUCKET operation: up to 1.9B fraudulent ad requests/day in Jan 2020 from data-center servers impersonating ~2M users in 30+ countries, spoofing 300+ publishers, at peak ~28% of programmatic CTV traffic in White Ops' visibility, with ~46% of traffic impersonating Roku devices.
s: [30] HUMAN/White Ops disclosure; [31] VideoWeek; [32] SecurityWeek

claims.t: Oracle Moat disclosed in Dec 2020 the StreamScam operation, which spoofed more than 28.8M US household IP addresses, ~3,600 apps and ~3,400 CTV device models via servers impersonating SSAI infrastructure, with ~$14.5M stolen over four months; DoubleVerify stated it had detected the same scheme in July 2020 as 'LeoTerra.
s: [33] AdExchanger; [34] MediaPost

claims.t: DoubleVerify disclosed ParrotTerra (Feb 2021), a counterfeit-SSAI scheme spoofing ~3.7M devices and ~2.7M IPs per day with projected theft of $30-50M; and SmokeScreen (Aug 2021), a screensaver-hijack scheme generating up to 10M fraudulent requests daily (~$6M/month) from ~10,000 devices running ads behind switched-off TV screens, detected partly via anomalous overnight traffic patterns.
s: [35][36] DoubleVerify (Tier 1/5 hybrid); [37] AdExchanger; [38] StreamTV Insider

claims.t: In Case C-582/14 (Breyer v Bundesrepublik Deutschland, judgment Oct 19, 2016), the CJEU held that a dynamic IP address held by a website operator constitutes personal data where the operator has legal means reasonably likely to be used to identify the user via the ISP's records — the foundational ruling under which GDPR (Recital 30 naming IP addresses among online identifiers) treats ad-tech IP processing as personal-data processing.
s: [39] Bird & Bird; [40] Covington; [41] EU Law Analysis; [42] GDPR Recital 30

claims.t: The CCPA (enacted 2018, effective 2020) explicitly lists IP addresses among 'personal information' identifiers when reasonably linkable to a consumer or household — AG guidance clarifying unlinked IP logs may fall outside the definition — and subsequent US state privacy laws broadly followed, putting household-IP-keyed advertising in scope of US privacy regulation for the first time.
s: [43] CCPA / Cal. AG; [44] IAPP

claims.t: Apple announced iCloud Private Relay at WWDC June 2021 (shipping with iOS 15 as a paid iCloud+ beta feature), routing Safari traffic and DNS queries through a two-hop architecture (Apple ingress, third-party egress) so no single party sees both user identity and destination, replacing the user's IP with a coarse regional one — read by trade press as a direct strike against IP-based tracking and fingerprinting.
s: [45] 9to5Mac; [46] Six Colors; [26] AdExchanger

claims.t: Google's IP Protection (descendant of 'Gnatcatcher,' announced for Chrome Oct 2023) was confirmed in 2025 for rollout in Chrome Incognito no sooner than Q3 2025, masking IPs in third-party contexts for Masked Domain List domains via a two-hop proxy (Google first hop, external CDN second) — surviving the April 2025 Privacy Sandbox retreat as one of the few privacy features Google kept.
s: [47] Google IP Protection docs; [48] GitHub explainer; [49] The Hacker News; [50] Digiday

claims.t: IPv6 temporary-address privacy extensions (RFC 4941, 2007; updated by RFC 8981, 2021) — rotating the interface-identifier portion of IPv6 addresses to prevent long-term device tracking — are enabled by default in Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android, so IPv6 delivers rotating device addresses behind a stable /64 (or larger) household prefix, reproducing household-level (not device-level) identifiability.

IANA allocated its last five /8 blocks to the five Regional Internet Registries in February 2011; ARIN exhausted its free pool Sept 24, 2015; RIPE NCC announced its final /22 allocation Nov 25, 2019 — meaning throughout CTV's entire growth period, new internet connectivity has been provisioned under IPv4 scarcity.
s: [53] RIPE NCC/APNIC; [54] APNIC/RIPE; [55] Infoblox

claims.t: In March-April 2011, Microsoft paid $7.5M for 666,624 IPv4 addresses from bankrupt Nortel (~$11.25 per address), approved by the US Bankruptcy Court for the District of Delaware on April 26, 2011 — the first publicly disclosed large-scale IPv4 address sale, establishing addresses as transferable priced assets.
s: [56] Internet Governance Project; [57] CircleID; [58] Network World

claims.t: IAB Tech Lab released OpenRTB 2.6 for public comment Dec 9, 2021 and finalized it April 2022, with CTV ad podding (structured, dynamic, hybrid pods) as its flagship feature — while the Device-object IP fields continued unchanged as the bid request's location/identity substrate.
s: [59] IAB Tech Lab; [60] BidSwitch; [2] OpenRTB 2.6 spec

claims.t: EMARKETER forecasts US CTV ad spending of ~$38 billion in 2026 (up from $33.35B in 2025, ~14% YoY), reaching $46.89B and surpassing linear TV by 2028.
s: [1][2][3] EMARKETER forecast pages; IAB 2026 forecast via MediaPost/StreamTV Insider

claims.t: Programmatic accounts for 84.2% of US CTV video ad spend per EMARKETER's 2025 forecast, with other cuts and MNTN's reading putting it at ~90% of CTV display spend.
s: [4][5] EMARKETER; MNTN Research

claims.t: IAB Europe's AdEx Benchmark put 2024 European digital ad spend at €118.9B (+16% YoY), total video at €12.4B; SVOD ad spend grew 222%, BVOD +29.5%, AVOD +16.9% — European CTV is a single-digit-billions, broadcaster-VOD-dominated market growing at venture rates.
s: [6][7] IAB Europe AdEx Benchmark 2024; VideoWeek

claims.t: India's CTV ad market grew ~35% in 2024 to ~₹1,500 crore (~$180M), with 50–60 million CTV households projected by end-2025 (overtaking the DTH pay-TV base) and 2025 ad revenue estimates of ₹2,300–2,500 crore.
s: [8][9] GroupM PMAR via BW Marketing World; Storyboard18/TheMediaAnt

claims.t: Japan's CTV ad spending is on track to reach roughly $1 billion in 2026 (+17.4% YoY per EMARKETER-derived figures), while China's programmatic spend is overwhelmingly concentrated in BAT/ByteDance walled gardens with no meaningful open-bidstream CTV market.
s: [10][11][12] EMARKETER Japan forecast; Dentsu release; Campaign Asia/ExchangeWire

claims.t: LiveRamp's official CTV documentation 'highly recommends sending only IPv4 IP addresses,' stating IPv6 addresses 'in most cases... will not be able to match,' and its cross-device bid-stream evaluation includes only IPv4 addresses, applicable only to CTV inventory.
s: [13][14] LiveRamp CTV docs; FreeWheel Buyer Cloud user guide

claims.t: The OpenRTB spec carries IPv4 in device.ip and IPv6 in a separate device.ipv6 field, leaving dual-stack handling, preference, and truncation to exchange/DSP implementation choice rather than protocol mandate.
s: [15] IAB Tech Lab, OpenRTB 2.6 spec

claims.t: Google's IPv6 statistics recorded IPv6 carrying half of traffic to Google for the first time in April 2026; country-level adoption diverges sharply — India ~72%, France ~86%, Germany ~68–75%, US ~50% — so the bid-stream's IPv4 monoculture sits atop an internet majority-IPv6 in several CTV growth markets.
s: [16][17][18] Internet Society Pulse; APNIC; Google IPv6 Statistics

claims.t: Benchmarking ~1B IP records from six major providers against ISP/MVPD ground truth, Truthset (commissioned by CIMM and GoAddressable, Nov 2025) found IP-to-postal linkages accurate on average 13% of the time, IP-to-email 16%; providers agree on only 6.4% of postal and 2.8% of email linkages; IPv6 is under-represented by 72% with only 15% of commercial files capturing it; and there are ~3x more IPs per postal address than ISP records indicate.
s: [19] Truthset, 'IP Address Accuracy: The Hidden Variable in CTV Performance,' 2025-11-13

claims.t: Peer-reviewed measurement (Richter et al., IMC) found more than 92% of cellular ASes and 17–20% of fixed eyeball ASes deploy carrier-grade NAT, with ~40% of ISPs deploying or planning CGNAT; CGNAT is most prevalent in Asia, Eastern Europe, the Middle East, South America, and Africa — shared public IPv4 is the norm exactly where CTV household growth is fastest.
s: [20][21] Richter et al. ACM IMC 2016/CAIDA 2018; Cloudflare

claims.t: Through 2025 into early 2026, /16 blocks fell below $13–15 per address (10-year lows) while small blocks (/22–/24) held near $30; IPXO platform leasing averages ~$0.40/IP/month (down from $0.51–0.69 in 2022), with APNIC-region leases at a premium above $0.60.
s: [22][23][24] CircleID; IPXO market stats

claims.t: IPv4.Global (Hilco Streambank) claims to have transferred more than 65 million IPv4 addresses generating over $1.3 billion for clients, the most visible broker in a market that also includes leasing platforms (IPXO) and private brokers (Prefix Broker, Brander Group).
s: [22][25] IPv4.Global sales reports; CircleID

claims.t: A CGNAT vendor worked example (6WIND) puts the cost of serving 8,000 subscribers via CGNAT at ~$31k TCO ($6k for 127 public IPs, ~$5k hardware, ~$20k licensing; 63 subscribers per public IP) versus ~$392k to buy 8,000 addresses at the then-current $49/IP; broker commentary (Prefix Broker) counters that CGNAT is “not always more cost-effective” once carrier-grade hardware and logging equipment are priced, and that outright purchase is “generally equally expensive.
s: [26][27] NetElastic/Nfware vendor examples; Prefix Broker analysis

claims.t: Parks Associates (April 2026) puts Roku at 28% and Samsung at 23% of US CTV platform share; Pixalate's ad-traffic-based measurement (Q2 2025) ranks Roku 37%, Amazon 17%, Samsung 12% — different methodologies, same duopoly-plus-Amazon shape. Walmart completed its $2.3B Vizio acquisition December 3, 2024, folding SmartCast into Walmart Connect retail media.
s: [28][29][30] Parks Associates; Pixalate via The Desk; Walmart corporate release

claims.t: As of late 2025, Amazon claims 315M monthly ad-supported Prime Video viewers globally (130M US; inflated by default opt-in since January 2024), Netflix claims 190M ad-tier monthly active viewers (up from 94M in May 2025 — metric redefinitions apply), and Disney's streaming portfolio reaches ~164M monthly actives.
s: [31][32] TheWrap; Deadline

claims.t: Magnite is the only independent SSP with direct CTV integrations into Disney, Netflix, Roku, and Warner Bros. Discovery; CTV made up 44–46% of contribution ex-TAC in 2025 (Q2 2025 CTV contribution $71.5M, +14% YoY). FreeWheel (Comcast) and PubMatic are the other major CTV supply platforms, with PubMatic CTV revenue growing >50% YoY.
s: [33][34] W Media Research on Magnite Q2 2025; PubMatic Form 8-K (SEC EDGAR)

claims.t: The Trade Desk's Q3 2025 revenue was $739M (+18% YoY) per its 8-K, with CTV its largest and fastest-growing channel (~40% of revenue per analyst estimates); Amazon DSP is gaining CTV budgets via exclusive access to its own inventory plus 2025 deals extending to Disney+/Hulu/ESPN inventory.
s: [35][36] TTD Form 8-K Q3 2025 (SEC EDGAR); Yahoo Finance/Zacks analyst estimate

claims.t: Pixalate's Q3–Q4 2025 benchmarks put global CTV IVT at 18–21% (US ~19%) on >100B analyzed impressions, with IVT rates 110% higher where SSAI is used; landmark schemes — HUMAN's ICEBUCKET (2M+ impersonated users in 30+ countries via SSAI spoofing) and DoubleVerify/Roku's CycloneBot (up to 250M falsified ad requests and 1.5M spoofed devices daily, ~$7.5M/month advertiser impact) — both exploited the weak device/IP signal environment of SSAI.
s: [37][38][39] Pixalate benchmarks; HUMAN ICEBUCKET; DoubleVerify/Digiday CycloneBot

claims.t: The identity-graph layer consolidated in 2024–25 into LiveRamp (RampID), Experian (Tapad 2020 + Audigent Dec 2024, combining offline household data with device graphs and sell-side activation), TransUnion (TruAudience), and WPP/InfoSum (clean-room vendor acquired April 2025; reported price between $63M and ~$150M — disputed), forming the household-resolution oligopoly CTV buyers license.
s: [40][41] Experian release/AdExchanger; AdExchanger/Digiday/Marketing Dive on WPP-InfoSum

claims.t: Google shipped IP Protection for Chrome as an Incognito-only, masked-domain-list, two-hop-proxy feature (rollout from Q3 2025) after abandoning browser-wide plans; Apple's iCloud Private Relay (Safari + iCloud+ only) measured at ~1–2% of purported Apple-device traffic in Pixalate's 2022 study. Neither currently touches CTV devices, whose IPs flow from the device/SSAI server, not a browser — making CTV the least obfuscated IP surface in the consumer internet today.
s: [43][44][45] Google Privacy Sandbox IP Protection docs; ppc.land/Hacker News; Pixalate 2022 Private Relay study

claims.t: RFC 791 defines the IPv4 address as a 32-bit locator of a network attachment point ("an address indicates where it is"), explicitly permits multiple addresses per physical host, and specifies nothing about assignment stability — meaning IP-as-household-identity is an operational inference, not a protocol property.
s: Postel (ed.), RFC 791, Sept 1981, rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc791.txt [1]

claims.t: RFC 8200 defines an IPv6 address as a 128-bit "IPv6-layer identifier for an interface or a set of interfaces," with address architecture delegated to RFC 4291, whose 64-bit-prefix/64-bit-IID split is the structural basis of the prefix-vs-IID privacy asymmetry.
s: Deering & Hinden, RFC 8200/STD 86, July 2017, rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8200.txt [2]

claims.t: Under RFC 4862 SLAAC, devices form addresses by appending a self-generated interface identifier to a router-advertised /64 prefix; under RFC 8415 DHCPv6-PD, the home router receives a delegated prefix (typically /48–/56) whose renewal-time stability the protocol does not guarantee — making the delegated prefix, not any full address, the technically coherent "household identifier" in IPv6, with its persistence set by ISP policy.
s: RFC 4862 (rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4862.txt) and RFC 8415 (rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8415.txt) [3][4]

claims.t: Because typical residential delegations are /56, a 6-byte (48-bit) IPv6 truncation of the kind used by major exchanges can aggregate up to 256 distinct households into one value in /56-delegating networks, while isolating exactly one household where /48 delegation is used — i.e., identical truncation policy yields different effective privacy and targeting granularity in different markets.
s: RFC 4862/RFC 8415 + Google Authorized Buyers RTB FAQ [3][4][12]

claims.t: RFC 8981 rotates only the IPv6 interface identifier (defaults: 2-day valid / 1-day preferred lifetimes) and itself states that "the network-prefix portion of an address also serves as a constant identifier" whose rotation is outside the host's control — so host-side privacy extensions defeat per-device full-address tracking but leave prefix-based household identification intact.
s: Gont et al., RFC 8981, Feb 2021, rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8981.txt [5]

claims.t: RIPE-690, the operator best-practice document, recommends persistent /48–/56 delegations and calls non-persistent prefixes "harmful," while acknowledging privacy-motivated non-persistent assignment "in countries with specific legal environments" — the documentary basis for the regional split between stable-prefix markets and rotation markets such as Germany.
s: RIPE-690, 16 Oct 2017, ripe.net/publications/docs/ripe-690/ [6][7]

claims.t: Rye, Beverly & claffy (IMC 2021) demonstrated that ISP prefix rotation is undermined at scale by legacy CPE whose EUI-64 addresses embed a stable router MAC, identifying 9M+ affected edge routers and ~13,000 rotating /48s and showing remote re-linking of households across rotated prefixes.
s: Rye, Beverly & claffy, "Follow the Scent," Proc. ACM IMC 2021, arXiv:2102.00542 [8]

claims.t: RFC 6598 reserved 100.64.0.0/10 specifically so ISPs could insert carrier-grade NAT between CPE and the public internet without RFC 1918 collisions, and the RFC itself lists geolocation among services adversely affected by the resulting address sharing.
s: Weil et al., RFC 6598/BCP 153, April 2012, rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6598.txt [9]

claims.t: Richter et al. (IMC 2016) measured CGN in 17–18% of non-cellular eyeball ASes and >92% of cellular networks, with observed multiplexing of up to 128 subscribers per public IPv4 address (port allocations as small as 512 ports/subscriber) — the empirical ceiling-breaker for any one-IPv4-equals-one-household assumption, with a 2016-vintage caveat.
s: Richter et al., "A Multi-perspective Analysis of Carrier-Grade NAT Deployment," Proc. ACM IMC 2016, arXiv:1605.05606 [10]

claims.t: The OpenRTB 2.6 specification defines device.ip/device.ipv6 only as the address "closest to device" and contains no IP truncation or masking provisions; truncation regimes (e.g., Google's first-3-bytes IPv4 / first-6-bytes IPv6 policy) are exchange-level policies frequently misattributed to the spec.
s: IAB Tech Lab OpenRTB 2.6 (GitHub); Google Authorized Buyers RTB FAQ [11][12][13]

claims.t: Breyer (C-582/14) held that a dynamic IP address held by a website operator is personal data only "where the [operator] has the legal means which enable it to identify the data subject with additional data which the internet service provider has" — a conditional, relative test (with a para-46 carve-out where identification is legally prohibited or practically impossible), not the unconditional "IPs are personal data" rule it is usually cited for; in GDPR-era ad-tech practice the condition is almost always met.
s: CJEU, Breyer v Bundesrepublik Deutschland, C-582/14, ECLI:EU:C:2016:779, 19 Oct 2016, EUR-Lex [14]

claims.t: Apple's own documentation scopes iCloud Private Relay to "web browsing in Safari, DNS resolution queries, and insecure http app traffic" on iOS/iPadOS/macOS for iCloud+ subscribers — no tvOS/smart-TV coverage and no HTTPS app-traffic coverage — so it does not proxy CTV ad traffic, while its published egress geofeed deliberately preserves coarse city-level IP geolocation.
s: Apple Developer Support "Prepare your network for iCloud Private Relay"; Apple Support article 102602 [15][16]

claims.t: Google's IP Protection documentation scopes the feature to masking IPs in third-party contexts on the Masked Domain List, in Incognito mode only, via a two-hop proxy (Google first hop, external CDN second), while assigning egress IPs that "represent the user's coarse location, including country" published in a geofeed — i.e., it severs IP-identity while deliberately preserving IP-geography, and touches no CTV device traffic.
s: Google, "IP Protection," Privacy Sandbox documentation, privacysandbox.google.com/protections/ip-protection [17]

claims.t: The Truthset/CIMM/Go Addressable study (announced 5 Nov 2025) found commercial third-party IP-to-postal linkages accurate on average 13% of the time and IP-to-email 16%, with inter-provider agreement of only 6.4%/2.8% and IPv6 under-represented by 72% in commercial files — figures that measure third-party linkage-file precision against deterministic ISP/MVPD truth, not the momentary validity of IP-household assignment or short-window IP use; "misses 87% of households" is a derived inversion, not a study finding.
s: Truthset/CIMM/Go Addressable announcement, 5 Nov 2025; Brandt, FreeWheel Insights [18][19]

claims.t: HUMAN/White Ops's ICEBUCKET investigation (Apr 2020) documented ~1,700 datacenter SSAI-server IPs in 9 countries declaring ~2 million spoofed device IPs (>99% US-located) across 300+ counterfeit appIDs and 1,000+ user-agents, peaking at ~1.9B ad requests/day and ~28% of the programmatic CTV traffic in HUMAN's visibility — demonstrating that in SSAI architecture the device IP in the bid request is a declared, spoofable value.
s: HUMAN (White Ops) ICEBUCKET, April 2020, via VideoWeek and security trade coverage [20][21][22]

claims.t: In April 2026 Google's measure (share of users accessing Google over IPv6, unweighted) crossed 50% while APNIC Labs' measure (ad-based per-economy capability, ~25–30M tests/day, re-weighted by national internet-user populations) read 42%; the eight-point gap is a documented artifact of denominator and weighting choices, and neither measures IPv6 presence in CTV ad traffic.
s: Google IPv6 Statistics; APNIC Labs "How we measure: IPv6" (14 Nov 2025); Huston, "Google hits 50% IPv6" (28 Apr 2026) [23][24][25]

claims.t: A November 2025 study commissioned by CIMM and Go Addressable, conducted by Truthset, benchmarked ~1 billion IP-linkage records from six major identity providers against ground truth from two ISPs and one MVPD (Dec 2024–Feb 2025) and found IP-to-postal linkages accurate on average 13% of the time and IP-to-email linkages 16%.
s: [1] CIMM/Go Addressable/Truthset release, Nov. 2025; [2] Schiff, AdExchanger, Nov. 5, 2025

claims.t: The same study found different identity providers agreed with each other on a given IP-to-postal linkage only ~7% of the time (6.4% postal / 2.8% email in detailed reporting), with >90% of linkages unique to a single provider.
Truthset publicly estimated $7.36B of ~$38B in US CTV ad spend is wasted due to inaccurate IP-based targeting.
s: [3] Truthset blog; [4] PPC Land, Feb. 2026

claims.t: FreeWheel's blog (Barrie Brandt) cites the 13%/16% figures, states FreeWheel uses IP addresses for just 17% of targeting decisions, and recommends verified household addresses, streaming first-party IDs, and direct ISP connections — while conceding ISP-sourced IP 'is as good as any identifier.
s: [6] Brandt, FreeWheel Insights blog, ca. Feb. 2026

claims.t: Go Addressable is an MVPD-founded addressable-TV consortium and FreeWheel is owned by Comcast; both benefit commercially if buyers shift from open-market IP graphs to ISP/MVPD-verified household data — a structural conflict relevant to weighing the 'IP is broken' framing.

The most accurate of the six benchmarked providers was approximately 4.5x more accurate than the least — the IP-graph camp's strongest internal evidence that practice, not signal, drives the failures.
s: [2] Schiff, AdExchanger, Nov. 5, 2025

claims.t: Beyond RFC 8981 interface-ID rotation (24–72h), large broadband ISPs now rotate entire /56–/48 customer prefixes as often as daily, making one household appear as many; IPv6 traffic share is ~52.5% (US), 86.7% (France), 78.7% (India), 75.1% (Germany).
s: [12] Donnini, IPinfo blog, Nov. 2025

claims.t: Chrome's IP Protection launched for Incognito mode only (Q3 2025 target, desktop + Android), masking IP only in third-party contexts for domains on a Masked Domain List, via a two-hop proxy preserving coarse geolocation; Google had separately reversed third-party-cookie deprecation in 2025.
s: [15] GoogleChrome/ip-protection spec + Privacy Sandbox overview; [30] CyberInsider/Digiday

claims.t: Alex Cone (then VP Privacy, IAB Tech Lab, May 2021) wrote that with Private Relay 'one company making decisions for the internet is not even close to ideal,' argued privacy solutions 'should be developed out in the open,' and endorsed Microsoft's open PARAKEET proposal as the standards-based alternative.
s: [27] Cone, IAB Tech Lab, May 2021

claims.t: CJEU C-582/14 (Oct. 19, 2016) held a dynamic IP address is personal data for a website operator with lawful means to identify the user via the ISP, while also holding member states cannot narrow the legitimate-interest basis below EU law's standard.
s: [16] CJEU C-582/14 judgment; [20] Zuiderveen Borgesius, EDPL 2017

claims.t: CNIL guidance treats targeted advertising/profiling as consent-required, and its consent-exempt audience-measurement regime requires recording only the first three octets of the IP; French segmented TV operates under CNIL supervision with GDPR/ePrivacy applying.
s: [21] CNIL publicité ciblée guidance; [22] Silexo summary; [25] alloforfait.fr on segmented-TV décret

claims.t: The Datenschutzkonferenz's Orientierungshilfe Telemedien holds that information necessarily transmitted at connection (including the public IP) does not trigger §25 TTDSG/TDDDG consent, but subsequent processing (e.g., for advertising identity) is assessed under GDPR, where the DSK reads consent broadly for profiling.
s: [23] DSK OH Telemedien 2021 v1.1; [24] Piwik PRO / German legal-blog summaries

claims.t: CCPA's personal-information definition names IP addresses and uniquely extends to households; Oregon's OCPA covers data linkable to devices of 'one or more consumers in a household'; ~20 states have comprehensive laws — all opt-out-of-sale/share regimes rather than EU-style consent-default.
s: [17] Perkins Coie state-law recap; [18] DWT/Osano/Ketch analyses

claims.t: As of 2025, UID2 integrations span Disney, NBCUniversal, Paramount, Roku, AMC Networks, Dish Media, and FreeWheel, positioning authenticated identity as the premium-CTV incumbent-in-waiting; Experian's CTV materials explicitly frame UID2 as emerging because IP durability is degrading.
s: [19][33] Experian Marketing, authenticated audiences in CTV

claims.t: VideoAmp, iSpot, and Comscore passed the US JIC's 699-test certification audit for the 2025-26 broadcast season; their commingled ACR+STB datasets resolve to households via identity-graph crosswalks in which IP is a core join key, and VideoAmp/iSpot license TVision panel data for person-level calibration.
s: [35] Marketing Dive / Variety; [36] Adweek; [38] VideoAmp VALID; [39] Beet.TV; [40] TVision repost of AdAge

claims.t: Nielsen's Big Data + Panel launched for the 2025 season combining its ~42,000-home panel with return-path/ACR data from ~45M households / 75M devices.
s: [34] PPC Land; NextTV

claims.t: Per DoubleVerify fraud-lab telemetry: 140% scheme growth, 10x fraudulent CTV apps 2025 vs 2024, SneakyTerra spoofing ~2M devices/day with ~$5M/month unprotected exposure; datacenter-IP traffic dominates violations in APAC (98%) and LATAM (91%) vs bot fraud (82%) in North America.
s: [48] DoubleVerify newsroom; [49] PPC Land / AdExchanger coverage

claims.t: IAB Tech Lab's ads.cert 2.0 (Sept. 2021) provides cryptographic authentication of server-to-server connections aimed at SSAI request/billing fraud; Tech Lab has repeatedly urged universal SSAI implementation, and adoption remains the acknowledged gap nearly five years on.
s: [50] IAB Tech Lab press release, Sept. 30, 2021; [51] MediaPost / VideoWeek

claims.t: Samsung and LG keep ACR data captive to their own ad businesses; Vizio (Walmart-owned) licenses ACR broadly via Inscape; the Texas AG sued five major TV manufacturers (Dec. 2025) over ACR surveillance without consent, and Samsung settled in February 2026.
s: [43] AdExchanger ACR walled-gardens pieces; [44] ComplianceHub + Lobato, Convergence (SAGE) 2025; [45] State of Surveillance tracker

claims.t: Pixalate documented the 'iP64' exploit in which fraudsters hid behind iCloud Private Relay's IP space, estimating ~$65M fraud cost and that ~90% of purported Private-Relay traffic was invalid (Aug. 2022 study).
s: [31] Pixalate iP64 report, Nov. 2022; [32] AppleInsider, Nov. 22, 2022

claims.t: Google's measurement of users reaching its services over IPv6 crossed 50% for the first time on/around 28 March 2026 (50.10%), per Internet Society Pulse's report on the Google dataset.
s: Internet Society Pulse blog, April 2026 [1]; APNIC Labs corroboration [4]

claims.t: US IPv6 adoption is ~50–53% (Google); dominant cable ISPs run native dual-stack (Comcast documents dual-stack with IPv6 prefix delegation and one dynamic public IPv4 per household, not CGNAT); US CTV ad spend is ~$33.35bn in 2025 with programmatic share 84–90%+.
s: Google data via Pulse/secondary [1][2]; Comcast technical documentation [21]; eMarketer [9]; Señal News/IAB (84%) and MNTN (90%+) [10][11]

claims.t: France's IPv6 adoption measures ~73% (ISOC Pulse, mid-2025) to ~86% (Google statistics as reported Feb 2026) — the highest of any large economy.
s: The Register reporting ISOC Pulse, June 2025 [2]; DNS Made Easy citing Google, Feb 2026 [3]

claims.t: Germany measures ~70–76% IPv6, but Vodafone provisions residential cable as IPv6-native DS-Lite with IPv4 only via CGNAT; Deutsche Telekom's legacy Zwangstrennung shaped dynamic-IP expectations, and Telekom's current practice includes IP renewal at least every 180 days plus Speedport router privacy features rotating parts of the IPv6 address daily or both IPv4/IPv6 every four days.
s: Practitioner documentation of Vodafone DE DS-Lite/CGNAT [13][14]; Telekom hilft community pages [15]

claims.t: Spain measures ~10% and Italy ~17% IPv6 adoption — among the lowest in Western Europe — while fixed-line address sharing is widespread: in Spain via MásOrange (MásMóvil/Yoigo/Pepephone), Digi, Finetwork and Orange/Jazztel (DS-Lite), with incumbent Movistar assigning public IPv4 on fixed fiber and CGNAT-ing only mobile; in Italy via Sky WiFi's MAP-T (~16:1 sharing), with TIM fixed-line CGNAT practitioner-reported but not regulator-verified.
s: DNS Made Easy/IPXO reporting Google data [3][12]; PureVPN (Tier 6, corroboration only) and IlSoftware.it (Tier 5) [16][37]

claims.t: The CJEU ruled in Breyer v Germany (C-582/14, 19 Oct 2016) that dynamic IP addresses constitute personal data for a website operator with legal means to obtain identification from the ISP — the foundational case making IP-based CTV identity a GDPR-regulated activity across the EU.
s: CJEU judgment C-582/14, 2016 [20]

claims.t: India measures ~72–73% IPv6 (tied with France at the top of large economies), driven by Jio's and Airtel's mobile networks; remaining IPv4 access is heavily CGNAT'd; India's CTV ad revenue grew 42% YoY to ₹99bn (~US$1.2bn) in 2025, with ~68M CTV households (~40M weekly active), per FICCI-EY 2026.
s: Pulse/Register [1][2]; PureVPN corroboration [16]; EY newsroom and Indian trade press [22][23][24]

claims.t: China's national IPv6 program (2017 action plan; 2025 'Key Points' directive) produced 865M active IPv6 users (77.02% of internet users) by Sept 2025, with IPv6 carrying ~69% of mobile but only ~31% of fixed traffic; its dominant OTT/CTV platforms resolve identity through platform logins and parent-ecosystem data (WeChat/QQ, Baidu, Alibaba), not IPs, and global programmatic demand is structurally absent.
s: APNIC Blog, Aug 2025 [5]; ISOC Pulse, Jan 2026 [6]; CNNIC report (not read directly) [7]; China-market trade sources [25][26]

claims.t: Japan returned to ~55% IPv6 (mid-2025); the dominant fixed-line architecture (NTT East/West NGN with IPoE) delivers IPv4 as IPv4-over-IPv6 (MAP-E 'v6plus' and similar), so multiple households share one public IPv4 with allocated port ranges; ad-supported streaming is dominated by TVer (44.7M monthly unique browsers, Jan 2026) and ABEMA (28.47M weekly actives, Sept 2025).
s: ISOC Pulse via The Register [2]; JPNIC and practitioner documentation of NTT IPoE/MAP-E [27]; Adjust and Japan trade press [28][29]

claims.t: Despite world-class broadband, South Korea's consumer IPv6 adoption is far below Japan's ~55% — attributed in academic literature to long capital cycles on pre-IPv6 broadband gear and abundant legacy IPv4 holdings; government '~95% public-sector adoption' claims measure something different from consumer eyeball capability. A precise current consumer figure was not verifiable this session and is flagged as a gap.
s: Hovav et al., Research Policy 2011 [30]; APNIC regional commentary [4]; Korea CTV via [31][32][33]

claims.t: APNIC-derived measurements put Malaysia (~66%), Vietnam (~52–60%, under an explicit VNNIC national program), and Thailand (~49–50%) among regional IPv6 leaders, while the Philippines (~18.5% per DOST-ASTI citing APNIC) and Indonesia lag; mobile access across the region is heavily CGNAT'd; the practical 'CTV' surface is dominated by YouTube-on-TV and platform apps rather than a mature programmatic open market.
s: APNIC Blog [4]; The Register [34]; DOST-ASTI press release [35]; regional hosting/trade commentary [36]

claims.t: Brazil's IPv6 share of traffic rose from ~50% to ~54% in the year to late 2025 (NIC.br; 98% of Brazilian ASNs hold IPv6 allocations); Mexico passed 50% (54%, ISOC Pulse June 2025); LACNIC exhausted its IPv4 free pool in June 2014 and calls CGNAT a regional growth bottleneck; Brazil's CTV ad market is anchored by Globo, whose identity spine is the logged-in Globo ID (>140M registered IDs) rather than IP.
s: ipv6.br/NIC.br [38]; ISOC Pulse via The Register [2]; LACNIC blog [17]; Meio & Mensagem, Tela Viva [39][40]; Greenbook/Comscore [41]

claims.t: Saudi Arabia measures ~65% IPv6 (a deliberate CITC-driven boom from ~2019); continental Africa averages ~4%; AFRINIC's IPv4 pool effectively exhausted 2017–2020; AFRINIC has operated under a Mauritius court-appointed receiver, its June 2025 board election was annulled over a proxy dispute and a re-run completed Sept 2025; MENA's digital ad market reached ~$8.2bn in 2025 (IAB MENA) with CTV fastest-growing and MBC/Shahid the dominant premium-streaming ad seller.
s: APNIC Labs/Blog [18][19]; ISOC Pulse [42]; AFRINIC communiqués [43]; election reporting [44]; BroadcastPro ME/IAB MENA [45]; Variety [46]

claims.t: A Truthset study (Dec 2024–Feb 2025, ~1bn IP records from six data providers validated against two ISPs and one MVPD, publicized by FreeWheel in Feb 2026) found IP-to-postal linkages accurate 13% of the time, IP-to-email 16%, and cross-provider agreement on the same IP-to-household connection just 6.4%.
s: ppc.land on FreeWheel/Truthset, 28 Feb 2026 [47]; FreeWheel framing [48]; AdExchanger background [49]

claims.t: The IPv6 league table's top (India, China, Vietnam, Malaysia, Saudi Arabia; France partially excepted) is dominated by markets whose internet growth was mobile-first, and mobile IPv6 addresses (per-session prefixes, privacy extensions, device-not-household granularity) are the least household-resolvable IP signal that exists; IPv6 adoption percentage is therefore a negative or at best orthogonal proxy for IP-identity usability in CTV.
s: Synthesis; APNIC Blog [4][5]

claims.t: The conditions enabling US-style IP household identity (legacy IPv4 abundance per capita, long-lease dual-stack cable broadband, single-family household structure, no Breyer-style blanket personal-data jurisprudence at federal level) do not jointly exist in any other major CTV market; the Truthset finding plus growth of CGNAT'd 5G fixed-wireless access means the comfort is overstated even domestically.
s: Synthesis; Comcast [21]; ppc.land/Truthset [47]

claims.t: IAB Europe's AdEx Benchmark 2024 put European digital ad spend at €118.9bn, with video at €12.4bn (+24.5% YoY) and SVOD advertising up 222% as ad tiers rolled out; UK (€41.3bn), Germany (€17.9bn), France (€11.2bn) are the three largest digital markets.
s: IAB Europe AdEx Benchmark 2024 via IAB Europe and VideoWeek [50][51]

claims.t: Per-address IPv4 transfer prices peaked at roughly $60 (ARIN/RIPE /24s, late 2021); by February 2026 average pricing for /16-and-larger blocks had fallen to just under $10 per address, with /16s first breaking below $20 in June 2025 and small /24 blocks holding a $35–45 premium.
The 2025 IPv4 price decline coincided with near-record transfer volume (~8,062 transfers globally in 2025).
AWS's February 2024 public-IPv4 charge ($0.005/hr, ~$43/yr) converted IPv4 into a metered cloud cost, suppressing hyperscaler demand and nudging IPv6 adoption.

At 2026 prices, buying or leasing IPv4 is competitive with CGNAT for many fixed-line ISPs, relieving the pressure to expand CGNAT in mature CTV markets and slowing decay of the IPv4-household mapping.
Google measured 50.10% native IPv6 access on 28 March 2026 — the first 50% crossing — while APNIC Labs' reweighted measurement puts global IPv6 capability at ~42%.

IPv6 adoption growth is linear (~10 percentage points per 3 years, stable since 2018), neither accelerating nor plateauing globally, implying ~60% by 2029 and ~65% by 2031 on mechanical extrapolation.

IPv6 adoption is extremely uneven — India ~72%, France ~73%+, Germany ~76% vs Italy ~17%, Spain ~10%, Egypt ~4% — with the US plateaued near 45–50% and China showing high mobile (64.6%) but low fixed-line (~21%) IPv6 traffic with decelerating growth.

RFC 8981 temporary addresses — enabled by default in Windows, macOS/iOS, and Android, rotating roughly daily — structurally cap device-level IPv6 identity; the full 128-bit address in a bid request is engineered to be a poor persistent device identifier.

ISP prefix delegation (/56–/64) preserves household-level identity under IPv6 wherever prefixes are held stable, and ad infrastructure already operates at prefix grain (Google truncates IPv6 to /48 for RTB buyers).

Apple Private Relay's genuine adoption is low (~1–2% of Apple-device traffic per Pixalate 2022) and over 90% of traffic claiming Private Relay IP space showed signs of spoofing (the 'iP64' exploit, ~$65M+ estimated fraud).

Chrome IP Protection shipped in Chrome 140 (September 2025) scoped to Incognito mode, third-party contexts, and a curated Masked Domain List — leaving regular-mode browsing and all CTV device traffic uncovered.
Neither Apple Private Relay nor Chrome IP Protection covers CTV device or SSAI traffic today; platform IP-masking is a tail risk and norm-setter for CTV, not a present force.
The European Commission formally withdrew the ePrivacy Regulation proposal on 11 February 2025, leaving the 2002 ePrivacy Directive and its 27 national transpositions in force as a patchwork.

Roughly 19–20 US states have comprehensive privacy laws in effect during 2026 (Indiana, Kentucky, Rhode Island effective 1 Jan 2026), all treating IP addresses as personal information, covering well over half the US population.
India's DPDP Rules were notified in November 2025 with phased enforcement through May 2027, placing the world's largest IPv6-majority CTV growth market under a consent-first regime as it matures.

The September 2025 CJEU EDPS v SRB ruling adopted a recipient-relative view of pseudonymized data, modestly easing the legal status of truncated/hashed IPs for parties without re-identification means; the Council's February 2026 compromise stripped an attempted codification, leaving case-by-case as the standard.

US CTV ad spend reaches ~$38B in 2026 (+14% YoY, fifth straight double-digit year), with logged-in walled gardens (YouTube 24.4% gross, Amazon >10%, Hulu+Disney+ ~10.8%, Netflix fastest-growing) commanding over half of gross spend.
The June 2025 Amazon–Roku DSP partnership combined identity graphs covering an estimated 80% of US CTV households, extending deterministic resolution into formerly IP-resolved open inventory.

A Truthset study publicized by FreeWheel found IP-to-postal-address linkages accurate only 13% and IP-to-email linkages 16% of the time, indicting probabilistic IP-household graphs used for CTV targeting and frequency capping.

CTV invalid-traffic rates ran ~18% in mid-2025, IVT is ~110% higher where SSAI is used, and DoubleVerify's SneakyTerra SSAI scheme spoofed ~2M devices/day at an estimated $5M+/month cost to unprotected advertisers.
ads.cert 2.0 (announced September 2021) has open-source implementations but no publicly evidenced at-scale production enforcement four-plus years later; trade-press silence is suggestive.

Residential proxy networks renting tens of millions of household IPs (one provider claims 115M+, egress at a few dollars per GB) have commoditized residential-IP spoofing, degrading IP's fraud-signal integrity; any IP-range trust heuristic becomes an attack surface.

Contextual/AI targeting is growing as an identity substitute in CTV, but nearly all quantitative support is vendor-sponsored (41% contextual-primary, ID5's 91% alt-ID figures), and contextual cannot substitute for frequency capping or reach measurement — capping this driver's ceiling at the targeting layer.

Cheap IPv4 and linear IPv6 form a negative feedback loop that maintains a half-transitioned dual-stack, mixed-signal equilibrium through and beyond 2030 — the price mechanism actively maintains 'the transition stays half-finished' as the equilibrium, not a failure scenario.

T-Mobile's SEC-filed Q4 2025 release reports 8.450M 5G broadband (FWA) customers at year-end 2025 (9.447M total broadband incl. ~1.0M fiber; 1.879M 2025 5G broadband net adds); in Feb 2026 it raised its target from 12M by 2028 to 15M 5G broadband by 2030 (plus 3–4M T-Fiber, 18–19M total).
s: [1][2][3] — SEC 8-K ex. 99.1 (Q4/FY2025); T-Mobile Capital Markets Day release Feb 2026
