T-Mobile FWA provides no public, household-unique IPv4: IPv6-native network with IPv4 via 464XLAT through carrier-grade NAT; port forwarding and inbound connections unsupported; residential service cannot be converted to static/public IPv4 (business-account add-on only). The IPv4 a CTV SSP observes is a tower/region egress shared across an unknown number of households.
s: [12][13][14][15] — T-Mobile Community threads; FlexRadio forum; CleanBrowsing doc; Pinggy guide

claims.t: Verizon 5G Home places residential customers behind CGNAT (shared public IPv4, inoperative port forwarding/DMZ; static IP via paid/business path); AT&T Internet Air mixes CGNAT (100.64.0.0/10 shared-address-space WANs) and public dynamic IPv4 by market/account, with no bridge mode on AIA gateways and AT&T support docs recommending cloud-relay devices for inbound needs.
s: [16][17][18][19] — Verizon Community/theispinfo; PureVPN (corroboration only); AT&T device-support article; Netgate forum

claims.t: Starlink reached ~2.7M US subscribers by May 2026 (~10M global, base doubled in 2025), a top-10 US ISP; Residential and Roam plans are CGNAT'd by default (no inbound IPv4), public routable IPv4 only on Local/Global Priority (business) plans; Starlink runs native IPv6 with delegated prefixes. Only ~20% of US customers switched from cable — Starlink mostly ADDS NAT'd households rather than converting unique-IP homes.
s: [20][21][22][23] — Broadband Breakfast (New Street); Starlink Help Center (excerpt); Hostifi; jmcglock/satspeedcheck

claims.t: Per Leichtman Research Group, fixed wireless was ~90% of top-provider US broadband net adds in 2022 and ~104% in 2023 (exceeding total market growth as cable/DSL shrank); pattern persisted through 2025 (top-cable share ~62.5% by end-3Q 2025; FWA residential gross adds +24% YoY Q4 2025 per New Street); Comcast lost 587K broadband customers in 2025 (31.842M→31.255M) and 65K more in Q1 2026; Charter lost 120K in Q1 2026.
s: [24][25][26][27][28] — IEEE ComSoc/LRG; Telecompetitor/LRG; LRG site; Fierce/New Street; Comcast 8-Ks (EDGAR) + Fierce (Charter)

claims.t: The incumbent wireline base anchoring the US anomaly has not flipped: Comcast documents native dual-stack with one dynamic public IPv4 per household plus DHCPv6 PD; Charter/Spectrum and major cable ISPs remain public-IPv4-per-home; AT&T Fiber assigns public dynamic IPv4 and delegates a /60 IPv6 prefix — the erosion is additive at the growth edge, not (yet) a conversion of the wireline stock.
s: [30][31][32][33][12] — Comcast IPv6 deployment doc; AT&T Community; lilchancep GitHub + Wanderer Medium; forwardingplane.net; T-Mobile Community

claims.t: Summing Q1 2026 bases — T-Mobile ~8.9M (Tier 1 floor 8.45M YE2025) + Verizon 6.006M + AT&T 2.332M + Starlink ~2.7M — yields ≈19.9M connections behind CGNAT, ≈14.8% of 134.79M US households. Projecting carriers' stated targets (T-Mobile 15M/2030; Verizon 8–9M/2028; AT&T ~4–5M and Starlink US ~4–5M extrapolated) gives ~31–34M (~23–25% of households) by 2030; a conservative case (targets missed ~25%) still lands ~24–27M (~18–20%).
s: [1][5][7][10][20][29][34][35] — carrier filings; FRED TTLHH (134,790K households, 2025); Fierce/New Street; growth-bracketing sources

claims.t: A CTV ad request from an FWA/Starlink home carries a shared carrier-egress IPv4: IP-keyed frequency caps pool hundreds-to-thousands of households into one 'home' (cap contamination, premature exhaustion) or break when egress rotates; IP-to-postal graphs mis-link by construction (IP geolocates to a carrier gateway, often another city); the available IPv6-prefix alternative is not operationally used — Truthset finds IPv6 under-represented by 72% in commercial IP datasets, with IP-to-postal accurate only ~13% and 3× more IPs-per-postal than plausible.
s: [36][37][12][16][21] — Truthset study; ppc.land/FreeWheel; operator NAT sources

claims.t: FWA/satellite adoption concentrates in suburban/rural and value-seeking segments (T-Mobile markets FWA to suburban/rural/smaller markets; Starlink predominantly rural with ~20% from cable), while FAST/AVOD viewing over-indexes among lower/middle-income households — so CGNAT erosion concentrates in the highest-FAST-consumption homes, where IP-identity failure does the most damage to AVOD monetization.
s: [6][9][20][38][39] — trade carrier coverage; Broadband Breakfast; Adwave income analysis; Tubi 'The Stream' reports

claims.t: A targeted sweep of CTV trade coverage (AdExchanger, Digiday) and vendor publications (FreeWheel, Truthset, LiveRamp, Adswerve, Experian/TransUnion-adjacent) found extensive treatment of IP frailty in CTV — privacy, Apple/Google obfuscation, accuracy, MDU confusion — but zero public treatment of FWA or satellite CGNAT as a household-identity problem; the closest is FreeWheel's MDU 'acutely wrong' concession.
s: [36][37][40][41][42][43] — Truthset; ppc.land/FreeWheel; Digiday; AdExchanger; Adswerve; LiveRamp

claims.t: The VPPA (18 U.S.C. § 2710), enacted 1988 after Judge Bork's video-rental history was published, creates civil liability for a "video tape service provider" that knowingly discloses PII concerning any consumer; "consumer" means any renter, purchaser, or subscriber of goods or services; PII "includes" information identifying a person as having requested or obtained specific video materials; remedies include liquidated damages of not less than $2,500 per violation, punitive damages, and fees — the figure that powers class-action economics and pre-trial settlements.
s: [1] 18 U.S.C. § 2710 (Cornell LII); [2] Yershov v. Gannett, 1st Cir. 2016; [12] ABA Business Law Today (Apr. 2025); [13] WilmerHale 2024 year-in-review

claims.t: The 2012 "Netflix amendment" (H.R. 6671, Pub. L. 112-258, signed Jan. 2013) permitted electronic, advance consent for up to two years so Netflix users could auto-share viewing to Facebook; Congress left "consumer," "PII," and "video tape service provider" untouched, and no narrowing bill has advanced since — the de facto reform venue is now the Supreme Court.
s: [2] Yershov opinion; [3] H.R. 6671 text (GovTrack); [4] S. Rep. 112-258 (govinfo); [5] Hunton alert (Dec. 2012); [6] H.R. 8818 APRA status (Congress.gov)

claims.t: The First Circuit held Gannett's disclosure to Adobe of video title + GPS coordinates + Android ID was PII because "the linkage, as plausibly alleged, is both firm and readily foreseeable to Gannett" — Adobe has the "game program" to convert device ID + location into a named person — and held a free-app user is a "subscriber" because access required "consideration in the form of that information." PII turns on the recipient's foreseeable ability to re-identify; the data-as-consideration theory is the direct ancestor of Salazar v. NBA.
s: [2] Yershov v. Gannett, 820 F.3d 482 (1st Cir. Apr. 29, 2016), slip op.; [7] Ropes & Gray and Eric Goldman analyses; [8] Salazar v. NBA (2d Cir. 2024)

claims.t: The Third Circuit held VPPA PII "applies only to the kind of information that would readily permit an ordinary person to identify a specific individual's video-watching behavior" and that "digital identifiers like IP addresses" fall outside the Act's protections, warning a contrary rule would make third-party cookies on any video-streaming site "presumptively illegal." The court distinguished (not rejected) Yershov and left a technology contingency: if a tool ever lets an ordinary person resolve an IP to a person, the outcome flips. Decided four months before the CJEU's Breyer went the other way for EU law.
s: [9] In re Nickelodeon Consumer Privacy Litig., 827 F.3d 262 (3d Cir. 2016), slip op.; [10] Covington Inside Privacy; Davis Wright Tremaine (July 2016)

claims.t: Robinson v. Disney Online (SDNY 2015) dismissed a claim over a Roku device serial number + viewing history shared with Adobe; Eichenberger v. ESPN (9th Cir. 2017) adopted Nickelodeon's ordinary-person standard on the same Roku fact pattern while holding a VPPA violation is itself concrete Article III injury; Solomon v. Flipps Media (2d Cir. May 1, 2025) held a Facebook ID + title in a Meta Pixel transmission is not PII. The identifier case law governing CTV device IDs was made on CTV (Roku) facts and came out defendant-friendly everywhere except the First Circuit.
s: [11] Robinson v. Disney Online, 152 F. Supp. 3d 176 (S.D.N.Y. 2015) + Proskauer; [14] Eichenberger v. ESPN, 875 F.3d 979 (9th Cir. 2017) + Wilson Sonsini, Fenwick; [15] Solomon v. Flipps Media, No. 23-7597 (2d Cir.

claims.t: Beginning fall 2022, plaintiffs' firms filed hundreds of putative VPPA class actions — roughly 200/year, at least 28 in early 2025 — against streamers, sports leagues, broadcasters, and publishers (Paramount, AMC, NBA, NFL, FloSports, Boston Globe), almost all alleging the Meta Pixel or similar tags transmitted video titles plus identifiers to ad-tech recipients; several firms run parallel threatened mass arbitrations; no federal VPPA class action has gone to trial. The Meta Pixel sits on ~47% of websites (55% of the S&P 500), so the playbook scales mechanically.
s: [12] ABA Business Law Today (Apr. 2025); [13] WilmerHale (Feb. 2025); [16] ClassAction.org VPPA tracker; [17] Robinson+Cole

claims.t: Salazar v. NBA (2d Cir. Oct. 15, 2024) held a "consumer" includes a subscriber of any of the provider's goods or services (a free email newsletter), treating exchange of name/email/IP address/cookies as the value-exchange of a subscription — the VPPA is "no dinosaur statute." The Sixth Circuit (Salazar v. Paramount Global, Apr. 3, 2025) held the opposite; the Seventh (Gardner v. MeTV) sided with the Second; the D.C. Circuit (Pileggi) with the Sixth. SCOTUS granted certiorari in Salazar v. Paramount Global (No. 25-459) on January 26, 2026.
s: [8] Salazar v. NBA (2d Cir. 2024); [13]; [17]; [18] Holland & Knight, Sidley, Benesch; [19] Salazar v. Paramount Global (6th Cir. 2025); [20] WilmerHale (Jan. 30, 2026); [21] Oyez No.

claims.t: (a) In re Vizio (C.D. Cal. Mar. 2017) refused to dismiss a VPPA claim against a TV OEM, holding Vizio plausibly a "video tape service provider" where ACR viewing data was shared with IP addresses, MAC addresses, zip codes. (b) On Apr. 29, 2025, the Michigan AG sued Roku under the VPPA/COPPA/Michigan law, alleging Roku shared viewing-linked PII — including IP addresses, device serials, location — with Google, Meta, LinkedIn, Innovid, New Relic without consent, with non-functioning privacy toggles; first state-AG VPPA action against a CTV platform. (c) A Jan.
s: [23] In re Vizio, 238 F. Supp. 3d 1204 (C.D. Cal. 2017) summaries; [24] Michigan v. Roku complaint (michigan.gov) + Hunton, Troutman, Privado; [25] Top Class Actions (Jan. 2026)

claims.t: AMC Networks settled a consolidated Meta Pixel VPPA class action covering six streaming services (AMC+, Shudder, Acorn TV, AllBlk, Sundance Now, HIDIVE; class period Jan. 18, 2021-Jan. 10, 2024) for an $8.3M fund plus injunctive terms requiring suspension/removal/modification of the Meta Pixel and tracking tools from Google, Twitter, Snapchat, TikTok, and Braze. FloSports ($2.6M, 2023) and a Patreon resolution confirm a low-to-mid seven-figure settlement market per defendant. The injunctive terms matter more than the dollars: standard VPPA settlements now contractually remove ad-tech tags from streaming services.
s: [12] ABA; [26] Angeion AMC VPPA settlement notice + Top Class Actions; [27] Sourcepoint (FloSports, single-source flagged)

claims.t: Major CTV publishers withhold show-/episode-level content metadata from programmatic bid requests when identity signals (device IDs, IPs) are present, attributing this to the VPPA: NBCU's Ryan McConville ("you just can't have identity data next to show-level data"), Tubi CRO Mark Rotblat, GroupM/Essence's Mike Fisher. Buyers route around via ACR data, cohorts, clean rooms. Read against Claims 9.4-9.5, the practice is more conservative than case law requires in most circuits, suggesting the VPPA partly functions as legal cover for hoarding competitively valuable content data.
s: [28] AdExchanger, "The Blockbuster-Era Law Behind Connected TV's Transparency Problem" (Jan. 5, 2023), with corpus cross-reference to docs 03-04

claims.t: Defendants respond with (1) arbitration clauses with mass-arbitration provisions under 2024 AAA rules, (2) the VPPA's consent safe harbor — informed written consent in distinct form, electronic, up to two years — now implemented as consent language and interstitials in streaming sign-up flows, (3) Article III standing challenges under TransUnion, (4) PII defenses under the ordinary-person standard, and (5) First Amendment/due-process challenges to $2,500 statutory damages. Law-firm alerts uniformly counsel pixel audits, consent capture, and tracker inventories for video pages.
s: [12] ABA; [14] Wilson Sonsini; [15] Perkins Coie, Morgan Lewis; [18] Holland & Knight; [26] AMC settlement terms

claims.t: Through mid-2026, no European DPA has levied a major GDPR fine specifically on CTV viewing-data/IP sharing in bid streams, while the VPPA has generated hundreds of suits, seven-figure settlements with pixel-removal injunctions, a state-AG action against a CTV platform, and a SCOTUS case — making the private US channel the more concretely realized deterrent on streaming-data disclosure.
s: Synthesis of [2], [8]-[28] and corpus docs 05-06

claims.t: Poese, Uhlig, Kaafar, Donnet, and Gueye, auditing five geolocation databases (MaxMind, IP2Location, InfoDB, HostIP, Software77) against PoP-level ground truth from a large European ISP, found country-level accuracy of 96–98% but city-level errors systematically on the order of hundreds of kilometers — concluding verbatim: 'Geolocation databases can claim country-level accuracy, but certainly not city-level.' Fine /29 block splitting worsened accuracy ('granularity theater'); >45% of all entries concentrated in the US.
s: [1] Poese et al., SIGCOMM CCR 41(2), Apr 2011; corroboration [2][3]

claims.t: Shavitt & Zilberman compiled vendors' circa-2010 published accuracy claims (IP2Location 99% country/80% city; MaxMind 99.8%/83% US city; NetAcuity 99.9%/95%; Akamai 97.22%/100% US city; Quova 99.9%/97.2% state) and documented these were self-reported, methodologically opaque, or audited against undisclosed reference data; their own PoP-level evaluation of ~100,000 grouped IPs found databases placing only 33–73% of IPs within 40 km of the cross-database majority location, error tails of thousands of km holding up to 15% of addresses, and 100% cross-database agreement on fewer than 4% of PoPs.
s: [2] Shavitt & Zilberman, IEEE JSAC 29(10), 2011 (arXiv:1005.5674); corroboration [1][15][16]

claims.t: Gharaibeh et al. (IMC 2017), evaluating geolocation databases against a 16,586-router ground-truth set, found country-level accuracy of 77.5–78.6% for MaxMind and IP2Location (vs MaxMind's published 99.8% claim, cited directly in the paper) and 89.4% for NetAcuity; at city level (40 km threshold), MaxMind-Paid achieved 66.5% accuracy on only 50.3% coverage (RTT-proximity dataset; 43.9% on DNS-based data), with the explicit recommendation: 'We do not recommend MaxMind databases if high city-level accuracy and coverage are required.
s: [3] Gharaibeh et al., IMC 2017; with [4][11]

claims.t: As of May 2019, MaxMind's published self-assessment stated GeoIP2-City maps an IP to the correct ZIP code 36% of the time, within 10 km 62%, within 100 km 90%; MaxMind's current (2026) documentation states ~99.8% country, ~80% US state, 66% US city within 50 km, city accuracy '20% to 75%' globally — and, verbatim, that geolocation data 'is never precise enough to identify or locate a specific household, individual, or street address.
s: [5] Ganelin 2019 (preserving May 2019 MaxMind page); [6][7] MaxMind support/marketing pages (accessed 2026-06-11); [8] flagged-unfetched tool

claims.t: Ganelin (MIT MEng thesis, 2019; supervised by Isaac Chuang), comparing MaxMind-geolocated ZIP codes against ground-truth ZIPs from mailing addresses supplied by MITx/HarvardX MOOC registrants, found the MaxMind ZIP matched ground truth for 18% of users — 'half the advertised number' — with errors socioeconomically biased: larger geographic and economic errors for users from more economically distressed areas.
s: [5] Ganelin, MIT MEng thesis 2019 (arXiv:1907.03834); corroboration [9]

claims.t: The Truthset/CIMM headline — ~13% IP-to-postal accuracy across six identity vendors, 6.4% cross-vendor agreement, 4.5x best-to-worst spread — is quantitatively consistent with, and predictable from, figures already public: MaxMind's ~36% self-claimed correct ZIP (2019), Ganelin's 18% audit (2019), and the 2011–2017 literature; the decrement from 18% to 13% requires no new mechanism — staleness, vendor heterogeneity, and IPv6 underrepresentation suffice. The dispute is not 'is the 13% real?' but 'why did an industry transact for a decade against numbers its own dominant vendor had disclaimed?

Saxon & Feamster (PAM 2022), using GPS-located smartphone ground truth in New York, Chicago, and Philadelphia, found MaxMind paid GeoIP2 median errors of 2.62/3.31/4.02 km on fixed-line broadband; the median fixed-line /24 moved <1 km over two months and address churn 'takes months'; geolocation is far worse on mobile; paid databases often not significantly better than free.
s: [9] Saxon & Feamster, PAM 2022 (arXiv:2105.13389); corroboration [10]

claims.t: Nabi, Bliton, Chung, and Hasan (arXiv preprint, May 2026), evaluating MaxMind GeoLite2, IPinfo, IP2Location, and DB-IP against RIPE Atlas and UNICEF Giga ground truth across 175 countries, found mobile-network median errors of 179–207 km vs 3–16 km on fixed networks; city-level failure rates of 53–61% in Asia and 66–72% in Africa vs 9–20% in Europe; ~70% of mobile prefixes span >100 km, with provider gaps attributed to prefix granularity coarser than BGP announcements.
s: [10] Nabi et al., arXiv:2605.21937, May 2026; corroboration [1][9]

claims.t: Operator-published geofeeds grew tenfold in 18 months (3.22M IPv4 addresses Apr 2022 to 34.3M Oct 2023, per Fainchtein & Sherr PAM 2024) yet covered only ~0.80% of IPv4 space across 2,805 ASNs (~2.4% of allocated ASNs); 95.3% of geofeed-published addresses were in Europe, Oceania, and North America (Africa 0.18%); a NOMS 2025 follow-up found 10.49% of geofeed lines malformed, with RIPE NCC accounting for 82–88% of geofeed-enabled records. Geofeeds cannot plausibly underwrite postal-level accuracy at CTV scale before 2030 absent a step-change in operator incentives.
s: [12] Fainchtein & Sherr, PAM 2024; [13] Desai et al., NOMS 2025; [14] RFC 8805/9632/9092

claims.t: Across the corpus's documented accuracy-war record (CIMM/Truthset release, AdExchanger coverage, FreeWheel's response, vendor rebuttals — docs 02, 03, 05 and their source lists), no participant cites Poese et al., Shavitt & Zilberman, Gharaibeh et al., Ganelin, Saxon & Feamster, or MaxMind's own published accuracy tables; the debate proceeds as though IP-location accuracy had never been measured before November 2025. The absence is symmetrical and self-harming: Camp A forgoes a 15-year falsification pedigree; Camp B forgoes Saxon & Feamster's residential-broadband results.
s: Corpus docs 01–07 (internal grep); [15][16] for the war's actual citation base

claims.t: RFCs 9297 (Aug 2022), 9298 (Aug 2022), and 9484 (Oct 2023) are IETF Proposed Standards authored/edited by Google, Cloudflare, Apple, and Ericsson engineers; Cloudflare confirms MASQUE enables Private Relay, Akamai built Private Relay egress on MASQUE, and Chrome IP Protection uses CONNECT/CONNECT-UDP (MASQUE).

The MASQUE charter states the WG 'is not intended to be a long-lived working group'; remaining items are extensions (connect-ethernet at IESG; QUIC-aware proxying in WG Last Call; bound-UDP in IETF Last Call ending June 23, 2026; DNS config draft), plus RFC 9931's security update to RFC 9298. Deployment, not design, is what remains through 2030.

RFC 9298 warns of 'significant risks in allowing arbitrary clients to establish a tunnel to arbitrary targets... attributed to the UDP proxy,' recommending restriction to authenticated users — the standards-layer root of both the iP64 exploit pattern (doc 05, Claim 5.20) and the Privacy Pass token-gating answer. The iP64 linkage is interpretive.

RFC 9458 (Jan 2024) splits relay (sees IP, not content) from gateway (sees content, not IP) and is 'only useful for an application that does not carry state between requests'; production deployments include Apple's ODoH/OHTTP support and Mozilla–Fastly Firefox telemetry (since Oct 2023), and Fastly sells OHTTP relaying as a metered product. The fit to impression beacons/attribution postbacks is the document's flagged inference; no ad-measurement deployment is publicly documented.

RFCs 9576/9577/9578 (June 2024) define Client/Origin/Issuer/Attester roles enabling authentication 'without learning any unique, per-Client information'; RFC 9578 defines privately verifiable (VOPRF) and publicly verifiable (blind RSA) token issuance; authors span Cloudflare, Fastly, Google, and Brave.

Apple shipped PATs at WWDC 2022 (iOS 16/macOS 13) with secure-enclave device attestation and Cloudflare/Fastly issuer services accepted in place of CAPTCHAs; Chrome IP Protection uses an RSA blind signature scheme to isolate client identity from all proxy servers, with daily quotas, short token lifetimes, and per-token caps.

Chrome's PRT explainer specifies tokens on proxied requests (for enrolled domains) decryptable 'after a delay' with the original IP present 'in a small percent of tokens issued,' using re-randomizable ElGamal so reuses are unlinkable; stated purpose is fraud measurement, not real-time blocking — statistical IP access replacing deterministic IP access.

Cloudflare, Fastly, and Akamai confirm in their own blogs that they operate Private Relay egress (Cloudflare: 'second relay... pool of IP addresses for exclusive use by Private Relay'; Fastly: Private Gateway 'second internet relays'; Akamai: managed MASQUE/ODoH egress services); Google states external CDNs will run IP Protection's proxy B on Google-purchased IP blocks with deferred BGP control; Fastly separately sells OHTTP relay per-GB/per-request. This creates a third constituency with growth incentives for obfuscation volume.

APNIC-published measurement of the Private Relay network (Jan 2023) found ingress addresses partially in the same Akamai AS present in the egress collection, such that 'a single entity can observe both ingress and egress traffic' on some paths, enabling Tor-style correlation in principle.

Apple's deployment guide states network relays — built on MASQUE, carrying all TCP and UDP traffic, configurable per-app/per-domain/device-wide via MDM or NERelayManager — are available on devices with iOS 17, iPadOS 17, macOS 14, tvOS 17, or later. No default-on consumer relay service exists on tvOS (Private Relay not extended to it), so corpus Claim 4.13 stands as written — but the capability now precedes the toggle.

Ericsson — RFC 9484 co-author — has published architecture placing a MASQUE server/function at the 5G User Plane Function; framed as QoE assistance, it is structurally an operator relay. No commercial ISP consumer privacy-relay deployment was found as of 2026-06-11; the W3C has no work item on non-browser IP masking (checked absence).

As of June 2026 the privacypass WG has active drafts on Anonymous Rate-Limited Credentials (crypto and protocol), Batched Token Issuance (WG Last Call), public-metadata issuance, and token expiration — the standards pipeline is moving from binary real/not-real tokens toward bounded-count anonymous credentials, the primitive a frequency-cap-without-identity system would need. The frequency-capping application is inference; no such application is documented.

Attested tokens substitute a platform-rooted cryptographic 'real client' signal for IP reputation, demoting fraud vendors from independent observers to credential verifiers (Rescorla's centralization risk: 'further entrenching the existing big players'); simultaneously, hardware attestation is unforgeable by the server-side device-spoofing schemes (ICEBUCKET, SneakyTerra) that constitute the marquee CTV fraud cases, making attestation a structurally stronger IVT signal where deployed.

Calibrated inference: ~60–70% that ad-funded TV OS traffic remains unproxied by default through 2030; ~25–35% that some default-on platform proxy touches a meaningful CTV device class (tvOS most likely first); ~40–55% that Privacy Pass-style attestation enters production CTV anti-fraud. Grounds: protocol preconditions met (Claims 11.1–11.10), incentives absent among ad-funded vendors (docs 03/07), fraud-economics pull strong (Claim 11.13).
s: Synthesis of Claims 11.1–11.13 and corpus docs 02/03/05/07

claims.t: In SSAI, the ad decision server's connection terminates at the stitcher's datacenter IP, not the household IP; per IAB Tech Lab VAST 4.2 §1.1.3 the end-device IP must therefore be conveyed separately as application-layer payload (header or macro), and the spec itself states this makes legitimate SSAI traffic "look similar to invalid traffic" to the receiving ad server.
s: IAB Tech Lab, VAST 4.2 specification, §1.1.3 (June 2019) [1]

claims.t: VAST 4.1+ (per VAST 4.2 §1.1.3) makes X-Device-IP a "must"-include header carrying "the IP address of the device on whose behalf this request is being made," and explicitly deprecates X-Forwarded-For to backward-compatibility only; the spec's sole integrity provision is the unenforced sentence "The information included in these headers must match the information in the original ad request payload.
s: IAB Tech Lab, VAST 4.2 §1.1.3 [1]; history corroboration Pixalate (2019) [9]

claims.t: Per IAB Tech Lab SSAI VAST Macro Guidance v1.0 (Nov 2020), server-side macros and headers are populated by "the party that performs VAST HTTP requests" — in SSAI, the stitching server — meaning the end-device IP is structurally an assertion by the intermediary, never a value the device authenticates for itself.
s: IAB Tech Lab, SSAI VAST Macro Guidance v1.0, Nov 2020 [2]

claims.t: VAST 4.1's [DEVICEIP] macro carries "IP address of the device that is rendering the ad," explicitly "only relevant when another device (server) is making the request on behalf of that client"; the companion [SERVERSIDE] macro defaults to 0 (client) when missing — so an SSAI request that omits server-side macros declares itself client-side by default, the lowest-scrutiny posture for a datacenter-originated call.
s: IAB Tech Lab SSAI VAST Macro Guidance [2]; IAB Tech Lab VAST 4.x Macros living list [3]

claims.t: AWS Elemental MediaTailor conveys the device IP to the ADS by proxying the legacy x-forwarded-for header or via the [session.client_ip] variable, which it defines as "the remote IP address that the MediaTailor request came from"; the docs warn that with a CDN in front, the operator "must proxy the correct header from the player," making each upstream hop (player→CDN→MediaTailor) a place the household IP can be lost or overwritten.
s: AWS MediaTailor ad server integration requirements [4]; MediaTailor session variables [5]

claims.t: MediaTailor's session-level reportingMode (client vs server, default client) determines whether the impression beacon is fired from the glass device's IP or from MediaTailor's datacenter IP — the operational fact that OpenRTB's imp.ssai signal exists to disclose, and the basis on which a DSP can flag a datacenter-IP'd beacon against a client-side declaration as suspect.
s: AWS MediaTailor, Client-side ad tracking / reportingMode [6]

claims.t: Google DAI carries the device IP via interchangeable macros (%%USER_IP%% / [DEVICEIP] / [IP_ADDRESS]) and flags server-originated impressions with ipe=ssb ("originate from the server, not the client"); Google's documented CTV frequency-capping identifier is sid/rdid (IFA-family), not the IP — confirming that in production CTV stacks the IP is the fallback household key, not the primary one, where a clean IFA is available.
s: Google Ad Manager, Macros for Dynamic Ad Insertion [7]; Google VAST ad tag URL parameters / SSB docs [8]

claims.t: FreeWheel (ad.vip), Broadpeak ($CLIENT_IP / default X-Forwarded-For forwarding), and MediaTailor ([session.client_ip]) all define the conveyed "device IP" as the source address of the connection the stitcher received, recoverable behind a CDN only if the CDN populated X-Forwarded-For; Broadpeak's docs make the CDN-strip hazard explicit by marking X-Forwarded-For "mandatory … when forwarding requests through a CDN.
s: FreeWheel parameters via Uplynk integration docs [10]; Broadpeak ad macros [11]; Broadpeak ad insertion with a CDN [12]; cf. AWS [4][5]

claims.t: Real production chains commonly compose two or more "source-IP-of-the-connection-I-received" definitions (e.g., CDN → MediaTailor [session.client_ip] → FreeWheel ad.vip), so the household IP that reaches the ad server is the product of every upstream hop having faithfully forwarded it; a single hop that omits or rewrites X-Forwarded-For silently substitutes its own address with no error surfaced downstream.
s: Inference from AWS MediaTailor [4], FreeWheel via Uplynk [10], Broadpeak [11]

claims.t: OpenRTB 2.6 defines device.ip only as "IPv4 address closest to device" with no SSAI-specific guidance on whether to populate the end-device or the SSAI-server address — the exact mispopulation surface ICEBUCKET exploited (doc 04 Claim 4.15) — and adds imp.ssai (0=unknown, 1=all client-side, 2=assets server-side/tracking client-side, 3=all server-side) as a self-declared detection aid, not an integrity mechanism; the field that should carry the truth is unconstrained and the field that flags the architecture is itself forgeable.
s: IAB Tech Lab, OpenRTB 2.6 spec (GitHub) [14]; Index Exchange, OpenRTB 2.6 features, May 2022 [15]

claims.t: The IAB/MRC SSAI and OTT Guidance (Aug 2021) states that in CTV "the routing of this traffic through a proxy or data center alone does not invalidate it," because legitimate SSAI is datacenter-originated by design; the datacenter-IP test that works on the web is therefore inverted in CTV, and the MRC shifts the trust model from the IP value to vetting the SSAI provider as a "material business partner" and to client-initiated/authenticated measurement.
s: Media Rating Council, SSAI and OTT Guidance, FINAL, Aug 2021 [16]

claims.t: Per The Trade Desk's frequency documentation, SSAI "doesn't necessarily help from a frequency cap standpoint, as ad server frequency capping will still use device IDs and IP addresses, which exist in both SSAI and client side environments" — confirming that the capping mechanism is unchanged by SSAI; what degrades is the trustworthiness of the device-IP input, which is no better than the weakest forwarding hop.
s: The Trade Desk, Frequency / partner portal documentation [17]

claims.t: Across the device→CDN→SSAI→ADS→exchange→DSP chain, the household IP can be (a) lost at the CDN→SSAI hop if X-Forwarded-For is not populated, (b) replaced with the stitcher's datacenter IP at the SSAI→ADS hop if device macros/headers are omitted (with [SERVERSIDE] defaulting to client), or (c) forged at the SSAI→ADS hop by declaring fabricated device IPs — the last being spec-indistinguishable from honest population, since the only integrity provision (VAST 4.2's "must match" sentence) governs one hop, is opt-in, and is downstream-unverifiable.
s: Synthesis of VAST 4.2 [1], SSAI Macro Guidance [2], MediaTailor [5], FreeWheel via Uplynk [10], Broadpeak [12], OpenRTB 2.6 [14]

claims.t: Blue Stream Fiber (FL FTTH) reported on NANOG (Oct 2024) that port-block-exceeded errors forced CGNAT compression from 64:1 to 28:1; GVTC (TX, ~53k subscribers) reported (May 2021) ~2,750 public IPv4 addresses with 3,000 ports/subscriber, roughly 19:1. Port-block math, not marketing ceilings, sets the ratio.
s: NANOG via seclists.org mirror: [1] Lewis 8 Oct 2024; [5] Scott 18 May 2021; [6] Gould 18 May 2021

claims.t: Blue Stream Fiber found Hulu Live TV's city-level IP geolocation for local-channel determination cannot work when one CGNAT pool spans Miami to Jacksonville; no clean fix existed within a single-pool architecture. Operators collide with geolocation, not identity/advertising.
s: NANOG [1][2], seclists.org/nanog/2024/Oct/25, /27

claims.t: When streaming services misclassify an ISP as VPN/proxy, the fix is: publish an RFC 8805 geofeed, email per-service correction aliases, consult community-maintained contact lists — no SLA, no formal channel. Dominican ISP Televiaducto was VPN-blocked by HBO Max 'for months' with geofeeds published and no response.
s: NANOG [7][8]; Brothers WISP list [32] unverified

claims.t: Lee Howard presented 'Total Cost of Ownership of CGN' (NANOG 56/APNIC 36, 2013) and 'Prisoner of IPv4' (NANOG 76, 2019), estimating CGN at ~$3,800/Gbps (hardware $1,000, IPv4 $2,000 at $50/address and 10:1 compression, software/ops $800/yr), concluding ISPs should buy IPv4 only until price exceeds ~$35; analysis monetizes latency/conversion effects on ad-supported sites.
s: Retevia [10]; APNIC 36 PDF [9]; NANOG participation [3][8]

claims.t: T-Mobile's official Home Internet documentation states streaming services relying on IP for location 'are not compatible' (naming Hulu Live and Sling Live TV), that dynamic IP changes make geolocation diverge from the gateway's physical location, and that T-Mobile cannot make the IP static. The network has been IPv6-only with 464XLAT since 2014.
s: T-Mobile support [15]; Byrne NANOG 61 [18]; ISOC [17]; forums [16]

claims.t: RFC 8978 cites German data-protection advice ([GERMAN-DP]) for delivering dynamic IPv6 prefixes by default; RIPE-690 recommends persistent prefixes but carves out countries with 'specific legal environments' for privacy-oriented non-persistent prefixes. US-side, NANOG shows stability as a side effect: dynamic DHCP leases so persistent customers 'perceive themselves as having static addresses.

Strowes (RIPE Labs, 2021; RIPE Atlas + ~30bn CDN address associations) found IPv6 assignments persist significantly longer than IPv4 (DT IPv4 users ~60% of time on ≤1-day assignments; 81% of registered assignment sizes are /56). Rye/Beverly/claffy (IMC 2021) found ~13k rotating /48s dominated by German residential ISPs (Versatel ~40%, daily) and showed ~9M EUI-64 edge routers let an observer re-link households across rotations.
s: Strowes RIPE Labs [13]; Rye, Beverly, claffy IMC 2021 [14]

claims.t: The v6ops/6man record (RFC 8978; draft-gont-v6ops-ipv6-addressing-considerations) frames address stability as a direct tradeoff with tracking-resistance; no working-group document or surfaced thread shows advertising-industry participants arguing for stable prefixes, despite the ad industry's multi-billion-dollar dependence on that property.
s: RFC 8978 [12]; draft-gont [30]; v6ops archive attempt [33]

claims.t: As of June 2026, OpenSincera's published metrics (ads-in-view, ads-to-content, page weight, refresh, identity absorption rate) contain no IP-layer metrics; Jounce's public CTV research covers bid duplication, pod deconstruction, supply-path concentration — not IP fields; Scope3 publishes per-bid-request emissions defaults (0.11442 gCO2/impression ctv-bvod) with no IP/IPv6 analysis.
s: TTD [21]; AdExchanger [22][24]; AdMonsters [23]; Yahoo/Jounce [25]; Playwire [26]; Scope3 [27]

claims.t: Pixalate published (Nov 2017) that 29.7% of programmatic CTV/OTT impressions went to IPv6-enabled devices vs 61.6% mobile app, 59.7% desktop, 44.1% mobile web (cellular 80.1% vs fixed 46.6%). No more recent vendor publication of an IPv6-share-of-CTV figure was found. Pixalate still publishes monthly AdFraud IPv4/IPv6 address reports (May 2026: 5 IPv6 in top-50 high-risk).
s: Pixalate 2017 [28]; Pixalate May 2026 [29]; bundle-ID [31]

claims.t: In June 2016 Netflix began blocking Hurricane Electric IPv6 tunnel-broker prefixes as VPN/proxy traffic, cutting off users (including those without native IPv6 options), advising affected users to disable IPv6 entirely; HE responded that its allocation is US-registered and Netflix could whitelist.
s: TorrentFreak 8 Jun 2016 [19]; forum record [20]

claims.t: Repeated targeted searches of r/adops and r/programmatic surfaced no substantive practitioner threads on IPv6 in DSPs, household graphs, or CTV frequency-capping failures; the visible IP-layer breakage record lives on the consumer/ISP side. The brief's hypothesis that DSPs silently drop IPv6-only bid requests from household graphs found neither confirmation nor refutation.
s: Methodology search-absence; [16][20][34][35]

claims.t: A mainstream historical-critical core of Jesus's life — baptized by John, taught the Kingdom, gathered disciples, crucified under Pilate c. 30 CE, proclaimed risen by his followers — is supported across virtually all current academic reconstructions.

The apocalyptic-prophet reading (Schweitzer, Sanders, Allison, Ehrman, Fredriksen) currently dominates mainstream academic historical-Jesus scholarship; the Cynic-sage reading (Crossan, Borg) and the restoration-prophet reading (Wright) are minority positions.
The Kingdom of God (basileia tou theou) is the integrating concept of Jesus's teaching; every other element — parables, beatitudes, antitheses, love commands — hangs from it.

Jesus's love-of-enemies command is the structural breaking of the retaliation cycle (lex talionis), and constitutes a distinctive philosophical position when compared to Stoic apatheia and Buddhist ahimsa.

High Christology emerged within the first decade of Christianity (Hurtado/Bauckham) rather than slowly under Hellenistic influence (Dunn/Casey/Vermes); the marana tha prayer and Pauline hymns are the key evidence.

The Chalcedonian Definition (451) — one person in two natures, 'without confusion, without change, without division, without separation' — is the load-bearing wall of historic Christology against which every subsequent dispute is measured.
Theosis is the corollary of incarnation: 'He became human so that we might become divine' (Athanasius, On the Incarnation §54) is the formula that orients Eastern Christian spirituality.

Eckhart's Gottesgeburt (birth of God in the soul) and Seelenfünklein (spark of the soul) are read both as orthodox Trinitarian Christology (McGinn) and as heterodox ground-mysticism (the 1329 condemnation), and the reading affects what Carlyle/Whitman/Jung inherit.

Modern philosophical Christologies fall into eight recurring families: speculative (Hegel), experiential (Schleiermacher), paradox-decision (Kierkegaard/Barth/Bonhoeffer), ontological-sacramental (Tillich/Rahner/Balthasar), political-liberative (Moltmann/Gutiérrez/Cone), anthropological-unmasking (Girard), weak-radical (Caputo/Žižek), and historical-realist (Wright).
Carlyle reads Christ as the 'divinest Symbol' — supreme Hero, absolute Sincerity against Sham — implicitly above the schema of his Heroes lectures rather than fitting inside it.
Whitman places Christ as one of an 'average unending procession' of divine souls; the divinity in Christ is the same divinity in every human, supremely realized in him but not different in kind.

Jung reads Christ as archetype of the Self for the Pisces aeon, with the necessary corollary that the Christ-image alone is incomplete because the shadow has not been integrated (Aion, Answer to Job).
Peirce reads the Gospel of John as cosmology: agapasm (growth by love) is the deepest of three evolutionary modes, and the universe is structured by what 1 John 4:8 calls 'God is love.
None of the four thinkers can be classified as either orthodox confessional or as merely skeptical-secular; each found himself unable to finish his thinking without Christ.

The composite four-thinker Christ is a high Christology in substance but by routes other than Chalcedon's; it is deeply continuous with the patristic-mystical tradition of theosis and the Gottesgeburt.

The composite has surprising convergences with Bonhoeffer's suffering God, Hegel's incarnational dialectic, and Girard's anti-sacrificial reading, while preserving the universal-democratic note from Whitman that orthodoxy under-articulates.

The composite's costs are real: vulnerability to dissolution into average humanity (Whitman risk), to authoritarian individualism (Carlyle risk), to thinness on the cross and resurrection (Peirce risk), and to category-confusion between psychology and theology (Jung risk).

The single most likely scenario for the trajectory of Christology in Western intellectual culture through 2050 is Mystical-Individualist Revival (30-40% probability): institutional decline continues, the mystical/Jungian/symbolic-reading line becomes culturally dominant though institutionally minor.

The four-thinker complex (Carlyle/Whitman/Jung/Peirce) is genealogically the intellectual ancestry of Scenario A (Mystical-Individualist Revival); the user's interest in these four is itself a small data point about the cultural drift.
John the Baptist is independently attested by both Josephus and the Gospels; their points of convergence constitute the historical bedrock.
s: Josephus Ant. 18.116-119
Mark 1, 6; Matthew 3, 11; Luke 3, 7

claims.t: The Josephus John passage is authentic; it contradicts Christian baptism theology and makes no Jesus connection.
s: Josephus Ant. 18.116-119; Hansen review of Marcus (2020)

claims.t: A major scholarly position (not unanimous) reads the Fourth Gospel's strenuous subordination of John as polemical response to a persistent Baptist-venerating community.
s: Baldensperger; Bultmann; Acts 19

claims.t: Mandaeans are the only surviving community for whom John is central (as chief prophet/teacher, not forerunner), historically in southern Iraq and Khuzestan.
s: Haberl-McGrath 2020; Buckley 2002

claims.t: The Synoptics deliberately and explicitly identify John with the returning Elijah of Malachi 4:5-6; this is engineered intertextuality, not analogical resonance.
Jonathan Z. Smith demolished the dying-and-rising-god category; John is excluded from it — he dies and stays dead.
s: Smith, Encyclopedia of Religion entry

claims.t: Jung produced no developed treatment of John; the shadow-precursor reading is a legitimate Jungian application but is inference, not documented Jungian analysis.
s: Jung, Aion CW 9ii (framework); absence of John in index confirmed by corpus search

claims.t: Jesus was baptized by John — among the most secure historical facts; John was most likely Jesus's greatest human influence.
(Inference) Marcus argues John saw himself as initiator of the Kingdom; Gospels muffled a real rival Baptist movement.
s: Marcus (2018) — single-source; contested by Hansen review

claims.t: US grand strategy is the inheritance of a 130-year operating system with seven permanent patterns (hemispheric primacy, Open Door, freedom of the seas, 1945 architecture, continental security, Mead's four traditions, the permanent foreign-policy state) operating continuously since at least 1898

The Monroe Doctrine as originally formulated by Monroe and J.Q. Adams in 1823 was not a hegemonic claim but a non-recolonization principle; the expansively interventionist interpretation comes later (Roosevelt Corollary 1904)

The 'isolationist 1930s' framing is substantially misleading; recent scholarship (Wertheim, others) shows continuous US engagement in trade, finance, and Asia policy even when avoiding European entanglements

Containment as articulated by Kennan in 1946-1947 was operationally different from the containment of NSC-68 (1950); Kennan favored political-economic containment, NSC-68 globalized military containment
The shift from engagement to competition with China occurred over 2015-2020 with bipartisan continuity: late Obama beginning, Trump I escalating, Biden codifying, Trump II continuing
Iraq is the paradigmatic case of cross-administration continuity: Bush invaded, Obama withdrew, Obama re-engaged against ISIS, Trump I continued, Biden continued, Trump II continues
The pivot to Asia is bipartisan: Obama announced (2011), Trump I disrupted-then-continued, Biden formalized (CHIPS, AUKUS, Camp David), Trump II continues

The Trump II hemispheric repositioning (cartel FTO, Operation Southern Spear, Maduro operation) is the most distinctive new feature of 2025-2026 US strategy but sits inside the 200-year Monroe Doctrine tradition

claims.t: Brand safety (binary floor) vs brand suitability (graduated, brand-specific); center of gravity shifted to suitability ~2017-2021.
GARM launched June 2019; Sept 2020 framework defined 11 categories (+Misinformation 2021 = 12), a floor, and low/med/high tiers.
CTV breaks the web brand-safety toolkit: no URL, app-level not content-level, SSAI severs verification, ACR partial, MFA recurs.
Content metadata is publisher-declared and sparse (~0.73 biddable categories/program).
No JS on most CTV devices, so post-bid render-time blocking largely disappears; enforcement shifts pre-bid.
CTV fraud lineage: ICEBUCKET -> StreamScam/LeoTerra -> ParrotTerra -> SneakyTerra; SSAI weaponized.
Open-programmatic CTV IVT ~18% global Q1 2025 (up from ~12%), an order of magnitude above protected web.
MRC 50%/2s viewability is a web/in-browser construct; mechanics do not transfer cleanly to full-screen CTV.
IAS taken private by Novacap, completed Dec 23 2025; the 'public-market duopoly' framing is now partly stale (DV public, IAS private).
Scope3 exited verification, selling Adloox to Peer39 (June 2026).
GARM framework survives in IAB Tech Lab taxonomy/benchmarks; no body has formally assumed stewardship to evolve it.
X antitrust suit dismissed with prejudice March 26-27 2026 (not 2025); X appealed to 5th Circuit.
FTC consent orders (Omnicom/IPG 2025; WPP/Publicis/Dentsu April 2026) bar coordinated, politically-keyed brand-safety standards.
EU CTV brand safety gated by consent law: TCF litigation (Jan 7 2026 partial IAB Europe win; TCF v2.3 mandatory Feb 2026) + DSA.
India DPDP Rules notified Nov 13 2025; full compliance May 13 2027; near-categorical ban on targeted ads to under-18s.
LATAM has highest CTV IVT Pixalate measures (Brazil 43%, Mexico 21%, Q2 2025); fraud is the binding constraint.
Content-level transparency shipped real product in 2026 (IAS Total TV; Gracenote-PubMatic) but covers premium head, not FAST tail.
Most likely 2030 governance outcome is a fragmented floor (35-45%): no GARM successor, suitability set by vendor defaults/lists/platforms.
Multi-seller curated deal IDs reached ~73% of programmatic bidding opportunities by April 2025.
s: Jounce Media, April 2025 (via AdExchanger)

claims.t: The structural grammar of western democratic socialism — history moving toward justice, the present order corrupt at its roots, a redeemed commonwealth achievable through collective transformation — derives from western Christian eschatology
Winstanley grounded common ownership of land in God-as-Reason theology and identified private property with the Fall — the clearest English-language proto-socialist Christian communalism before Marx
British Labour's founding moral energy was primarily nonconformist Methodist Christianity, not Marxism — Keir Hardie stated he owed more to the Sermon on the Mount than to all other political sources

The SPD's August 4, 1914 vote for war credits was driven primarily by institutional self-interest (protecting 2.5M members, cultural apparatus, professional staff) rather than nationalist sentiment per se

The defeat of the Meidner Plan (1975–1984) demonstrated the structural ceiling of democratic socialism within capitalism: redistribution is achievable, socialization of ownership is blocked by capital's structural power

Syriza signed a Troika memorandum on July 13, 2015 — five days after a 61.3% referendum vote against austerity — demonstrating the structural limit of democratic socialism within the Eurozone's monetary architecture
Tillich's The Socialist Decision (1933) argues that socialism's 'unconditional demand' for justice inherits the form of biblical prophetism and loses its moral grounding when it forgets this root
Zohran Mamdani won the New York City mayoral election in November 2025 with 50.4% on an explicit democratic-socialist platform
The US top-1% wealth share reached 31.7% in Q3 2025 (Federal Reserve FRED data) — a record

SHA-256 is a one-way hash function by design but is practically reversible for common email addresses because email address spaces are small and pre-computed lookup tables mapping common addresses to their SHA-256 digests are commercially available; the absence of a per-record salt exacerbates this.
s: LiveRamp, 'The Trouble with Hashed Emails (HEMs),' LiveRamp Blog, 2023. https://liveramp.com/blog/the-trouble-with-hashed-emails-hems

claims.t: UID2 requires: (1) trim leading/trailing whitespace, (2) lowercase conversion, (3) for @gmail.com addresses, remove dots and strip plus-addressing. Identical email addresses processed without these steps produce completely different SHA-256 digests, breaking identity matching silently.
s: The Trade Desk / Unified ID 2.0, 'Normalization and Encoding,' UID2 Documentation, accessed 2026-06-19. https://unifiedid.com/docs/getting-started/gs-normalization-encoding

claims.t: LiveRamp's own blog materials assert that RampID-to-RampID matching delivers 44% higher match rates than HEM-to-HEM matching, but no methodology, sample, publisher list, or time period is disclosed in those materials, and no independent third-party source corroborates the figure. The mechanistic explanation — that HEM fails on "any" syntactic normalization divergence — overstates a real but partial cause: normalization failures are one documented failure mode, but RampID's graph also matches across multiple email addresses per person and alternative PII, advantages unrelated to normalization.
s: LiveRamp, 'The Trouble with Hashed Emails (HEMs),' 2023. https://liveramp.com/blog/the-trouble-with-hashed-emails-hems
