claims.t: Experian's Digital Graph, integrated into MiQ's Identity Spine, produced a 70% match rate for associating MiQ-provided IP addresses with universal IDs, a 51% increase in seed audience reach, a 64% increase in reach using universal IDs, and an average of 6.5 additional device matches per IP address (published May 2025).
s: Experian, 'Experian's Digital Graph Strengthened MiQ's Identity Spine,' May 2025. https://www.experian.com/blogs/marketing-forward/how-miq-strengthed-identity-spine-with-experian-digital-graph/.

claims.t: Epsilon CORE ID covers more than 200 million individuals according to company self-reporting, grounded in deterministic offline identifiers (name/address) and transaction records — no independently audited figure exists. Epsilon PeopleCloud (the broader platform of which CORE ID is one component) was reported as embedded in more than half of Publicis Groupe's top 30 advertiser accounts as of 2020–2021 disclosures; attributing this metric to CORE ID specifically overstates the sourcing.
s: Epsilon product communications (Tier 5); AdExchanger, 'Epsilon Is Making Its Identity Platform Interoperable With Unified ID 2.0,'…

claims.t: Adweek (2025) reported that WPP, IPG, Dentsu, Havas, at least four independent agencies, and one brand-side programmatic team purchased inventory through the Epsilon SSP and that competing agencies subsequently blocked Epsilon SSP over concerns that campaign data — bidding strategies, creative assets, and target audiences — was exposed to Publicis Groupe as a direct competitor.
s: Adweek, 'EXCLUSIVE: Media Buyers Block Publicis' Epsilon SSP Over Data Leakage Concerns,' 2025. https://www.adweek.com/media/publicis-epsilon-ssp-data-reseller-buyer-concerns/. Tier 4 — major trade publication.

claims.t: Google PPID requires publishers to hash or encrypt their identifier such that it is "meaningless to Google." For Google's own demand channels (reservations, Google Demand), Ad Manager re-partitions the identifier into per-publisher partitioned IDs, preventing cross-publisher profiling through Google's own infrastructure. However, for third-party programmatic demand (Authorized Buyers, Open Bidders), Ad Manager shares the raw PPID value directly with buyers exactly as received from the publisher — without partitioning or transformation.
s: Google, 'About Publisher Provided Identifiers,' Google Ad Manager Help, https://support.google.com/admanager/answer/2880055. Tier 1 — primary product documentation. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: PAIR encrypts both advertiser and publisher first-party data three times using three different keys (an advertiser key, a publisher key, and a key shared between advertiser and publisher). No single participating party — advertiser, publisher, or shared-key holder — holds all three keys, preventing any one of them from reverse-decrypting the raw IDs. The claim's assertion that "including Google" cannot decrypt is not supported by the cited source, which does not address Google's own platform-level access.
s: Google Ad Manager Help, 'About PAIR,' https://support.google.com/admanager/answer/15067908 (Tier 1); IAB Tech Lab, 'PAIR,' https://iabtechlab.com/pair/ (Tier 1). Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: IAB Tech Lab launched PAIR as an industry standard at v1.0 in January 2025 and released v1.1 in July 2025, adding clearer technical definitions, standardized Base64 encoding, and a new Open PAIR Prebid module. The protocol originated from Google's Ads team (developed October 2022) before donation to IAB Tech Lab.
s: IAB Tech Lab, 'PAIR (Publisher Advertiser Identity Reconciliation),' https://iabtechlab.com/pair/. Tier 1 — standards body primary documentation. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: LiveRamp's Interoperable IDs feature allows UID2 tokens to be embedded inside ATS envelopes, enabling publishers using ATS to pass a UID2 alongside their LiveRamp envelope in bid requests. Publishers must contact their LiveRamp representative to enable this feature — it is not on by default — and SHA-256 hashing of the email address is required. The cited source does not characterize this as "bilateral translation" (which implies a conversion layer mapping one ID to the other), nor does it describe the result as simultaneously signaling a RampID and UID2 as twin co-equal identifiers in a single request.
s: Unified ID 2.0, 'LiveRamp Integration Tips,' https://unifiedid.com/docs/guides/integration-liveramp-tips. Tier 1 — primary technical documentation. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Prebid.js User ID module supports simultaneous passage of multiple identity namespaces (UID2, ID5, LiveRamp, Yahoo ConnectID, and others) as an eIDs array in OpenRTB 2.6 format. The eIDs standard is a carrier — it allows multiple identity namespaces to coexist in a bid request — but not a resolver; each DSP independently decides which IDs it can read and transact against.
s: Prebid.org, 'Module — User ID for Header Bidding,' https://docs.prebid.org/dev-docs/modules/userId.html (Tier 1).

claims.t: Identity graph full interoperability faces structural headwinds on commercial, legal, and technical dimensions, but characterizing these as categorical "blocks" overstates the evidence. Commercially, providers face disincentives to full bidirectional interoperability because it would erode network-effect moats, but many selective free integrations exist (UID2 and EUID are open-source; RampID is free to access), making "commercially blocked" too strong — "commercially disincentivized toward selective rather than universal interoperability" is more accurate.
s: Multiple: LiveRamp FY2026 10-K [Tier 1]; UID2 documentation [Tier 1]; AdExchanger EUID/GDPR [Tier 5]; AdExchanger UID2 implementation failure [Tier 5]. Inference explicitly flagged.

claims.t: The directional content of the claim is plausible — MAID identifiers do decay meaningfully each month, iOS ATT does accelerate that decay, HEM addresses do erode over time, and weekly refresh is a reasonable industry preference for programmatic activation. However, the specific figures (3–7% monthly MAID decay, 8–15% annual HEM decay) are sourced exclusively from GSDSI, a privately held commercial data brokerage, not an industry standards body.
s: GSDSI, 'Device Graph Decay: MAID and HEM Freshness Math,' https://www.gsdsi.com/resources/device-graph-decay-how-fast-maid-hem-freshness-degrades. Tier 5 — industry standards body analysis. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: The IAB Tech Lab's OpenRTB 2.6 specification, released April 2022, promoted Extended Identifiers (user.eids) from a popular extension field into the core specification, standardizing how identity solutions like UID2 and RampID are passed in CTV and digital advertising bid requests.
s: IAB Tech Lab, OpenRTB 2.6 Final Specification, April 2022. https://iabtechlab.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/OpenRTB-2-6_FINAL.pdf [Tier 1]. InteractiveAdvertisingBureau, openrtb2.x/2.6.md, GitHub.

claims.t: OpenRTB 2.6's geo.type field (defined via AdCOM 1.0, List: Location Types) enumerates three source methods — 1 (GPS/Location Services), 2 (IP Address), 3 (User Provided, e.g., registration data) — allowing buyers to assess the reliability of metro, zip, and lat/lon values before making targeting decisions. There is no value 4 ("inferred") in the specification.
s: IAB Tech Lab, OpenRTB 2.6, Section 3.2.19 (Geo Object). https://iabtechlab.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/OpenRTB-2-6_FINAL.pdf [Tier 1]. CIMM/Go Addressable/Truthset, Landmark Report on IP-to-Household Accuracy, 2024.…

claims.t: The CIMM and Go Addressable study, benchmarking nearly one billion IP records from six major data providers against ISP-provided ground truth, found IP-to-postal linkages accurate on average 13% of the time, and data providers agree on IP-to-postal assignments only 6.4% of the time.
s: CIMM and Go Addressable, Landmark Report on IP-to-Household Accuracy, conducted by Truthset, 2024.…

claims.t: The CIMM/Truthset study found IPv6 addresses underrepresented by 72% in large commercial IP datasets, with only 15% of commercial files capturing them — creating a systematic blind spot in CTV geo and identity targeting as IPv6 adoption increases.
s: CIMM and Go Addressable, Landmark Report on IP-to-Household Accuracy, conducted by Truthset, 2024.…

claims.t: In OpenRTB bid requests, UID2 tokens are passed in user.eids with source: 'uidapi.com' for US and source: 'euid.eu' for EUID (European), with atype: 3 indicating a person-based cross-device identifier.
s: Equativ, Extended ID Integration. https://help.equativ.com/extended-id-integration-alternativeuniversal-ids [Tier 1 — primary SSP technical documentation]. Prebid.org, UID2 User ID Submodule.

claims.t: The IAB Tech Lab's September 2024 update to OpenRTB 2.6 added three new fields to the EID object — inserter, matcher, and mm — specifically to address ID bridging, where alternative identification methods were silently populating bid request fields without buyer awareness.
s: IAB Tech Lab, ID Generation Provenance and Clarification. https://iabtechlab.com/id-generation-provenance-and-clarification/ [Tier 1]. IAB Tech Lab, ID Provenance Added to OpenRTB.

claims.t: The device.ext.ifa_type field (not device.ifa_type) was introduced by IAB Tech Lab in its 2018 OTT IFA guidelines to disambiguate which identifier system populated device.ifa. The original specification defined platform-specific values including rida (Roku), tifa (Samsung), afai (Amazon Fire TV), vida (Vizio), lguid (LG), idfa (Apple), and aaid (Android/Google), and these became widely used in the industry.
s: IAB Tech Lab, IFA Type Specifications (via Scribd reference). Publica, The State of CTV Targeting. https://www.getpublica.com/blog/dont-chase-cookies-learn-how-ctv-targeting-really-works-the-state-of-ctv-targeting-1-2…

claims.t: Many major CTV programmers, including NBCU, Tubi, and Roku, cite VPPA as their reason for not simultaneously passing device identifiers and show-level content information in programmatic bid requests — a practice reflecting a conservative, contested legal interpretation, not a confirmed legal prohibition. Whether VPPA actually covers bid-stream device identifiers as PII remains judicially unresolved: the Second Circuit's 2025 "ordinary person" standard in Solomon v.
s: AdExchanger, The Blockbuster-Era Law Behind Connected TV's Transparency Problem. https://www.adexchanger.com/digital-tv/the-blockbuster-era-law-behind-connected-tvs-transparency-problem/ [Tier 5].

claims.t: Amazon has claimed its authenticated graph reaches approximately 90% of US households, but this figure is Amazon's own internal estimate with no independent third-party audit. It was not announced at the 2025 upfront (May 12): Amazon's official upfront recap does not mention it, and the load-bearing Roku partnership that makes 90% achievable was not announced until June 16, 2025. Third-party data (CIRP, eMarketer) puts Prime alone at roughly 80% of US households.
s: Cherry Picked, citing Amazon upfront 2025, 'Understanding Amazon's Data Advantages and the Path to $100B in Ad Revenue.'…

claims.t: Amazon and Roku announced in June 2025 a partnership using a custom identity resolution service that lets Amazon DSP exclusively recognize logged-in viewers deterministically across Roku OS devices, reaching approximately 80 million US CTV households (80%+ of US CTV homes per ComScore) with Q4 2025 availability.
s: Roku Newsroom, Amazon Ads and Roku Announce Partnership Creating the Largest Authenticated CTV Footprint, June 16, 2025.

claims.t: HP's UID2-based CTV campaign reached approximately 8% of an estimated 12.5 million targeted households at a frequency of 5.7 impressions per household, at a cost per unique household of $0.16 — 23% lower than HP's prior CTV campaign strategies without UID2.
s: AdExchanger, HP Taps UID2 for Better CTV Targeting. https://www.adexchanger.com/ctv-roundup/hp-taps-uid2-for-better-ctv-targeting/ [Tier 5; single-source from Trade Desk]. The Trade Desk, HP CTV UID2 Case Study.…

claims.t: Magnite, the largest independent SSP, derived approximately 42% of its revenue from CTV as of 2025, with integrations across more than 1,500 premium publishers.
s: Publisher Collective, 20+ Best SSPs for Publishers 2025. https://www.publisher-collective.com/blog/best-ssps-for-publishers [Tier 5; single-source for specific figure].

claims.t: LG Ads Solutions signed a multi-year deal with Magnite (announced June 21, 2022) to make ACR data from opted-in LG smart TVs available to the buy side through Magnite's CTV SSP infrastructure. No specific TV-count figure was disclosed in the LG Ads–Magnite announcement. The "more than 20 million opted-in LG smart TVs" figure belongs to a separate 4.5-year licensing deal between LG Ads Solutions and iSpot.tv, not Magnite. Additionally, the cited eMarketer URL ("Samsung Ads Expands Magnite Deal") covers Samsung's distinct partnership with Magnite and provides no corroboration for this LG claim.
s: StreamTV Insider, LG Ads, Magnite Sign Multi-Year Deal for ACR Data. https://www.streamtvinsider.com/advertising/lg-ads-magnite-sign-multi-year-deal-acr-data [Tier 5]. eMarketer, Samsung Ads Expands Magnite Deal.…

claims.t: Microsoft announced in May 2025 that Microsoft Invest (the DSP formerly known as Xandr Invest) would be shut down on February 28, 2026. The replacement is the Microsoft Advertising Platform, a consolidated self-serve buying tool that uses Copilot as its underlying AI technology — not a product called "Microsoft Invest." The parenthetical in the original claim inverts the naming: Microsoft Invest is the product being killed, not the replacement.
s: VideoWeek, The WIR: Microsoft Shuts Down Xandr DSP, May 2025. https://videoweek.com/2025/05/16/the-wir-microsoft-shuts-down-xandr-dsp-both-sides-claim-victory-in-tcf-ruling-and-itvs-ad-sales-drop-in-q1/ [Tier 5].

claims.t: The shift from panel-based statistical projection to identity-anchored census-level measurement is the defining structural change in TV audience measurement, illustrated by Nielsen's Big Data + Panel product covering 45M households and 75M devices alongside a 1.2M-person panel.
s: Nielsen press release, January 22, 2025: https://www.nielsen.com/news-center/2025/2025-the-media-rating-council-accredits-nielsens-innovative-big-data-panel-national-tv-measurement/; Axios wire report confirming same…

claims.t: True census-level CTV measurement requires a persistent identity token on each impression. This is achievable on authenticated supply (logged-in streaming) via HEM or UID2, but on non-authenticated supply (FAST channels, many CTV apps), only a device IFA or household IP is available — household-level but not person-level, and requiring probabilistic inference to link to a real identity.
s: Experian Marketing, 'Our Guide to TV Measurement in 2024,' https://www.experian.com/blogs/marketing-forward/tv-measurement-2024/; LiveRamp…

claims.t: A single viewer who sees the same CTV campaign on a smart TV, smartphone, and laptop generates three separate impressions in three separate identity namespaces. Without identity-level de-duplication, reach is inflated and frequency management is impossible.
s: Nielsen, 'Nielsen Launches Deduplicated YouTube CTV Campaign Measurement in the UK,' June 2024, https://www.nielsen.com/news-center/2024/nielsen-launches-deduplicated-youtube-ctv-campaign-measurement-in-the-uk/…

claims.t: HEM and UID2 are significant identity bridges in CTV, but characterizing them as the "two dominant" solutions overstates UID2's market position given active competition from LiveRamp's RampID and other authenticated ID solutions. The LG Ad Solutions figures (165M smart TVs globally, 40M in U.S.) and the named publisher adoptions (FOX, Disney, WBD, NBCUniversal) are factually supported by primary sources, but Disney and WBD adoptions date to 2022–2023, not 2024.
s: LG Ad Solutions/Business Wire, May 9, 2024, https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20240509935801/en/LG-Ad-Solutions-Will-Adopt-Unified-ID-2.0-Empowering-Advertisers-to-Utilize-Their-First-Party-Data-at-Scale…

claims.t: The specific figures of 71% HEM match rate (authenticated CTV) and 47% (open-web) cannot be found in the cited eMarketer source. Direct fetch of the cited eMarketer "FAQ on Identity Resolution" (Jan 7, 2026) confirms the article exists but contains neither figure — only a data-clean-room adoption statistic. The Strategus CTV attribution page likewise contains no 70–85% IP-match figure and no Nielsen 2024 citation. The Nielsen 70–85% IP-match claim cannot be traced to any retrievable Nielsen-published document; it appears to be a practitioner-circulated figure of unknown provenance.
s: eMarketer, 'FAQ on Identity Resolution,' 2026, https://www.emarketer.com/content/faq-on-identity-resolution-navigating-privacy-cookies-cross-channel-fragmentation-2026…

claims.t: Nielsen's Big Data + Panel methodology received MRC accreditation in January 2025 for national TV audience measurement — the first MRC accreditation of a hybrid panel/big-data product inclusive of persons-level estimates. The product fuses a 1.2M-person meter panel with data from 45M U.S. households and 75M devices from partners including Vizio/Inscape, Roku, DirecTV, Comcast, and Dish Network.
s: Nielsen, January 22, 2025, https://www.nielsen.com/news-center/2025/2025-the-media-rating-council-accredits-nielsens-innovative-big-data-panel-national-tv-measurement/; Nielsen, November 2024,…

claims.t: Nielsen ONE, the cross-media unified measurement product designed to deduplicate audiences across linear TV, streaming, and digital video in a single number, is not yet submitted to the MRC for accreditation as of early 2026.
s: Axios, January 2025, https://www.axios.com/2025/01/22/nielsen-big-data-panel-accredited; Marketing Dive, https://www.marketingdive.com/news/nielsen-big-data-panels-mrc-accreditation-measurement/738058/

claims.t: VideoAmp's VALID platform, built on commingled ACR and set-top box data from 40M U.S. TV households and 65M devices, fused with a Commingled Identity Graph (five providers: TransUnion, Blockgraph, Experian, Verisk Marketing Solutions, others), guaranteed $3 billion in currency transactions by close of 2024 (880%+ YoY growth) and achieved full JIC currency certification including Personified Demographics for 2024–2025. Sell-side currency partners include Paramount, A+E Networks, NBCUniversal, Warner Bros. Discovery, and TelevisaUnivision.
s: VideoAmp press release, December 2024, https://videoamp.com/press/videoamp-leads-the-industry-to-mass-adoption-of-advanced-currencies-closes-2024-with-3-billion-in-currency-transactions-and-complete-jic-certification/…

claims.t: VideoAmp holds complete JIC certification as of December 2024 (covering national currency, advanced audiences, and Personified Demos). VideoAmp has not received MRC accreditation for its measurement methodology as of mid-2026; however, it formally initiated the MRC audit process in May 2025, meaning it is actively in the audit pipeline rather than having no MRC engagement. The original claim's framing — relying solely on the December 2024 press release's silence on MRC — omits this materially important subsequent development.
s: VideoAmp press release, December 2024 (absence of MRC claim); MRC accreditation records (absence of VideoAmp entry).

claims.t: iSpot holds MRC accreditation for national TV ad occurrence reporting (verified to 98.6%+ accuracy across network, timestamp, ad type, duration, advertiser, creative) — not for audience measurement. iSpot received full JIC currency certification across all categories including Personified Demographics in August 2024.
s: iSpot.tv, 'iSpot Achieves First-Ever MRC Accreditation for National TV Ad Occurrence Reporting,' https://www.ispot.tv/hub/ispot-tv-earns-mrc-accreditation-for-national-tv-ad-occurrence-reporting/; iSpot.tv…

claims.t: iSpot acquired 605 in September 2023 (announced September 13), expanding its total U.S. TV device footprint to 82.7 million by adding 605's Charter Spectrum set-top box data covering 16.6 million homes. The acquisition also brought Inscape ACR data (also licensed by iSpot directly), and attribution partnerships with Catalina, PlaceIQ, and Polk Automotive Solutions.
s: iSpot.tv, September 2023, https://www.ispot.tv/hub/ispot-acquires-next-gen-measurement-attribution-company-605/; AdExchanger, https://www.adexchanger.com/tv/ispot-acquires-tv-measurement-competitor-605/

claims.t: Comscore received MRC accreditation on March 20, 2024 for Total Household Rating and Average Audience estimates in national and local TV across all 210 measured local markets — at that point the only measurement vendor accredited for local TV measurement. Age/gender "households with" demographic breaks were explicitly excluded and remained unaccredited at that announcement. Comscore subsequently received MRC accreditation for those "households with" household-level age/gender demographic metrics in April 2025 (national and local).
s: Comscore, March 20, 2024, https://www.comscore.com/Insights/Press-Releases/2024/3/MRC-Accreditation-for-National-and-Local-TV-Household-Level-Measurement; Comscore, July 10, 2025,…

claims.t: What is established: Nielsen holds MRC accreditation for national Big Data + Panel; Comscore holds MRC accreditation for national and local household measurement; iSpot holds MRC accreditation for ad occurrence only. Nielsen does NOT hold JIC currency certification — it publicly refused to participate in the JIC from April 2023, a stance that remained unchanged through the 2025–2026 upfront cycle.
s: AdExchanger JIC/MRC accord, https://www.adexchanger.com/measurement/the-jic-and-the-mrc-clarify-their-purpose-and-how-theyre-different/; JIC Currency Certification guide (December 2024)…

claims.t: The dominant CTV sales lift architecture chains CTV impressions (tagged with UID2 or HEM) to purchase records (from Circana/NCSolutions, Experian, TransUnion, or LiveRamp) inside a data clean room, computing incremental lift for exposed vs. control households without raw data exchange. Circana announced agreements to acquire NCSolutions and Nielsen's MMM business in August 2024, with an expected Q4 2024 close — but neither deal closed in Q4 2024. The NCSolutions acquisition closed June 2, 2025; the Nielsen MMM acquisition closed August 21, 2025.
s: Circana/NCSolutions case study, https://www.circana.com/case-studies/its-a-sales-lift-party; AdExchanger, August 2024, https://www.adexchanger.com/daily-news-roundup/tuesday-27082024/; Roku…

claims.t: CTV-to-foot-traffic attribution bridges CTV device identifiers (via household IP or device graph) to MAIDs (mobile advertising IDs), then matches those MAIDs to location visit data. Foursquare Attribution covers CTV, linear TV, digital, and OOH, drawing on 15B human-verified check-ins, 2B transactions, and 83B annual visits. Placer.ai covers 1.5B+ monthly visitors across 20M devices and 13M+ venues.
s: Foursquare, MediaPost, September 11, 2024, https://www.mediapost.com/publications/article/399199/; Placer.ai, 2024, https://www.placer.ai/anchor/articles/2024-retail-foot-traffic-recap

claims.t: Website visit attribution for CTV uses household IP matching, but the accuracy of this method is far lower than claimed. The CIMM/Go Addressable/Truthset study (November 2025) — benchmarked against ISP ground-truth records across nearly one billion IP records from six major data providers — found IP-to-postal linkages accurate on average only 13% of the time, and IP-to-email linkages accurate 16% of the time, with providers agreeing only 6.4% of the time on postal matches.
s: Strategus, 'TV Attribution Explained,' https://www.strategus.com/blog/tv-attribution; ATTN Agency, 'CTV Attribution & Incrementality,' https://www.attnagency.com/blog/ctv-attribution-incrementality

claims.t: Smart TV platforms with proprietary ACR (Roku, Vizio/Inscape, Samsung Ads) can link their glass-level viewing signal directly to purchase outcomes via clean-room joins with retail partners, without a third-party identity bridge. The Roku–Kroger Precision Marketing partnership is the named exemplar. Glass-level ACR is also immune to server-side discrepancies: Vizio cites an industry finding that up to 17% of ads served to streaming peripheral devices play while the TV is off — a failure glass-level ACR detects but bid-stream data does not.
s: Roku, https://advertising.roku.com/learn/resources/advanced-measurement-for-tv-streaming-ad-campaigns-on-roku; VIZIO Platform Plus…

claims.t: The TV-to-digital attribution problem is at its root an identity namespace fragmentation problem: CTV impressions are indexed by streaming service user IDs, UID2 tokens, or device IFAs; digital conversions are indexed by browser cookies, MAIDs, or logged-in user IDs. These environments do not natively overlap. The bridges (device graphs from LiveRamp, Neustar/TransUnion, Tapad; Experian Digital Graph with 4B identifiers including 275M CTV IDs) each introduce probabilistic matching error.
s: Experian, https://www.experian.com/blogs/marketing-forward/tv-measurement-2024/; LiveRamp, https://liveramp.com/blog/ctv-measurement-challenges

claims.t: The structural mechanism is accurate: CTV builds awareness and consideration days to weeks before purchase, and last-click attribution assigns 100% of conversion credit to the final channel (typically branded search), giving CTV zero measured contribution. However, the specific "30% of branded search conversions trace to a CTV exposure in the prior week" figure is not supported by the cited sources. The Strategus /blog/tv-attribution page contains no such statistic. The AdExchanger 2024 article does not address CTV-to-branded-search attribution at all.
s: Strategus, https://www.strategus.com/blog/tv-attribution; AdExchanger, 2024, https://www.adexchanger.com/marketers/the-ad-measurement-trends-that-reshaped-online-advertising-this-year/

claims.t: Incrementality testing — comparing outcomes between exposed and holdout groups or via geo-testing — is a methodologically defensible attribution approach for CTV because it measures causation rather than correlation and does not require cross-environment individual-level identity bridging. AdExchanger characterized 2024 as "the breakout year of incrementality" in ad measurement broadly, not specifically in CTV. The tvScientific/MetricWorks partnership is a real named CTV incrementality implementation but was announced in July 2022, not 2024, and cannot serve as evidence of 2024 CTV growth.
s: AdExchanger, 2024, https://www.adexchanger.com/marketers/the-ad-measurement-trends-that-reshaped-online-advertising-this-year/; Roku…

claims.t: The 30% CTV return premium figure should be attributed to Analytic Partners' ROI Genome (750+ brands, 45 countries), not to "Digital Applied," which is a content site that does not produce this proprietary benchmark and whose CTV guide does not cite this figure. The Analytic Partners finding also does not specify MMM as its methodology — it derives from a broader commercial analytics database. The Circana acquisition of Nielsen's MMM business was announced in August 2024 but did not close until August 2025, so describing it as a "Q4 2024 acquisition" is inaccurate.
s: AdExchanger, 2024, https://www.adexchanger.com/marketers/the-ad-measurement-trends-that-reshaped-online-advertising-this-year/; Circana…

claims.t: ACR data derived from the glass-level signal of what displays on a smart TV screen operates independently of the programmatic bid stream and is substantially more difficult to manipulate than bid-stream signals, because it captures pixel and audio fingerprints at the display layer rather than through ad-delivery infrastructure — though the absolute claim that it "cannot be spoofed" is unsupported.
s: VIZIO Platform Plus, https://platformplus.vizio.com/insights/why-glass-level-acr-data-is-the-best-solution-for-ctv-ad-viewability-brand-safety-and-fraud-detection; FreeWheel/Samba TV, September 2024…

claims.t: ACR detects all ads displaying on the screen, including competitor ads, enabling competitive intelligence on which competitor creatives were seen, at what frequency, and on which networks — without any relationship with the competitor or the network.
s: Tatari TV, https://www.tatari.tv/insights/automatic-content-recognition-acr-whys-and-hows; The Drum, 2024, https://www.thedrum.com/open-mic/how-acr-and-oems-are-revolutionising-the-connected-tv-landscape

claims.t: Glass-level ACR confirms that an ad actually appeared on a lit TV screen, versus bid-stream verification which only confirms the ad was served to an OS layer. Vizio's Inscape uses watermarking in its ACR database to confirm brand-safe, viewable delivery. A vendor-cited industry study finds up to 17% of ads served through streaming peripheral devices play while the TV is off — undetectable by bid-stream data but detectable by glass-level ACR.
s: VIZIO Platform Plus / Inscape, https://platformplus.vizio.com/insights/why-glass-level-acr-data-is-the-best-solution-for-ctv-ad-viewability-brand-safety-and-fraud-detection

claims.t: Roku, which self-reports approximately 40% U.S. smart TV unit share (Tier 5; not independently verified), uses its ACR data to identify which households saw linear TV campaigns and then activates CTV campaigns targeting incremental viewers not yet exposed — a reach and frequency optimization approach confirmed on Roku's advertising resources page.
s: Roku, https://advertising.roku.com/learn/resources/how-advertisers-can-leverage-rokus-acr-data; Roku…

claims.t: A data clean room is a secure computational environment where two or more parties can analyze their combined datasets without any party seeing the other's raw PII; only aggregate, de-identified results — never individual rows — are returned; minimum audience thresholds prevent reconstruction of individual records.
s: AWS Clean Rooms GA blog (March 2023); Google ADH developer docs; Snowflake differential privacy docs

claims.t: Federated SQL clean rooms (AWS Clean Rooms, Google Ads Data Hub, LiveRamp Safe Haven) keep each party's data in its own storage; only aggregate query results leave the environment; minimum thresholds and column-level access controls prevent re-identification.
s: AWS blog aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/aws-clean-rooms-now-generally-available/ (Tier 1); developers.google.com/ads-data-hub (Tier 1); docs.liveramp.com privacy-preserving-techniques (Tier 1)

claims.t: MPC allows multiple parties to jointly compute a function over their private inputs such that no party learns anything beyond the output — in most deployed protocols this is achieved via secret sharing or garbled circuits rather than literal computation on ciphertext (which is homomorphic encryption, a distinct and costlier method).
s: Communications of the ACM, 'Secure Multiparty Computation' (Vol. 63, No. 4, 2020) — Tier 2; Criteo Engineering blog on MPC PETs 2023 — Tier 5, self-reported cost benchmark

claims.t: Differential privacy adds calibrated mathematical noise to clean room aggregate outputs; AWS Clean Rooms added it in preview November 2023 and GA April 2024; Snowflake documents it natively; it allows more flexible queries but degrades signal quality for small segments.
s: aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2024/04/aws-clean-room-differential-privacy (Tier 1); docs.snowflake.com cleanrooms/differential-privacy (Tier 1)

claims.t: The market conflation of 'data clean rooms' with 'data collaboration platforms' is a real and documented distinction — Lotame's published content does draw this line, and the LiveRamp/Habu acquisition logic supports the activation-gap argument. However, the specific 23%-to-47% brand adoption figure between 2020 and 2024 is misattributed. It originates from a May 2024 Winterberry Group report ("The Current State and Future Outlook for Data Collaboration Platforms") sponsored by Adobe — not from Lotame analysis or the IAB State of Data 2023, which are cited as sources but do not contain these figures.
s: Lotame, 'Standalone Data Clean Rooms vs. Data Collaboration Platforms' (Tier 5); IAB State of Data 2023, iab.com (Tier 2/5)

claims.t: AWS Clean Rooms launched in preview January 2023, reached GA March 21, 2023; data is analyzed in place in S3 via AWS Glue catalog configured tables (not accurately described as a 'federated SQL architecture'); launch customers named in the GA blog included DISH Media, Fox Corporation, Comscore, and Amazon Marketing Cloud — Omnicom's Annalect does not appear in the cited GA blog post and should be removed or separately sourced; at launch, pricing used CRPU-hours with a 9 CRPU-hour monthly free tier for 12 months, though this free tier has since been discontinued and the current pricing page no longer offers it…
s: aws.amazon.com/blogs/aws/aws-clean-rooms-now-generally-available/ (Tier 1); aws.amazon.com/clean-rooms/pricing/ (Tier 1); aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2023/01/ (Tier 1)

claims.t: InfoSum's Bunker architecture enabled a five-party linear+CTV campaign for beer brand Cristal; wave-two deduplication of already-reached viewers increased combined reach from 23.4% to 58% of the 25-44 demographic (2.5x incremental reach) and produced a 2.8x purchase intention uplift; no PII moved between parties.
s: InfoSum, 'Multi-party collaboration delivers 2.5x incremental reach across linear and CTV for Ads & Data,' infosum.com/case-studies (Tier 5 — self-reported)

claims.t: LiveRamp acquired Habu in a deal valued at approximately $200 million (approximately $170M cash, remainder in stock), closing January 31, 2024; Habu provided native integrations into Google Ads Data Hub and Amazon Marketing Cloud that Safe Haven lacked; the deal was framed as adding an 'activation layer' to Habu's collaboration-only capability.

claims.t: Snowflake acquired clean room startup Samooha in December 2023 (described by VentureBeat as its ninth acquisition of that year, though some outlets counted it as the eighth); the technology runs as a Snowflake Native App. In August 2024, Netflix announced partnerships with three clean room providers — Snowflake, LiveRamp, and InfoSum — simultaneously; Snowflake's offering launched immediately while the other two were described as coming in subsequent months. Netflix did not characterize Snowflake as its "first available clean room partner" in its newsroom announcement.
s: Snowflake, 'Snowflake to Acquire Samooha,' snowflake.com/en/blog (Tier 1); Netflix Newsroom about.netflix.com August 2024 (Tier 1); Snowflake blog data-clean-rooms-multiparty-collaboration (Tier 1)

claims.t: Google Ads Data Hub is a BigQuery-based SQL clean room; it supports CTV identifiers (IFAs) and was expanded beyond mobile/desktop to include CTV; it is structurally limited to Google's ad inventory (YouTube, DV360) and cannot join signals from non-Google publishers; data enters with a latency of several hours to a day.
s: developers.google.com/ads-data-hub (Tier 1); improvado.io/blog/google-ads-data-hub (Tier 5 for latency corroboration)

claims.t: Decentriq (founded 2019, Switzerland) uses Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs) to encrypt data even while in use, so neither Decentriq nor its cloud provider can access data; it is positioned as the GDPR-native European clean room; a documented CTV use case involves Ad Alliance and OBI activating first-party data across premium video and CTV inventory.
s: decentriq.com/article/what-is-a-data-clean-room (Tier 1 vendor documentation); decentriq.com/case-study/ad-alliance-and-obi (Tier 5 self-reported)

claims.t: NBCU's Audience Insights Hub is a first-party data clean room launched in 2021 on One Platform, built on Snowflake (not AWS Clean Rooms), seeded with 150 million individual IDs and 50 million household IDs per NBCU CDO John Lee's disclosure to AdExchanger (self-reported, not independently audited). Separately, NBCU conducted a proof of concept labeled "Enhanced Audience Insights" — a Peacock + Amazon Ads integration via Amazon Publisher Cloud built on AWS Clean Rooms — that reportedly reached 3.6x more target consumers with 67% lower CPM…

claims.t: Disney's clean room (on Snowflake/Habu infrastructure) covers 110 million U.S. households through the Disney Select audience graph; as of 2024 it enrolled 136 brands and all major agency holding companies; typical match rates are 60–80%, with premium implementations above 92%; agency-reported cost savings from reduced wasted impressions range 6–25%.

Discovery launched Olli in April 2024, a first-party data platform and Snowflake-powered clean room drawing on 100 million U.S. households and 700 million devices; self-reported outcomes include 3.2x more targetable IDs versus third-party methods and 67% more on-target impressions across 25 test campaigns.

In September 2025 Amazon removed the onboarding/access barrier that had previously required Sponsored Ads advertisers to engage a partner or go through a registration process, giving them direct self-service access within the ads console.

However, this ecosystem is not a settled "de facto standard": as of 2025, only 48% of U.S.

claims.t: Minimum audience size thresholds — typically 50 to 1,000 users per result cell depending on platform — suppress small segments from clean room results, making clean rooms structurally unusable for niche audience targeting.
s: Snowflake docs.snowflake.com/en/user-guide/cleanrooms/differential-privacy (Tier 1); Google ADH description-of-methodology (Tier 1); LiveRamp docs privacy-preserving-techniques (Tier 1)

claims.t: Clean room latency varies materially by architecture. Google ADH carries a documented delay of approximately 6 hours (reduced from a prior 24–48 hour ceiling), making it unsuitable for same-day operational monitoring. ETL-pipeline-based clean rooms do face meaningful asynchrony that currently confines most deployments primarily to planning and retrospective measurement.

claims.t: Clean rooms require SQL proficiency and data science skills that most marketing teams lack; nearly half of DCR users assign six or more workers to the technology; 30% have 11 or more; the IAB identified smaller brands, agencies, and publishers as facing 'tremendous market disadvantage'; AMC became free in September 2025 but SQL proficiency remains a barrier for complex modeling.

claims.t: 41% of retail media clean room users cite integrating clean rooms into existing optimization and analysis practices as their top hurdle (Skai 2025). The "39% of organizations broadly" figure is not an independent eMarketer finding — it is the same Skai dataset being passed through by eMarketer's FAQ article, which explicitly attributes it to "the 2025 State of Retail Media report." There is therefore only one underlying source, not two independent surveys providing corroboration.
s: Skai 'The 2025 State of Data Clean Rooms in Retail Media' skai.io (Tier 5); eMarketer 'FAQ on Data Clean Rooms' emarketer.com (Tier 5)

claims.t: The Video Privacy Protection Act (18 U.S.C. § 2710) was enacted November 5, 1988 after journalist Michael Dolan published Supreme Court nominee Robert Bork's video rental history from Potomac Video in the Washington City Paper; Congress passed the statute within months.
s: 18 U.S.C. § 2710 (LII/Cornell); S.2361, 100th Congress (Congress.gov); CaseGuard article on VPPA legislative history

claims.t: The VPPA's disclosure prohibition reaches the programmatic CTV stack: including a user-level identifier and a video title or URL in a bid request to a DSP or DMP constitutes prohibited disclosure of personally identifiable information under § 2710(b)(1), absent proper consent. NBCUniversal and Tubi have publicly stated they withhold show-level metadata from bidstream identity data as a direct result.
s: AdExchanger, 'The Blockbuster-Era Law Behind Connected TV's Transparency Problem'; 18 U.S.C. § 2710(b)(1)

claims.t: VPPA § 2710(b)(2)(B) requires informed written consent 'in a form distinct and separate from any form setting forth other legal or financial obligations of the consumer.' A combined terms-of-service acceptance does not qualify. Consent is also capped at 2 years and must include a clear withdrawal mechanism.
s: 18 U.S.C. § 2710(b)(2)(B); Pub. L. 112-258 (Jan. 10, 2013); National Law Review VPPA analysis

claims.t: VPPA class action filings rose from 137 in 2023 to over 250 in 2024, targeting streaming platforms including Peacock, Tubi, Viki, Roku, and FuboTV. FuboTV's $3.4 million settlement received final approval October 8, 2025. Suits center on Meta Pixel transmitting video-viewing URLs and Facebook user IDs simultaneously.
s: Select Justice VPPA Lawsuit April 2025; Burdette v. FuboTV settlement site; Top Class Actions (Peacock, FuboTV)

claims.t: Peacock was sued for embedding Meta Pixel and disclosing registered users' viewing histories to Facebook; Tubi was sued in 2024 for using Meta Pixel to track video interactions without VPPA-compliant consent; FuboTV settled for $3.4 million in a case raising VPPA, CIPA, and Cal. Civil Code § 1799.3 claims.
s: Top Class Actions (Peacock); classaction.org / claimdepot.com (FuboTV); Select Justice (2025 VPPA overview)

claims.t: The Supreme Court DENIED certiorari in National Basketball Association v. Salazar (No. 24-994) on December 8, 2025. The case the Supreme Court actually granted cert in to resolve the VPPA "consumer" circuit split is Salazar v. Paramount Global, No. 25-459 (cert granted January 26, 2026), which came up through the Sixth Circuit (the narrow ruling), not the Second Circuit. The Second Circuit's holding in Salazar v. NBA, 118 F.4th 533 (2d Cir. 2024) — that newsletter subscribers qualify as VPPA consumers without a video-specific subscription — is accurately described, as is the circuit split itself.
s: SCOTUS docket 24-994 (cert. petition); Salazar v. NBA, 118 F.4th 533 (2d Cir. 2024); WilmerHale Jan. 2026

claims.t: CPRA (Cal. Civil Code § 1798.100 et seq.) grants consumers the right to opt out of 'sharing' personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising. Hashed email (derived from an email address that is personal information), CTV device IDs (explicitly 'unique identifiers' under § 1798.140(v)(1)(A)), and precise geolocation are all subject to this right. Uploading a first-party email list to a DMP and matching it to a CTV audience constitutes 'sharing' under the statute.
s: Cal. Civil Code § 1798.140(ae), (v)(1)(A); Jackson Lewis CCPA/CPRA FAQ (Jan. 2026)

claims.t: In February 2026 (announced February 11), California Attorney General Rob Bonta announced a $2.75 million settlement with Disney — the largest CCPA enforcement settlement at that time — arising from Disney's failure to honor consumers' opt-out-of-sale-and-sharing requests across its streaming platforms (Disney+, ESPN+, Hulu) and connected TV apps in a comprehensive, account-wide manner, as required by the CCPA. The violation was an opt-out implementation failure, not a failure of disclosure or consent.
s: ComplianceHub.Wiki, 'California's CPPA Is Fining Real Companies Now,' 2026 [secondary — CA AG press release should be verified]

claims.t: Virginia (VDPA), Colorado (CPA), Connecticut (CTDPA), Texas (TDPSA), and Oregon (OCPA) all require businesses broadly to honor consumer opt-outs from targeted advertising, defined as advertising selected based on personal data from consumer activity across nonaffiliated (or unaffiliated) websites and online applications.
s: Matomo blog (July 2024); TrustArc 2025 update; Feroot state law comparison; Ketch CTDPA guide

claims.t: The Texas Data Privacy and Security Act (TDPSA, effective July 1, 2024) does not set a revenue or data volume threshold — it applies to any commercial entity that conducts business in Texas or produces products/services consumed by Texas residents and processes personal data, unless the business qualifies as a small business under the SBA definition (which is industry-variable, not a fixed cutoff). Critically, even SBA-qualifying small businesses cannot sell sensitive personal data without prior consumer consent. The TDPSA's applicability structure is among the broadest of any major U.S.
s: Bass Berry & Sims, 'Texas Data Privacy and Security Act Goes Into Effect'; DWT TDPSA overview 2023

claims.t: In its December 3, 2024 action against Mobilewalla (finalized January 2025), the FTC issued its first-ever prohibition on collecting consumer data from real-time bidding (RTB) exchanges for any purpose other than participating in those auctions. Mobilewalla had collected 500+ million device IDs with location data from failed RTB bids — prohibited by exchange terms — and sold the resulting profiles commercially.
s: FTC press release Dec. 3, 2024; Federal Register 2024-28745; FTC finalized order Jan. 2025

claims.t: EUID (European Unified ID) was created by The Trade Desk and LiveRamp (announced February 28, 2022) as a Europe/UK-specific variant of UID2 to address GDPR and UK data-protection requirements. EUID's participant documentation explicitly requires that consent be freely given (prohibiting cookie walls), specific, informed, unambiguous, demonstrated by clear affirmative action, and accompanied by withdrawal rights — all accurately described in the claim.
s: euid.eu/docs/intro; AdExchanger (GDPR roadblocks for UID2)

claims.t: Singular's Quarterly Trends Report (observational panel from Singular's measurement network) reported global ATT opt-in rates declining from 26 percent in July 2021 to 18.9 percent in Q4 2023, 15.9 percent in Q1 2024, and 13.85 percent in Q2 2024. Category variation is substantial — news and medical apps below 5 percent; weather apps approximately 38 percent. Approximately 86 percent of iOS users globally do not grant IDFA access.
s: Singular, 'ATT Opt-In Rates 2024: Down, Down, Down,' https://www.singular.net/blog/att-opt-in-rates-2024/ [Tier 5 — measurement vendor panel]

claims.t: Google officially retired the Privacy Sandbox initiative in October 2025 for both Chrome and Android, shutting down Attribution Reporting, Topics, Protected Audience, and related APIs due to 'low levels of adoption,' regulatory pressure, and weak performance results. GAID deprecation, which was planned as part of this initiative, did not proceed. As of mid-2026, GAID remains operational on Android with no announced sunset date.
s: Usercentrics, 'Google Privacy Sandbox officially shuts down' (Oct. 2025); Engadget (Oct. 2025); Google Developers documentation

claims.t: CGNAT, dynamic IP reassignment, Apple iCloud Private Relay, and VPNs attack IP-based identity in two distinct ways: audience matching (linking an IP to a specific household across sessions) requires IP uniqueness and stability — both destroyed by CGNAT and Private Relay; DMA-level geolocation requires only geographic block resolution, which survives CGNAT (users stay within the same ISP region) but degrades under VPNs and Private Relay. The two use cases degrade at different rates and must be managed separately.
s: SIDN, 'CGNAT frustrates all IP address-based technologies'; eMarketer '3 Non-Cookie Threats to Ad Targeting'; Apple Private Relay documentation

claims.t: Cookies are not a native CTV mechanism, but CTV-driven web conversion attribution (measuring whether a CTV ad drove a website purchase) requires matching a CTV device identifier to a web session, historically identified by cookie. Cookie degradation or consumer deletion breaks this cross-environment attribution link. Google's reversal on mandatory Chrome cookie deprecation (July 2024) and Privacy Sandbox shutdown (October 2025) means cookies remain intact for now, but structural alternatives must be built.
s: VideoWeek, 'Cookie Deprecation Could Have Implications for CTV Measurement,' April 16, 2024; Advertising Week Q1 2024

claims.t: As of 2024, only 5 percent of Consent Management Platforms (CMPs) support web, mobile, and CTV environments simultaneously. This means the majority of CTV publishers lack a certified multi-platform consent solution, creating a gap between a consumer's stated opt-out preference and its operationalized enforcement in CTV bid streams.
s: Smaato, 'What CTV Publishers Need to Know to Comply with IAB's Consent Framework v2.2' [Tier 5 — single source; verify against IAB Europe TCF compliance report]

claims.t: The CTV identity vendor market divides into three categories with distinct economics: identity infrastructure providers (LiveRamp, UID2/TTD, ID5) that mint and resolve IDs and earn from onboarding, resolution, clean room, and measurement fees; data/graph providers (Experian, Neustar/TransUnion, Epsilon) that supply consumer data enrichment; and platform-native first-party identity holders (Amazon, Google, Roku, Samsung) whose signals are deterministic and accessible only on the platform's terms.
s: LiveRamp Holdings FY2026 10-K, SEC EDGAR [Tier 1]; TransUnion newsroom, TruAudience press releases [Tier 1 — what entities claim]; Amazon/Roku partnership press release, June 16, 2025 [Tier 1 — what entities claim]

claims.t: LiveRamp generated $812.9 million in revenue in fiscal year 2026 (ended March 31, 2026) — reported as $813 million in summary disclosures — at a 71 percent GAAP gross margin ($575 million GAAP gross profit) and 73 percent non-GAAP gross margin. The Publicis Groupe all-cash acquisition at $38.50 per share, representing a 29.8 percent premium to the May 15, 2026 close, $2.546 billion equity value, and $2.167 billion enterprise value, is accurately stated.

claims.t: UID2 is a free, open-source framework that enables publishers and DSPs to adopt email-based pseudonymous targeting without LiveRamp, creating genuine competitive pressure on one layer of LiveRamp's onboarding business — but it is not a clean fee-bypass of LiveRamp's HEM onboarding, as UID2 and LiveRamp are interoperable and address partly distinct use cases (authenticated first-party email tokens vs. offline CRM-to-online-ID matching across device graphs).
