claims.t: The Publicis acquisition of LiveRamp (combined with prior Epsilon and Lotame ownership) creates the most vertically integrated agency-owned identity stack in the industry. Multiple named industry observers — ID5 CEO Mathieu Roche, CleanTap's Will Rand, Ray Media Advisory's Doug Ray — publicly stated LiveRamp's neutrality cannot survive the acquisition. Omnicom CEO John Wren confirmed that Acxiom's Real ID was already being built as an alternative, and Omnicom was planning to exit LiveRamp at contract expiry (Q1 2028) — a timeline likely accelerated by the Publicis announcement.
s: The Current, 'Publicis Says LiveRamp Will Stay Neutral. The Industry Isn't Buying It,' thecurrent.com, May 2026 [Tier 4]; Digiday, 'Identity Is the Qualifier for AI,' May 2026 [Tier 4]; Digiday, 'Ad Tech Briefing…

claims.t: IP-to-email matching accuracy in CTV averages 16 percent, per a Coalition for Innovative Media Measurement (CIMM) study cited by AdExchanger. FAST (Free Ad-Supported Streaming TV) channels frequently source email signals from third-party data brokers rather than direct first-party user logins, undermining the signal quality that justifies email-based identity premium pricing.
s: AdExchanger, 'Why Critics Say Email-Based IDs Don't Work For CTV,' adexchanger.com [Tier 4 — trade press; CIMM study cited but not directly accessed by this workstream]

claims.t: OpenRTB is the bid-request/response protocol that auctions individual ad impressions in real time; the RTB Project (formerly OpenRTB Consortium) was assembled in November 2010, with OpenRTB 2.0 unifying display/video/mobile in 2011, 2.5 in 2017, and 2.6 (adding CTV/ad-pod features) in April 2022.
s: IAB Tech Lab, OpenRTB standard page, https://iabtechlab.com/standards/openrtb/; OpenRTB API Spec v2.5 PDF (iab.com), accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: AdCP is an open standard letting AI agents discover, plan, buy, sell, and measure media across channels, built to run over Anthropic's MCP and the A2A protocol.
s: adcontextprotocol.org homepage; github.com/adcontextprotocol/adcp README; Digiday 'WTF is AdCP', Oct 15 2025. Accessed Jun 19 2026.

claims.t: AdCOM (Advertising Common Object Model) is a reusable, extensible vocabulary of objects (ad, placement, user, device, site, publisher) that OpenRTB references in bid requests, reducing integration errors and bid-request size; it was introduced alongside the OpenRTB 3.0 effort (public comment Sept 2017, companion specs Nov 2018).
s: IAB Tech Lab, AdCOM standard page, https://iabtechlab.com/standards/adcom-advertising-common-object-model/; The Drum (2018-11-15), accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: AdCP's central function is standardizing the discovery-and-negotiation exchange that precedes a transaction, which per the Media Buy docs 'occurs outside real-time bidding systems' rather than through DSPs or exchanges.
s: docs.adcontextprotocol.org Media Buy protocol; MediaPost (Sullivan) Oct 16 2025. Accessed Jun 19 2026.

claims.t: VAST (Video Ad Serving Template) is the XML template telling a video player how to fetch, render, and track an ad; first introduced in 2008, VAST 4.0 released Jan 21 2016, 4.2 June 2019, 4.3 Dec 2022, with a CTV Addendum in 2024, and underpins CTV server-side ad insertion (SSAI).
s: IAB Tech Lab, VAST standard page + VAST 4.0 PDF (2016-01-21), https://iabtechlab.com/standards/vast/; Wurl VAST glossary, accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: The pre-agentic stack standardized the message format but left DSP-SSP-data integrations hand-built, producing an 'ad tech tax' in which roughly one-quarter of programmatic ad spend was effectively wasted in the supply chain (ANA/TAG TrustNet, 2024).
s: BidSwitch, 'Bidstream bloat'; HUMAN Security supply-path blog; ANA/TAG TrustNet (2024, as reported in trade press), accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: RTB operates in milliseconds with DSPs processing tens of millions of bid requests per second; IAB Tech Lab's ARTF targets cutting bid round-trips from roughly 600-800ms to about 100ms, an up-to-80% reduction, by co-locating agents and real-time systems in the same data center.
s: IAB Tech Lab ARTF press release (2025-11-13); MediaPost (2025-11-14), accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Premium CTV inventory is transacted heavily via curated private deals: PMPs account for roughly 47% of CTV spend versus roughly 15% via the open exchange, programmatic guaranteed made up about a quarter of CTV buys in 2024, and over 90% of US CTV ad spend in 2025 ran through programmatic pipes.
s: eMarketer, 'CTV trends for 2026'; CTV programmatic deals trade coverage (BidsCube/AI Digital), accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Targeting signal decayed in the early 2020s: iOS ATT (iOS 14.5, 2021) drove IDFA opt-in to a ~25% plateau; Google cancelled forced third-party-cookie deprecation in July 2024 and reaffirmed cookies-on-by-default in April 2025; the UK CMA's June 2025 report found per-impression publisher revenue roughly 30% lower under Privacy Sandbox tools.
s: Adtelligent/Campaign Asia/Adweek cookie+IDFA coverage; UK CMA June 2025 report (as cited), accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: US CTV ad spending reached roughly $28.75B in 2024 (~18.8% growth) per eMarketer's March 2024 forecast, with 2026 forecast at ~$37.95B (~14.5% growth, Dec 2025); by 2024 CTV was ~1 in 10 US digital ad dollars, clustered among YouTube, Hulu, Amazon, Roku, Netflix, Disney+ and Max, with no cross-platform measurement standardization.
s: eMarketer, 'Guide to connected TV' (Mar 2024 forecast) and 'CTV trends for 2026' (Dec 2025 forecast), accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Anthropic announced and open-sourced the Model Context Protocol (MCP) on November 25, 2024 as a standard for connecting AI assistants to external data/tools via an MCP client/server model, solving the model-to-tool M×N integration problem; it shipped with Python/TypeScript SDKs and pre-built servers for Google Drive, Slack, GitHub, Git, Postgres, and Puppeteer.
s: Anthropic, 'Introducing the Model Context Protocol' (2024-11-25), https://www.anthropic.com/news/model-context-protocol, accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: On December 9, 2025 Anthropic donated MCP to the newly formed Agentic AI Foundation (a directed fund under the Linux Foundation), co-founded with Block and OpenAI and backed by Google, Microsoft, AWS, Cloudflare and Bloomberg; reported scale was around 97 million monthly SDK downloads and 10,000+ active servers.
s: MCP Blog (2025-12-09); Linux Foundation AAIF press release, accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Google announced the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol in April 2025 — an open standard for agents from different vendors to discover (via Agent Cards), authenticate, and delegate over HTTP/JSON-RPC — and contributed it to the Linux Foundation in June 2025, with support exceeding 150 organizations within a year.
s: Linux Foundation A2A press release; Google Cloud Blog A2A posts, accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Google announced the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) on September 16, 2025, built with 60+ partners, using cryptographically signed 'Mandates' (Intent and Cart) backed by verifiable credentials to address Authorization, Authenticity, and Accountability in agent payments; AP2 extends A2A and MCP and is payment-method-agnostic.
s: Google Cloud Blog, 'Announcing Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)' (2025-09-16); DigitalCommerce360 (2025-09-19), accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: OpenAI and Stripe launched the Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP) and ChatGPT Instant Checkout on September 29, 2025, enabling agent-ready checkout (US Etsy sellers at launch, Shopify to follow), with OpenAI reportedly charging merchants a 4% transaction fee on completed Instant Checkout purchases.
s: Stripe Newsroom 'Instant Checkout' + Stripe Blog (2025-09-29); DigitalCommerce360, accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: The Ad Context Protocol (AdCP) launched October 15, 2025 — founding members Yahoo, PubMatic, Scope3, Optable, Swivel and Triton Digital, with CTV-weighted launch supporters (Magnite, LG Ad Solutions, Samba TV, MiQ, Kargo, The Weather Company) — as an open, MCP/A2A-based standard for AI agents to discover, plan, buy, sell and measure media, governed by the independent AgenticAdvertising.org.
s: VideoWeek (2025-10-15); adcontextprotocol.org and docs.adcontextprotocol.org, accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: As read on the official AdCP docs, AdCP's specifications include the Media Buy Protocol, Creative Protocol, Signals Protocol, Governance Protocol, Brand Protocol (brand.json) and Accounts Protocol, all transported over MCP and A2A, with an HTTP discovery layer (adagents.json, brand.json) and a registry — a set that differs from the launch-era naming (Signals Activation / Media Buy / Creative / Curation-coming-Q2).
s: docs.adcontextprotocol.org (live), accessed 2026-06-19; cf. AdCP launch coverage.

claims.t: AdCP's lead proponent is Brian O'Kelley, co-founder/CEO of Scope3 and previously co-founder/CEO of AppNexus (sold to AT&T for $1.6B in 2018), widely credited as an inventor of the ad exchange and a Prebid co-creator, who frames AdCP as 'the universal ads API' for the open web.
s: Scope3 company page; MediaPost (2025), accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: IAB Tech Lab released the Agentic RTB Framework (ARTF) v1.0 for public comment on November 13, 2025 (comment window through January 15, 2026), introducing a containerized architecture that runs agents and real-time systems in the same virtual environment, targeting up-to-80% latency reduction and applying agentic standards through OpenRTB with MCP/A2A support.
s: IAB Tech Lab ARTF press release (2025-11-13); MediaPost (2025-11-14), accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: IAB Tech Lab published an Agentic Roadmap on January 6, 2026 (building on OpenRTB, AdCOM, OpenDirect, VAST and the Deal API paired with MCP, A2A and gRPC) and on February 26, 2026 formally named its umbrella initiative AAMP (Agentic Advertising Management Protocols), with three pillars: Agentic Foundations (ARTF + guardrails), Agentic Protocols, and Trust & Transparency (an Agent Registry).
s: IAB Tech Lab Agentic Roadmap release (2026-01-06); ppc.land AAMP article (2026-02-26), accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: By late 2025 the agentic-advertising standards landscape split into two camps: AdCP, building new AI-native standards on MCP under an independent coalition, versus IAB Tech Lab's ARTF/AAMP, extending existing deterministic standards; the compatibility-versus-competition relationship between them was, as of the research window, explicitly unresolved.
s: Digiday, 'AdCP vs. IAB Tech Lab'; The Current agentic-framework coverage, accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: On October 16, 2025, a live agent-to-agent media buy was demonstrated over AdCP with Scope3 on the buy side, Swivel as seller-side ad server, and LG Ads supplying real inventory; agents ran the full workflow from brief through targeting, proposal, creative upload and a real-money transaction.
s: MediaPost, 'The First Agentic Media Buy, More To Come' (2025-10-16), accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Major ad platforms shipped their own MCP servers to expose ad APIs to agents in natural language: Amazon Ads MCP Server (open beta per Amazon's announcement, with a trade-cited earlier closed beta around Nov 13 2025), Google's Google Ads/Analytics MCP servers, and Meta Ads AI Connectors (an MCP server + CLI, reported ~April 29 2026) — present-tense statuses that may go stale via rename, sunset, or GA.
s: Amazon Ads, 'Introducing the Amazon Ads MCP Server' (open beta); ppc.land Meta connectors coverage; Synter/Scalemate platform-MCP roundups, accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: OpenRTB 3.0 (public comment 2017, specs 2018) saw low adoption because it broke backward compatibility and required rewriting underlying code; the industry instead back-ported its wanted elements into the 2.x line, leaving a brownfield stack that the agentic standards now route around.
s: BidSwitch, 'OpenRTB 3.0: Why Is (Almost) Nobody Using It?'; The Drum (2017/2018), accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard for connecting an AI application to external systems (data, tools, workflows) through one common interface; Anthropic open-sourced it on November 25, 2024 with spec version 2024-11-05 and Python/TypeScript SDKs.
s: modelcontextprotocol.io intro + architecture (accessed 2026-06-19); VentureBeat 'Anthropic releases MCP' Nov 2024.

claims.t: AdCP launched with three sub-protocols — Audience Activation, Curation, and Media Buy — enabling agents to discover/activate audiences, offer curated products, and execute/manage campaigns across platforms.
s: MediaPost Oct 16 2025; Samba TV press release Oct 15 2025; Adweek/Radio World (via search) Oct 2025.

claims.t: MCP follows a client-server architecture with three participants: an MCP Host (the AI application), MCP Clients (one per server), and MCP Servers (local via stdio or remote via Streamable HTTP); it splits into a JSON-RPC 2.0 data layer and a transport layer.
s: modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/learn/architecture (Tier 1, accessed 2026-06-19).

claims.t: The Media Buy protocol exposes tasks including get_products (brief/refine), create_media_buy, update_media_buy, and get_media_buy_delivery, supporting iterative pre-buy refinement before transacting.
s: docs.adcontextprotocol.org Media Buy protocol. Accessed Jun 19 2026.

claims.t: MCP defines three server primitives — Tools (executable actions), Resources (read-only context data), Prompts (reusable templates) — and three client primitives — Sampling (use host LLM), Elicitation (ask the user), Logging — discoverable via */list methods with notifications for changes.
s: modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/learn/architecture (Tier 1, accessed 2026-06-19).

claims.t: As of v3.1.0 (Jun 18 2026) AdCP spans Media Buy, Creative, Signals, Accounts, Governance, Brand, Sponsored Intelligence (Curation 'coming soon'), plus Trusted Match, Discovery/Registry, Catalogs, Events/Performance.
s: github.com/adcontextprotocol/adcp README; docs.adcontextprotocol.org. Accessed Jun 19 2026.

claims.t: Anthropic donated MCP to the Agentic AI Foundation — a directed fund under the Linux Foundation, co-founded by Anthropic, Block, and OpenAI with support from Google, Microsoft, AWS, Cloudflare, and Bloomberg — on December 9, 2025; MCP's governance model is stated to remain unchanged.
s: Anthropic, 'Donating the Model Context Protocol and establishing the Agentic AI Foundation,' Dec 9 2025 (Tier 1 primary/announcement).

claims.t: A2A (Agent2Agent), introduced by Google in April 2025 and transferred to the Linux Foundation in June 2025, is an open standard for agent-to-agent communication and is explicitly complementary to MCP — 'MCP is for agent-to-tool communication while A2A is for agent-to-agent communication.
s: a2a-protocol.org/latest (Tier 1); Linux Foundation press release; The New Stack (accessed 2026-06-19).

claims.t: The Ad Context Protocol (AdCP) launched October 15, 2025 from a supply-side coalition (founding members Optable, PubMatic, Scope3, Swivel, Triton Digital, Yahoo), is built on MCP and A2A, and shipped initial protocols for Audience Activation, Curation, and Media Buy.
s: docs.adcontextprotocol.org/docs/intro (Tier 1); Digiday WTF AdCP Oct 15 2025; VideoWeek Oct 15 2025; Samba TV press (accessed 2026-06-19).

claims.t: AdCP operates as a protocol layer above real-time bidding, not within it: it is asynchronous (responses can take seconds to days, accommodating human-in-the-loop approval) and replaces the impression auction with direct buyer-agent-to-seller-agent negotiation over custom packages, curation, and guaranteed deals.
s: docs.adcontextprotocol.org/docs/intro (Tier 1); eMarketer (Tier 5); Digiday; AdExchanger (accessed 2026-06-19).

claims.t: AdCP runs the SAME tasks and schemas over two transports — MCP (for AI assistants calling tools) and A2A (for agent-to-agent collaboration): 'Same tasks, same schemas, different transport.
s: docs.adcontextprotocol.org/docs/intro (Tier 1, accessed 2026-06-19).

claims.t: AdCP defines specialized agents (media-buying, creative, signals, governance, orchestrator) and a seller/sales agent that interprets buyer briefs against its own inventory; sellers and brands expose capabilities via machine-readable discovery files adagents.json (publishers) and brand.json (advertisers/operators).
s: docs.adcontextprotocol.org/docs/intro (Tier 1); Digiday (Tier 5, accessed 2026-06-19).

claims.t: AdCP's documented task vocabulary spans get_products (brief/refine discovery), create_media_buy (execution), get_media_buy_delivery (tracking), list_creative_formats/build_creative/sync_creatives (creative), get_signals/sync_audiences/activate_signal (signals), check_governance/get_plan_audit_logs (governance), get_brand_identity (brand), and the Trusted Match Protocol separating Context Match from Identity Match.
s: docs.adcontextprotocol.org/docs/media-buy + /docs/intro (Tier 1, accessed 2026-06-19).

claims.t: ARTF (Agentic RTB Framework), released for public comment by IAB Tech Lab around November 12-13, 2025, specifies a containerized execution model for real-time bidding: host platforms run third-party agent services as colocated containers (same data center/server/Kubernetes cluster) to enrich and modify the bidstream inside the auction.
s: artf.ai + artf.ai/technical-specs (Tier 1); PR Newswire/IAB Tech Lab press; AdExchanger Nov 13 2025; The Current Nov 13 2025 (accessed 2026-06-19).

claims.t: ARTF standardizes host-agent communication using gRPC with Protocol Buffers; agents return bidstream changes as OpenRTB Patch objects (minimal diffs, each tagged with an intent), and ARTF is designed to coexist with — not replace — OpenRTB, which remains the bid-object spec.
s: artf.ai/technical-specs (Tier 1, accessed 2026-06-19).

claims.t: ARTF claims it can reduce bid request/response times from a typical range of 400-800ms to roughly 100ms — about 80% — by eliminating most external network hops, with the spec itself qualifying 'up to approximately 80%, depending on implementation.
s: artf.ai/technical-specs + artf.ai + IAB Tech Lab/PR Newswire press (Tier 1 spec, but single-camp; accessed 2026-06-19).

claims.t: AdCP and ARTF solve different layers: AdCP is a negotiation/conversation layer (agents talking to seller agents OUTSIDE the bidstream, async, on the AI substrate MCP+A2A), while ARTF is an infrastructure/transport layer (colocated containers making the EXISTING RTB auction agent-and-latency-friendly, sync ~100ms, extending OpenRTB). The fault line is the auction boundary.
s: docs.adcontextprotocol.org/docs/intro + artf.ai/technical-specs (Tier 1); The Current Nov 13 2025; eMarketer (accessed 2026-06-19).

claims.t: Google's Agent Payments Protocol (AP2), announced September 16, 2025 with 60+ partners, secures agent-led payments via three cryptographically signed Mandates (Intent, Cart, Payment) carried as W3C Verifiable Credentials, and 'can be used as an extension of the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol and Model Context Protocol (MCP).
s: Google Cloud, 'Announcing Agent Payments Protocol (AP2),' Sept 16 2025 (Tier 1); ap2-protocol.org (accessed 2026-06-19).

claims.t: The Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP) is maintained by OpenAI and Stripe (initial spec September 29, 2025, beta), defining agentic checkout, cart/feed, delegate payment (Stripe's Shared Payment Token), and delegate authentication (OAuth 2.0); it went live in ChatGPT's Instant Checkout in late September 2025 and added an MCP component in its April 17 2026 release.
s: github.com/agentic-commerce-protocol (Tier 1); Stripe newsroom 'Instant Checkout in ChatGPT' (Tier 1, accessed 2026-06-19).

claims.t: On October 16, 2025 the first agent-to-agent media buy executed with real money against real LG Ad Solutions inventory under human oversight, and Swivel (seller agents) with Olyzon (buyer agents) subsequently launched agent-to-agent CTV activation over AdCP.
s: VideoWeek Oct 15 2025; AdExchanger 'Why CTV Is Becoming The First Real Test' Apr 13 2026; Swivel/Olyzon PR Newswire (accessed 2026-06-19).

claims.t: CTV inventory (premium placements, content adjacency, sponsorships, guaranteed delivery, custom packaging) 'never fit cleanly into campaign execution models built for RTB,' making the AdCP negotiation layer a more natural fit than the impression auction and positioning CTV as agentic advertising's first real test.
s: AdExchanger, 'Why CTV Is Becoming The First Real Test Of Agentic Advertising,' Apr 13 2026 (Tier 5, accessed 2026-06-19).

claims.t: AdCP's seller-agent design lets advertiser agents transact directly with publisher seller agents and their ad servers as 'true direct buys,' outside RTB — a flow that can bypass DSPs and the open auction.
s: docs.adcontextprotocol.org Media Buy; MediaPost Oct 16 2025; AdExchanger (Hercher) Oct 15 2025.

claims.t: Some AdCP-aligned voices (Equativ blog; Scope3's Brian O'Kelley) characterize AdCP as the negotiation/interface layer that complements DSP execution rather than eliminating it.
s: Equativ blog ~Feb 2026; The Current (Clark) Jan 28 2026.

claims.t: AdCP's 'Embedded Human Judgment' principle keeps humans in the loop on consequential decisions; a governance agent escalates anything exceeding a set authority threshold (docs use a $20K example).
s: adcontextprotocol.org; docs.adcontextprotocol.org Governance; AdExchanger Oct 15 2025.

claims.t: AdCP's six co-founding members are Yahoo, PubMatic, Optable, Scope3, Swivel, and Triton Digital, each committing ~$10,000/year.
s: MediaPost Oct 16 2025; AdExchanger Oct 15 2025; Samba TV release Oct 15 2025.

claims.t: ARTF (Agentic Real-Time Framework) is a deployment architecture defined by IAB Tech Lab that lets host platforms run third-party 'agent services' as colocated containers inside their own data center/infrastructure, using a standardized API to enrich and modify the bidstream during the auction — its core idea is colocation (running the other party's code locally instead of calling it over the network).
s: artf.ai (accessed 2026-06-19); IAB Tech Lab 'Breaking Down the Walls' blueprint; Index Exchange 'What Is ARTF?'; Digiday Nov 2025

claims.t: The founding/launch roster is dominated by supply-side and premium-publisher/CTV/audio companies (PubMatic, Magnite, LG Ad Solutions, Samba TV, Triton, Yahoo), with comparatively light buy-side representation at founding.
s: MediaPost (supply-side consortium framing) Oct 2025; Samba TV release; AdExchanger Oct 15 2025.

claims.t: The headline 'up to ~80%' latency reduction (trade-rendered as '600-800ms → ~100ms') is an IAB Tech Lab DESIGN TARGET explicitly attributed to the Tech Lab, hedged as 'designed to'/'up to approximately'/'subject to implementation', with no published independent benchmark.
s: IAB Tech Lab PRNewswire Nov 13 2025; artf.ai/technical-specs; MarTech Nov 13 2025; PPC Land

claims.t: By June 2026, AdCP/AgenticAdvertising.org claimed 102+ member companies.
s: adcontextprotocol.org / agenticadvertising.org. Accessed Jun 19 2026.

claims.t: The IAB camp's own latency figures do not reconcile: the IAB headline is ~80% reduction / ~100ms end-to-end round trip; contributor Index Exchange claims 'up to 95%' / 'under 10ms' container execution; IAB Tech Lab's own technical blueprint claims 'low to sub-millisecond' container response — spanning two orders of magnitude, most likely because they measure different things (round trip vs. container execution vs. local-call overhead), and the spec publishes no single reproducible measurement.
s: Index Exchange 'What Is ARTF?'; IAB Tech Lab 'Breaking Down the Walls'; artf.ai; MarTech (all accessed 2026-06-19)

claims.t: The pre-ARTF baseline latency is reported three different ways in the same news cycle: AdExchanger quotes Katsur at '400-600ms'; Digiday says '400-600ms'; MarTech/aggregations say '600-800ms'; artf.ai's technical specs say '400-800ms' — indicating the figure is not pinned to a defined measurement protocol.
s: AdExchanger Nov 2025; Digiday Nov 2025; MarTech Nov 13 2025; artf.ai/technical-specs

claims.t: ARTF is explicitly 'designed to coexist with, not replace, OpenRTB': agents return changes as 'OpenRTB Patch' objects (atomic mutations referencing OpenRTB paths, each tagged with an intent), mutation paths use semantic references derived from OpenRTB/AdCOM concepts, and AAMP more broadly builds on OpenDirect, Deals API, AdCOM and OpenRTB taxonomies; ARTF applies across display, video, CTV, and DOOH.
s: artf.ai/technical-specs; IAB Tech Lab ARTF public-comment spec PDF; IAB Tech Lab AAMP standards page (accessed 2026-06-19)

claims.t: ARTF's interaction model is asymmetric: agent containers return PROPOSED mutations (OpenRTB Patch + intent) and the HOST decides which to merge into the live bid request under its own policies and least-privilege data access — containers cannot unilaterally change the auction.
s: artf.ai/technical-specs; IAB Tech Lab 'Breaking Down the Walls'; Index Exchange explainer; Amit Goel bidstream.amitgoel.me Jun 3 2026

claims.t: ARTF specifies OCI-compliant containers (Docker/Kubernetes-class, orchestrated via Kubernetes/Docker Compose/Amazon ECS) communicating over gRPC with Protocol Buffers (protobuf, claimed more space/time-efficient than JSON), with containers prohibited from external network ingress/egress except to the orchestrating host — a clean-room security property.
s: IAB Tech Lab 'Breaking Down the Walls' (Miguel Morales); artf.ai/technical-specs; PPC Land container-based article

claims.t: On Feb 26, 2026 IAB Tech Lab formally named its umbrella agentic initiative AAMP (Agentic Advertising Management Protocols) to end 'market confusion' (observers treating ARTF + Agentic Audiences as the whole program); AAMP has three pillars — Agentic Foundations (execution; ARTF + Agentic Guardrails), Agentic Protocols (management; seven components mapped to existing IAB standards), and Trust & Transparency (the Agent Registry).
s: PPC Land 'IAB Tech Lab names its agentic ad initiative AAMP' (Feb 2026); IAB Tech Lab AAMP standards page (accessed 2026-06-19)

claims.t: Agentic Audiences (formerly the User Context Protocol, UCP) is a schema for agents to exchange audience signals — identity, contextual, and reinforcement information — that LiveRamp DONATED to IAB Tech Lab on Nov 3, 2025; its distinctive design is to exchange signals as EMBEDDINGS (compact learned vectors, 256-1,024 dimensions) rather than text, to hit sub-100ms RTB response times, governed by a lightweight Commit Group.
s: IAB Tech Lab Agentic Audiences standards page (updated Jan 28 2026); PPC Land LiveRamp donation article; CDP Institute (accessed 2026-06-19)

claims.t: As of June 2026, ARTF v1.0 is finalized: its public-comment period closed Jan 15, 2026; the IAB Tech Lab standards page (updated Feb 18, 2026) states the spec 'will be finalized soon' and that 'Version 2.0 development is already underway'; a v1.0 FINAL PDF was posted ~March 2026.
s: IAB Tech Lab ARTF standards page (Feb 18 2026); IAB Tech Lab PRNewswire Nov 13 2025; iabtechlab.com 2026/03 FINAL spec PDF

claims.t: AAMP 2.0 was announced April 29, 2026, adding transaction-ready Buyer Agent SDK 2.0 and Seller Agent SDK 2.0 (programmatic deals, not just direct), an Agentic Audiences OpenRTB extension, a Prebid module merged into Prebid core, and an open-source scorer; the Seller SDK names integrations with Google Ad Manager, FreeWheel, PubMatic, Index Exchange, and Magnite; AAMP 3.0 is 'well underway'.
s: IAB Tech Lab 'AAMP 2.0 Release...' page; IAB New Zealand / LexisNexis 'AAMP 2.0' (Apr 29 2026)

claims.t: The IAB Tech Lab Agent Registry — the trust/transparency pillar providing agent identity, verification, and disclosure (entries tied to GPP ID / TCF GVL IDs for validation) — launched via the Tools Portal on March 1, 2026, and by March 11, 2026 had expanded to 10 entries (adding Amazon, Burt Intelligence, Optable, Dstillery, HyperMindZ.ai) with a three-tier deployment classification.
s: IAB Tech Lab 'Introducing the IAB Tech Lab Agent Registry'; PPC Land 'agent registry hits 10 with Amazon' (Mar 2026)

claims.t: Architecturally ARTF and AdCP operate at different layers and are described (chiefly by SSPs in both camps) as complementary rather than strictly rival: AdCP is an application/negotiation layer ('what to buy and why', asynchronous, built on MCP), while ARTF is a transaction/execution layer ('how to execute quickly', synchronous millisecond, extending OpenRTB), with ARTF keeping the bidstream/SSP host central while AdCP's seller-agent model could route around the DSP.
s: PubMatic 'Moving Beyond AdCP vs ARTF' blog; Spyrosoft AdTech explainer (accessed 2026-06-19)

claims.t: For CTV the principal benefit of ARTF's colocation is clean-room collaboration: a streaming seller wary of leaking show-level/household viewing data into the open bidstream can let a buyer's logic run next to that data inside a no-egress container and return only a result, with the raw data never leaving the seller's perimeter — enabling enrichment that 'previously only existed in walled gardens'.
s: Adweek 'IAB Launches Technical Standard...'; Digiday Nov 2025 (Heimlich quote); IAB Tech Lab 'Breaking Down the Walls

claims.t: ARTF's contributor/working-group roster is weighted toward CTV supply and CTV-capable demand: the Container Project Working Group includes Index Exchange, OpenX, The Trade Desk, and Chalice, with extended participants including Amazon Ads, Netflix, Paramount, Yahoo, Magnite, PubMatic, Optable, HUMAN Security, WPP Media, and Basis Technologies.
s: PPC Land 'container-based advertising' article; Digiday Nov 2025; Adweek (via search excerpt)

claims.t: The strongest critique of ARTF is that it solves the wrong problem: it optimizes execution speed/interoperability while the binding constraints (brand safety, accountability, measurement, identity) go unaddressed — 'who is accountable when an agent makes a brand-damaging buy that was technically within spec... has no clean answer today, not from AdCP, not from ARTF' — and the coalition is infrastructure-vendor-led with brand marketers 'largely advisory at best'.
s: Alanna Laforet, 'Ad Tech's Agentic Arms Race Is Solving the Wrong Problem,' ExchangeWire, Mar 12 2026

claims.t: Analyst Amit Goel argues the 'agentic' label is largely window dressing — the ARTF spec does not claim goal-directed autonomy; containers are 'specialists that propose' while the host decides, preserving incumbent control — and that 'three protocols address execution, zero address measurement,' so without a real-time outcome-measurement loop today's systems are 'assisted automation,' not agency ('necessary but not sufficient').
s: Amit Goel, 'The Protocols Are Being Debated. The Agents Haven't Arrived Yet,' bidstream.amitgoel.me, Jun 3 2026

claims.t: Because ARTF's unit of action is an OpenRTB Patch applied INSIDE the auction hosted by the existing SSP/exchange, the architecture by construction keeps value flowing through the incumbent DSP→SSP→exchange chain rather than letting an agent route around it — the principal strategic argument that ARTF entrenches the bidstream and the DSP/SSP positions it claims to modernize.
s: Synthesis of artf.ai spec; The Current (Katsur quotes); The Current 'not a fan of AdCP' (Heimlich); Laforet ExchangeWire; Goel Substack

claims.t: AgenticAdvertising.org governs AdCP as a nonprofit (501(c)(6)) with four equally-weighted voting classes (brands, agencies, publishers, technology providers), an open Working Group, and Apache 2.0 licensing with express patent grants.
s: github.com/adcontextprotocol/adcp README; agenticadvertising.org. Accessed Jun 19 2026.

claims.t: The Ad Context Protocol (AdCP) launched October 15, 2025 as an open agent-negotiation standard built on Anthropic's MCP, with founding members PubMatic, Scope3, Swivel, Yahoo, Optable, and Triton Digital plus a CTV/supply-heavy launch cohort.
s: Samba TV press release, Oct 15 2025; PPC Land 'AdCP launches', Oct 2025; Digiday 'WTF is AdCP', 2025. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: AdCP separates spec governance (AgenticAdvertising.org) from reference-implementation development (the Prebid community) by design.
s: github.com/adcontextprotocol/adcp README. Accessed Jun 19 2026.

claims.t: AgenticAdvertising.org (AAO) is a Delaware 501(c)(6) nonprofit, founded 2025, that governs AdCP, with interim leadership Randall Rothenberg (former IAB CEO) and Matthew Egol (ex-Booz/Strategy&), and a planned 40-seat elected board.
s: AgenticAdvertising.org 'About', 2026; Digiday 'Rival trade bodies emerge', 2026. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: IAB Tech Lab CEO Anthony Katsur publicly called AdCP 'deeply flawed,' 'resource consuming,' and 'just another acronym,' said the industry doesn't need 'another trade group,' and argued the Tech Lab already addresses AdCP's problems.
s: The Current, 'Agentic AI is the new advertising battleground. Does it have to be?', ~Jan 28 2026; The Current 'IAB Tech Lab... don't expect any love for AdCP',

claims.t: IAB Tech Lab released ARTF v1.0 for public comment on November 13, 2025 (comment period to Jan 15, 2026); it containerizes vendor logic inside the SSP's infrastructure and claims latency cuts of 'up to 80%,' from ~600-800ms round trips to roughly ~100ms.
s: IAB Tech Lab/PRNewswire, 'ARTF v1.0 for Public Comment', Nov 13 2025; AdExchanger Nov 13 2025; MarTech 2025. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: IAB Tech Lab formally named its agentic umbrella AAMP on February 26, 2026 (the name appears variously as 'Agentic Advertising Management Protocols' / 'Agentic Advertising and Marketing Protocol'), bundling ARTF, Agentic Audiences (ex-UCP, donated by LiveRamp), buyer/seller agent SDKs, and an agent registry, built on existing standards (OpenRTB/AdCOM/OpenDirect/VAST).
s: IAB Tech Lab 'Agentic Advertising and AI Initiatives', 2026; PPC Land 'IAB names AAMP', Feb 26 2026; The Current 2025. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: As of 2026 IAB Tech Lab has released AAMP 2.0 with 'transaction-ready' Buyer and Seller Agent SDKs (public GitHub repos, built on OpenDirect 2.1, Deals API v1.0, AdCOM, sellers.json) that automate deal discovery, negotiation, and booking within existing standards.
s: IAB Tech Lab, 'AAMP 2.0 Release Brings Transaction-ready Buyer and Seller Agent SDKs', 2026; github.com/IABTechLab/seller-agent. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: The most consequential players sit in both camps: Brian O'Kelley helms AdCP while serving on the IAB Tech Lab board; PubMatic is an AdCP founding member whose leaders sit on IAB/IAB Tech Lab/Prebid boards and which self-describes as a coexistence 'bridge'; Yahoo is an AdCP founder and IAB Tech Lab Governance Council member.
s: PubMatic blog 'Moving Beyond AdCP vs ARTF', Jan 8 2026; Alejandro Cremades interview w/ O'Kelley; Digiday 'Rival trade bodies', 2026. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: PubMatic argues AdCP and ARTF are complementary layers, not rivals: AdCP is the application/negotiation layer ('how agents express intent'), ARTF is the transaction/transport layer ('extends existing transaction standards to support agentic behavior'), and they intersect at execution time.
s: PubMatic, 'Moving Beyond AdCP vs ARTF', Jan 8 2026 (Tier 6 vendor position); AdExchanger MCP explainer, Mar 9 2026. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Google released an open-source, read-only Google Ads API MCP server (repo googleads/google-ads-mcp, two tools) on October 7, 2025, and launched a unified Gemini agent 'Ask Advisor' across Ads/Analytics/Merchant Center on May 20, 2026 (beta, English-only), consolidating the earlier Ads Advisor and Analytics Advisor.
s: Google Ads Developer Blog, Oct 7 2025; PPC Land Oct 2025; Google blog.google 'Meet Ask Advisor', May 2026; Search Engine Land May 20 2026. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Amazon Ads opened its write-capable MCP server to global open beta on February 2, 2026 (announced by VP Paula Despins at the IAB ALM); it lets any MCP-compatible agent (Claude/ChatGPT/Gemini) create campaigns, run reports, and manage accounts/billing on Amazon inventory via natural language.
s: Amazon Ads, 'Introducing the Amazon Ads MCP Server', Feb 2 2026; AdExchanger Feb 2026; Digiday Feb 2026. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Meta launched official Meta Ads AI Connectors in open beta on April 29, 2026, including an MCP server at mcp.facebook.com/ads plus a CLI, exposing 29 tools across reporting, campaign management, catalog, diagnostics, and datasets for any MCP-compatible client.
s: Meta for Business, 'Introducing Meta Ads AI Connectors', Apr 29 2026; GoMarble/Pasquale Pillitteri Apr 2026. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: The substantive contest is over governance because whoever controls the standard controls the rents (dues, certification, agent registry, defining a compliant transaction); an AAO backer framed it as 'why pay for a trade association whose only job is stewarding a protocol you may not use anymore,' and analyst Amit Goel calls the governance question the one that determines which technical approach scales.
s: Digiday 'Rival trade bodies', 2026; Amit Goel, Bidstream, 2026. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: A material share of ad tech margin derives from information asymmetry ('a lot of the margins in ad tech come from the fact that nobody has the full picture'), so a truly open agentic standard is a transparency engine that threatens the spread — giving intermediaries a quiet incentive to prefer complex, partial, vendor-controlled standards over clean open ones.
s: AdExchanger, 'Understanding MCP, The Universal Adapter', Mar 9 2026. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: AdCP's seller-agent model lets publishers expose inventory directly to buyer agents as 'true direct buys' within publisher ad servers/curated marketplaces, bypassing the exchange/DSP; O'Kelley likened the launch to 'the debut of header bidding,' implying it compresses the supply chain and shifts margin toward publishers/SSPs.
s: Digiday 'WTF is AdCP', 2025; Broadbrand 'Protocol War', 2026; AdExchanger 'Agentic Marketplace', Apr 2 2026. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Under agentic buying, advertisers 'end up paying a DSP and an SSP fee for something that can be processed in a different way' (Olyzon CEO Jules Minvielle), with the critique sharpest in CTV where one observer calls programmatic 'obsolete'; balanced view holds DSPs/SSPs survive where scale or sole-access advantages remain.
s: AdExchanger, 'The Agentic Marketplace Is Here. Where Does That Leave DSPs and SSPs?', Apr 2 2026; AdExchanger curation-fees piece, 2026. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: The standards war precedes meaningful volume: early reporting found zero dollars transacting through AdCP; first live campaigns appeared December 2025 (PubMatic/Butler+Till/Clubtails, a PubMatic-reported +40% impressions, not independently audited), with the IAB agent registry reaching ~10 entries by March 2026 — against hundreds of billions of ad transactions daily.
s: INMA 'Understanding the agentic advertising moment', 2026; PPC Land 'Affinity joins AdCP', Jun 9 2026; Amit Goel, Bidstream, 2026. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: The Trade Desk is absent from the AdCP roster and sits on the IAB Tech Lab Governance Council, but its operative posture is 'build my own' — launching Koa Agents on its own MCP (Stagwell pilot) — exemplifying the protocol-agnostic-orchestration stance that lets no single standard lock it in.
s: Broadbrand 'Protocol War', 2026; The Current 'Stagwell pilots TTD agentic capabilities', 2026; PPC Land Kokai updates, 2026. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: By v3.1, AdCP includes a Creative protocol (list_creative_formats, build_creative, sync_creatives, brand.json-driven) and an Events/Performance feedback loop reporting conversions back to sellers.
s: docs.adcontextprotocol.org; github.com/adcontextprotocol/adcp. Accessed Jun 19 2026.

claims.t: US connected-TV ad spend is projected at roughly $37.7-38 billion in 2026 (up ~14% from ~$33.4B in 2025), and 2026 US CTV upfront spending (~$17.73B) is expected to exceed primetime linear-TV upfront spending (~$16.98B) for the first time.
s: eMarketer, 'US CTV ad spend growth slows but remains strong' & 'US TV and Connected TV Ad Spending Forecasts H2 2025' (2025-2026), accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: AdCP's roadmap targets v4.0 for early 2027 as a breaking-changes window whose floor requirement is mandatory request signing — agents must sign spend-committing operations and sellers must verify.
s: docs.adcontextprotocol.org/docs/reference/roadmap. Accessed Jun 19 2026.

claims.t: Per eMarketer, the CTV ad market is 'far more diffuse than the social network landscape': only three companies are expected to clear 10% of US CTV ad sales in 2026 — YouTube (11.9%), Amazon (>10%), and Disney/Hulu+Disney+ (10.8%).
s: eMarketer, 'YouTube, rising prices, and the shifting balance of CTV in 2026' (2026), accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: Over 90% of US CTV ad spend in 2025 transacted through programmatic pipes, but the dominant deal types are programmatic guaranteed, private marketplace, and programmatic direct; genuinely biddable open-exchange premium CTV supply is thin.
s: AI Digital 'CTV Media Buying'; Equativ 'CTV Advertising 2026 Guide' (2026), accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: Automatic content recognition (ACR) — software in smart TVs that fingerprints on-screen content frame-by-frame — is the signal that distinguishes CTV; it is device-manufacturer-proprietary and exposed to agents only as packaged segments, giving walled gardens leverage to keep agents on a leash.
s: Samsung Ads 'AI-enhanced advertising solutions' (2026); AI Digital 'CTV Advertising Trends 2026', accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: CTV addressability rests on a patchwork (device IDs, IP/household graphs, logins, ACR, clean-room matches) with no shared identifier, which is why platforms bolt on third-party signals (Netflix added Amazon Audiences and Yahoo ConnectID, ~232M logged-in US users, in 2026) and why a walled garden's own agent has an identity edge over a neutral one.
s: PPC Land 'Netflix Ads gets Amazon audiences, Yahoo signals, conversion API' (2026-03-04); AdCP docs, accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: The Trade Desk's take rate has sat at roughly 20% of spend since 2017 (20.3% in 2024), with CEO Jeff Green committing to '15-20% for as far as we can see into the future' — the single fattest, most defensible slice of the CTV spread and the most obvious agentic target.
s: AdExchanger, 'As CTV Blooms, It's Knives Out For The Trade Desk's Take Rate', accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: Amazon Ads launched its Ads MCP Server in open beta on February 2, 2026 (announced by VP Paula Despins), built on MCP as a translation layer turning natural-language prompts into structured API calls, connecting Claude/ChatGPT/Gemini to campaign, reporting, account, and billing functions; available globally to API-credentialed partners.
s: Amazon Ads, 'Introducing the Amazon Ads MCP Server' (2026-02-02), accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: Amazon's Feb 2 2026 MCP announcement does not mention Prime Video, CTV, or the DSP by name; the MCP server is a general API access layer and Amazon's CTV inventory is reached via Amazon DSP separately — so Amazon's CTV-specific agentic exposure is implicit, not separately productized as of that announcement.
s: Amazon Ads, 'Introducing the Amazon Ads MCP Server' (2026-02-02), accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: At CES 2026 (Jan 8, 2026) Disney unveiled the Disney Ads Agent, a chatbot that reduces media-planning prep (inventory search, audience ID, campaign tracking, brief-to-plan), plus generative-AI ad creation (:15/:30/:60 from a brief) and a Brand Portal expanding Disney Compass measurement.
s: The Current, 'Disney introduces AI-driven ad planning and creative tools at CES' (Jan 2026); Next TV, 'Disney Ad Sales Bolsters Automation', accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: Disney's DRAX (Disney Real-Time Ad Exchange) biddable/self-service platform reported biddable transactions up 70% since launch and 8,000+ video advertisers at the CES 2026 cycle, with a goal to automate over half its ad business within five years and Disney Select first-party audiences activatable programmatically via DRAX (clean room announced October 2025).
s: Next TV/Broadcasting+Cable, 'Disney Ad Sales Bolsters Automation' (2026); AdExchanger 'DRAX Attacks!' (older), accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: Roku's ad stack as of mid-2026: Roku Exchange (launched June 2024, connecting Amazon DSP/Trade Desk/Yahoo/FreeWheel/DV360), Ads Manager (Sept 2024, self-serve with Shopify integration and AI creative upscaling), and Roku Curate (April 2026, bundling first-party data with six retail partners: Best Buy Ads, Criteo, Fandango, Fetch, Instacart, Kroger Precision Marketing).
s: PPC Land, 'Roku explores a sale...' (citing Reuters 2026-06-12), accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: Roku is exploring strategic options including a full sale per Reuters (June 12, 2026); market cap ~$19.4B; shares jumped ~20% on the news; Reuters cited discussions with at least one US media company, no final decisions — a live going-concern flag for Roku's ad/identity platform and any agentic posture.
s: PPC Land relaying Reuters (2026-06-12), accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: Netflix runs a multi-DSP programmatic ad stack (Trade Desk, Google DV360, Microsoft, Yahoo DSP, Amazon DSP — Amazon added as 5th partner Sept 10 2025) and on March 4 2026 added Amazon Audiences (Q2 2026 US), Yahoo ConnectID signals, and its own Conversion API (CAPI), with early Tinuiti testing showing >75% benchmark outperformance; 2025 ad revenue >$1.5B, 2026 projected ~$3B.
s: PPC Land 'Netflix Ads gets Amazon audiences...' (2026-03-04); StreamTV Insider 'Netflix partners with Amazon DSP', accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: Ahead of CES 2026 Samsung Ads announced its entire ad suite is now AI-powered; at IAB NewFronts 2026 it launched 'Performance TV,' a full-funnel performance platform with shoppable innovation and an Amazon commerce integration, partnering with Snowflake to unify audience/linear/CTV data and exposing homescreen inventory programmatically via DSPs.
s: Samsung Newsroom 'Samsung Launches Performance TV' (2026); Samsung Ads blog; ExchangeWire (2026-02-12), accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: Magnite embedded a seller agent into SpringServe (its ad-server/SSP, benchmarked by Jounce at 99% of US streaming supply; clients incl. Disney, Paramount, Roku, Samsung, Warner Bros. Discovery), announced January 6 2026, after completing one of the first AdCP test buys in December 2025 with Scope3 as buyer agent and MiQ on the buy side.
s: PPC Land 'Magnite builds seller agent into SpringServe' (2026-01-06); Magnite blog, accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: On April 27 2026 Magnite expanded with its first proprietary buyer agent (testing with Kepler and MiQ on Disney inventory), seller-agent workflows with Publicis Media Exchange, and three AI-assisted SpringServe mediation features (anomaly detection, demand-path optimization, dynamic pricing).
s: PPC Land 'Magnite expands AI buyer agent and SpringServe mediation with Disney and MiQ' (2026-04-27), accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: Magnite launched Magnite Orchestration on June 11 2026, a coordination layer letting buyers connect their buyer agents to Magnite's seller agent across premium inventory; publishers build custom inventory/audience packages, buyers create media plans from RFPs and launch omnichannel campaigns across CTV home screens and audio; testing partners include dentsu and DIRECTV Advertising.
s: GlobeNewswire/Magnite IR 'Introducing Magnite Orchestration' (2026-06-11); PPC Land corroboration, accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: PubMatic runs AgenticOS, a full buy-side agent stack, and on December 15 2025 launched (with agency Butler/Till) a fully autonomous end-to-end agentic CTV campaign for Clubtails (Geloso Beverage Group) — a natural-language brief via Claude, AdCP for agent-to-system communication, on geo-targeted premium CTV; results slated for Q1 2026. AgenticOS opened to independent agencies via an Untapped Growth Collective partnership (March 2026) citing 28 of top 30 streamers.
s: PubMatic/Yahoo Finance 'PubMatic and Butler/Till Launch AdCP-Enabled Agentic AI Campaign Across CTV' (2025-12-15); PubMatic Untapped Growth release (Mar 2026),

claims.t: PubMatic reports early AgenticOS campaigns reduce supply-chain costs by 40-50%, deliver 40% more impressions at 30% lower eCPMs, and cut campaign setup time by 87% — vendor-reported, not independently audited.
s: PubMatic, 'Independent Agencies Gain Advanced Agentic Media Buying...' press release (Mar 2026), accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: The Trade Desk introduced Koa Agents (closed beta as of March 2026) that automate pre-campaign workflow (media-plan ingestion, campaign build, creative troubleshooting, recommendations) via an Open Agentic Kit connecting to AI models including Claude — but 'the agent is not buying ads, at least not yet,' with CEO Jeff Green saying 'autonomous bidding is not the near-term priority.
s: Digiday 'Inside The Trade Desk's Claude-powered campaign agent' (2026); AdTechRadar (2026-04-21), accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: NBCUniversal, agency RPA, FreeWheel, and Newton Research announced (early January 2026) agentic AI buying spanning linear and digital premium video, with the first execution a brand's Q1 2026 investment in live football playoff games — described as the first time AI agents automate live-sports inventory on linear TV, operating 'separate from the OpenRTB spec' and sidelining the usual buying/selling platforms.
s: FreeWheel/NBCUniversal press release (Jan 2026); VideoWeek (2026-01-07), accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: Shoppable CTV is positioned in 2026 as a critical retail-media channel (platforms incl. Roku, Amazon Freevee, YouTube TV, Hulu, Peacock, Tubi, Samsung TV+, Netflix Ads, Disney+, Paramount+; Pinterest links Pins to shoppable actions in Roku after acquiring tvScientific in Dec 2025); Google documents shoppable CTV and agentic commerce together — but autonomous agent purchase from a CTV ad is aspirational-to-piloted, not a shipped production flow.
s: Starti 'Shoppable CTV for E-commerce 2026'; Rise 'CES 2026'; PPC Land 'Google's 2026 retail ad playbook', accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: eMarketer expects retail-media CTV ad spend to grow 45.5% in 2025 with one in five CTV ad dollars going to retail media by 2027; US retail-media ad spend overall forecast at $58.79B (2025) rising to $69.33B (2026), much of it to Amazon Ads and Walmart Connect.
s: eMarketer, 'CTV, retail media, social, and search drive US ad spend growth' (2026), accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: AdCP (launched Oct 15 2025 by Scope3/Yahoo/PubMatic/Swivel/Triton/Optable, built on MCP, with a Curation Protocol scheduled Q2 2026) attacks CTV's dominant deal type (curation/PMP/deal construction), while IAB Tech Lab's ARTF (colocated RTB claiming ~90% latency cut, ~600-800ms to ~100ms, under the AAMP umbrella) optimizes CTV's minority biddable deal type — an asymmetry that is the most important CTV-specific consequence of the standards war.
s: AdCP docs; The Current/Broadbrand on AdCP+ARTF; MediaPost 'Katsur Clears The Air' (2026-02-27), accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: Ari Paparo (Marketecture Media) argues agentic media-buying protocols don't address the business obstacles to automation — publishers won't put sensitive pricing in an MCP server, buyers won't be price-takers, sellers won't reveal rate cards, small buys create unbeatable overhead, and most sellers lack the data — so agents reinforce intermediary roles with value accruing 'to very large publishers and cross-publisher ad networks, in much the same way it has with programmatic more generally.
s: PPC Land, 'Industry expert questions AdCP media buying protocol for ad automation' (2025-11-03), accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: AdCP's Curation and seller-agent model maps onto how premium/PMP CTV is already sold — negotiated, packaged, relationship-based — making CTV its natural first proving ground.
s: docs.adcontextprotocol.org Media Buy; Samba TV release; Equativ blog (Netflix/HBO Max framing, vendor-lean).

claims.t: Google announced the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) on 16 September 2025 with more than 60 partner organizations including Mastercard, PayPal, American Express, Coinbase, Salesforce, JCB, and UnionPay International.
s: Google Cloud Blog, 2025-09-16; Digital Commerce 360, 2025-09-19

claims.t: CTV addressability signals (ACR data and identity) are the kind of audience signal AdCP's Audience Activation/Signals sub-protocol activates, and ACR-native firms (Samba TV, LG Ad Solutions) are on the roster.
s: MediaPost Oct 2025; docs.adcontextprotocol.org Signals.

claims.t: AP2's trust model chains three cryptographically-signed Mandates — Intent (what the user wants/constraints), Cart (the exact items and price the agent assembled and the user approved), and Payment (the authorized amount and funding instrument that the payment network actually sees) — forming a non-repudiable audit trail for human-present and human-not-present transactions.
s: Google Cloud Blog 2025-09-16; ap2-protocol.org spec; AP2 explainer (search-indexed)

claims.t: The live AP2 spec (mid-2026) reframes the model as a Checkout Mandate and Payment Mandate each with Open/Closed states, even though the September 2025 announcement and most explainers use Intent/Cart/Payment — so the conceptual model is stable but the exact noun-set has changed.
s: ap2-protocol.org spec, accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: AP2 is published as an open-source spec with reference implementations on a public GitHub repository, and reached version 0.2.0 on 28 April 2026.
s: GitHub google-agentic-commerce/AP2, accessed 2026-06-19

claims.t: AP2 is designed as an extension of the A2A and MCP protocols, is payment-rail-agnostic (cards, real-time bank transfer, stablecoins), and includes an A2A x402 extension for crypto built with Coinbase, the Ethereum Foundation, and MetaMask.
s: Google Cloud Blog, 2025-09-16

claims.t: The Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP) was announced on 29 September 2025, co-developed by OpenAI and Stripe, as the open (Apache 2.0) standard powering Instant Checkout in ChatGPT, launching with US Etsy sellers and 'over a million Shopify merchants coming soon.
s: Stripe Blog/Newsroom 2025-09-29; OpenAI 'Buy it in ChatGPT' 2025-09-29

claims.t: By March 2026, six months after debut, OpenAI's Instant Checkout had only roughly 30 live Shopify merchants (against a 'million coming soon' claim), faced arduous merchant onboarding and stale item data, and Walmart pulled its ~200,000 SKUs out to run its own Sparky agent inside ChatGPT and Gemini.
s: CNBC 2026-03-20; Digital Commerce 360 2026-03-24

claims.t: OpenAI publicly shifted strategy from owning the agentic transaction to owning product discovery, allowing merchants to use their own checkout experiences after the first Instant Checkout version 'did not offer the level of flexibility' it wanted.
s: CNBC 2026-03-20; Digital Commerce 360 2026-03-24

claims.t: Google announced the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) on 11 January 2026, co-developed with Shopify, Etsy, Wayfair, Target, and Walmart and endorsed by 20+ companies, positioned as compatible with (not a replacement for) A2A, AP2, and MCP and covering discovery through post-purchase.
s: Google blog 2026-01-11

claims.t: By April 2026 Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Salesforce, and Stripe had joined the UCP Tech Council, and trade press characterized UCP as 'by and far the most dominant commerce protocol.
s: Adweek guide 2026 (search-indexed)

claims.t: By mid-2026 an industry consensus had formed describing the stack as 'MCP for tool integration, A2A for agent communication, UCP + AP2 for e-commerce,' indicating the payment/commerce protocols mostly settled into complementary layers rather than direct substitutes.
s: Adweek guide 2026 (search-indexed)

claims.t: Coinbase released the x402 whitepaper on 6 May 2025; it revives the HTTP 402 status code as a four-step machine-to-machine stablecoin payment flow (commonly USDC on Base, also Solana/Ethereum) designed for agents/APIs without human intervention.
s: Coinbase x402 launch 2025-05-06; The Block (search-indexed)

claims.t: On 2 April 2026 the Linux Foundation launched the x402 Foundation with 20+ members (including Google, Microsoft, Visa, Mastercard, Stripe, Cloudflare, AWS, Circle, Coinbase, Solana Foundation), moving x402 to vendor-neutral governance; Solana reported driving nearly 65% of 2026 x402 transaction volume.
s: Linux Foundation press release 2026-04-02

claims.t: Google integrated x402 into AP2 (via the A2A x402 extension) as its default stablecoin rail.
s: Google Cloud Blog 2025-09-16; x402 explainers (search-indexed)

claims.t: Google announced A2A on 9 April 2025 and donated the protocol to the Linux Foundation in June 2025; by April 2026 more than 150 organizations supported it, and it defines Agent Cards, Tasks, and an HTTP/SSE/JSON-RPC transport.
s: Linux Foundation press release 2025-06; Google Developers Blog 2025-06

claims.t: Mastercard Agent Pay (announced 29 April 2025, using Agentic Tokens on MDES) and Visa Intelligent Commerce (scoped tokenized agent credentials plus Intelligent Commerce Connect) provide agent-aware payment credentials that plug into AP2/ACP/UCP rather than competing as protocols.
s: Mastercard Newsroom 2025-04-29; TechInformed (Visa) 2026

claims.t: On 14 April 2026 American Express launched the Agentic Commerce Experiences (ACE) Developer Kit with an industry-first pledge to protect eligible customers from charges resulting from registered AI-agent error when authenticated purchase intent is provided, partnering with Adyen, Stripe, PayPal, Fiserv and merchants Delta, Expedia, Hilton.
s: Amex Newsroom 2026-04-14; Fortune 2026-04-14; Digital Commerce 360 2026-04-14

claims.t: Across the proposed agentic-commerce protocols the merchant remains the merchant of record and continues to own fraud exposure and chargebacks; an agent ordering the wrong item from misread intent typically leaves the merchant liable, and standard chargeback evidence (IP, device, navigation) is weakened because it was agent-generated.
s: Sam Boboev, Finextra/Fintech Wrap Up, 2026

claims.t: One analyst source claims disputes on agent-initiated transactions run roughly 2.4x the rate of comparable human card-not-present transactions, weighted toward 'did not authorize' and 'not as described' rather than fraud — but this figure is single-source and could not be independently corroborated.
s: Sam Boboev, Finextra/Fintech Wrap Up, 2026

claims.t: A claimed 'CFPB January 2026 advisory' framing agent-initiated card transactions within Regulation Z (with consumer recourse narrowed but not extinguished by a scoped mandate) could not be independently verified against CFPB's published record and should not be treated as established.
s: Analyst source (Boboev/TrustSphere) 2026; CFPB.gov searched 2026-06-19 with no match

claims.t: In agentic commerce, advertising's job shifts from capturing human attention to being selected by the agent — brands compete on data quality, protocol compliance, and catalog completeness, and ads influence AI decisions that result in human purchases.
s: commercetools 2026; Ad Age/Yotpo 2026 (search-indexed)

claims.t: Ad inventory is appearing inside the agents themselves: OpenAI rolled out an early ChatGPT Ad Manager interface for selected advertisers in May 2026, and Google launched a 'Direct Offers' pilot (11 Jan 2026) letting retailers present discounts to high-intent shoppers in AI Mode (Petco, e.l.f., Samsonite, Rugs USA, Shopify merchants).
s: Google blog 2026-01-11; ad trade coverage 2026-05 (search-indexed)

claims.t: AdCP (the agent-native advertising-transaction protocol, built on MCP/A2A) negotiates and buys ad inventory but does not itself specify payment/settlement infrastructure, leaving a seam where the commerce/payment 'other standards' could connect — though no evidence exists yet that AdCP buys settle over AP2 or x402.

claims.t: As of 2026 shoppable CTV (T-commerce) still completes purchases via QR code or send-to-phone hand-off to mobile checkout, not via a TV-resident agent completing an AP2 Payment Mandate; an end-to-end agentic CTV purchase is announced/aspirational, not a shipping product in any source reviewed.

claims.t: eMarketer (December 2025) projects US e-commerce sales via AI platforms to exceed ~$20 billion in 2026 (≈$20.9B, nearly quadrupling 2025) and reach $144 billion by 2029 — large in growth terms but still a small fraction of total e-commerce.

claims.t: The trust/communication layers (MCP, A2A, AP2, x402) are converging on genuine, neutrally-governed interoperability (Linux Foundation donations, AP2-as-A2A/MCP-extension, rails providers integrating with everyone), while the commerce/checkout layer is a real land-grab between Google's UCP and OpenAI's ACP — with retailers like Walmart running their own agents, raising a fragmentation risk that could keep that layer contested.
s: Synthesis of sources 1,2,5,6,8,15,16,21,22; reasoning is the author's

claims.t: IAB Tech Lab CEO Anthony Katsur has called AdCP 'deeply flawed' and 'resource-consuming,' said the industry needn't have 'another industry trade group,' and that AdCP 'went far in trying to standardize something that's unproven' vs. IAB's OpenRTB-based ARTF.
s: The Current (Clark) 'IAB Tech Lab, not a fan of AdCP...' Nov 13 2025; The Current Jan 28 2026.

claims.t: Auction defenders argue agentic AI should sit above deterministic programmatic execution rather than replace the transparent auction; a DSP executive told The Current it should be 'an additional layer that sits above programmatic execution' while 'auctions continue to execute deterministically underneath.

claims.t: As of mid-2026 the public record establishes membership (102+), spec maturity (v3.1), governance, and demos, but not independently-verified production scale (transacted dollar volume, count of live revenue-handling seller agents); proponents themselves call it 'early stages.

claims.t: The current released version of AdCP is v3.1.0, dated June 18, 2026.
s: github.com/adcontextprotocol/adcp release v3.1.0, Jun 18 2026. Accessed Jun 19 2026.

claims.t: IAB Tech Lab released ARTF v1.0 for public comment Nov 13, 2025 and named its umbrella initiative AAMP (Agentic Advertising Management Protocols) on Feb 26, 2026, with the former User Context Protocol rebranded 'Agentic Audiences.

claims.t: The seller-agent 'bypass the DSP' thesis most directly empowers whoever owns the buyer agent, and the holding companies are best positioned to own one at scale via their budgets, client relationships, first-party data, and trading desks.
