claims.t: MiQ generates $600M+ in revenue, above the ~$500M often cited.
s: Marketecture, MiQ $600M+ revenue, 2025-2026, accessed 2026-06-20

claims.t: On June 12 2025 Dentsu named MiQ its official Intelligence Partner, the first holding company to integrate MiQ Sigma at the strategic center of its media practice.
s: MediaPost / MiQ, Dentsu goes all-in with MiQ, June 12 2025, accessed 2026-06-20

claims.t: About 51% of US brands have partially moved programmatic buying in-house.
s: The Version2, in-housing programmatic 2025, accessed 2026-06-20

claims.t: Holdcos are restructuring buying/trading under cost and AI pressure (Omnicom offshoring; WPP Media integration), reshaping the field MiQ sells into.
s: Marketing Dive / Storyboard18, 2025, accessed 2026-06-20

claims.t: US retail media ad spend was ~$58.8B in 2025 and forecast at ~$69-71B in 2026, among the largest and fastest-growing channels.
s: EMARKETER via multiple, 2026, accessed 2026-06-20

claims.t: US retail-media spend on CTV grew ~45.5% YoY in 2025, with retailers extending first-party commerce data into CTV in 2026.
s: EMARKETER, advertisers adjust budgets for retail media, 2026, accessed 2026-06-20

claims.t: Amazon generates $60B+ in annual ad revenue and ~77% of US retail media, with ~90% concentrated in Amazon+Walmart.
s: Adtelligent / Osmos, retail media outlook 2026, accessed 2026-06-20

claims.t: Amazon DSP is the fastest-growing top-five DSP (~24% YoY, ~14% share); The Trade Desk holds ~19% and a disproportionate share of premium CTV/open-internet inventory.
s: Digital Applied / AI Digital, programmatic stats 2026, accessed 2026-06-20

claims.t: Commerce media reached ~15.6% of total global ad revenue (~$178.2bn) in 2025 per WPP Media/GroupM, with retail media ~15.9%, and is the fastest-growing major ad segment, forecast toward a quarter of digital ad spend by 2028.
s: Marketing Brew, 2025-12-09 (reporting WPP Media/GroupM); eMarketer commerce-media FAQ 2025. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: Amazon (~79.7% US share, 2025) and Walmart Connect (~8.0%) together took >84% of US retail-media spend in 2025 and ~89% of the incremental dollar in 2026, with nearly every other RMN's share forecast flat or declining through 2027.
s: eMarketer, 'FAQ on retail media networks 2026' and '2025 trend: long-tail squeeze'; PYMNTS 2025. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: MiQ positions itself as the neutral layer harmonizing across 200+ globally fragmented retail media networks (each a walled garden), connecting 'the basket to the wallet' — a defensible niche outside the Amazon/Walmart duopoly.
s: MiQ US, 'The new commerce opportunity,' 2025-11-10; eMarketer (long-tail). Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: MiQ launched Consumer Link on 2023-05-08 as a CPG shopper-intelligence data spine claiming 90% of US households, with Shopper TV / Shopper / Merchant Intelligence; current brand status is confirmed only via continued marketing pages plus reflection in 2025-2026 Sigma materials, not a fresh dated re-launch.
s: MiQ/BusinessWire, 2023-05-08; MiQ Consumer Link product page. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: MiQ Commerce launched in Canada on 2024-09-10 via a NielsenIQ data agreement, integrating NIQ Precision Areas modelled retail sales data at Forward Sortation Area level to attribute in-store sales lift; the measurement is geo-level modelled, not person-level deterministic.
s: MiQ Canada & NielsenIQ, 2024-09-10. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: MiQ's commerce data is federated from third parties — NielsenIQ (modelled sales, 2024), Circana and Numerator (Sigma-integrated panels, 2025), Ibotta (deterministic receipts, announced 2021) — and the Ibotta partnership has no 2024-2026 re-confirmation while Numerator is attested only as a Sigma integration name.
s: MiQ-Ibotta BusinessWire 2021-07-22; MiQ Sigma launch 2025-06-04; Circana-Ibotta 2025-09-30; MiQ Sigma expansion 2026-06-11. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: MiQ's commerce data feeds Sigma, its AI platform (launched June 2025, ~$100m, Bengaluru CoE); Sigma was described as 300+ feeds / 700T signals at June 2025 launch and 600+ feeds / 2.5PB at the June 2026 expansion that introduced Sigma Total Measurement — figures whose units changed and are not directly comparable.
s: MiQ/BusinessWire 2025-06-04 and 2026-06-11; Marketing-Interactive 2025. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: MiQ Commerce provides cross-channel attribution across CTV/OLV/YouTube/Display/Social, linking upper-funnel TV brand media to in-store sales; Shopper TV Intelligence and shoppable CTV units make commerce data the mechanism that closes CTV's measurement loop.
s: MiQ Canada Commerce pages; MiQ 'Everything is shoppable.' Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: On 2026-03-25 MiQ acquired Adsmovil's LatAm business (12 markets, 150+ staff), bringing Adsmovil Personas and Linki — a multi-channel retail media platform — into MiQ; US business excluded, terms undisclosed; Sigma LatAm + Linki launched May 2026.
s: MiQ/BusinessWire 2026-03-25; ppc.land; Portada 2026. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: Even as an owned asset, Linki (a multi-channel RMN platform) likely brokers access to retailers' environments rather than giving MiQ proprietary first-party shopper data at Amazon/Walmart scale; its data-ownership depth is undisclosed, so it deepens activation footprint and regional independence without resolving the 'owns no first-party data' critique.
s: MiQ/BusinessWire 2026-03-25 (absence of disclosed first-party data). Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: Across every commerce capability the data originates with partners (NIQ, Circana, Numerator, Ibotta, retailers); MiQ contributes identity resolution, cross-network harmonization, activation and measurement — an orchestration layer, more exposed in commerce because the most valuable asset (proprietary deterministic first-party purchase data) is exactly what MiQ lacks.
s: Synthesis of sources 3-6, 9, 12-14. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: MiQ has no closed-loop deterministic environment and no path to one, so its strategy is complementary not competitive — the neutral layer operating across the long tail of RMNs and connecting retail media to CTV/open-web brand media — confining it to the non-duopoly slice whose incremental growth the duopoly is capturing.
s: eMarketer 2025-2026; MiQ US blog 2025-11-10. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: Cookie/MAID deprecation and privacy tightening raise the value of deterministic first-party purchase data, advantaging data owners (Amazon/Walmart, NIQ/Circana/Numerator/Ibotta) over a data-borrowing orchestration layer; MiQ partially offsets via contextual-lookalike modelling and Sigma identity resolution.
s: MiQ-Ibotta 2021-07-22; MiQ Sigma 2025-06-04. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: Bridgepoint took a majority stake in MiQ from ECI Partners on 2022-09-13 (~$1bn valuation, ECI ~6.1x); under PE ownership MiQ has run an explicit roll-up (Grasp, Samba, AirGrid, Pathlabs, Adsmovil/Linki), and commerce fits the thesis as the fastest-growing, software-leveraged adjacency.
s: Bridgepoint 2022-09-13; PE Hub 2022; MiQ acquisition releases. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: MiQ announced acquiring Pathlabs (Missoula MEP, founded 2021, ~100 staff) on 2024-07-29 to reach mid-size independent agencies; Pathlabs runs standalone and widens the distribution funnel through which MiQ's commerce stack reaches independent agencies' CPG clients.
s: MiQ/Pathlabs/BusinessWire 2024-07-29. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: Agentic advertising denotes autonomous AI agents that plan and execute media buys ACROSS platforms toward a goal, distinct from intra-platform AI automation (Advantage+, Performance Max) which predates it.
s: eMarketer, 'FAQ on AI media buying' 2026; TensorOps AdTech Lab, 'Agentic AI in Advertising: A 2026 Field Guide.' Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: The MiQ Sigma Trading Agent is a natural-language layer executing optimizations across multiple DSPs, trained on the reasoning of three LLMs (Claude, Gemini, ChatGPT), monthly data from ~6,000 programmatic campaigns, and 15 years of MiQ trading data / tacit trader knowledge.
s: MiQ, Business Wire, 2026-06-11; PPC Land Jun 2026; B&T 2026. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: MiQ states its Sigma Trading Agent reduces cross-DSP/SSP audience activation from ~6 hours to ~30 seconds — a self-reported, single-source vendor claim attributed to a MiQ sales lead with no disclosed methodology, sample, or independent verification.
s: B&T (Australia), 'MiQ Sigma' 2026, https://www.bandt.com.au/miq-sigma/. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: As of January 2026 MiQ is a named early participant in PubMatic AgenticOS (launched Jan 5, 2026), integrating the Sigma Trading Agent with PubMatic's supply-side agentic OS to test agent-led workflows on live campaigns through Q1 2026.
s: PubMatic, Business Wire, 2026-01-05; PPC Land Jan 2026; NewscastStudio 2026-01-06. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: PubMatic launched the Agentic AI Acceleration Program alongside AgenticOS (Jan 2026), a limited-capacity initiative to move participants from early testing to live agentic workflows 'within weeks' during Q1 2026.
s: PubMatic Business Wire 2026-01-05; PPC Land Jan 2026. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: As of January 2026 MiQ is an early integration partner of Yahoo DSP's embedded agentic AI (MCP/API connectivity under 'Yours, Mine, and Ours'), and as of April 27, 2026 a buyer-agent test partner in Magnite's first proprietary buyer agent using Disney inventory.
s: PPC Land, 'Yahoo DSP embeds AI agents' Jan 2026; PPC Land, 'Magnite expands AI buyer agent...Disney and MiQ' 2026-04-27. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: As of late January 2026, MiQ CSO John Goulding characterized MiQ's live agentic/protocol-enabled direct-media-buy tests as 'in the five-figure territory' (nascent), even as MiQ publicly states a 2026 plan to 'start scaling agentic ad buying' — making the scaling announced-not-shipped.
s: Digiday, 'Inside the debate over agentic advertising and standards,' 2026-01-26. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: AdCP launched October 15, 2025 as a supply-led open standard built on MCP (Yahoo, PubMatic, Scope3, Optable, Swivel, Triton Digital), with 100+ companies joining within months; PubMatic embeds AdCP and MCP in AgenticOS, the surface MiQ's Trading Agent integrates with.
s: Samba TV press release / MediaPost, 2025-10-15/16; adcontextprotocol.org; PubMatic Business Wire 2026-01-05. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: MiQ's Trading Agent is best read as a defensive necessity with a narrow embedded moat: defensive because it automates the managed-service labor MiQ sells (which agents threaten to commoditize), moated only via (a) its proprietary conditioning corpus and (b) structurally neutral cross-DSP/SSP orchestration unavailable to single-platform agents.
s: Synthesis of MiQ Business Wire 2026-06-11; PubMatic 2026-01-05; Yahoo Inc. press Jan 2026; eMarketer/TensorOps 2026. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: The verifiable substance of MiQ's agentic bet is the Trading Agent's existence, its proprietary conditioning corpus, and dated multi-surface integration partnerships; every quantified performance/speed claim is self-reported and unverified, and the 'scaling in 2026' plan is announced-not-shipped by the CSO's own account.
s: MiQ Business Wire 2026-06-11; B&T 2026; Digiday 2026-01-26. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: As of early 2026, named industry critics identify decreased transparency/control, premature transparency demands, and protocol fragmentation as the principal risks of agentic buying — risks MiQ's public agentic materials do not directly address.
s: Digiday, 'Inside the debate over agentic advertising and standards,' 2026-01-26. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: Titan OS remains an independent, Barcelona-based, founder-led company that raised a €50M (~$58M) Series A led by Highland Europe in December 2025 — after the MiQ deal — bringing total funding to ~$70M, and is raising again in 2026.
s: TechCrunch, 2025-12-02, https://techcrunch.com/2025/12/02/titan-os-raises-58-million-from-highland-europe-for-its-smart-tv-os/ ; StreamTV Insider, 2025-12. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: Philips (via TP Vision) is dropping Google TV from its entire 2026 television lineup in favour of Titan OS across all models, announced March 2026, after ~two years of testing — sharply increasing Titan's first-party data and inventory scale.
s: PPC Land, 2026-03-23, https://ppc.land/philips-drops-google-tv-for-titan-os-on-all-2026-models-what-it-means-for-ctv-ads/ . Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: The MiQ–Titan OS partnership (announced 18 Nov 2025) is restated in identical terms across MiQ's multilingual newsroom and independent trade coverage with no rename, narrowing, or withdrawal: MiQ is 'first to license Titan OS log-level data,' the 'only managed-service partner with direct access,' with Sigma integration timed for Q1 2026.
s: MiQ newsroom, 2025-11-18, https://www.wearemiq.com/resources/news/miq-builds-unparalleled-tv-intelligence-in-europe-through-deal-with-titan-os ; The Media Leader; Advanced Television, 2025-11-18. Acce

claims.t: The 'over 20 million connected TVs' figure was explicitly MiQ's COMBINED Samba TV + Titan OS pool, not Titan alone; Titan's own 2026 reach is now 'over 30 million streaming households across Europe' (vs ~4M directly-operated MAU and 18M MAU cited late 2025) — the load-bearing figure is current and arguably conservative.
s: MiQ newsroom, 2025-11-18; PPC Land, 2026-03-23. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: MiQ's exclusivity covers managed-service log-level/OS-level DATA, not Titan OS's ad inventory or audience segments: Titan sells home-screen video programmatically via Equativ (May 2026), monetises both Titan and TiVo OS inventory via its own Titan Ads arm (Oct 2025), and runs FAST/home-screen ads with others — so the surface is multi-buyer while MiQ holds the privileged data feed.
s: Equativ press, 2026-05; Broadband TV News, 2026-05-27 & 2025-10-14; Advanced Television, 2025-10-14. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: Omdia (April 2026) forecasts the emerging independent OSes (VIDAA, Titan OS, TiVo) to rise from ~21% of the European TV-OS market in 2025 to ~28% by 2030 while Google TV falls from ~32% to ~26%; the named drivers (OEM revenue share, data control) reinforce rather than undermine data-licensing, and no LG/currency/holdco move to internalise the aggregation is visible.
s: VideoWeek, 2026-04-22; Broadband TV News, 2026-04-23 (reporting Omdia). Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: As of 13 March 2026 MiQ publicly described its partnership with Samba TV in the present tense as adding cross-screen TV insights to Sigma (India launch), and Samba was in the Sigma integration roster at the June 2025 platform launch.
s: Indian Television Dot Com, 'MiQ launches AI platform Sigma in India,' indiantelevision.com, 13 Mar 2026 (accessed 2026-06-20); MiQ/BusinessWire, 'MiQ Sigma Breaks the Fragmentation Cycle,' 4 Jun 2025.

claims.t: In December 2025 Samba TV secured a growth-capital facility of up to $60M from Horizon Technology Finance ($30M initial + $30M accordion); independent reporting put Samba as profitable with revenue growing 20-30% YoY, with CEO Ashwin Navin choosing debt as less dilutive/cheaper.
s: GlobeNewswire/Samba TV/Horizon, 8 Dec 2025; Axios, 'Exclusive: Samba TV raises up to $60M venture debt,' 8 Dec 2025; TV News Check, 8 Dec 2025.

claims.t: The 'Samba US handover' was the one-time Jan 2023 transfer of Samba's US managed-media-sales business to MiQ when Samba exited managed media to focus on data/measurement, a consummated business swap, not a renewable exclusivity, and it confers no exclusive claim on Samba's data.
s: Samba TV/GlobeNewswire, 'Samba TV and MiQ Reach Multi-year Commercial Agreement,' 13 Jan 2023; Deadline, Jan 2023; AdExchanger, 'A MiQ-Drop Moment For Samba Ad Sales,' 17 Jan 2023.

claims.t: Samba sells its TV data and measurement directly into multiple DSPs/platforms, bypassing managed-service intermediaries: exclusively in TTD's Planner since 2019, self-service in the Yahoo DSP, into Acxiom/IPG, and the Dec 2025 raise is explicitly to scale Samba as a cross-platform measurement partner to global DSPs, SSPs, TikTok and Snap.
s: TTD/Samba TV, 2 May 2019; Yahoo/Samba TV releases (AU/UK/CA); Samba TV/Acxiom, 11 Jun 2025; GlobeNewswire/Samba TV/Horizon, 8 Dec 2025.

claims.t: Samba's ACR is integrated at the chipset level across ~24 top smart-TV brands in 100+ countries on a 100% opt-in basis (Sony, Sharp, TCL, Philips, Toshiba named), and Samba is reinvesting (Semasio acquisition Oct 2024, agentic-AI roadmap, Dec 2025 capital); the Samsung/LG/Roku in-housing risk lands on Samba's coverage completeness, which MiQ inherits.
s: Samba TV press kit/business pages, samba.tv (accessed 2026-06-20); AdExchanger, 'Samba TV Acquires Semasio,' 31 Oct 2024; GlobeNewswire/Samba TV/Horizon, 8 Dec 2025.

claims.t: The ANA's Dec 2023 Programmatic Media Supply Chain Transparency Study, on log-level data covering ~$123M spend / ~35.5B impressions from 21 brands, found MFA took ~15% of spend and ~21% of impressions, campaigns averaged ~44,000 sites, and only ~36 cents per dollar reached working media.
s: ANA, Programmatic Media Supply Chain Transparency Study, Dec 2023; Marketing Dive 2023-06-19; accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: The ANA/TAG TrustNet first benchmark (June 2024) reported MFA spend across 11 brands fell from 15% to ~4% and site counts roughly halved (44,000 to 23,000), but DoubleVerify data showed MFA impressions rising ~19% YoY in 2023 — divergence rooted in the absence of an agreed MFA definition.
s: AdExchanger, 'The ANA Says Advertisers Are Spending Way Less On MFA,' 2024-06; accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: Adalytics exposed the hidden ad-stuffed Forbes www3 subdomain (May 2024) and, in a March 2024 report on Jan 2024 data, named DV360 (highest MFA volume), Amazon DSP, dozens of SSPs and the major verifiers as transacting/observing MFA, while The Trade Desk and Walmart DSP appeared clean and MiQ was not named.
s: Adalytics, 'Ads observed on made-for-advertising sites in January 2024'; Forbes www3 coverage The Drum/Digiday May 2024; accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: In a July 2023 OpenX case study, MiQ contributed its own MFA domain list which, paired with Jounce's, lifted excluded MFA domains 37% (~1,600 removed in one day), with under a third overlapping both lists; Lara Koenig (MiQ Global Head of Product) is quoted on inventory-quality assurance.
s: OpenX, 'How OpenX Increased MFA Domains Excluded in Direct Deals With MiQ by 37%,' 2023-07-24; Digiday 2023-07-19; accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: MiQ states it is TAG Certified Against Fraud, IAB Gold Standard, and JICWEBS/DTSG certified, but these cover fraud/IVT/brand-safety; no industry accreditation yet exists for supply-path transparency, working-media share, or take-rate disclosure (MRC's Jan 2026 auction-transparency standards only contemplate future MFA considerations).
s: MiQ 'Reducing Ad Fraud'/Brand Safety Policy, wearemiq.com; MRC Digital Advertising Auction Transparency Standards, Jan 2026; accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: MiQ does not publish its blended take rate (per corpus doc 07) and emphasizes dashboard-level (app/content-genre) reporting rather than raw client-owned log-level data with fee decomposition — leaving it exposed on the LLD-access and take-rate-disclosure demands the ANA/ISBA studies elevated.
s: Internal corpus doc 07; MiQ resources blog, wearemiq.com; ISBA/PwC summaries; accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: Through 2024–2026 the 4A's-convened group (ANA, IAB Tech Lab, BSI, Jounce, DeepSee — without DSPs/SSPs) has not agreed an MFA definition; the field shifted toward 'made-for-arbitrage' and competing lists diverge, evidenced by MiQ's and Jounce's lists overlapping on under a third of excluded domains.
s: AdExchanger, 'Inside The Secret Meetings To Define MFA,' 2024; Digiday MFA-definition coverage; accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: The Trade Desk's 2025 Sincera acquisition and OpenSincera launch (publishing publisher-level metrics — ads-to-content ratio, ads-in-view, refresh rate) reframe supply quality as a measurable platform-exposed feature, eroding the differentiation of a managed layer that curates MFA manually.
s: Digiday 'Curation can be a vacuous term,' 2025; TTD/BusinessWire OpenSincera, 2025-05-13; accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: Third-party workforce-data firm Revelio Labs places MiQ at ~1,900-1,950 employees, independently corroborating the corpus's ~1,900 figure; the lower '1,200 employees' figure is a stale May-2023 Marketecture snapshot, not a contradiction.
s: Revelio Labs, 'How many employees work at MiQ?', accessed 2026-06-20, https://www.reveliolabs.com/companies/miq/employees/ [Tier 5]; Marketecture, recorded May 2023, https://news.marketecture.tv/p/miq

claims.t: Digiday's independent reporting confirms MiQ revenue 'comfortably north of $600 million,' a ~$900M-$1B Bridgepoint (Sept 2022) valuation, and a ~5.9-6x exit multiple for prior backer ECI; 2021 revenue ~$465M / ~$45.4M profit.
s: Seb Joseph / Digiday, 'MiQ mulls M&A moves with new PE-backers,' 2022-09-13, https://digiday.com/media/miq-mulls-ma-moves-with-new-pe-backers/ [Tier 4-5]

claims.t: Public employee-review platforms put MiQ in a middling band: Glassdoor ~3.4/5 across ~528-537 reviews with only ~57-58% recommending the company; Indeed ~3.4/5 with management the weakest sub-score (~2.8).
s: Glassdoor, 'MiQ Reviews,' accessed 2026-06-20, https://www.glassdoor.com/Reviews/MiQ-Reviews-E719780.htm [Tier 7]; Indeed, https://www.indeed.com/cmp/Miq/reviews [Tier 7]

claims.t: The dominant negative review themes cluster on US senior-leadership style, opaque promotions/firings, and target-gated bonuses; there is little to no visible employee chatter blaming the Sigma/agentic pivot for attrition.
s: Glassdoor MiQ Reviews (Trader/leadership/commission review sets), accessed 2026-06-20 [Tier 7]; Indeed (management 2.8) [Tier 7]

claims.t: Documented restructurings are real but bounded and dated: a 2023 ~4% RIF with German-office closure; an anonymously-reported Bengaluru cut that dates to that same 2023 episode; and a Feb-2026 APAC leadership reorg with no reported headcount cut. None is a 2025-26 agentic-automation RIF.
s: Layoff trackers (Tech.co/Crunchbase/sunsethq) [Tier 5/7]; Grapevine anonymous post [Tier 7]; Mission Media, 2026-02-08, https://missionmedia.asia/miq-restructures-apac-leadership-replaces-regional-ceo

claims.t: MiQ does not appear as a rated vendor in the Forrester Wave (omnichannel DSPs, Q3 2023), Gartner Magic Quadrant/Peer Insights ad-tech coverage, or with a G2/TrustRadius review corpus for Sigma — so the outcomes/platform story has no third-party analyst validation layer.
s: Gartner Peer Insights 'Ad Tech Platforms,' accessed 2026-06-20, https://www.gartner.com/reviews/market/ad-tech-platforms [Tier 5]; Forrester Wave Omnichannel DSPs Q3 2023 (via secondary) [Tier 5]

claims.t: The one substantive independent caveat on Sigma comes from PPC Land (June 2026): the $2.22/$1 figure covers the EXISTING platform, not the new agentic Planning Agent, whose outputs' reliability 'remains to be tested at scale'; even AI-bullish buyers keep humans in the strategic loop.
s: Luis Rijo / PPC Land, 'MiQ upgrades Sigma a year in,' 2026-06-11, https://ppc.land/miq-upgrades-sigma-a-year-in-planning-agent-and-2-5pb-of-daily-data/ [Tier 5]; AdExchanger Sigma launch piece, 2025 [

claims.t: The independent-desk model sits in a contested structural position (in-housing + self-serve DSPs + spend concentration vs. continued transparency/skills demand), and no substantial body of candid, attributable buy-side testimony on MiQ specifically surfaced on Reddit, podcasts, or comment threads — the practitioner voice on MiQ is, in public, surprisingly quiet.
s: Digiday, 'The future of agency trading desks: Evolve or die,' https://digiday.com/marketing/future-agency-trading-desks-evolve-die/ [Tier 5]; MarTech/WFA on ATD transparency/in-housing [Tier 5]

claims.t: The 2013-era holdco trading desks were advertising's highest-margin businesses precisely because their arbitrage spread between purchase and resale price was hidden from clients (a 'black box').
s: Digiday, 'A History of Ad Tech Ch.3: The Holdcos Strike Back,' https://digiday.com/media-buying/a-history-of-ad-tech-chapter-3-the-holdcos-strike-back/ — Tier 5. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: The June 2016 ANA/K2 Intelligence report (rebates/non-transparency 'pervasive') and Pritchard's Jan 29 2017 IAB speech ('murky at best and fraudulent at worst,' ~25% of spend reaching consumers, all P&G contracts reviewed) converted scattered advertiser unease into an organized in-housing movement.
s: ANA, https://www.ana.net/content/show/id/pr-2016-rebates-other (Tier 1/2); CNBC, 2017-01-31, https://www.cnbc.com/2017/01/31/procter-gamble-chief-marketer-slams-crappy-media-supply-chain.html (Tier 3/

claims.t: The WFA's 2017 survey found 90% of large advertisers using agency trading desks were 'reviewing and resetting' contracts; only 51% still used legacy holdco desks, independent-desk adoption rose to 46% (+12pts vs 2014), in-house/hybrid exceeded 20%, and only 9% were comfortable with principal-trading conflicts (62% disagreed).
s: MarTech, 'WFA survey finds agency trading desks facing challenges,' 2017-01-30, https://martech.org/wfa-agency-trading-desks-transparency-independent-models/ — Tier 5. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: The holdco trading desks were not abolished but were forced to disclose (collapsing the arbitrage margin) and/or redistributed into agencies (Publicis dissolved VivaKi Feb 2015), so the category persisted in form while losing the high-margin spread that justified it.
s: Marketing Magazine (CA), 'Publicis ditches the agency trading desk,' Feb 2015, https://marketingmag.ca/tech/publicis-ditches-the-agency-trading-desk-138032/ — Tier 4/5. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: Programmatic in-housing penetration is high and durable but has plateaued into a hybrid equilibrium: IAB May 2018 = 65% full-or-partial (18% full); IAB/Accenture Aug 2020 = 69%; by mid-2020s the dominant and growing mode is hybrid (~25% fully in-house, with brand holding data/DSP contracts and specialists supplying bandwidth).
s: AdExchanger/IAB 2018, https://www.adexchanger.com/agencies/iab-agencies-fall-into-specialist-roles-as-more-brands-bring-programmatic-in-house/; Chief Marketer/IAB+Accenture 2020, https://chiefmarketer

claims.t: The IAB's own framing is that in-housing commoditizes the basic-media-buying layer but pushes agencies/specialists into surviving specialist roles (data science, advanced ad ops, proprietary capability), with recruitment/skills the binding constraint (~3/4 of advertisers cite it) and an 18-month in-housing timeline.
s: AdExchanger, 'IAB: Agencies Fall Into Specialist Roles,' https://www.adexchanger.com/agencies/iab-agencies-fall-into-specialist-roles-as-more-brands-bring-programmatic-in-house/; WARC, https://www.war

claims.t: The Trade Desk's Kokai/Koa (launched June 2023; ~2/3–3/4 of client spend migrated by mid-2025), Amazon's Ads Agent (unBoxed, Nov 11 2025), and Google's Ads Advisor (Nov 12 2025) all frame AI agents as letting buyers run campaigns directly, with the IAB Tech Lab's Agentic RTB Framework (Nov 13 2025) standardizing autonomous buying — compressing the need for a managed-service desk.
s: TTD press room, https://www.thetradedesk.com/press-room/the-trade-desk-launches-kokai-a-new-media-buying-platform...; PPC.land, https://ppc.land/amazon-launches-ai-agent-for-automated-campaign-managem

claims.t: Across ad-tech history the killing mechanism is commoditization of the intermediary's core skill, not in-housing per se: the DSP commoditized the ad network; disclosure commoditized the non-disclosed ATD; the independent-DSP rush ended in MediaMath's June 30 2023 Chapter 11 ($600M+ raised, once >$1B valued). Agentic buying is the next commoditizing wave, aimed at the trading craft MiQ sells as labor.
s: Marketing Dive, 'MediaMath's bankruptcy demonstrates difficulties of DSP model,' July 2023, https://www.marketingdive.com/news/mediamath-files-bankruptcy-dsp-programmatic/686006/ — Tier 4/5. Accessed

claims.t: MiQ's three holding defenses (disclosed/agnostic model, proprietary TV data, can't-in-house mid-market segment) are necessary but not sufficient; survival requires value to migrate from commoditizable human trading to a durable data/software layer licensed even after a client in-houses — a conversion that is unfinished, with the Dentsu 'Intelligence Partner' deal the leading positive tell and no confirmed holdco #2/#3.
s: Derived from corpus docs 05/06/07/10 + IAB specialist-role framing. Analytical inference. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: The base rate for MiQ's specific survival path (independent desk → licensed data-and-software layer) is low but non-zero, and the one reasonably clear survivor archetype is re-platforming into licensed software (Centro → Basis Technologies, rebranded 2022), against several failure archetypes (gutted holdco desks; bankrupt independent DSP).
s: Basis Technologies (formerly Centro) 2022 rebrand, trade coverage e.g. https://www.gourmetads.com/programmatic/basis-by-centro/ — Tier 5/6. Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: On May 14, 2025 Microsoft Advertising announced it would close its buy-side DSP — Microsoft Invest, the lineal descendant of Xandr and AppNexus — effective February 28, 2026.
s: AdExchanger, May 14 2025; Digiday, 'Microsoft Advertising is closing the Xandr DSP,' May 14 2025 (accessed 2026-06-20)

claims.t: Microsoft killed only the buy side, retained and continued investing in Monetize (SSP) and Curate, and steered buyers to a single AI-assisted Microsoft Advertising Platform rather than migrating demand to a third-party DSP.
s: Digiday, May 14 2025; bestmediainfo, 2026 (accessed 2026-06-20)

claims.t: The Canadian Bell DSP doc 03 calls an exclusive door is itself powered by Xandr's buy-side platform, launched 2021 as 'SAM DSP, powered by Xandr Invest,' so the Feb 28 2026 Invest shutdown directly implicates its underlying engine.
s: Bell Media / Newswire press release, Apr 28 2021; Media in Canada, Nov 2 2021 (accessed 2026-06-20)

claims.t: As of the June 2026 access date, MiQ's public Connected TV page still named 'Warner Media through Xandr' as a working agnostic-reach example — a present-tense claim describing a route closing Feb 28 2026.
s: MiQ, 'Connected TV | MiQ US,' wearemiq.com (accessed 2026-06-20)

claims.t: Trade analysis frames the Invest shutdown as accelerating buy-side consolidation around The Trade Desk, DV360, and Amazon DSP; the specific 'Amazon as Microsoft's preferred migration partner' claim is uncorroborated AI-content-farm material and is rejected.
s: Digiday Ad Tech Briefing, May 16 2025; bestmediainfo, 2026 (accessed 2026-06-20)

claims.t: Post-Xandr, MiQ's '7 platforms' should be restated as ~6 live named rails plus a Canada path being re-grounded; the count change does not undermine doc 03's aggregation-moat thesis, which already located the edge in workflow and data layering, not exclusive pipes.
s: Inference grounded in Claims 18.1-18.4 and doc 03 aggregation thesis; no external citation for the precise count

claims.t: As of April 2026, Pathlabs operates as a live, independently branded MiQ-owned company with William Lapointe still CEO and the MEP model still its core product.
s: Pathlabs blog (2026-04-27), homepage, newsroom — https://www.pathlabs.com/blog/2026-digiday-future-leader-awards ; https://www.pathlabs.com/ ; https://www.pathlabs.com/news . Accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: There is dated evidence Pathlabs is a growing, scaled unit — 188% growth onto Inc. 5000 two years running, with retrospective 50+ agency clients and $200M+ annual media spend — though Sigma cross-sell penetration into that book is not quantified.

s: Dentsu release (2025-06-12) https://www.dentsu.com/news-releases/dentsu-selects-miq-sigma-to-help-power-next-gen-media-operations ; MediaPost (2025-06-12) https://www.mediapost.com/publications/articl

claims.t: Dentsu's own digital head, James Banks, said on June 9, 2025 that Dentsu 'isn't using Sigma yet' — three days before the June 12, 2025 partnership announcement — and no dated source rebuts that status.

claims.t: MiQ runs a material but publicly undisclosed share of its managed-service media spend through The Trade Desk; no MiQ-through-TTD-vs-DV360-vs-Amazon percentage is verifiable from any public source.
s: Marketecture MiQ/Hundal profile; TTD resource-desk MiQ case studies, accessed 2026-06-20; doc 06.

claims.t: MiQ is not among TTD's named Certified Service Partners (Goodway, Mogl, MINT Square); its relationship is that of a large independent DSP-agnostic buyer, not a contractually tied reseller, which is its single best protection against repricing.

claims.t: TTD's minimum-spend floors and platform complexity make it uneconomic to service mid-market brands and small agencies directly, which is why it runs a reseller program at all — the structural basis for MiQ's seat at the table.
s: TTD Q4 2025 prepared remarks, 2026-02-25; TTD Certified Service Partners page; DSP buyer-guides (Improvado et al.), accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: TTD's Feb-2026 go-to-market reorganization explicitly increased direct advertiser relationships and eliminated agency-team overlap, but targets the largest brands and their holdco agencies — not the mid-market specialists MiQ aggregates.
s: The Trade Desk, Q4 2025 Earnings Call Prepared Remarks, 2026-02-25.

claims.t: OpenPath disintermediates the SSP/supply-side and the holdco SPO margin (positioned 'at cost'), not MiQ's buy-side managed service — an indirect threat that compresses one MiQ service line, not the business.
s: Digiday SPO/OpenPath pieces; AdExchanger 'Encroaching on SSP Turf'; B2B Stack, accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: TTD's Ventura CTV operating system competes with Roku/Amazon device OSes, not directly with MiQ's TV Intelligence panel, but moves TTD into the TV-signal layer — giving it a first-party CTV data source that MiQ today must license from Samba/Titan, widening the supplier-power gap on a 2027-2029 horizon.
s: AdExchanger 'Inside The Trade Desk's Pitch For Ventura TV OS'; Axios 2024-11-20; docs 09, 14, accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: Kokai (~100% client adoption) and Koa agents move decisioning into TTD's platform and threaten to commoditize the trading craft MiQ sells as labor, but as of mid-2026 Koa speeds setup, not autonomous buying — the same bounded state as MiQ's own agent.
s: TTD Q4 2025 prepared remarks; AdTech Radar/Digiday on Koa; The Current; docs 12, 17, accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: TTD's ~68% 2025 stock collapse and decelerating growth (Q1-2026 guide of just 10% vs 26% in 2024) create structural pressure to push direct and defend its ~20% take rate, both margin-eroding for intermediaries — but no reseller-specific repricing has been announced.
s: TTD Q4 2025 prepared remarks, 2026-02-25; Globe and Mail / collapse coverage, accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: The Feb-Mar 2026 conflict between TTD and three of five largest holdcos (Publicis 'can no longer recommend' TTD after a FirmDecisions fee audit; WPP and Dentsu pulled back from OpenPath) proves TTD will risk intermediary relationships, but vindicates MiQ's agnostic posture since redirected spend flows to DV360 that MiQ can ride.
s: Tradehouse Media TTD/Publicis fallout; B2B Stack 'Publicis Publicly Dumps Trade Desk' (citing AdWeek), accessed 2026-06-20.

claims.t: No public history of TTD restricting, repricing, or de-prioritizing managed-service intermediaries was found, and MiQ has no disclosed contractual or volume protection; its only demonstrated defense is the option to re-route (multi-DSP), not a right to stay on favorable terms.
s: Search of TTD partner terms, trade press, and MiQ materials, accessed 2026-06-20; no source attests either restriction or protection.

claims.t: The Great Awakening" is a retrospective, capitalized name asserting an intercolonial coherence that the strongest modern scholarship contests; contemporaries did not use the term and there was no comprehensive scholarly history between Joseph Tracy's 1842 book and the late twentieth century.
s: Jon Butler, 'Enthusiasm Described and Decried,' JAH 69:2 (1982): 305–325; Free Soil Review historiographical analysis (2017); accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Jon Butler argued in 1982 that 'the Great Awakening' is an interpretative fiction that distorts the extent, nature, and cohesion of the revivals, on four grounds: chronological unevenness (New England faded by ~1745, Virginia began in the 1750s), limited geography, overstated social effects ('tumult should not be confused with democracy'), and anachronistic naming.
s: Butler, JAH 69:2 (1982); HJ International Graduate School essay (2022); Free Soil Review (2017); accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Frank Lambert (1999) located the 'invention' of the Great Awakening not with later historians but in 1735–45, performed by the revival's own evangelical promoters — Edwards via 'A Faithful Narrative,' Whitefield via journals and newspapers — who used the new transatlantic print market to report local revivals in a way that produced the perception and reality of a single general, intercolonial outpouring.
s: Frank Lambert, Inventing the 'Great Awakening' (Princeton UP, 1999); Lambert, 'Pedlar in Divinity' (Princeton UP, 1994); accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Thomas Kidd (2007) concedes the conceptual problems with the singular label but argues a real and durable thing was produced — a new variation of Protestantism, evangelicalism, defined by the new birth, the Spirit's work in revival, and a radical notion of spiritual equality — resolving the debate by speaking of a 'long First Great Awakening.
s: Thomas S. Kidd, The Great Awakening (Yale UP, 2007); reviews in Journal of Religion 90:3, Church History; accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: The Half-Way Covenant, adopted by a New England synod in 1662, created partial church membership allowing baptized-but-unconverted adults who 'owned the covenant' to present their children for baptism while being barred from the Lord's Supper and church governance.
s: Britannica, 'Half-Way Covenant'; M.G. Hall & D. Hall, 'The Half-Way Covenant of 1662,' AAS Proceedings; accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Edmund Morgan's 'Visible Saints' (1963) argued the practice of requiring a relation of conversion experience for full church membership crystallized among non-separating Puritans in Massachusetts Bay in the 1630s, and named the expected staged sequence of conversion (knowledge, conviction, faith, combat, assurance) the 'morphology of conversion.
s: Edmund S. Morgan, Visible Saints (Cornell UP, 1963); accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Solomon Stoddard, Edwards's grandfather and Northampton's pastor from 1672, argued the Lord's Supper was itself a 'converting ordinance' to be opened to the unconverted ('Stoddardism'), loosening the gathered-church ideal and rehearsing the congregation for revival before his 1729 death.
s: Britannica, 'Half-Way Covenant'/Solomon Stoddard summaries; accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: The American revivals were the western front of a transatlantic awakening rooted in Continental Pietism — Spener's Pia Desideria (1675), Francke's Halle Foundations — which shaped Zinzendorf's Moravians (Herrnhut, 1720s) and the early Methodists (Wesley, Whitefield); W.R. Ward dated the evangelical movement back to the 1670s rather than the 1730s.
s: Encyclopedia of Greater Philadelphia, 'Pietism'; Hoselton intro (Penn State Press); W.R. Ward via these summaries; accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: An intense season of conversions broke out in Edwards's Northampton congregation in winter 1734–35; his account, 'A Faithful Narrative of the Surprising Work of God' (composed 1736, published London/Edinburgh 1737, soon translated), supplied a portable, replicable model of revival that promoters used to recognize and expect further awakenings.
s: Edwards, A Faithful Narrative (1737); Works of Jonathan Edwards Vol. 4 (Yale UP, ed. Goen); Lambert (1999); accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: George Whitefield's American preaching tour beginning late 1739 carried him from Georgia to New England, drawing large open-air crowds across denominational lines and igniting the New England phase of the revival in autumn 1740 through itinerant preaching that ignored parish boundaries.
s: Harry S. Stout, The Divine Dramatist (Eerdmans, 1991); Frank Lambert, Pedlar in Divinity (Princeton UP, 1994); accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Whitefield and his associates organized, advertised, and funded the revivals using emerging consumer-marketplace techniques — advance publicity, newspaper coverage, serialized journals, coordinated reporting of one town's awakening to spark the next — and the press did the essential work of creating an intercolonial evangelical identity.
s: Frank Lambert, Pedlar in Divinity (Princeton UP, 1994); Stout, Divine Dramatist (1991); accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Benjamin Franklin, testing Whitefield's audibility by walking down Market Street in 1739, estimated by acoustic computation that Whitefield could be heard by upward of thirty thousand people; modern acoustic reconstructions suggest a realistic maximum nearer 20,000 (up to ~50,000 only under ideal conditions).
s: Benjamin Franklin, Autobiography; Acoustical Society of America lay paper (Boren); The Gospel Coalition, 'Science of Sound'; accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: William Tennent Sr. founded the 'Log College' at Neshaminy, PA (~1727) to train revival-minded Presbyterian ministers; his son Gilbert Tennent preached 'The Danger of an Unconverted Ministry' at Nottingham in March 1740, comparing anti-revival clergy to Pharisees and authorizing congregants to judge their ministers' spiritual state — a proximate cause of the Presbyterian schism. Franklin printed and distributed it.
s: Gilbert Tennent, 'Danger of an Unconverted Ministry' (1740); Log College Press; Encyclopedia.com; accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: The mainstream revivalists were Calvinists (total depravity, unconditional election, regeneration as God's sovereign work) opposed to Arminianism (a real grace-assisted human capacity to accept or reject salvation); 'enthusiasm' was a pejorative naming claims to direct, immediate spiritual inspiration bypassing Scripture and reason. Edwards's Freedom of the Will (1754) is the rigorous Calvinist assault on the Arminian free will.
s: Jonathan Edwards, Freedom of the Will (1754); Gospel Coalition; EBSCO research starters; accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Charles Chauncy's 'Seasonable Thoughts on the State of Religion in New England' (1743) was the most systematic anti-revival treatise — a five-part attack on 'enthusiasm' as emotionalism, spiritual pride, and disorder, replying directly to Edwards's pro-revival 'Some Thoughts' (1742); Chauncy later moved toward a liberal theology that made him an ancestor of New England Unitarianism.
s: Charles Chauncy, Seasonable Thoughts (1743); Britannica; Encyclopedia.com; accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: James Davenport, an itinerant of extreme zeal, was arraigned in Connecticut in 1742 and judged to be under 'enthusiastical impressions and impulses' disturbing his rational faculties; in March 1743 at New London he led a notorious bonfire of religious books and luxury clothing (including his own breeches), then publicly recanted his excesses in 1744 — and became, for Old Lights, the emblem of the revival's dangers.
s: New England Historical Society; 'James Davenport's Post-Bonfire Ministry, 1743–1757,' The Historian 59:1 (1996); accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Edwards sought to save the revival from both critics and radicals: 'The Distinguishing Marks of a Work of the Spirit of God' (1741) argued bodily/emotional phenomena were in themselves neither proof nor disproof of a true work, and 'A Treatise Concerning Religious Affections' (1746, from 1742–43 sermons) made the genuineness of 'holy affections' depend on inner quality and fruit in a changed life, not intensity.
s: Edwards, Distinguishing Marks (1741), Religious Affections (1746); Marsden, Jonathan Edwards: A Life (Yale UP, 2003); accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Colonial Presbyterianism split in 1741 when the Synod of Philadelphia divided over ministerial education (Log College vs. the 1738 European/Harvard-Yale requirement), itinerancy across parishes, and the meaning of subscription to the Westminster Confession under the Adopting Act of 1729; the pro-revival New Side formed the Synod of New York (1745) and the two reunited in 1758 on terms vindicating the New Side revival method.
s: Orthodox Presbyterian Church, 'Old Side versus New Side, 1741'; This Day in Presbyterian History; accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Alan Heimert's 'Religion and the American Mind' (1966) argued, inverting Parrington, that evangelical Calvinism — not liberal rationalism — supplied the populist, quasi-democratic, nationalist energy behind the American Revolution, claiming the Revolution would have been 'improbable' without the Awakening; the thesis was initially attacked (incl. by Edmund Morgan in the William and Mary Quarterly, 1967) and remains contested rather than established.
s: Alan Heimert, Religion and the American Mind (Harvard UP, 1966); 'Revivals and Revolution,' Church History; accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Patricia Bonomi's 'Under the Cope of Heaven' (1986) argued colonial religious life was more vital and widespread across the eighteenth century than the older 'declension' narrative allowed, implying 'declension anxiety' is better read as a clergy-internal rhetorical/theological construct than a measurable collapse of religiosity.
s: Patricia U. Bonomi, Under the Cope of Heaven (Oxford UP, 1986; rev. 2003); accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Joseph Tracy's 'The Great Awakening: A History of the Revival of Religion in the Time of Edwards and Whitefield' (1842) effectively named the event roughly a century after the fact and created the interpretive framework later historians would defend or deconstruct.
s: Joseph Tracy, The Great Awakening (1842/1845), via Free Soil Review and Butler-historiography summaries; accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: The 1740s-1790s 'interval' between the Awakenings was not a religious vacuum but a period of continuous local revival and structural change; the apparent 'lull' is partly an artifact of the contested 'Awakening' category (Butler) and partly real war-driven institutional disruption.
s: Butler, Awash in a Sea of Faith (1990); Boles, The Great Revival 1787-1805 (1972)

claims.t: Finke and Stark estimate national religious adherence at roughly 17 percent in 1776 (~3,228 congregations, ~242,000 members) - a figure that is contested because the definition of 'active' membership is doing heavy lifting.
s: Finke & Stark, The Churching of America (1992); Hall, Law & Liberty

claims.t: Only about 27% of Anglican clergy in the colonies supported the Revolution (3 of 55 north of Pennsylvania); more than half relinquished their pulpits, leaving the largest pre-war establishment near collapse just as the religious market opened.
s: America250/AEI, 'Religion and the American Revolution

claims.t: Between Virginia (1786) and Massachusetts (1833) the states dismantled tax-supported religious establishments, replacing a coerced monopolistic order with the 'voluntary principle' - churches living on voluntary support and competing in an open market.
s: Witte & Latterell, SSRN; Encyclopedia Virginia; First Amendment Encyclopedia (MTSU)

claims.t: Jefferson's Virginia Statute for Establishing Religious Freedom (drafted 1777, enacted 1786, shepherded by Madison) disestablished the Church of England in Virginia and became the intellectual template for the First Amendment's religion clauses.
s: Encyclopedia Virginia, 'Virginia Statute (1786)

claims.t: The Finke-Stark 'religious economy' model reads the whole subsequent history through disestablishment: once the state stopped propping up a monopoly, energetic low-cost 'upstart sects' won and subsidized establishments lost - a descriptively strong but mechanistically contested claim.
s: Finke & Stark, The Churching of America (1992)

claims.t: The perceived religious nadir of the 1790s (deism, 'infidelity' at Yale) was a low ebb of institutional religion's cultural confidence and partly a mobilizing self-description retailed by the revivalists who then claimed credit for reversing it - not a literal absence of vital religion (Connecticut revivals had already begun by 1797-98).
s: Britannica, 'Lyman Beecher'; Yale History essays

claims.t: The decisive interpretive move of modern scholarship is to stop treating the Second Great Awakening as one phenomenon: it dissolves into at least three distinct theatres differing in geography, theology, emotional register, and method (frontier camp meeting, New England Edwardsian revival, Finney's urban revivalism).
s: Madison Historical Review (JMU); Curtis D. Johnson, Islands of Holiness (1989)

claims.t: The camp meeting as an institution grew from James McGready's Logan County, Kentucky revivals (Red River, June 1800; Gasper River, July 1800), modeled on the Scottish four-day communion season, where attendees spontaneously camped on the grounds.
s: Boles, The Great Revival (1972); restorationmovement.com

claims.t: The Cane Ridge communion (6-12 August 1801, Bourbon County, Kentucky) under Barton W. Stone became the largest and most famous camp meeting of the era, with roughly eighteen Presbyterian ministers preaching alongside Methodist and Baptist clergy.
s: Conkin, Cane Ridge: America's Pentecost (1990)

claims.t: Contemporary attendance estimates for Cane Ridge (August 1801) ran 10,000-20,000 (some accounts to 25,000); with roughly 20,000 distinct attendees over the week amounting to nearly one in ten (about 10%) of Kentucky's 1800 population, though logistics suggest no more than ~10,000 were present at any one moment (Conkin).
s: Conkin (1990); Encyclopedia of the Stone-Campbell Movement (2004)

claims.t: Cane Ridge was marked by involuntary bodily 'exercises' - the falling, jerks, dancing, running, barking, laughing, and singing exercises - catalogued by Barton Stone in his Autobiography; nothing comparable characterized New England's revivals.
s: Barton W. Stone, Autobiography (Tier 1, via Christian History Institute)

claims.t: New England's revival began before Cane Ridge and resembled Edwards far more than Finney: thirty Connecticut churches admitted ~1,699 members in 1798-1800, and the Yale revival of 1802 (about a third of ~230 students) was sober and intellectual, with no jerks or falling.
s: 9Marks, 'Forgotten, Real Revivals'; flagged single-source for exact figures

claims.t: Asahel Nettleton's deliberate, God-centered, Edwardsian revivalism was a genuine alternative to Finney's engineered revivalism; the two traditions clashed at the New Lebanon Conference (July 1827), which ended in a standoff after which Finney's measures prevailed and Nettleton's model receded.
s: Christian Communicators Worldwide on Nettleton (citing Sweeney, Hambrick-Stowe)

claims.t: Finney consolidated and publicized the 'new measures' - the anxious bench, protracted meetings, praying for individuals by name, women praying aloud in mixed assemblies, and rapid admission of converts - which the New Englanders attacked as a practical denial of original sin.
s: Christian History Institute, Finney biography; Finney, Lectures (1835)

claims.t: In his Lectures on Revivals of Religion (1834-35) Finney denied that revival is a miracle, calling it 'a purely philosophical result of the right use of the constituted means' - converting revival from a sovereign work of God into a reproducible technique, the birth of modern revivalism.
s: Finney, Lectures on Revivals of Religion (1835), Lecture I (Tier 1)

claims.t: Nathaniel W. Taylor's Concio ad Clerum (Yale chapel, 10 September 1828) relocated sin from a sinful nature to the sinner's own free voluntary act ('sin is in the sinning') and held that the sinner, though certain to sin, retains a real 'power to the contrary' - the theological permission slip for the new revivalism's urgent demand for immediate decision.
s: Taylor, Concio ad Clerum (1828, Tier 1); Nicholls, Marquette dissertation

claims.t: The single most consequential result of the arc was the inversion of the denominational order: by Finke-Stark's market-share reconstruction, Congregationalists fell from ~20.4% of adherents in 1776 to ~4% in 1850 while Methodists rose from ~2.5% to ~34.2% (the largest), with Baptists at ~20.5%.
s: Finke & Stark, The Churching of America (1992)

claims.t: Methodists grew from a tiny society of roughly 65 churches in 1776 to 13,302 congregations and more than 2.6 million members by 1850 - in Finke and Stark's compression, '1 in 40' religious Americans in 1776 to '1 in 3' in 1850.
s: Finke & Stark (1992) via Watson

claims.t: The Awakening's energy spilled into the 'benevolent empire' of voluntary reform societies (American Board of Commissioners for Foreign Missions 1812, American Bible Society 1816, American Sunday School Union 1824, American Tract Society 1825, plus temperance and antislavery), which gave middle-class evangelicals - and especially women barred from the pulpit - a vast field of public action.
s: American Yawp, 'Religion and Reform

claims.t: The slavery question split the two great upstart denominations along sectional lines on the eve of the Civil War: the Methodists divided in 1844 and the Baptists in 1845 (founding the Southern Baptist Convention), a schism sometimes read as a dress rehearsal for national disunion.
s: Andrews University Seminary Studies, 'Methodists, Baptists, and Slavery

claims.t: Richard Allen organized the African Methodist Episcopal Church as an independent denomination in 1816, becoming its first bishop, giving free Black Methodists a body of their own outside white control.
s: Britannica, 'Richard Allen

claims.t: The standard scholarly definition of evangelicalism is David Bebbington's four-mark 'quadrilateral' — conversionism, biblicism, activism, crucicentrism — articulated in his 1989 monograph, which dates the movement 'from the 1730s,' i.e., the Awakening decade.
s: The Gospel Coalition (Evangelical History) summary of Bebbington; David W. Bebbington, Evangelicalism in Modern Britain (1989). Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: The Awakenings normalized the revival as a repeatable institution, a form that outlived its Calvinist origins and runs continuously from the camp meeting through Finney's 'new measures' to the urban mass crusades of Moody, Torrey, Sunday, and Graham.
s: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Revivalism'; The Gospel Coalition, 'Why Dwight Moody Was Billy Graham's Key Predecessor.' Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Methodists rose from ~2.5% of religious adherents in 1776 to 34.2% in 1850 (the largest body), with Baptists second at 20.5%, displacing the colonial Congregationalist, Episcopalian, and Presbyterian establishments.
s: Finke & Stark, The Churching of America, 1776–2005 (Rutgers UP), as summarized via Google Books / Kevin M. Watson. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: The Southern Baptist Convention reported 12,722,266 members in its 2024 Annual Church Profile, a ~2% (−259,824) decline and its 18th consecutive year of membership decline, making it smaller than at any point since 1974, though baptisms (250,643) and attendance (~4.3M) rose; it remains the largest US Protestant denomination.
s: Lifeway Research, 'Southern Baptists' Membership Decline Continues Amid Other Areas of Growth,' 2025-04-30; Religion News Service, 2025-04-30.

claims.t: In the United Methodist Church's disaffiliation under Paragraph 2553 (window closing Dec 31, 2023), about 7,600 congregations - roughly 25% of U.S. congregations and ~24% of U.S. membership - left, overwhelmingly over LGBTQ+ inclusion.
s: Lewis Center for Church Leadership, 'Twenty-Five Percent of Churches Disaffiliated...,' 2024-01-16; Christianity Today, Dec 2023.

claims.t: At the 2024 General Conference (April–May 2024) the UMC voted by large margins to remove bans on ordaining 'self-avowed practicing' LGBTQ+ clergy and on clergy officiating same-sex marriages, and struck the 1972 'incompatible with Christian teaching' language, effective January 1, 2025, with conscience protections.
s: UM News, 'United Methodists remove same-sex wedding ban,' May 2024; WFDD/NPR, 2024-05-05.

claims.t: Per a November 2025 GCFA report (via UMC.org), the post-disaffiliation United Methodist Church reports roughly 11.3 million members worldwide, of which about 5.4 million are in the United States - the U.S. total now below the international (largely African) membership.
s: UMC.org, 'United Methodists At-A-Glance' (GCFA), figures as of November 2025. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Per Pew Research Center's 2023-24 Religious Landscape Study, the U.S. is 62% Christian and evangelical Protestants are 23% of U.S. adults (the largest Protestant tradition); the long Christian decline appears to have slowed or leveled off since ~2019.
s: Pew Research Center, '2023-24 Religious Landscape Study: Executive summary' and 'Decline of Christianity... May Have Leveled Off,' 2025-02-26.

claims.t: Pentecostalism's symbolic founding is the Azusa Street Revival in Los Angeles, led by African-American Holiness preacher William J. Seymour, beginning April 9, 1906; there are on the order of 644 million Pentecostal Christians worldwide in the mid-2020s (~8% of world population, ~26% of Christians).
s: ARDA, 'William Seymour and Azusa Street Revival'; Center for the Study of Global Christianity, 'Status of Global Christianity, 2025.' Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: The charismatic (neo-Pentecostal) movement spread Pentecostal practice into mainline Protestant churches beginning ~1960 (Episcopal priest Dennis Bennett, Van Nuys, April 3, 1960) and into the Roman Catholic Church from 1967, reaching tens of millions.
s: Hartford Institute for Religion Research, 'Charismatic Movement'; Episcopal Church glossary, 'Charismatic Renewal.' Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: A routine Asbury University chapel service in Hughes Auditorium on February 8, 2023, became a continuous student-led 'outpouring' lasting ~16 days, drawing an estimated 50,000–70,000 cumulative visitors (peak ~15,000/day) to Wilmore, Kentucky, and was interpreted within the inherited revival tradition by historians such as Michael McClymond.
s: Asbury University, 'The Outpouring Story of Revival'; Michael McClymond, 'What Revivals Can Teach Us,' Christianity Today, Feb 2023; Plough, 'The Asbury Outpouring.

claims.t: Joseph Smith's family settled in the revival-saturated 'Burned-over District' of western New York by ~1817, where he organized the LDS Church in 1830; at year-end 2024 the LDS Church reported worldwide membership of 17,509,781 across 31,676 congregations.
s: Deseret News, 'Latter-day Saint membership passed 17.5 million in 2024,' 2025-04-05; New York Heritage, 'The Burned-Over District.' Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Out of the Millerite movement and the 'Great Disappointment' of October 22, 1844, Seventh-day Adventism was organized (formally 1863); as of December 31, 2024 the SDA Church reported worldwide membership of 23,684,237, up ~899,000 over 2023, driven by the Global South.
s: EUD News / SDA Statistical Report 2024; Encyclopaedia Britannica on Millerites. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: The Restoration (Stone-Campbell) movement originated through Barton Stone (moved by the 1801 Cane Ridge revival) and the Campbells, who united in 1832 (growing from ~25,000 in 1832 to ~200,000 by 1861); it has since split into three streams (Disciples of Christ, Churches of Christ, Christian Churches/Churches of Christ) with combined adherents estimated at several million.
s: ARDA, 'Restoration Movement' timeline; 'An Overview of the Restoration Movement,' Word & Work. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: The Holiness movement radicalized the Wesleyan doctrine of entire sanctification ('second blessing') from the 1830s, producing the Church of the Nazarene (1908), the Wesleyan and Free Methodist Churches, and the Salvation Army, and was the direct theological parent of Pentecostalism.
s: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Holiness movement.' Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: The Awakenings' Baptist and Methodist surge drew enslaved and free Black people into evangelicalism in large numbers — Baptists winning the most converts due to congregational autonomy and lay preaching — producing a distinctive Afro-Christianity, the 'invisible institution' described by Albert Raboteau.
s: Albert J. Raboteau, Slave Religion: The 'Invisible Institution' in the Antebellum South (1978); Christianity Today, 'A Battle That Shaped Black Evangelicals,' 2025-05.

claims.t: Richard Allen, a formerly enslaved Methodist preacher, founded Mother Bethel AME (1794, after a segregated-seating walkout from St. George's in Philadelphia) and in 1816 led the formation of the African Methodist Episcopal Church — the first independent Black denomination in the US — becoming its first bishop; the AME today reports ~2.5–3.5M members across ~7,000 congregations.
s: EBSCO Research Starters, 'Founding of the AME Church'; BlackPast.org, 'Mother Bethel AME.' Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Historian Randall Balmer argues the Religious Right did not mobilize over Roe v. Wade (1973) but over the IRS threat to the tax-exempt status of segregated Christian schools, with abortion adopted later as a more respectable cause — a contested thesis he says Paul Weyrich effectively conceded.
s: Religion News Service, 'Randall Balmer on why racism, not abortion, birthed the religious right,' 2021-09-22; Randall Balmer, Bad Faith (2021).

claims.t: Kristin Kobes Du Mez's Jesus and John Wayne (2020) argues white evangelical support for Donald Trump fulfilled rather than betrayed a 75-year-cultivated culture of militant, patriarchal masculinity, reframing contemporary evangelicalism as a gendered cultural formation as much as a theological one.
s: Kristin Kobes Du Mez, Jesus and John Wayne (Liveright/Norton, 2020); W.W. Norton publisher page. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Nathan Hatch's The Democratization of American Christianity (1989) argues that early-republic common people seized religious initiative from elites across five movements (Christian/Restorationist, Methodist, Baptist, Black churches, Mormons), and that the resulting 'dialectic of decentralization and charisma' is the enduring source of American evangelicalism's strength — explaining why the present landscape is competitive, decentralized, and movement-generating.
s: Nathan O. Hatch, The Democratization of American Christianity (Yale University Press, 1989); Yale Books page. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: On the Great Awakenings the scholarly fault lines are unusually deep because the central object - whether there was a coherent 'Great Awakening' - is itself contested; six nested debates organize the field.
s: Butler (1982); Kidd (2007); Goff, Church History survey

claims.t: Jon Butler's 'Enthusiasm Described and Decried: The Great Awakening as Interpretative Fiction' (Journal of American History, 1982) is the field-defining skeptical intervention, arguing the unified 'Great Awakening' is a retrospective construction imposed on geographically patchy, chronologically diffuse revivals.

Eighteenth-century participants never called what they experienced 'the Great Awakening'; the capital-letter term is retrospective - a factual point now essentially conceded across the field, even by Butler's critics.
s: Journal of Unification Studies survey; Butler (1982)

claims.t: Frank Lambert's Inventing the 'Great Awakening' (1999) accepts that the event is a construction but relocates the inventing from nineteenth-century historians to the eighteenth-century revivalists themselves, who used commercial strategies and print media to promote a transatlantic 'great and general awakening' as it happened.
s: Lambert, Inventing the 'Great Awakening' (Princeton, 1999)

claims.t: The decisive analytical move is to separate two claims the polemics fuse: that the revivals happened (essentially undisputed) and that they formed a single coherent 'event' (genuinely disputed); once separated, a near-consensus emerges on the factual layer and the live dispute is interpretive.
s: Synthesis of Butler, Kidd, Lambert

claims.t: Thomas Kidd (The Great Awakening, 2007) grants the label is constructed but argues the revivals were 'great' because they produced the evangelical movement, reframing the phenomenon as a 'long Great Awakening' running transatlantically with the Second Awakening as an extension of the first.
s: Kidd, The Great Awakening (Yale, 2007)

claims.t: Harry Stout's The Divine Dramatist (1991) argues Whitefield's theatrically trained, media-savvy itinerancy created a genuinely new intercolonial form of mass religious communication ('Anglo-America's first religious celebrity'), supplying the mechanism by which diffuse local revivals could be perceived as one movement.
s: Stout, The Divine Dramatist (1991)

claims.t: The weight of recent evidence leans toward the chastened defenders: the unified label is a construction, and the phenomenon it labels is real and consequential; Butler raised the evidentiary bar and the field cleared it by defending a 'connected, transatlantic, productive movement' model rather than a naive 'single event.
s: Synthesis of Lambert, Stout, Noll, Kidd

claims.t: The Second Awakening's occurrence is undisputed; the contest is over causation, and the field has cycled through an older social-control thesis, Hatch's democratization thesis, and Johnson's market-revolution reading, plus a recent institutional/regional counter-thread.
s: Second Great Awakening historiographical surveys

claims.t: The older consensus read the revivals and the benevolent empire as instruments of social control - elites managing the disorder of a society in rapid transformation through internalized self-discipline rather than coercion (Foster, Cole, Cross, Timothy Smith).
s: Foster, An Errand of Mercy (1960); Cross (1950)

claims.t: Donald Mathews ('The Second Great Awakening as an Organizing Process,' 1969) reframed the Awakening as a vast exercise in voluntary institution-building that gave dispersed, mobile populations the churches and associations to cohere - explaining the Awakening's institutional output better than either social control or democratization.
s: Mathews, American Quarterly 21 (1969): 23-43

claims.t: Paul Johnson's A Shopkeeper's Millennium (1978) reads Finney's Rochester revival as a class phenomenon - a way for manufacturing proprietors to restore order to a workforce no longer disciplined by the dissolving household master-journeyman bond - giving the social-control tradition empirical density via membership records cross-tabulated by occupation.
s: Johnson, A Shopkeeper's Millennium (1978)

claims.t: Nathan Hatch's The Democratization of American Christianity (1989) displaced social control for a generation, arguing that ordinary people seized religious authority in a populist, anti-elite crisis of authority - the same revivals inverted, read as the masses taking power from below rather than elites managing from above.
s: Hatch, The Democratization of American Christianity (Yale, 1989)

claims.t: John Wigger's Taking Heaven by Storm (1998) extended Hatch with a deep study of Methodist growth - from fewer than 1,000 members in 1770 to over 250,000 by 1820 - explained by Methodism's openness to dreams, visions, and lay exhorters and its circumvention of conventions of education, standing, gender, and race.
s: Wigger, Taking Heaven by Storm (Oxford, 1998)

claims.t: The sharpest current critique holds that Hatch conflated popularization (leaders appealing to popular taste) with democratization (real expansion of lay institutional power): Methodism, the paradigm case, was governed by a highly centralized, episcopal, authoritarian connectional structure under Asbury - the appeal was popular, the power was not lay.
s: After Democratization?', The Junto (2013)

claims.t: A second post-Hatch correction targets the 'free market of religion' assumption: states continued to shape religious competition through incorporation laws, test oaths, tax assessments, and property regimes, so the 'voluntary marketplace' was a legal construction, not a state of nature.
s: The Junto (2013); Porterfield, Conceived in Doubt (2012)

claims.t: The evidence supports a layered synthesis rather than a single thesis: the market revolution supplies the structural conditions, democratization the cultural-rhetorical style, and institutionalization/region the necessary correction - with 'popularization' the honester term than 'democratization' for the institutional layer.
s: Synthesis of Hatch, Johnson, the Junto critics

claims.t: The textbook 'orderly Calvinist Edwards vs. emotional Arminian Finney' contrast is partly a caricature: an Edwardsian, orderly revivalism persisted through the Second Awakening, and the road from Edwards to Finney runs as a gradient through the New Divinity (Hopkins, Bellamy) and New Haven theology (Taylor), not a clean cliff.
s: Carwardine (1978); Modern Reformation; Kidd 'long Great Awakening

claims.t: Alan Heimert's Religion and the American Mind (1966) argued the Revolution's intellectual origins lie in evangelical Calvinism, not Enlightenment rationalism - inverting Parrington by casting the rationalist 'liberals' as the conservatives and the New Light Edwardsians as the radical, egalitarian, mobilizing energy.
s: Heimert, Religion and the American Mind (Harvard, 1966)

claims.t: Heimert's thesis was initially vilified (Morgan: asserted not demonstrated; Mead: method; Bailyn's secular republican ideology became dominant) then partially rehabilitated (Hatch's Sacred Cause of Liberty 1977, Stout's New England Soul 1986, Bonomi 1986) - the mature view rejects the strong causal form but recovers evangelical religion as one genuine tributary of the revolutionary stream.
s: Goff, 'Revivals and Revolution,' Church History

claims.t: On race the record is genuinely double-edged and both sides are established: evangelical revivalism was the principal vehicle of Black Christianization and the seedbed of an autonomous Black church tradition (Raboteau's Slave Religion; Frey & Wood), AND Southern white evangelicalism accommodated itself thoroughly to slavery and patriarchy (Heyrman's Southern Cross: 'the South changed Evangelicalism more than Evangelicalism changed the South').
s: Raboteau, Slave Religion (1978); Heyrman, Southern Cross (1997)

claims.t: Mark Noll's The Civil War as a Theological Crisis (2006) shows the proslavery side had the easier literalist biblical case - the Old Testament permitted slavery and the New did not explicitly condemn it - so abolitionists had to argue from a 'broader sweep'; the churches could not resolve it by exegesis, split, and then the nation went to war.
s: Noll, The Civil War as a Theological Crisis (UNC, 2006)

claims.t: Women demonstrably predominated among converts and members (established), but the 'feminization' interpretation (Welter, Douglas) is contested: Ann Braude's 'Women's History Is American Religious History' (1997) argues women were always the majority, so reading their predominance as a Victorian decline embeds a male-normative assumption, and Brekus recovered ~123 women preachers (1740-1845) the domestic frame omits.
s: Welter (1966); Douglas (1977); Braude (1997); Brekus (1998)

claims.t: Read together the six debates are variations on a single methodological problem - how much coherence the evidence licenses - and in each the strong thesis proves half right; the recurring villain is the inherited declension-and-awakening narrative, and the mature position is consistently a layered both/and, which is what the evidence supports.
s: Synthesis across the six debates

claims.t: W. R. Ward's The Protestant Evangelical Awakening (1992) reconstructs the eighteenth-century revival as a pan-European Protestant movement with deep roots in Central/Eastern European Pietism, of which the American Awakening is one provincial front rather than a self-contained colonial episode.
s: W. R. Ward, The Protestant Evangelical Awakening (Cambridge UP, 1992); publisher/review summaries accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Susan O'Brien's 1986 AHR article showed that participants in the American, English, and Scottish revivals of 1735-1755 perceived them as a single phenomenon, a perception produced and sustained by a transatlantic network of correspondence, revival magazines, and a shared book trade.
s: Susan O'Brien, AHR 91, no. 4 (Oct. 1986): 811-832, https://academic.oup.com/ahr/article-abstract/91/4/811/47430, accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: The 1742 Scottish revival at Cambuslang ('wark' = work), under William McCulloch and catalyzed by Whitefield's summer-1742 preaching, fused with the existing Scottish 'communion season,' a liturgical form that prefigures the later American camp meeting (Cane Ridge, 1801).
s: Secondary accounts of the Cambuslang revival accessed 2026-06-19; scholarly anchor Arthur Fawcett, The Cambuslang Revival (1971), cited not consulted.

claims.t: John Wesley met the Moravian Peter Bohler in February 1738 and recorded his Aldersgate 'heart strangely warmed' assurance on 24 May 1738; Moravian small-group ('class') models shaped Methodist organization, making American Methodism a downstream tributary of a German-Pietist/English-Methodist confluence.
s: Wesley, Journal, 24 May 1738; UMC.org and Wesley-scholarship summaries accessed 2026-06-19, https://www.umc.org/en/content/ask-the-umc-what-is-aldersgate-day

claims.t: David Bebbington's Evangelicalism in Modern Britain (1989) defines evangelicalism by a 'quadrilateral' of conversionism, biblicism, crucicentrism, and activism, and dates the emergence of this configuration to the 1730s, making 'the transatlantic Awakening' and 'the rise of evangelicalism' the same event seen twice, though the novelty-vs-continuity ('Bebbington thesis') claim is itself contested.
s: David Bebbington, Evangelicalism in Modern Britain (1989); multiple scholarly summaries accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: The 1857-58 'Businessmen's'/'Prayer Meeting' Revival began with Jeremiah Lanphier's noon prayer meeting at Manhattan's North Dutch (Fulton Street) church in autumn 1857 and was distinctively urban, lay-led, interdenominational, and organized around prayer rather than fiery preaching.
s: Christian History Institute and other reference summaries accessed 2026-06-19; Kathryn Teresa Long, The Revival of 1857-58 (Oxford UP, 1998).

claims.t: The 'Third Great Awakening' label, most often attached to the Social Gospel era (Walter Rauschenbusch, Christianity and the Social Crisis, 1907) and derived largely from McLoughlin's 1978 periodization, is genuinely disputed: many historians treat the Social Gospel as a movement rather than a unitary 'awakening,' and multiple events compete for the 'Third' slot.
s: Britannica, 'Walter Rauschenbusch'; McLoughlin, Revivals, Awakenings, and Reform (1978); summaries accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: William McLoughlin's Revivals, Awakenings, and Reform (1978) frames American history as a sequence of awakenings on roughly 80-100-year cycles, each a period of 'cultural revitalization' born in a crisis of belief and issuing in reform, drawing on anthropologist Anthony F. C. Wallace's 'revitalization movement' concept and later borrowed by Fogel.
s: McLoughlin, Revivals, Awakenings, and Reform (Univ. of Chicago Press, 1978); review summaries accessed 2026-06-19, https://press.uchicago.edu/ucp/books/book/chicago/R/bo33937066.html

claims.t: Robert Fogel's The Fourth Great Awakening and the Future of Egalitarianism (2000) borrows McLoughlin's periodization to argue American history is structured by awakenings linked to techno-economic change, locating a 'Fourth' from c. the 1960s focused on 'spiritual equity'; the thesis is among the most criticized applications of the awakening model.
s: Robert W. Fogel, The Fourth Great Awakening and the Future of Egalitarianism (2000); review summaries accessed 2026-06-19, https://press.uchicago.edu/ucp/books/book/chicago/F/bo3619006.html

claims.t: Jon Butler's 1982 article argued 'the Great Awakening' is largely a retrospective 'interpretive fiction' that exaggerated and falsely unified scattered colonial revivals, urging historians to drop the term; Frank Lambert's Inventing the 'Great Awakening' (1999) split the difference, casting it as both real and a press-driven 'early American culture war.
s: Jon Butler, JAH 69, no. 2 (1982): 305-325, https://academic.oup.com/jah/article-abstract/69/2/305/835716; Frank Lambert, Inventing the 'Great Awakening' (Princeton UP, 1999); accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Global Pentecostalism, descended through the nineteenth-century holiness movement and the 1906 Azusa Street revival from American revivalism, numbers roughly 600-644 million adherents (Gordon-Conwell CSGC: ~644M 'Spirit-Empowered' as of 2020, ~26% of all Christians; Pew-cited syntheses near 600M), making it the revival tradition's largest long-run descendant.
s: Gordon-Conwell CSGC, 'Global Pentecostalism,' https://www.gordonconwell.edu/center-for-global-christianity/research/global-pentecostalism/; Pew-cited syntheses; accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: Finke & Stark's The Churching of America (1992; updated to 2005) explains American religious vitality with a supply-side 'religious economy' model: churches as competing firms, deregulation/pluralism breeding vitality, and a church-sect cycle in which high-tension 'upstart sects' (Methodists, Baptists, later Pentecostals) are the long-run 'winners' and the accommodating mainline the 'losers.
s: Roger Finke & Rodney Stark, The Churching of America, 1776-2005 (Rutgers UP, 2005); summaries accessed 2026-06-19, https://www.rutgersuniversitypress.org/the-churching-of-america-1776-2005/97808135355

claims.t: Critics (notably Steve Bruce) argue the religious-economy model's core empirical claim fails under scrutiny: that religious pluralism more often correlates with decline than vitality, that deregulation does not reliably produce vitality, and that several celebrated positive pluralism-participation findings were statistical artifacts.
s: Steve Bruce (e.g., God Is Dead, 2002) and critics, via review/interview summaries accessed 2026-06-19, https://www.modernreformation.org/resources/interviews/the-decline-of-religion-q-a-with-steve-bru

claims.t: Voas & Chaves (American Journal of Sociology, 2016) argued, by focusing on trends rather than levels, that U.S. religiosity has been declining for decades via the same generational/cohort mechanism observed across the secularizing West, so the United States 'should no longer be considered a counterexample' to the secularization thesis.
s: David Voas & Mark Chaves, AJS 121, no. 5 (2016): 1517-1556, https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/abs/10.1086/684202; https://discovery.ucl.ac.uk/1476386/1/Voas_684202.pdf; accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: The doctrine of the New Birth — conversion as a radical, datable, experiential transformation of the affections — is intrinsically revivalist because it makes a reproducible inner event, not inherited status or sacrament, the unit of true religion, turning revival into a propagable method rather than an accident of grace.
s: Sweeney, Nathaniel Taylor, New Haven Theology, and the Legacy of Jonathan Edwards (OUP 2003), via DTS Voice review; Edwards primary texts referenced not read. Accessed 2026-06-19.

claims.t: New England theology drifted from Edwards's Calvinist determinism toward free will, culminating in Nathaniel W.
