claims.t: Containerization is a margin-RELOCATION event, not elimination: the DSP slice (~16% combined per ANA) compresses, the SSP-plus-intelligence slice grows (the SSP adds a compute-hosting line on top of its take), a new explicit buy-side-intelligence line appears, and the publisher is roughly flat-to-better — total intermediary take relocates from the DSP tier toward the SSP-plus-intelligence tier rather than collapsing.
s: Author synthesis from ANA Q3 2025 [5.7/5.8], Adalytics [5.11], ExchangeWire [5.13].

claims.t: The structural thesis is the unbundling of the DSP: historically a DSP bundled the bidder (its moat), supply access, and the commercial relationship; containerization pulls the bidder out as a portable container, so supply access migrates toward the SSP (it IS the supply), the bidder becomes substitutable, and the commercial relationship is up for grabs.
s: Author synthesis; counter-case in doc 05 §7.3.

claims.t: The U.S. political-broadcasting regime descends from §18 of the Radio Act of 1927 (which created the FRC and first imposed equal opportunities) and was carried into the Communications Act of 1934, which replaced the FRC with the FCC.
s: Equal-Time Rule, MTSU First Amendment Encyclopedia; FCC, 'The Public and Broadcasting' (accessed 2026-06-23).

claims.t: 47 U.S.C. §315(a) requires a station that lets one legally qualified candidate use it to afford equal opportunities to opposing candidates, and bars the licensee from censoring candidate ad material.
s: 47 U.S.C. §315(a), via Cornell Legal Information Institute (accessed 2026-06-23). https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/47/315

claims.t: 47 U.S.C. §312(a)(7) requires commercial broadcast stations to provide reasonable access for legally qualified federal candidates to buy time across all dayparts; it is a federal-candidate right not extended to state/local candidates.
s: FCC, 'Political Programming'; Davis Wright Tremaine, 'Broadcasters: The 2024 Election…', Apr. 2024.

claims.t: 47 U.S.C. §315(b) caps charges to candidates at the station's lowest unit charge for the same class/amount of time during the 45 days before a primary and 60 days before a general or special election; outside those windows, comparable-use rates apply.
s: 47 U.S.C. §315(b), via Cornell LII (accessed 2026-06-23).

claims.t: Broadcast stations (and to a lesser degree cable, DBS, SDARS) must publicly disclose every candidate time-purchase request and certain national-issue ad requests — sponsor, schedule, rate, class of time — retained two years and uploaded to the FCC's online public inspection file at publicfiles.fcc.gov.
s: FCC Public Inspection Files (publicfiles.fcc.gov); Pillsbury, Sept. 2022; Wiley, 'FCC Clarifies Political File Rules.

claims.t: 47 U.S.C. §317 and 47 CFR §73.1212 require broadcast stations to disclose who paid for political/controversial-issue programming and keep a public executive/board list; the FCC's stated goals are preventing viewer deception and protecting advertiser competition.
s: CRS Report R46516, Sept. 9, 2020; 47 CFR §73.1212 via Cornell LII.

claims.t: A Designated Market Area is a Nielsen-defined, non-overlapping geographic region where local stations command dominant viewing; there are 210 DMAs covering the continental U.S., Hawaii, and parts of Alaska, a concept dating to the 1950s.
s: Nielsen, 'Need to know: What is a DMA, and why does it matter?', 2025.

claims.t: U.S. pay-TV penetration peaked around 88% of households in 2010 and has fallen below 50% by 2026, with providers shedding on the order of 25 million subscribers over the decade-plus.
s: Statista, 'Cord-cutting in the United States'; cablecompare.com (2026); broadbandsearch.net.

claims.t: In May 2025 streaming reached 44.8% of total U.S. TV usage and for the first time eclipsed combined broadcast (20.1%) and cable (24.1%, =44.2%), per Nielsen's The Gauge.
s: Nielsen, 'Streaming Reaches Historic TV Milestone…', 2025.

claims.t: In 2008 the Obama campaign matched its national voter file (VoteBuilder/VAN) against online interactions, an email list of roughly 13 million, and Facebook friend-graph data — an early voter-file/digital-identity fusion. (Earlier '190M voters / 23M emails' figures were dropped as unsupported by the cited sources.)
s: Phys.org, Mar. 2018; MIT Technology Review, Aug. 22, 2018.

claims.t: Cambridge Analytica, working for the Trump campaign, harvested data on ~50M Facebook users via the 'This Is Your Digital Life' app and friend-graph permissions; the scandal broke in March 2018 and became the symbol of data-driven political targeting, though its actual effectiveness is contested and its methods differed from Obama-era data use.
s: Facebook–Cambridge Analytica scandal coverage; PolitiFact, Mar. 22, 2018; NPR, Mar. 25, 2018.

claims.t: Because internet-delivered 'connected TV' needs no spectrum license, the FCC's authority does not reach it, so sponsors of targeted political/issue ads delivered to connected TVs by non-licensee entities need not disclose their identities to viewers.
s: CRS Report R46516, 'Identifying TV Political and Issue Ad Sponsors in the Digital Age,' Sept. 9, 2020.

claims.t: CRS notes that over the prior decade both traditional and nontraditional sellers promoted 'targeted television advertising' to political/issue campaigns, and that closing the CTV disclosure gap would require Congress to extend disclosure laws to ad-tech entities not regulated by the FCC.
s: CRS Report R46516, Sept. 9, 2020.

claims.t: CTV's share of digital political spend rose ~19% (2020) to ~45% (2024), while its share of ALL political ad spend rose ~2.7% (2020) to ~13% (eMarketer) / ~13%→14% (AdImpact) in 2024 — both true because broadcast still dominates the whole pie.
s: eMarketer via MNTN, 2024; eMarketer via Marketing Brew/Basis, 2024; AdImpact Political Projection Report, June 2024.

claims.t: CTV was not a meaningful discrete political line item in 2016; SSP Telaria reported CTV at roughly 1% of political ad spend on its platform that year.
s: MediaPost, 'Connected TV Political Ad Spend Soars,' Nov. 7, 2018.

claims.t: In 2018 Telaria reported CTV at ~30% of political ad spend on its platform (peak 37% in September), up from ~1% in 2016. (A widely cited SpotX '+900%' figure belongs to the 2020 cycle — since April 2020 — not 2018, and was removed.)
s: MediaPost, Nov. 7, 2018; Borrell Associates 2018 forecast (via MediaPost).

claims.t: In 2020 CTV reached ~19% of digital political spend, and eMarketer's figures imply a ~$260M U.S. political CTV base (the level its 600%-to-2024 projection grows from).
s: eMarketer via MNTN, 2024; The Current, June 25, 2024.

claims.t: In 2020 the Biden campaign reserved a record ~$60M in digital media (within a ~$280M buy), centered on CTV but also covering YouTube, ESPN, streaming audio/podcasts, and online gaming — not a CTV-exclusive figure.
s: Trade reporting summaries, 2020 (single-source; flagged in document).

claims.t: In 2022 CTV political spend was roughly 5x the 2020 level (attributed to unnamed media buyers), with Kantar Media estimating ~$1.4 billion in CTV/OTT political spend for the cycle.
s: Marketing Brew, 'Political ad spending on connected TV is 5x what it was in 2020,' Oct. 6, 2022.

claims.t: 2024 political CTV spend was projected at ~$1.5–1.56B mid-cycle but came in at ~$2.3B actual (AdImpact final) — about 21% of the record ~$11.1B cycle and the second-largest medium after broadcast.
s: AdImpact Political Projection Report, June 2024; eMarketer via The Current, June 2024.

claims.t: In 2024 CTV accounted for approximately 45% of digital political ad spend, up from ~19% in 2020.
s: eMarketer via MNTN, '45% of Digital Political Ad Spend in 2024 Will Go to CTV,' 2024.

claims.t: eMarketer projected U.S. political CTV ad spend would grow ~600% from 2020 to 2024 (~$260M to ~$1.56B).
s: The Current, 'U.S. political CTV ad spend projected to grow by 600%,' June 25, 2024.

claims.t: 2024 was the most expensive political cycle on record: AdImpact projected $10.69B for the 2023–24 cycle (19% over the $9.02B 2019–20 cycle); eMarketer's broader accounting projected $12.32B.
s: AdImpact Political Projection Report, June 2024; eMarketer via The Current, 2024.

claims.t: AdImpact's June-2024 projection of the $10.69B cycle split as $5.35B broadcast (>50%), $1.93B cable, $1.51B CTV, $1.12B digital, $381M radio, $309M network cable, $102M satellite — and attributed CTV's growth to capturing a larger slice of an expanding pie rather than reallocation away from broadcast.
s: AdImpact Political Projection Report 2023–2024, data updated June 2024 (read directly).

claims.t: Automatic content recognition (ACR) is software in a smart TV that identifies on-screen content by capturing short audio/video clips, fingerprinting them, and matching against a reference library built by 'listening posts'; it transmits the fingerprint with IP address, device ID, and timestamp every few seconds.
s: AdExchanger, 'The Marketer's Guide To ACR Tech In Smart TVs,' June 26, 2019.

claims.t: Commercial smart-TV ACR traces to roughly 2011 (Flingo/Samba TV's video-ACR patents; Shazam extending audio fingerprinting to TV), with manufacturers integrating ACR through the 2010s.
s: ACR history via cited sources in Wikipedia ACR entry; Samba TV company history.

claims.t: As of 2019, AdExchanger tallied opted-in/in-market ACR footprints of roughly Samsung Ads ~33M sets, Nielsen/Gracenote ~18.9M, Alphonso ~15M, Samba TV ~14.4M, Inscape/Vizio ~11.2M, and Roku ~10M+.
s: AdExchanger, June 26, 2019.

claims.t: On Feb. 6, 2017, Vizio agreed to pay $2.2M to settle FTC and New Jersey charges that its default-on ACR software (installed from Feb. 2014) collected viewing histories from ~11 million smart TVs second-by-second (>100 billion data points/day) without consent and shared them with third parties alongside IP/MAC/Wi-Fi data.
s: FTC press release, Feb. 6, 2017 (FTC URL 403; relied on law-firm summaries quoting the order).

claims.t: The Vizio order treated television viewing history as sensitive information requiring clear notice and affirmative opt-in consent, requiring Vizio to obtain 'affirmative express consent' for ACR collection/sharing — the consent footing on which all subsequent smart-TV ACR ad businesses operate.
s: WilmerHale, 2017; FTC, Feb. 6, 2017.

claims.t: Catalist, a large progressive data utility now covering the entire U.S. adult population (240M+), was founded in 2006 by former Clinton staffers, while NGP VAN became the DNC's national voter-data vendor under Howard Dean and remains the backbone tool across Democratic presidential campaigns.
s: Overture Global, 'The Secret Power of Political Data Trusts'; Catalist via Reach; NGP VAN.

claims.t: On the Republican side, the RNC's Data Trust and the Koch network's i360 built parallel voter-data infrastructure, with i360 explicitly aiming to become 'the NGP VAN of the right.
s: Overture Global; Medium/Political Moneyball, 'The Fight Over Political Data: RNC vs. i360.

claims.t: A layer of commercial voter-data firms (L2, TargetSmart, Aristotle, alongside Catalist and i360) productized the voter file as a matchable, licensable dataset usable by ad-tech and measurement firms — the precondition for fusing voter data with TV.
s: Overture Global; Comscore–L2 press releases, 2017/2022; voter-file vendor materials.

claims.t: The November 2017 Comscore–L2 partnership productized a national-voter-file-to-TV-measurement fusion — an early example, not the first (Rentrak/i360 2014, Rentrak/Targeted Victory 2014, and Nielsen/Sinclair 2015 predate it).
s: Comscore press release, Nov. 9, 2017.

claims.t: Comscore's 2017 release described L2's database as 265M+ adult consumer records and claimed L2's clients included 'almost every presidential candidate during the 2016 cycle' plus PACs and ~200 members of Congress.
s: Comscore press release, Nov. 9, 2017 (company claim).

claims.t: In January 2022 Comscore and L2 launched 'Comscore Predictive Audiences' — cookie-free voter segments crosswalking L2 voter profiles (party, turnout likelihood, issue stances) to privacy-friendly contextual signals, positioned for the midterm and post-cookie environment.
s: Comscore press release, Jan. 13, 2022 (company claim).

claims.t: The independent record of what political ads aired runs through CMAG (now Vivvix/CMAG, formerly Kantar Media/CMAG) and the Wesleyan Media Project, founded 2010 as successor to the Wisconsin Advertising Project (1998–2008), led by Fowler, Franz, and Ridout.
s: Wesleyan Media Project — About / Project Background / Data Access (2024–2025).

claims.t: Roku launched a public political ad archive in September 2020 disclosing payer, campaign IDs, and creative, commits to public disclosure of campaign details for at least seven years, and as of March 12, 2024 permits verified political advertisers to run ads via Roku Ads Manager subject to identity verification.
s: Roku Political Advertising Guidelines; Roku Self Serve Help Center 'Political ads,' 2024.

claims.t: A September 2020 Mozilla Foundation review called streaming political-ad transparency a 'Wild West'; CTV's 'public file' is a patchwork of voluntary platform archives of uneven completeness. (Date corrected from 2024 to 2020.)
s: Mozilla Foundation, 'Streaming Platforms are a Wild West of Political Ads,' 2024 (advocacy).

claims.t: Automatic content recognition (ACR) is software in a smart TV that takes rapid screen snapshots (Roku ~twice/second; ~7,200 samples/hour) and matches them against a content database to log what a household watches across cable, streaming, consoles, and antenna.
s: Roku Advertising 'A Guide to ACR' (vendor doc, accessed 2026-06-23); Lobato, Media International Australia/SAGE 2025

claims.t: Device/OS-level ('glass-level') ACR sees all content on the panel regardless of source, whereas app-level data only covers a single streaming app's own logged-in users — a distinction central to ACR's value for finding linear-only voters.
s: Samsung Ads and LG Ad Solutions vendor docs (accessed 2026-06-23)

claims.t: Roku, the #1 U.S. TV OS, surpassed 100 million global streaming households (announced April 2026) and is the subject of a pending $22B Fox acquisition announced June 15, 2026 that had NOT closed as of June 23, 2026 (expected to close 1H 2027; Roku to operate standalone).
s: Roku Newsroom Apr 2026; CNBC 2026-06-15; Fox Corporation press release 2026-06-15

claims.t: Vizio's Inscape ACR data business is owned by Walmart, which completed its ~$2.3B acquisition of Vizio on December 3, 2024; Vizio's SmartCast OS had 19M+ active accounts.
s: Vizio Form 8-K FY2024 (SEC EDGAR); AdExchanger; Lowpass (accessed 2026-06-23)

claims.t: LG Ad Solutions (a4/Alphonso heritage) claims ~200M LG smart TVs globally with a deterministic ACR feed from ~33M opted-in TVs; Samsung Ads draws ACR from 77M active Samsung smart TVs with up to 16 months of viewing history.
s: ppc.land on LG/Databricks; Samsung Ads vendor docs; apprupt 2025-26 (accessed 2026-06-23)

claims.t: A voter file has three strata of differing certainty: the public registration record and public vote history (government fact) and appended commercial data plus modeled scores for partisanship/turnout/issues (probabilistic estimates).
s: Pew Research Center 'Political data in voter files' 2018; L2/TargetSmart/i360 vendor docs

claims.t: L2, a non-partisan commercial voter-file vendor, reports a continuously-updated file of 200M+ registered voters, 2.3 billion vote-history records, and 250M+ consumer records, updated approximately semi-annually.
s: L2 Data (l2-data.com); university library guides (accessed 2026-06-23)

claims.t: The two parties run parallel sealed data ecosystems: the Republican GOP Data Trust (300M+ individuals, 2,500+ data points, 5,000+ campaigns in 2024) exchanging data with Koch-backed i360 since 2014; the Democratic side using NGP VAN, the progressive-only Catalist, and the Democratic Data Exchange (DDx) co-op.
s: Overture Global / Digital Public 'The Secret Power of Political Data Trusts'; i360 and Catalist vendor docs

claims.t: Pew Research's audit of five commercial voter files found modeled party affiliation matched self-reported party for about two-thirds of people on average (67%; range 76% to 59%), better for Democrats than Republicans, and better for party/race than education/income.
s: Pew Research Center, 'Commercial Voter Files' study and methods report, 2018-02-15

claims.t: The match layer resolves a voter's PII to reachable devices via onboarding to LiveRamp's RampID (a persistent pseudonymous person/household ID), hashed email (HEM) matching, mobile ad IDs (MAIDs), and IP-to-household graphs, with AbiliTec-style householding grouping people seen cohabiting over time.
s: LiveRamp identity/clean-room documentation (docs.liveramp.com, accessed 2026-06-23)

claims.t: Experian's Digital Graph links cookies, MAIDs, CTV IDs, UID2, ID5 IDs, and IP addresses to households/individuals and reports a graph of 126M U.S. households, 250M individuals, and 4B+ active digital IDs; a DSP case study claimed an 84% synced-ID rate.
s: Experian Digital Graph / data marketplace materials (accessed 2026-06-23)

claims.t: A data clean room is a secure neutral environment where a campaign's voter audience and a publisher's viewer data are matched on common keys (RampID/HEM/IP) to return only the overlap or pseudonymized targetable IDs, without either party seeing the other's raw records.
s: LiveRamp Clean Room docs; digitalapplied/AWS/Snowflake clean-room materials (accessed 2026-06-23)

claims.t: The clean-room vendor field consolidated in 2024–25: LiveRamp acquired Habu in 2024 and WPP/GroupM acquired InfoSum in April 2025, reducing the number of independent neutral matching venues.
s: digitalapplied 'Data Clean Rooms in 2026'; LiveRamp blog (accessed 2026-06-23)

claims.t: Vendors and trade sources put CTV voter-file household match rates at 50–70% for clean name/address files, 70–80% for email-based matching, and 85–90%+ with multiple keys on fresh files; DSPolitical claims 90%+ via multiple onboarders — all vendor/trade claims with no independent audit.
s: adwave 2026 onboarding guides; DSPolitical; Experian case study (accessed 2026-06-23)

claims.t: In January 2022 Comscore and L2 launched cookie-free political audiences combining L2 voter data with Comscore's Predictive Audiences methodology, offering 100+ issue/behavior segments across digital/mobile/CTV in leading DSPs; current 2026 status as a distinct product is unconfirmed.
s: Comscore-L2 press release 2022-01-13; Proximic by Comscore product pages (accessed 2026-06-23)

claims.t: On March 5, 2026 Comscore and Yahoo DSP launched Proximic Political Audiences for the 2026 cycle, combining Comscore's MRC-accredited linear measurement across 210 markets with Yahoo ConnectID (232M logged-in U.S. users), operating at DMA/district level and deduplicating linear vs CTV exposure for incremental reach.
s: ppc.land 2026-03; Advanced Television 2026-03-06 (accessed 2026-06-23)

claims.t: Madhive launched a local CTV political marketplace (Feb 27, 2024) across 400+ congressional districts and all 210 DMAs, with a political data layer drawing on Data Trust, TargetSmart, Experian, and L2 (corrected from a mis-listed 'Tunnl').
s: Adweek 2024-02; ppc.land on Gray Media/Madhive (accessed 2026-06-23)

claims.t: The political measurement back-end matches ad-exposure logs back to the voter file (in a clean room, on RampID/IP/HEM keys) to compare exposed vs unexposed turnout; this is correlational unless a randomized holdout is used, so vendor 'lift' claims often overstate causality.
s: Next TV on TVSquared/AdImpact; adwave guides; Experian CTV-political blog (accessed 2026-06-23)

claims.t: End-to-end addressability is a chain of joins whose key migrates from name+address to RampID/HEM/IP to a DSP segment ID and back to turnout; each join loses people (match rates) and imports error (modeled scores), so the system is household-level, partially-matched, partially-modeled — not true voter-level precision.
s: Synthesis of Pew 2018, LiveRamp/Experian docs, and trade match-rate figures (accessed 2026-06-23)

claims.t: The largest-reach CTV platforms (Amazon Prime Video, Netflix, Disney+, Apple TV) refuse political advertising while Roku, Hulu, YouTube/YouTube TV, Peacock, Paramount+/Pluto, Tubi, Samsung, LG, and Vizio accept it, concentrating spend onto accepting platforms and lifting their CPMs.
s: Campaigns & Elections, 'The Streaming Services on Political Advertisers' Wishlists,' 2024–2026; Amazon Ads prohibited content policy; accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: Hulu reversed its political-issue-ad rejection in July 2022 and now accepts candidate and issue ads aligned to Disney's policy, while Disney+ continues to refuse political ads.
s: Hollywood Reporter / NPR / IndieWire, July 2022; accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: Roku is sunsetting its owned DSP OneView (relaunched from DataXu in 2020) and shifting to a third-party-DSP strategy via Roku Exchange (Magnite-powered) plus self-serve Roku Ads Manager (Sept 2024, $500 minimum) and a Roku Ads API (Nov 2025).
s: Digiday, AdExchanger, AdTechRadar 2024; The Desk Nov 2025; accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: Roku accepts U.S. political advertising and maintains a public political ad archive (launched Sept 2020) disclosing payer, campaign IDs, and creative — but not spend, targeting detail, or impressions in researcher-accessible bulk.
s: Roku Advertising; Mozilla Foundation, 2020–2025; accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: The smart-TV ACR vendors central to political CTV targeting are LG Ad Solutions (former Alphonso, LG-majority since Dec 2020), Vizio's Inscape (Walmart-owned), and Samsung Ads, each licensing glass-level viewing data for targeting and exposure measurement.
s: AdExchanger, Korea Times, TechCrunch, Walmart corporate, Samsung Ads; accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: Walmart completed its $2.3B acquisition of Vizio on December 3, 2024 ($11.50/share, NYSE delist), making Vizio and its Inscape ACR unit a wholly owned Walmart subsidiary; Vizio Ads now blends Inscape ACR with Walmart retail-purchase data.
s: Walmart Corporate / TechCrunch / Talk Business, Dec 3 2024; accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: YouTube and YouTube TV together command ~12.5% of U.S. TV viewing (Nielsen, January 2026), exceeding any single broadcast network, making Google a structurally large political CTV inventory owner.
s: Basis Technologies, 'How Political Advertising Will Impact the Media Landscape in 2026,' citing Nielsen Jan 2026; accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: The Trade Desk is the largest independent DSP and deepest non-walled-garden CTV pipe; for 2024 it integrated Comscore/Proximic's voter-based and TV-ad-exposure political audiences exclusively, and marketed CTV as reaching households '36% more efficiently' than linear.
s: Comscore/Proximic Oct 2023; The Drum; The Trade Desk 2024; accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: Madhive is the leading political/local CTV specialist, trusted by major U.S. broadcasters covering all 210 DMAs; in Feb 2024 it launched a Local CTV Marketplace for political advertising spanning 400+ congressional districts, with Fox Television Stations as first-to-market client.
s: Adweek, Next TV, Madhive, Feb 2024; accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: The broader political CTV DSP/specialist field includes Viant (Household ID), MNTN (performance CTV, cited ~45% of digital political to CTV = ~$1.5B in 2024), Basis Technologies, Yahoo DSP, Cross Screen Media, and Tuesday Digital.
s: Viant, MNTN, Cross Screen Media, Tuesday Digital, 2024–2026; accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: Basis Technologies and LG Ad Solutions announced an exclusive U.S. political-CTV activation partnership on Nov 7, 2023, scoped through the end of 2024, granting Basis sole access to LG's ACR data (35M U.S. LG TVs) and voter files via Magnite — an exclusivity that, by its own terms, expired and should not be presumed current.
s: Basis / GlobeNewswire, Nov 7 2023; accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: The U.S. political voter-data market is partisan-segmented: i360 is Koch-funded and Republican-aligned; TargetSmart and Catalist are Democratic/progressive-aligned; L2 and Aristotle sell across the aisle.
s: i360, Catalist, TargetSmart, Overture Global, 2006–2026; accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: Comscore built cookie-free political audiences combining L2 voter insights with its Predictive Audiences method (Jan 2022, 100+ segments), then built a parallel progressive-only product with TargetSmart (Feb 2024), mirroring the partisan split into the audience-segment layer.
s: Comscore / PRNewswire, Jan 2022 and Feb 2024; accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: Commercial identity providers LiveRamp, Experian, and TransUnion supply the household-matching rails connecting voter files to CTV impressions; Experian is integrated directly into Samsung DSP (Dec 2023, expanded Feb 11 2026) at a ~95% match rate.
s: Experian / StreamTV Insider / NextTV, 2023–2026; accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: The TV measurement-currency market is contested: Nielsen's incumbency is challenged by Comscore, iSpot, and VideoAmp, all three JIC-certified (Comscore/VideoAmp Apr 2024, iSpot Aug) and re-certified ahead of the 2025–26 season; Comscore won MRC local+national accreditation while Nielsen held national-only.
s: Variety 2025; AdExchanger / Marketing Dive 2024–2025; accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: Political-spend tracking is dominated by four houses with different methods/totals: AdImpact (cycle projections, $11.6B for 2026), Borrell (local-ad forecasts), Kantar/CMAG (ad-occurrence/content), and the academic Wesleyan Media Project (content/tone).
s: AdImpact, Borrell (via Barrett Media), 2026; Wesleyan/CMAG referenced; accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: Political media buying is highly concentrated; Waterfront Strategies (GMMB-affiliated, Democratic) received ~$858M in 2024 — more than double the next-highest vendor — with Future Forward alone paying it ~$383M; the top-5 political vendors collectively took ~$2.1B in 2024.
s: OpenSecrets, Feb 2026; Sludge, Nov 2024; accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: Republican 2024 political ad spend was distributed across roughly ten vendors each receiving over $100M, versus a Democratic market centralized in Waterfront Strategies — an organizational asymmetry in how each party's money flows to media buyers.
s: OpenSecrets, Feb 2026; accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: Political media-buying agencies historically capture roughly a 15% commission on gross ad placements — the single largest and oldest take in the value chain — though the exact rate varies by firm/contract and is not uniformly disclosed.
s: Industry convention (broadcast-era media commission); not independently sourced in this pass; accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: Political CTV CPMs in 2026 run roughly $18–80 by tier — premium streamers (Hulu/Peacock/Paramount+) $35–80, mid-tier (Roku/Samsung) $25–45, FAST (Tubi/Pluto) $18–28 — with programmatic political CPMs spiking 40%+ above cycle average in the final weeks of 2024.
s: Turn It Blue Digital 2026; Basis Technologies 2024; accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: In swing states (Georgia, Pennsylvania, Arizona) CTV CPMs rose ~8% year-over-year in the 2024 season and inventory tightened, because political money concentrates geographically (13 states = 67% of 2024 cycle spend) and temporally (51% of spend in the final eight weeks).
s: MarTech 2024; TV Tech / AdImpact 2024; accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: The best peer-reviewed estimate of the effect of campaign contact and advertising on Americans' candidate choices in general elections is zero, per a meta-analysis of 40 field experiments plus 9 originals (49 total).
s: Kalla & Broockman, 'The Minimal Persuasive Effects of Campaign Contact in General Elections,' APSR 112(1), 2018, cambridge.org, accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Across 49 ads in 59 real-time randomized experiments on 34,000 subjects, political ads moved candidate favorability by only 0.05 points on a 5-point scale (small but significant) and moved vote intention by a statistically insignificant 0.007 of a percentage point.
s: Coppock, Hill & Vavreck, Science Advances 6(36), 2020, science.org; figures via Yale News 2020-09-02, accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: A ZIP-code-randomized Facebook/Instagram field experiment during the 2018 Florida midterms (1.1M+ impressions) found an effect on Democratic precinct-level vote share of −0.04 percentage points (SE 0.85) — indistinguishable from zero; CTV is digital video and inherits this evidence base.
s: Coppock, Green & Porter, 'Does digital advertising affect vote choice?' Research & Politics 9(1), 2022, sagepub, accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: A Comscore/Trade Desk case study (image-dated OCT2024) claims a political campaign 'reached households on CTV 36% more efficiently than linear TV' by using Proximic linear-exposure data to suppress already-reached households — a reach/frequency-efficiency metric, not a vote outcome.
s: Comscore, 'Reach Incremental Voters More Efficiently...' (Comscore/Trade Desk case study, OCT2024), comscore.com, accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: A FlexPoint case study for the Congressional Leadership Fund (super PAC) in the Miller-Meeks IA-01 race claims FlexPoint extended digital reach by 23%, with Comscore Campaign Ratings validating that 99% of voters reached via online video/CTV were unique (no linear overlap).
s: The Trade Desk, 'FlexPoint Political Advertising CTV Case Study' (CLF / Miller-Meeks IA-01), thetradedesk.com, accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: TV advertising's per-airing effect is 2-4× larger in gubernatorial, U.S. House and U.S. Senate races, and 10-19× larger in other statewide races (e.g., treasurer, attorney general), than in presidential contests, because ads inform voters in low-information races.
s: Sides, Vavreck & Warshaw, 'The Effect of Television Advertising in United States Elections,' APSR 116(2), May 2022, cambridge.org, accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Where TV ad persuasion is real it is fleeting: a $2M randomized 2006 Texas-governor experiment found a ~4.7pp current-week swing that collapsed to ~−0.17pp the next week; the persuasion half-life is ~1-2 days in subnational races, with some presidential effect lasting ~6 weeks.
s: Gerber et al., APSR 105(1), 2011, isps.yale.edu/research/data/d032; Hill et al., Political Communication 30(4), 2013, tandfonline.com, accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Analysis of campaigns' own archive of 146 experiments (617 ads, 51 campaigns, 500,000+ respondents) finds small-but-meaningful variation in ad persuasiveness, but common theories predict which ads work poorly, and the benefit accrues mainly to well-financed campaigns that can afford experimentation.
s: Hewitt et al., 'How Experiments Help Campaigns Persuade Voters,' APSR 118(4), 2024, isps.yale.edu, accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: A Digiday sponsored post (by PebblePost's CRO, a competing-channel vendor) argues ad-tech has a 'structural bias toward overclaiming results' and that CTV measurement 'characterizes exposure' rather than outcomes — vendor-sponsored content, not neutral trade press (re-attributed from a misidentified AdExchanger article).
s: AdExchanger, 'Why Today's CTV Attribution Models Fall Short'; Digiday, CTV incrementality coverage, accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: As of mid-2026 there is no peer-reviewed, publicly available randomized experiment demonstrating that the CTV format causes more persuasion or more turnout than linear or other digital video; all CTV-specific 'effectiveness' numbers are proprietary case studies measuring reach.
s: Author synthesis across Coppock-Green-Porter 2022, Broockman-Green 2014, and located CTV vendor case studies, as of 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Voter mobilization (GOTV) is a separate, better-evidenced problem than persuasion: across hundreds of randomized experiments, door-to-door canvassing produces the largest turnout effects, generic GOTV mail lifts turnout by slightly under 1 percentage point, phone calls are weak, and effects attenuate ~33-76% in high-salience elections.
s: Green & Gerber, Get Out the Vote (Brookings, eds. through 2019); Electoral Studies meta-analysis 2023, sciencedirect.com, accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Addressability makes CTV well-suited to mobilizing a known turnout universe and to fundraising/base/donor targeting (which have directly measurable behavioral outcomes), but there is no strong public randomized evidence that CTV specifically drives turnout better than other channels — this is a mechanism-plausible inference, not a demonstrated result.
s: Author synthesis of Green & Gerber GOTV evidence and CTV addressability, as of 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Comscore's Proximic political audience-targeting solutions (AI-powered, presidential/Senate/House/gubernatorial segments, originally exclusive to Trade Desk buyers in 2024) remain operational for the 2026 midterms, evidenced by the 2026 Proximic Political Targeting Playbook and a Comscore–Yahoo DSP CTV political partnership announced March 5, 2026.
s: Comscore, 'Proximic Political Targeting Playbook' (2026) and 'Comscore and Yahoo DSP Partner...' (2026-03-05), comscore.com, accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: An Optimum Media / Democratic Governors Association / GMMB CTV-frequency case study (May 2026, tested in the 2025 New Jersey governor's race) claims an 'optimal frequency' group showed stronger persuasion and decisiveness, but reports no effect sizes or confidence intervals and segmented voters by observed exposure rather than randomizing it — a selection design, not a causal one.
s: Optimum Media / DGA / GMMB, 'Finding the CTV Frequency Sweet Spot,' Campaigns & Elections (sponsored), 2026-05-05, accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Randomized online-ad experiments find voters exposed to ads are sometimes more likely to recall the ad but no more likely to recognize or favorably evaluate the candidate (point estimate ~1.6 points, SE ~1.4) — ad recall does not equal attitude or behavior change.
s: Broockman & Green, 'Do Online Advertisements Increase Political Candidates' Name Recognition or Favorability?' Political Behavior 36(2), 2014, springer.com, accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: U.S. political ad spending in the 2023–24 cycle reached a record ~$11.1 billion (AdImpact), the most expensive cycle in history.
s: TV Tech reporting AdImpact cycle review, Dec 20 2024; tvtechnology.com

claims.t: Political CTV spend in 2024 was ~$1.5–1.6 billion by eMarketer's CTV-as-slice-of-digital definition (≈45% of digital, 12.6% of total) and ~$2.3 billion (21% of total) by AdImpact's CTV-as-top-line-medium definition.
s: eMarketer, Jun 3 2024; AdImpact via TV Tech Dec 20 2024

claims.t: Political CTV's share of digital rose from ~5% (2018) to ~19% (2020) to ~45% (2024); its share of total rose from ~2.7% (2020) to ~12.6–21% (2024); 2022 midterm CTV was ~$1.09 billion.
s: MediaPost; Marketing Brew Oct 6 2022; eMarketer Jun 2024

claims.t: AdImpact projects the 2026 midterm at ~$10.8 billion total (most expensive midterm ever, +20% vs 2022) with CTV at ~$2.5 billion (~23% share), the only major medium projected to grow versus 2024.
s: Campaigns & Elections, Sep 5 2025, reporting AdImpact

claims.t: In 2024 broadcast took ~$5.3B (~48%), CTV ~$2.3B (~21%), non-CTV digital ~$1.6B (~14%), local cable ~$1.37B (~12%); broadcast holds share while CTV grows largely at declining cable's expense.
s: AdImpact via TV Tech, Dec 20 2024; cable decline cross-checked vs C&E 2026 ($1.7B→$1.29B)

claims.t: The Harris campaign reserved ~$370 million for Sept–Nov 2024 (~$170M TV + >$200M digital including CTV via Hulu, Roku, YouTube, Paramount+, Spotify, Pandora), described as the largest single ad buy in U.S. political history.
s: Washington Post, Aug 17 2024; Axios, Aug 17 2024

claims.t: Democrats allocated a larger budget share to digital/CTV in 2024 (Harris 40%+ vs Trump 22%) and held a ~43,000-airing CTV/OTT advantage, spreading airings more broadly (Dem 59% vs GOP 89% battleground-concentrated).
s: Wesleyan Media Project, Jun 24 2025; Search Engine Land, Nov 12 2024

claims.t: A recurring vendor/trade narrative holds Republicans used CTV as a precision tool while Democrats treated it as a broadcast channel; the 'Moneyball / half the media Trump ran' framing comes from a Democratic vendor attributing it to the Trump operation, and is not an audited media plan.
s: DSPolitical 'Swing Votes Stream' release, Dec 17 2024; PPC Hero blog (unverified)

claims.t: In 2024, 13 states absorbed $7.4B (67% of total) — Pennsylvania first to cross $1B, then Michigan $806M, Wisconsin $673M, Arizona $511M — and 51% of all spend landed in the final eight weeks.
s: AdImpact via TV Tech, Dec 20 2024; Digiday Aug 15 2024

claims.t: Down-ballot races drew the majority of 2024 spend (presidential ~$3.2B vs Senate $2.7B, House $1.7B, plus governor/state), roughly a 75/25 down-ballot/presidential split, and CTV's district/ZIP-level targeting suits the long tail broadcast serves inefficiently.
s: AdImpact via TV Tech Dec 20 2024; Experian 2024 political CTV blog

claims.t: The five highest-paid political vendors collected ~$2.1 billion in the 2024 cycle, each specializing in media buying; this thin intermediation layer is where commission margin concentrates.
s: OpenSecrets News, 'The billion-dollar middlemen,' Feb 12 2026

claims.t: Waterfront Strategies (ad-buying arm of Democratic consultancy GMMB) booked ~$858 million in 2024 — more than double the next vendor — with ~90% from three clients (Future Forward USA ~$383M, WinSenate PAC, House Majority PAC); Democratic buying is centralized while Republican buying is distributed across ~10 firms each over $100M.
s: OpenSecrets News Feb 12 2026; OpenSecrets Waterfront vendor profile (FEC)

claims.t: Political media consultants are traditionally paid a commission on dollars spent (historically ~15%, negotiated to ~4.5% on the largest presidential buys), a model that structurally rewards spending more and repurposing creative rather than producing platform-native content.
s: Center for Public Integrity 'Airtime Is Money'; OpenSecrets Feb 2026; TrinityP3

claims.t: Madhive launched a local CTV political-advertising marketplace in February 2024 with Fox Television Stations as first client, aggregating political data partners (TargetSmart, Experian, L2, DataTrust) and pre-curated streaming supply across all 210 DMAs.
s: Axios Feb 27 2024; StreamTV Insider Feb 2024; Madhive newsroom

claims.t: The platforms, DSPs, data providers, and consultants who promote 'CTV is the future' all profit if campaigns believe it; The Trade Desk explicitly discloses that election cycles can increase its revenue, and political CTV CPMs ran ~3.5x other devices in 2020.
s: Digiday Oct 27 2023 (TTD disclosure); MediaPost/MNTN on CPM premium

claims.t: The canonical academic finding (Kalla & Broockman meta-analysis of 49+ field experiments) is that the average persuasive effect of general-election campaign contact and advertising is statistically indistinguishable from zero, in direct tension with the persuasion value CTV vendors sell.
s: Kalla & Broockman, 'Minimal Persuasive Effects of Campaign Contact,' APSR 2018

claims.t: The FCC's political-broadcasting regime — equal time (§315), reasonable access (§312(a)(7)), lowest unit charge (§315(b)), and the public political file (§315(e)) — binds only FCC broadcast licensees, and streaming/CTV platforms hold no broadcast license, so none of these obligations apply to them.
s: CRS R46516 (Scherer, 2020-09-09); FCC Statutes/Rules on Candidate Appearances; AdWave 2026 compliance guide. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: The lowest-unit-charge requirement (§315(b)), which forces broadcasters to sell candidates time at the lowest rate charged any advertiser during the 45/60-day pre-election windows, does not apply to CTV, streaming, or digital advertising, removing statutory price protection for political buyers on streaming.
s: 47 U.S.C. §315(b); AdWave, 'FCC Political Advertising Rules: 2026 Compliance Guide' (2026); FCC media policy pages. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Broadcasters (and cable/DBS) must maintain a public political file of candidate and issue ad requests, rates, and sponsors — posted to the FCC's online database since 2017 — but CTV/streaming platforms maintain no equivalent regulatory public file, removing the principal transparency artifact in political advertising.

The FEC 'stand by your ad' disclaimer for candidate ads and the 'paid for by' requirement attach to the advertisement under 52 U.S.C. §30120 and 11 C.F.R. §110.11, so they apply to a candidate's CTV spot as to a broadcast spot — the one meaningful federal transparency rule that crosses onto streaming.
s: FEC, 'Advertising and disclaimers' (52 U.S.C. §30120; 11 C.F.R. §110.11). Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: On December 1, 2022 the FEC approved a final rule (effective March 1, 2023) revising 'public communication' to include ads 'placed for a fee on another person's website, digital device, application, or advertising platform,' requiring a disclaimer viewable 'without taking any action,' with an adapted abbreviated-disclaimer option; the rulemaking (REG 2011-02) took over eleven years.
s: FEC, 'Commission adopts final rule on internet communications disclaimers and the definition of public communication' (Dec. 2022). Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: The FEC's 'electioneering communication' category is defined by statute as broadcast, cable, or satellite communications referring to a clearly identified federal candidate within 60/30 days of an election; internet and streaming communications are not electioneering communications, leaving streaming issue ads that avoid express advocacy largely outside the FEC regime.
s: FEC electioneering-communications materials; CRS IF10758 'Online Political Advertising'. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: The FTC's truth-in-advertising authority under FTC Act §5 (15 U.S.C. §45) runs to commercial speech and largely does not reach core political/issue advertising, so the FTC's relevance to political CTV is as a privacy/data-practices regulator rather than a content cop.
s: 15 U.S.C. §45; FTC 6(b) report 'A Look Behind the Screens' (2024-09-11). Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: In The Washington Post v. McManus (4th Cir., Dec. 6, 2019), a unanimous panel struck down Maryland's Online Electioneering Transparency and Accountability Act as an unconstitutional content-based, compelled-speech burden failing exacting scrutiny, and distinguished broadcasters on spectrum-scarcity grounds.
s: WaPo v. McManus, No. 19-1132 (4th Cir. 2019); Broadcast Law Blog analysis (Dec. 2019). Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Washington's Fair Campaign Practices Act ad-disclosure mandate survived Meta's First Amendment challenge: a $35.2M penalty for 822 violations, affirmed by the Washington Supreme Court (per curiam, June 18, 2026), with six of nine justices affirming liability. (Date corrected from June 19; plurality nuance added.)
s: State v. Meta Platforms — Wash. Sup. Ct. (2026-06-19), Ct. App. (2024-12); Courthouse News; The Complete Lawyer; Campaign Legal Center case page. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: The contrasting outcomes — Washington's request-on-demand recordkeeping model surviving while Maryland's mandatory self-publication model was struck — suggest a more defensible design for state digital-ad disclosure laws, though the constitutional line remains contested.
s: WaPo v. McManus (4th Cir. 2019); State v. Meta (Wash. 2026). Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: The FCC released an NPRM (FCC 24-74; July 25, 2024) proposing on-air and political-file disclosure of AI-generated content in broadcast radio/TV political ads; it is disclosure-only, passed 3-2 on party lines, and explicitly could not reach streaming/online platforms because the FCC lacks authority over them.
s: FCC NPRM FCC 24-74 (2024-07-25); PBS NewsHour (May 2024); Wiley analysis. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: The 2024 AI-disclosure NPRM has not advanced to a final rule and is effectively dead: Brendan Carr — who as a commissioner called it 'as misguided as it is unlawful' — became FCC Chairman on January 20, 2025 and is not advancing it; this is a present-tense going-concern status as of June 2026.
s: TV Tech; Venable LLP (Jan. 2025); FedScoop on Carr. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Roughly 30 states have enacted laws addressing AI/deepfakes in political communications; ~17 use a labeling/disclosure model while a few (California, Minnesota, Texas) took a prohibition approach; unlike the FCC rule these state laws can reach streaming and online ads.
s: MultiState (Feb. 2026); R Street (2025-03-17). Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: California's AB 2839 (prohibiting AI-altered election content) was preliminarily enjoined in October 2024 and, in Kohls v. Bonta (E.D. Cal.), permanently enjoined via summary judgment on August 29, 2025, the court holding it could not survive strict scrutiny and that even deliberate lies remain protected absent cognizable harm.
s: Kohls v. Bonta, No. 2:24-cv-02527 (E.D. Cal.); EPIC documents. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Minnesota's criminal election-deepfake statute remains contested: a parody-creator/legislator challenge was dismissed for standing (Jan. 2025), and X Corp.'s pre-enforcement Section 230 claim was dismissed for lack of Article III standing on December 2, 2025, though the First Amendment challenge remains live (stayed).
s: X Corp. v. [Minnesota] (D. Minn., 2025-12-02); MediaPost (2025-12-04). Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: On December 11, 2025 President Trump signed an executive order ('Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence') directing DOJ litigation and an FCC proceeding to preempt conflicting state AI laws; whether it reaches state election-deepfake statutes is unsettled but it is the leading regulatory wildcard for 2026.
s: White House EO (2025-12-11); DLA Piper, Mayer Brown analyses. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Almost every state (North Dakota, which has no registration, is the outlier) makes the voter registration list — name, address, party, vote history — available to campaigns and often to commercial vendors, and there is no federal law making voter registration lists private.
s: U.S. EAC, 'Voter Roll Privacy' (2024); GovFacts. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: State comprehensive privacy laws leave voter/political data outside their reach: the CCPA excludes voter data as 'publicly available' records and campaigns (527s) as non-'businesses' — not via an express CCPA political carve-out, which is a feature of successor laws. Net effect: voter targeting proceeds without commercial consent mechanisms.
s: Cal. Civ. Code §1798.100 et seq.; IAPP analysis; EFF (April 2024). Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Roku, per its own guidelines (page marked 'Updated 2024'), requires political advertisers to be identified/verified before launch, bans foreign-national funding, prohibits deepfakes, requires a disclosure notice on AI/synthetically generated content, and publishes a voluntary public political-ad archive — a platform self-governance regime, not a regulatory public file.
s: Roku Advertising, 'Political Advertising Guidelines' / political ad archive (Updated 2024). Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: TikTok prohibits paid political advertising outright as a matter of platform policy, but enforcement is imperfect — NBC News and the Washington Post documented banned political content slipping through in 2024.
s: TikTok ad policy; NBC News (2024); Washington Post (Oct. 2024). Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Hulu/Disney reversed course in July 2022 to accept political issue ads (including abortion and gun-control spots) after a Democratic backlash over rejections, illustrating that platform content rules are discretionary and shift under political pressure.
s: Variety, Axios, Hollywood Reporter (July 2022). Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: The FTC's September 11, 2024 6(b) staff report found large social-media and streaming companies engaged in 'vast surveillance' with 'woefully inadequate' data-minimization, monetizing personal data and flagging risks of targeting on sensitive characteristics — the FTC's most consequential intervention touching CTV data practices.
s: FTC, 'A Look Behind the Screens' / 6(b) report (2024-09-11). Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: The Honest Ads Act — which would require digital platforms with 50M+ monthly U.S. visitors to maintain a public file of political ad buys over $500 and bar foreign-national purchases — has not become law; folded into the For the People Act (passed House, stalled Senate) and reintroduced as S.486/H.R.2599 (118th Congress) without passage, leaving the federal CTV transparency gap open for 2026.
s: S.486 / H.R.2599 (118th Cong.), congress.gov; Brennan Center; Sen. Warner. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Synthesizing the gaps, the most sophisticated voter-level-targeted political ads run on streaming — which lacks equal time, reasonable access, price control, a public file, robust AI rules, and meaningful issue-ad disclosure — making CTV the least-regulated and least-transparent political-ad medium even as it captures a fast-growing share of spend.
s: Composite of CRS R46516, FCC/FEC primary rules, WaPo v. McManus, state-law trackers, and Brennan Center analysis. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Streaming captured 44.8% of total U.S. TV viewing in May 2025, surpassing broadcast (20.1%) and cable (24.1%) combined (44.2%) for the first time, per Nielsen's The Gauge; by December 2025 streaming reached 47.5%.
s: Nielsen, The Gauge (May 2025 data), 2025; nielsen.com — accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: Only 36% of U.S. adults subscribe to cable or satellite TV (vs 83% who stream), and cable subscription falls sharply by age: 64% of 65+, 44% of 50-64, 23% of 30-49, and just 16% of 18-29.
s: Pew Research Center, July 1, 2025; pewresearch.org — accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: AdImpact's June-2026 update projects 2026 political CTV spend at ~$2.7B (revised up from $2.48–2.5B in September 2025) and broadcast at ~$5.6B (revised up, not down) — CTV remains the only major channel projected to grow over the 2024 presidential cycle.
s: The Current, Sep 15 2025, citing AdImpact; thecurrent.com — accessed 2026-06-23. The Current is owned by The Trade Desk (DSP).

claims.t: AdImpact raised its total 2026 political ad spend projection from $10.8B (Sep 2025) to $11.6B (Jun 2026), 'the most expensive midterm on record,' up more than 20% from 2022's ~$8.9B.
s: AdImpact, Political Projections 2025-2026 (updated Jun 11 2026); adimpact.com — accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: Political CTV ad spend grew roughly 800% from 2020 (~$260M) to 2024 (~$2.34B actual); the widely cited '~600%' measures 2020 to eMarketer's 2024 forecast of ~$1.56B. 2022 was ~$1.09B; CTV's share of political programmatic budgets rose 19%→30% (2020→2022).
s: The Current / MNTN; thecurrent.com — accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: After Apple's App Tracking Transparency launched in 2021, global IDFA opt-in fell to roughly 14% by mid-2024 (down from ~26% shortly after launch), a durable structural loss of mobile addressability that pushed advertising toward first-party matching.
s: Singular, 'ATT opt-in rates 2024'; Flurry monthly ATT updates; singular.net — accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: Google reversed its plan to deprecate third-party cookies in Chrome — confirming in April 2025 it would neither deprecate cookies nor show a user-choice prompt, and deprecating its Privacy Sandbox replacement APIs in October 2025 — so the open-web cookie survives, blunting one prong of the signal-loss thesis.
s: OneTrust, 'Google Drops Plans for Third-Party Cookie Choice Prompt'; onetrust.com — accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: Comscore and L2 launched cookie-free, voter-behavior-based predictive audiences in January 2022 spanning digital/mobile/CTV/audio, and as of September 2025 L2 is among 10+ providers in Comscore's AI-powered Data Partner Network — confirming the product line is currently operating.
s: Comscore press releases; comscore.com — accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: Comscore and Yahoo DSP launched 'Proximic Political Audiences' on March 5, 2026 — a CTV product unifying Comscore linear-exposure data with Yahoo ConnectID (claimed 232M logged-in U.S. users) across 210 DMAs for the 2026 midterms, activated through MiQ's political division.
s: PPC Land, Mar 7 2026; ppc.land — accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: L2 advertises 217M voter records, 260M consumer records, and 91 predictive fields; i360 advertises 190M+ voters/250M+ consumers with up to 1,800 data points per record; TargetSmart states 208M+ registered voters plus a 259M+ record match database — all currently operating as of June 2026.
s: L2 (l2-data.com), i360 (i-360.com), TargetSmart (targetsmart.com) product pages — accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: L2's national voter file and modeled scores are available for CPM-priced digital onboarding through LiveRamp, the rail that turns a hashed voter list into an addressable CTV audience across the programmatic landscape.
s: L2 Political, 'national voter file available through LiveRamp'; LiveRamp match-rate docs — accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: Kalla and Broockman's meta-analysis of 49 field experiments (American Political Science Review, 2018) found the best estimate of the persuasive effect of campaign contact and advertising in general elections is approximately zero, with effects only in narrow conditions — directly contradicting vendor lift claims.
s: Kalla & Broockman, APSR 112(1), 2018; cambridge.org — accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: FCC political-broadcasting rules — reasonable access, equal time, lowest-unit-rate, and the public political file — apply only to broadcast licensees and do not reach streaming/CTV, which the FCC explicitly acknowledged it 'cannot touch' when proposing 2024 AI-disclosure rules; FEC disclaimers and FTC standards do follow ads to streaming.
s: CBS News / PBS NewsHour, 2024; FCC Political Programming page; cbsnews.com — accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: As of mid-2026 roughly 30 states (Public Citizen — Maryland the 30th, May 13, 2026) have enacted laws regulating deepfakes/AI in election communications; California's AB 2839 was struck down in full (Kohls v. Bonta, E.D. Cal., Aug 29, 2025), not partially.
s: Public Citizen tracker (Jun 15 2026); R Street; citizen.org — accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: On September 19, 2024, the FEC declined to open a dedicated rulemaking on AI in campaign ads, instead issuing an interpretive rule affirming its existing fraudulent-misrepresentation prohibition applies regardless of technology.
s: Skadden, 'California Enacts New Laws' / R Street, 2024-2025 — accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: Netflix, Disney+, Amazon Prime Video, and Apple TV decline political advertising as of mid-2026 (Netflix maintaining the ban despite ~13M U.S. ad-tier subscribers), concentrating political dollars onto Hulu, Roku, YouTube, and FAST channels and spiking CPMs on those platforms in the Sept-Nov surge window.
s: Basis, 'How Political Advertising Will Impact the Media Landscape in 2026'; Campaigns & Elections — accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: Trade estimates put political-accepting CTV CPMs at roughly $35-80 for premium (Hulu, Peacock, Paramount+), $25-45 mid-tier (Roku, Samsung TV+), and $18-28 for FAST channels (Tubi, Pluto), with the platforms that accept political seeing the sharpest increases in the election surge window.
s: AdWave / TurnItBlue political CTV guides, 2026 — accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: Political ad spend follows an even-year pulse (presidential peaks 2020/2024/2028, midterm peaks 2018/2022/2026); CTV cycle figures (~$0.26B 2020 → $1.09B 2022 → $2.34B 2024 → ~$2.5B 2026) layer this on a rising secular base, with off-year troughs increasingly filled by issue/advocacy spend.
s: AdImpact; Borrell Associates via Radio Ink/Barrett Media, May 2026 — accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: Generative AI lowers the cost and speeds production of political video creative and enables multilingual/district-specific localization — benefits the FCC noted as especially valuable to smaller, lower-budget campaigns — while also enabling deepfakes that triggered platform disclosure rules (Meta Jan 2024; YouTube synthetic-content labels) and a state-law backlash.
s: Univ. of Illinois College of Media; Federal Register 2024-16977 — accessed 2026-06-23

claims.t: After Walmart's Dec 3 2024 close, Inscape continued licensing ACR data to third-party measurement firms, renewing/extending deals with Comscore (Oct 2024, 210 markets), VideoAmp (Mar 2025), Nielsen (multi-year, Jun 2025), and TVision (2025), all citing 24M+ opted-in TVs.
s: Adweek Wire (Oct 2024); eMarketer (Oct 7 2024); Inscape/VideoAmp release (Mar 27 2025); Nielsen release (Jun 2025); TVision (2025). Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Vizio Ads' political offering, built on the live AdImpact x Inscape partnership, was extended ahead of the 2026 election season and still provides ACR-driven candidate-exposure custom segments (unexposed / under-exposed / saw-the-opponent) and congressional-district-level targeting.
s: RBR; Next TV 'Vizio Expands Work With AdImpact Ahead of Elections'; TVREV/AdImpact 2026 projections; VIZIO Platform+ case study. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: The 2017 FTC/NJ stipulated order (against VIZIO, Inc. and VIZIO Inscape Services, LLC) carried a 20-year term to ~2037 and still governs: Vizio's current privacy policy keeps ACR Viewing Data behind a revocable setup-time opt-in AND keeps Vizio OS Data separate from the Walmart account until a separate 'Consent to Combine' opt-in.
s: WilmerHale (2017); Davis Wright Tremaine (2017); VIZIO Privacy Policy & 'Combine VIZIO OS Data with Walmart Account' page (current). Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: The data-licensing arm still trades as 'Inscape' / 'VIZIO's Inscape' (inscape.tv live; LinkedIn active; 2025 partner releases use the name); the ad product is Vizio Ads/Platform+. Walmart's renaming is of the TV/OS brand (toward its onn label) and the retail-media application via Walmart Connect, not the Inscape data unit.
s: Inscape.tv; Inscape Data LinkedIn; Nielsen/VideoAmp/TVision 2025 releases; Lowpass; Talk Business (Dec 2025). Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: The genuine going-concern risk is forward-looking: Walmart Connect's data-exclusivity thesis and Walmart's retail-media optimization of Vizio give standing motive to restrict the third-party (especially lower-margin, cyclical political) pipe in a future cycle; an analyst (Digilant) names in-housing as a 'conceivable scenario' to monitor, not a change that has occurred.
s: Talk Business (Dec 2025); AdExchanger; Digilant blog. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Fox and Roku entered a definitive Agreement and Plan of Merger dated June 14, 2026 (announced June 15), acquiring Roku at $160.00/share ($96 cash + 0.9693 FOXA shares), ~$22B enterprise value, ~60% cash/40% stock, with Fox holders owning ~73% and Roku holders ~27% post-close.
s: Roku Form 8-K, SEC EDGAR acc. 0001140361-26-025115, 2026-06-15; Fox Corporation press release 2026-06-15; CNBC 2026-06-15. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: As of June 23, 2026 the deal is unconsummated: closing is conditioned on Fox and Roku shareholder approval, expiration/early termination of the HSR waiting period, and approval under 'certain other antitrust and foreign' laws; Roku remains a standalone public company.
s: Roku Form 8-K 2026-06-15; Lachlan Murdoch via PPC Land 2026-06; Fox press release 2026-06-15. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: The merger agreement's Termination/outside date is June 14, 2027, extendable to December 14, 2027 and then March 14, 2028 under certain circumstances — so the 'expected 1H 2027' close is guidance, but the contract tolerates a slide into early 2028 if antitrust review drags.
s: Roku Form 8-K, SEC EDGAR acc. 0001140361-26-025115, 'Termination' section, 2026-06-15. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: The agreement carries an $866,084,000 ordinary termination fee and a larger $1,237,262,000 reverse fee payable by Fox to Roku if the deal terminates on antitrust or investment-screening grounds — direct contractual evidence that regulatory failure is a genuine, priced risk.
s: Roku Form 8-K 2026-06-15, termination-fee section; PPC Land 2026-06; TheWrap 2026-06. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Both boards unanimously approved; concurrently Anthony Wood and affiliated stockholders (~55% of Roku voting power via dual-class) signed a binding Voting and Support Agreement, plus a Buyside VSA covering ~38.7% of Fox voting power — making shareholder approval near-certain and foreclosing the 'was it ever real/speculation' question.
s: Roku Form 8-K 2026-06-15, Voting and Support Agreements; Rich Greenfield via TheWrap 2026-06. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Skeptical commentary concerns Fox's strategic logic and leverage (shares fell ~17%; ~2.8x net leverage; T.D. Cowen's Doug Creutz flagged industry-history skepticism) and whether platform neutrality survives — not whether the deal is genuine or will close; 'skeptical of competing bidders' actually favors this deal closing.
s: Investing.com 2026-06; TheWrap (Braden Perry) 2026-06; Deadline 2026-06. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: The principal antitrust theory is vertical: one owner would hold Fox News/Sports content, Roku's #1 TV-OS home screen/search/ad inventory, two FAST services (Tubi + Roku Channel), and ACR across ~100M+ households — raising self-preferencing, Tubi/Roku-Channel overlap, and rival-intelligence concerns; combined U.S. TV-viewing share rises ~7.2%→~10.2%.
s: MLex 2026-06; PPC Land 2026-06; TheWrap 2026-06; Fox press release 2026-06-15. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: No disclosed deal term addresses Roku's public political ad archive (launched Sept 2020) or ACR data licensing to third-party political buyers; the deal foregrounds Roku first-party data merged with Fox's TTD/UID2/OpenPath identity layer but is silent on political transparency — so the fate of the archive/ACR licensing under Fox is undisclosed and undetermined, an open question, not a settled change.
s: Fox press release 2026-06-15; PPC Land 2026-06; Roku Political Advertising Guidelines/Ad Archive (live policy); observer commentary on X (Tier 7, narrative only). Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: i360 is a live, going-concern conservative voter-data and targeting vendor in the 2026 cycle, marketing 270M+ voter / 300M+ consumer profiles and 1,800+ data points to right-of-center organizations, and actively hiring.
s: i360.com homepage + Campaigns page; Koch Inc. career-opportunities/i360; Tracxn/PitchBook 2026 profiles. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: i360 is branded 'A KOCH COMPANY' on Koch Inc.'s site and is a wholly owned Koch Industries/Koch Inc. subsidiary; Michael Palmer (ex-McCain '08 CTO) founded it in 2009 and remains Founder & President.
s: Koch Inc. career-opportunities/i360; DeSmog 'i360'; Tracxn 2026 profile. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: i360's Digital Audiences page explicitly markets its segments 'across social, programmatic, and connected TV,' confirming its current CTV-addressability-stack placement with first-party 2026 evidence.
s: i360 'i360 Digital Audiences,' https://www.i-360.com/i360-digital-audiences/. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: The Koch network recalibrated its political-spending posture (2019 'Stand Together' rebrand; record ~$150M+ AFP Action 2024 spend, Haley-over-Trump primary play, ~two-thirds to congressional races) but did not retire i360, which instead diversified commercially.
s: Sludge 2024-11-04; OpenSecrets News 2024-08; vendor profiles (Tracxn/PitchBook). Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Data Trust is the operative GOP voter-data exchange in 2026, publishing a dated Nov 14, 2025 voter-file modernization 'refreshed for the needs of the 2026 cycle' (33 fields added, 18 retired, geocoding 87%->98%), tracking 300M+ individuals / 2,500+ data points and reporting 5,000+ Republican campaigns supported in 2024.
s: Data Trust enhancing-data-trust post (2025-11-14) + homepage. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: The RNC-to-Data Trust relationship is intact and collaborative in 2026 — the RNC Data Department co-curates the file flowing through the GOP Data Center — and no 2025-2026 source shows the RNC taking the file in-house or switching vendors.
s: Data Trust 'About'; CAGOP Data 'GOP Data Center.' Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Republican data has a documented history of breaches and governance friction (the 2017 Deep Root Analytics breach exposing ~198M voters; ProPublica's reporting on RNC payment turbulence around a breached vendor), but none of it shows Data Trust replaced for 2026.
s: The Hill 2017; UpGuard 'The RNC Files'; ProPublica RNC-data-firm investigation. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: From the buying desk, CTV has become the reach-planning anchor displacing the linear-first order, but practitioners describe it as a 'mass reach tool' bought broad — not the addressable scalpel vendor decks sell.
s: The Current, 'Is CTV's political tipping point finally here?', pub. Mar 17 / ed. Jun 18, 2026 (TTD-owned; named-practitioner position-evidence). Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: The voter-file-matched, household-addressable share of political CTV is the minority; most dollars are deployed as geographic/demographic microtargeting or run-of-network across a geography, with the voter file informing where to weight spend rather than gating who sees the ad.
s: Adwave practitioner guides; AdImpact, 'The Role of CTV in 2025 Political Campaigns'; Jamloop, 'Why Most Political Streaming TV Campaigns Waste Impressions.' Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Realistic CTV match rates for a clean voter file run 50–70% per practitioner guides, against the 90%+ the buy-side vendor DSPolitical advertises — a ~20–40 point gap, with the spread driven by the deterministic (accurate, lower-volume) vs. probabilistic (higher-reach, lower-precision) tradeoff.
s: Adwave, 'Voter Data Onboarding for CTV Political Ads (2026 Guide)'; Deep Sync, 'CTV Targeting'; DSPolitical match-rate claim as cited in Adwave. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Most enterprise programmatic and CTV platforms gate at $25K–$50K+ minimum spends with $1,000–$5,000 custom onboarding fees and 3–7 business day LiveRamp activation, even as self-serve tools start at $50 — producing a two-tier market where deep-pocketed buyers access the full addressable stack and down-ballot/late-entry campaigns route to self-serve and buy broad.
s: Adwave, 'Voter Data Onboarding' and 'Programmatic Political Advertising: A Campaign Manager's Guide' (2026). Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Across CTV, just 8–15% of households exceed their intended frequency cap but absorb 42–60% of total impressions, because platforms withhold granular household-level frequency data, producing a 'lopsided delivery pattern' no single buyer fully sees.
s: tvScientific, 'Solving the CTV Frequency Problem'; consult.tv cross-channel frequency-capping analysis (2024–2026). Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Operators name a specific intelligence deficit absent in linear: programmatic CTV lacks the competitive visibility (who the opponent is buying) and reliable geographic confirmation ('location gap') that political buyers depend on, which a named agency strategist calls the primary thing holding back political digital growth.
s: The Current, 'Is CTV's political tipping point finally here?' (Goldberg quote); digitalelement.com on the CTV location gap. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: The open programmatic CTV market carries a fraud/invalid-traffic tax — over $1.1B lost to IVT in a single 2024 quarter, plus MFA apps and ~$1.4B routed through unauthorized 'direct' sellers — and buy-side ad-ops 'quietly reclassifies' much of this loss as 'ops' because agencies are 'often paid based on volume.
s: AdExchanger, 'CTV Still Has A Fraud Problem'; HUMAN Security and Pixalate-cited syntheses (2024). Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: The contested 'Republicans used CTV as a precision tool while Democrats treated it as a broadcast channel' claim functions in 2026 primarily as an argument Democratic practitioners and vendors make to their own side to justify more CTV spend — not as an independently audited comparison; no party has published an apples-to-apples addressable-vs-broad CTV breakdown for 2024.
s: DSPolitical, 'Swing Votes Stream' report; Adnan Mohamed (TargetSmart), 'Why Democrats Must Treat Streaming as the New Political Battleground,' Campaigns & Elections, 2026. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: For 2026 the political industry's own Reed Awards added a new category, 'Best Integration of Linear and CTV for a Campaign' — an institutional acknowledgment that the operator's unit of excellence is orchestrating reach and frequency across linear and streaming, not standalone addressable CTV targeting.
s: The Reed Awards / Campaigns & Elections 2026 categories. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Operators plan around a fragmented permission map — Amazon and Netflix prohibit political ads, LG restricts home-screen issue/candidate inventory, and even participating publishers selectively exclude inventory or whitelist only trusted advertisers — which a named sell-side exec says 'puts a floor under CPMs' so buyers can't 'execute at their bottom dollar.
s: Digiday, 'The cases for and against investing in CTV…' (Hansen quote); AdExchanger, 'Buyers Can Curate Deals Based On Voter Values' (OpenX/Givsly, Feb 23 2026). Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Zuiderveen Borgesius et al. (2018) is the canonical statement of the harms counter-tradition, enumerating threats to citizens (privacy/chilling, manipulation, exclusion), parties (cost, intermediary power), and public opinion (mandate problem, fragmentation of the marketplace of ideas).
s: Zuiderveen Borgesius, Möller, Kruikemeier, Ó Fathaigh, Irion, Dobber, Bodó & de Vreese, 'Online Political Microtargeting: Promises and Threats for Democracy,' Utrecht Law Review 14(1), 2018, pp. 82-96

claims.t: The counter-tradition's resolution of the 'if effects are near zero, why care?' tension is that most harms run through channels other than persuasion, captured in Borgesius et al.'s sentence: 'Even if microtargeting were not effective, the mere collection of data would still be a privacy threat.
s: Zuiderveen Borgesius et al., Utrecht Law Review, 2018, §4.1 and §5. https://utrechtlawreview.org/articles/10.18352/ulr.420. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: The only causal-leaning field estimate of digital voter-suppression's turnout impact finds exposure associated with a 1.86% national turnout decline and a 17.3% decline among non-Whites in minority-majority counties of battleground states — demonstrating harm via demobilization, not persuasion.
s: Kim, Dahlke, Song & Heinrich, 'Targeted digital voter suppression efforts likely decrease voter turnout,' PNAS, 2026. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12867748/. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: A persuasion effect of ≈0 (doc 04) and a measurable suppression effect are not contradictory: they answer different questions (flipping a supporter vs. keeping an opponent's voter home), and demobilization is mechanically easier and is what addressability is built for.
s: Synthesis of doc 04 §4; Kreiss, Internet Policy Review 2017; Vandewalker/Brennan 2020; Borgesius et al. 2018. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Ghosh & Scott argue the harm is the business model itself: the same ad-tech targeting stack built for commercial advertising delivers precision propaganda 'regardless of actor intent,' via an 'implicit but extraordinarily powerful alignment' between platforms and propagandists.
s: Ghosh & Scott, Digital Deceit, New America, Jan. 2018, via https://www.ned.org/forum-qa-dipayan-ghosh-on-the-commercial-drivers-of-precision-propaganda/. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Daniel Kreiss, a leading empirical scholar of data-driven campaigning, is a partial skeptic of the microtargeting moral panic: persuasion is hard, microtargeting's real work is mobilizing/reinforcing existing partisans, and 'we have anxieties about micro-targeting because we have anxieties about democracy itself.
s: Kreiss, 'Micro-targeting, the quantified persuasion,' Internet Policy Review 6(4), Dec. 31 2017. https://policyreview.info/articles/analysis/micro-targeting-quantified-persuasion. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: The mass-psychographic-persuasion version of the harm (Cambridge Analytica) is widely judged by quantitative social scientists to have been oversold 'snake oil' with 'basically nonexistent' evidence of independent effect — so the corpus should reject this version on the same evidence as doc 04.
s: NBC News 2018; Nature 'The scant science behind Cambridge Analytica' 2018; Stanford GSB; The Conversation. https://www.nature.com/articles/d41586-018-03880-4. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Mozilla's 2020 'Paid Programming' report graded streaming platforms on political-ad transparency, calling the category a 'Wild West' where ads 'microtarget, manipulate, and misinform … at a level unmatched by any other form of political speech'; YouTube TV scored B+ and Roku 'D' for an archive with 'barely any information' and no bulk data access.
s: Ricks/Mozilla Foundation, 'Paid Programming,' Sept. 22, 2020. https://www.mozillafoundation.org/en/blog/new-research-streaming-platforms-are-wild-west-political-ads/. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: The Brennan Center's 'Digital Disinformation and Vote Suppression' (Vandewalker, 2020) documents microtargeted suppression — deception on time/place/manner of voting, boycott calls, intimidation — disproportionately aimed at communities of color, with concrete cases (2010 MD robocalls, 2016 IRA boycott messaging, 2017 AL false polling-site texts).
s: Vandewalker/Brennan Center, 'Digital Disinformation and Vote Suppression,' Sept. 2 2020. https://www.brennancenter.org/our-work/research-reports/digital-disinformation-and-vote-suppression. Accessed 2

claims.t: Tactical Tech's 'Influence Industry' project reframes Cambridge Analytica as an outlier in how it navigated ethical/legal boundaries, not in its tools — most of its techniques are 'common throughout' a lightly regulated political-data industry of 'over 250 companies.
s: Tactical Tech, 'The Influence Industry,' Our Data Our Selves. https://ourdataourselves.tacticaltech.org/posts/influence-industry/. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: CTV sharpens every harm in the tradition — deeper ACR-fused surveillance, worse accountability (no Ad Library; Mozilla 'D'-graded archives), the same ad machine with fewer guardrails — making doc 06's 'streaming loophole' a democratic hazard rather than merely a regulatory gap, because it removes the auditability that is democracy's actual protection against addressable targeting.
s: Synthesis of docs 02/03/06 with Mozilla 2020, Tufekci 2014, Ghosh & Scott 2018. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: As of the 2025-26 season the U.S. TV market has no single agreed currency: Nielsen's reaccredited Big Data + Panel competes against three JIC-certified challengers (Comscore, iSpot, VideoAmp), each measuring a different universe, so the 'reach' in political-CTV vendor claims is currency-specific, not comparable.
s: eMarketer, 'JIC's measurement audit shows a sector diversifying beyond Nielsen,' 2025; AdExchanger JIC certification coverage; Nielsen Big Data + Panel MRC accreditation release, 2025. Accessed 2026-0

claims.t: The JIC was formed in 2023 (OpenAP + VAB + broadcasters) as a response to Nielsen's accreditation crisis and certifies transactability — a deliberately faster, lower bar than MRC accreditation's methodology audit, which 'literally takes years.
s: OpenAP/PRNewswire JIC formation and criteria, 2023; NextTV, 'Programmers Band Together…,' 2023; AdExchanger, 'The JIC And The MRC Clarify…,' 2024. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Comscore is the only firm MRC-accredited for both national and local big-data TV measurement (all 210 markets); Nielsen lost local accreditation in 2021 and had not regained it; iSpot is MRC-accredited only for ad occurrence (not audience); VideoAmp holds JIC certification but no MRC accreditation — and Comscore is simultaneously the dominant political-targeting data seller and the most-credentialed local scorekeeper.
s: Comscore IR/GlobeNewswire MRC accreditation releases, 2024-2025; Inside Radio on Nielsen local non-restoration, 2023; AdExchanger/Ad Age on iSpot/VideoAmp, 2024. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: The corpus's casual 'Nielsen 210 DMA' anchor describes a measurement regime that was de-accredited at the local level by the MRC throughout the cycles the corpus covers (2022, 2024); local-market TV measurement was un-accredited until Comscore's March 2024 accreditation.
s: Axios and Inside Radio on the April 2023 national-only reinstatement, 2023; Comscore March 2024 local accreditation release. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Nielsen was taken private for ~$16B ($28/share) by an Evergreen (Elliott affiliate) and Brookfield-led consortium, announced March 29 2022 and closed October 11 2022, removing public-market scrutiny during its MRC suspension and Big Data + Panel transition.
s: Nielsen/PRNewswire, 'Nielsen Enters into Agreement to be Acquired… for $16 Billion,' 2022-03-29; Variety, 'Measurement Giant Nielsen Sold to Private-Equity Group,' 2022. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Independent academic estimates of TV political-ad effects are built on Kantar/CMAG AIRINGS data (when/where each spot aired, via market-level Ad Detectors across 210 markets) accessed through the Wesleyan Media Project — not on any commercial reach currency — so the system that sells political CTV (impressions/reach) and the system that evaluates it (airings) share neither a primitive nor a denominator.
s: Wesleyan Media Project, 'Data Access' and 2022 release codebook; describing Kantar/Vivvix CMAG primary airings data. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: The best public estimate of TV advertising's vote effect (Sides, Vavreck & Warshaw, APSR 2022), built on county-matched CMAG airings 2000-2018, finds a 100-airing partisan advantage moves presidential vote share ~0.02 points but down-ballot races up to ~0.35 points — effects too small at the top of the ticket for any commercial reach currency to detect.
s: Sides, J., Vavreck, L., & Warshaw, C., 'The Effect of Television Advertising in United States Elections,' American Political Science Review, online Nov 2 2021 (2022 issue). Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Political campaigns do not transact CTV on a single ratings currency the way national brands do; they buy programmatic delivered impressions and voter-file-matched reach/lift inside DSPs, graded against vendor-reported proxies — making political CTV's transaction scoreboard the most seller-controlled of all, the structural engine behind doc 04's 'who holds the scoreboard' critique.
s: Madhive local CTV political marketplace release, 2024; The Trade Desk '2024 Election' materials; corpus docs 02/03; Digiday/AdExchanger on vendor-reported CTV metrics. Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: Because the JIC certifies transactability not effect-validity, and no commercial currency measures airings or runs randomized holdouts, even a fully resolved currency war would make political reach claims more comparable but no more causal — effectiveness lives on the separate airings-effects scoreboard.
s: Inference grounded in eMarketer JIC audit coverage 2025, AdExchanger JIC/MRC distinction 2024, and the airings-effects literature (Sides-Vavreck-Warshaw 2022). Accessed 2026-06-23.

claims.t: As of June 2026, Amazon Prime Video, Netflix, Disney+, and Apple TV+ each continue to decline U.S. political advertising; none opened a political-ad window for the 2026 cycle.
