claims.t: The 1993 Balamand statement declared 'uniatism' can 'no longer be accepted either as a method to be followed nor as a model of the unity our Churches are seeking' (para. 12), while affirming that existing Eastern Catholic churches 'have the right to exist and to act' (para. 3), grounded in sister-churches ecclesiology and a renunciation of proselytism and rebaptism (para. 13, 22).
s: Balamand Document, 'Uniatism...', Joint International Commission, 23 June 1993, christianunity.va, paras. 2, 3, 12-14, 22; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: Of roughly 75 institutions established in the Western world before 1520 that still exist in recognizable form, about 60 are universities and the remainder includes a handful of parliaments and the Roman Catholic Church — making the Church one of the oldest continuously operating institutions in the Western world.
s: Clark Kerr, The Uses of the University (Harvard UP, 1963), via biographical summaries; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: Every mechanism of Catholic endurance is double-edged: rule-governed papal succession and centralization enable global coordination but also global cover-up (the abuse crisis); slow doctrinal development preserves continuity but arrives late to every reckoning; celibate non-hereditary clergy prevents dynastic capture but produces the priest shortage that cedes ground to Pentecostal rivals.
s: Samuel P. Huntington, Political Order in Changing Societies (Yale UP, 1968), via summaries; J.H. Newman, development of doctrine; author synthesis; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: The classical secularization thesis (modernization necessarily erodes religion) has been substantially revised, most strikingly by Peter Berger, who renounced it and edited 'The Desecularization of the World' (1999); José Casanova (deprivatization) and Grace Davie ('believing without belonging'; Europe as the exception) further dismantled its universality.
s: P. Berger (ed.), The Desecularization of the World (1999); J. Casanova, Public Religions (1994); G. Davie (1994, 2002); via scholarly summaries; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: Pew's 2023-24 Religious Landscape Study (36,908 respondents, released Feb 2025) finds US Christianity declined from 78% (2007) to 62% but may be leveling off (60-64% since 2019); Catholics held stable at ~19-21% since 2014 despite native-born losses, now 54% White and 36% Hispanic, propped up by Latino immigration.
s: Pew Research Center, 'Decline of Christianity in the U.S. Has Slowed, May Have Leveled Off' (2023-24 RLS), 26 Feb 2025, pewresearch.org; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: The Latino base propping up US Catholic numbers is itself defecting: the share of US Hispanics identifying as Catholic fell from 58% a decade ago to 42% in 2024, with nearly a quarter of all US Hispanics now former Catholics — replicating inside the US the Latin American defection pattern.
s: Pew Research Center, 'Among U.S. Latinos, Catholicism Continues to Decline,' 13 Apr 2023, and 2023-24 RLS, Feb 2025; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: By 2025 roughly 69% of the world's Christians lived in the Global South, projected to reach about 78% by 2050 — shifting Catholicism's demographic center of gravity (and future leadership) away from the historic European/North American centers of wealth and authority.
s: Zurlo, Johnson & Crossing, World Christianity 2025, CSGC/Gordon-Conwell, World Christian Database; via accessible CSGC-derived reporting; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: There is no single global secular trend: Europe's institutional collapse with residual belief, the US's plateau-with-churn (stabilization masking heavy switching plus a fervent traditionalist minority), and the Global South's Christianization/inter-Christian competition are qualitatively different processes with different drivers — and Catholicism is large enough to be living all three at once.
s: Author synthesis of Pew (2025, 2026), World Christianity 2025, Annuarium 2023, and Casanova/Davie; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: Africa's Catholic population rose +3.31% in 2023 (272 million to 281 million), the largest of any continent, versus +1.15% globally; the next year it reached ~288 million.
s: Exaudi/Vatican News reporting ASE 2023, March 2025; The Catholic Thing/Catholic Culture reporting ASE 2024, March 2026; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: The global Catholic population reached 1.422 billion in 2024 (17.8% of world population, +1.14%); regional shares were Americas 47.7%, Africa 20.3%, Europe 20.1%, Asia 11.0%, Oceania 0.9% — Africa having overtaken Europe.
s: Catholic Culture, storyid 68923, March 2026 (reporting ASE 2024); The Catholic Thing, 2026-03-31; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: Pew's 2023-24 Religious Landscape Study finds that for every 1 person who joins the Catholic Church in the US, about 8.4 leave — the worst net retention of any major US tradition; 45% of former Catholics cite abuse scandals as a reason.
s: Pew Research Center RLS, 2025-02-26; OSV News/Catholic Review reporting, Feb 2025; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: Pew finds each US birth cohort has become less religious as it aged (2007-2024) with no recent cohort becoming more religious; the youngest adults are 46% Christian vs 80% for the oldest, pray daily 27% vs 58%, and attend monthly 25% vs 49%.
s: Pew Research Center, RLS Executive Summary, 2025-02-26; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: Pew finds the US Christian share has been roughly stable at ~62% since ~2019 and the religiously unaffiliated leveled near 29%, reconfirmed in December 2025 ('decline remains stalled; no revival yet') — but on a cohort base still tilted toward less-religious youth.
s: Pew Research Center, 2025-02-26; Religion Unplugged reporting new Pew data, 2025-12-08; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: Latino Catholic identity in the US fell from 67% in 2010 to ~43% in 2022 (Pew); foreign-born Latinos remain more Catholic (52%) than the US-born (36% Catholic, 39% unaffiliated), implying a Church that could become majority-Hispanic even as most Hispanics cease to be Catholic.
s: Pew Research Center, 2023-04-13; NBC News/America Magazine reporting; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: The number of US Catholic priests fell more than 40% from 1970 to 2024 (59,192 to 33,589, CARA), with a median priest age over 70 and ~1 in 4 US priests foreign-born.
s: CBS News reporting CARA, 2025; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: Worldwide major seminarians fell from 106,495 (2023) to 103,604 (2024), -2.72% in one year, part of a -14.1% 13-year and -9.2% 2019-2024 decline; the drop affected every continent except Africa (+1.1%; Europe -4.9%, Asia -4.2%, Americas -1.3%).
s: Catholic Culture, storyid 68922, March 2026 (reporting ASE 2024); accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: The global priest count ticked up marginally from 406,996 (2023) to 407,421 (2024) even as the seminarian pipeline contracted sharply — a lagging stock indicator masking a leading inflow collapse; permanent deacons numbered 52,102 and bishops 5,525.
s: Catholic Culture storyid 68923; Complicit Clergy reporting ASE 2024, 2026-04-01; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: US dioceses are consolidating parishes on a large scale driven by priest shortage, falling attendance, aging congregations, and abuse-litigation finances: >2,000 Northeast/Rust-Belt parishes closed in two decades; Baltimore merging 61 parishes into 21, Peoria 156 to 75 by 2027, Buffalo ~34% of parishes.
s: Catholic Project, Diocesan Restructuring; CNA 2024 (Buffalo); CWR 2024 (Baltimore); KWQC 2024 (Peoria); accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: US Catholic weekly Mass attendance averaged ~24% (CARA, May 2023-early 2025), a return to the 2019 pre-pandemic level of 24.4%, meaning only about a quarter of US Catholics meet the weekly obligation; Germany's practicing share is ~6.6%.
s: CARA via CNA/NCRegister, 2025; Gallup 2024; Omnes/CWR reporting German data, 2025; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: US Catholic dioceses and men's religious orders have spent over $5 billion on clergy sexual-abuse claims over roughly two decades (CARA/Georgetown).
s: Insurance Business Magazine / NCR reporting CARA, accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: 39 US Catholic dioceses have filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy (per Prof. Marie Reilly's tracking); as of early 2026 roughly 16 entities remain in bankruptcy and ~21+ have emerged, with California's AB 218 window law cited in multiple filings.
s: The Catholic Project bankruptcy data; NCRegister reporting Reilly; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: The Archdiocese of Los Angeles settled abuse claims for $880 million (Oct 2024, 1,353 claims) — the largest single US diocesan settlement, negotiated without bankruptcy — while Rockville Centre's $323 million (2024) is the largest diocesan-bankruptcy settlement to date.
s: NPR / America Magazine / Angelus News, 2024-10-17; NCRegister; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: Insurers are withdrawing from or litigating out of abuse coverage: a New York appeals court ruled (April 23, 2024) that insurers need not pay for the Archdiocese of New York's claims tied to systemic failures, and carriers have broadly narrowed terms and excluded decades-old incidents, pushing dioceses toward self-funding.
s: NCR / Florida Catholic, April 2024; Insurance Business Magazine; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: A funded conservative-Catholic infrastructure (the Napa Institute's ~$2,600/head donor gatherings; Knights of Columbus grants including $1.5m to EWTN; EWTN as broadcast spine), partly via non-disclosing nonprofits, channels resources to think tanks, media, and clergy and amplifies the traditionalist-progressive cleavage.
s: NCR; The New Republic 2021; U.S. Catholic 2023; Sojourners 2019; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: In January 2024 the African bishops' conferences collectively rejected the same-sex-blessing provisions of Fiducia Supplicans — with Pope Francis's acquiescence — an unprecedented continental doctrinal carve-out demonstrating rising Global-South leverage in Rome.
s: America Magazine, 2024-01-11; CNA, 2024-01-22; The Pillar, Jan 2024; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: The traditional Latin Mass is about 2% of US Catholic life (Pew) yet dominates online Catholic discourse, illustrating how algorithmic sorting and the 'Catholic internet' magnify intense, aesthetically distinctive factions far beyond their demographic footprint and have become a primary conversion on-ramp.
s: Tablet Magazine; WBUR Endless Thread, 2024-10-18; Catholic Herald 2024-25; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: The Holy See and the People's Republic of China extended their provisional agreement on the appointment of bishops for four years on 22 October 2024 (after 2018, 2020 and 2022 iterations); about ten bishops have been appointed under it, and Pope Leo XIV signaled continuity with a 2025 appointment, though the text is secret and Beijing has at points acted unilaterally.
s: Holy See Press Office communiqué, 2024-10-22; America Magazine 2024-10-22; ICC/CatholicVote 2025 (flagged); accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: Immigration is the principal Western decline buffer: ~1 in 4 US priests and 17% of US graduate seminarians are foreign-born, but US immigration-law tightening has been flagged (2025) as a 'serious new crisis' for staffing visa-dependent parishes, making the buffer time-limited.
s: CBS News reporting CARA, 2025; NCR, 2025; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: Catholicism declined sharply across Latin America from 2013-14 to 2024 — Brazil ~60% to 46%, Mexico ~77% to 67%, Colombia ~79% to 60%, Argentina 71% to 58% — with the religiously unaffiliated roughly doubling to quadrupling, showing high fertility can coexist with falling Catholic practice (a key caveat to the African-growth thesis).
s: Pew Research Center, 'Catholicism Has Declined in Latin America Over the Past Decade,' 2026-01-21; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: Pew projects the share of the world's Christians living in sub-Saharan Africa will rise from ~26% (2015) to ~42% (2060), and Catholic-specific commentary projects roughly one in three Catholics will be African by 2050 — model-dependent on assumed fertility and transmission.
s: Pew Research Center, 2015-04-02 (Future of World Religions; sub-Saharan Africa); CWR commentary; accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: The 1968 Medellin conference of CELAM (24 Aug-6 Sept 1968, opened by Paul VI, ~247 bishops) applied Vatican II to Latin America and named 'institutionalized violence,' structural sin, the preferential option for the poor, base communities, and the see-judge-act method, seeding liberation theology.
s: Medellin Conference Documents (CELAM II), 1968, via we-are-church.org / Education for Justice; See Judge Act, '1968: Latin American Bishops at Medellin.' Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: Gustavo Gutierrez (Peruvian Dominican, 1928-2024) gave the movement its name and first systematic statement in Teologia de la liberacion (1971), defining theology as 'critical reflection on praxis' read from the side of the poor, holding together liberation from oppression, from sin, and into communion with God.
s: Gutierrez, Teologia de la liberacion (1971); obituaries in Washington Post, America Magazine, NCR, 22-24 Oct 2024. Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: The CDF's 1984 Instruction Libertatis Nuntius (6 Aug 1984, signed Ratzinger and Bovone) condemned the uncritical use of Marxist class-struggle analysis on the premise it is inseparable from atheist ideology (VII.6, VII.8) and the collapse of the kingdom of God into a political liberation movement (IX.3), while explicitly calling 'liberation' a 'thoroughly valid term' (III.4) and disclaiming any approval of those who keep the poor in misery (XI.1).
s: CDF, Libertatis Nuntius, 6 Aug 1984, vatican.va, sections III.4, VII.6, VII.8, IX.3, XI.1. Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: The CDF issued a second, constructive instruction, Libertatis Conscientiae (22 March 1986), as the pars construens to the 1984 pars destruens, affirming a Gospel-rooted theology of Christian freedom and liberation, meant to be read as an organic pair with the first.
s: CDF, Libertatis Conscientiae, 22 March 1986, via vatican.va and Catholic Culture. Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: Leonardo Boff was sentenced to a roughly one-year 'obsequious silence' by a CDF Notification of 11 March 1985 (approved by John Paul II) for the 'ecclesiological relativism' of Church: Charism and Power; facing a second silencing in 1992 he resigned the Franciscan order and the priesthood that June, turning toward ecology.
s: CDF Notification on Boff, 11 March 1985, vatican.va; Sojourners, 'Leonardo Boff Resigns Priesthood,' Oct 1992; America Magazine, Jan 2024. Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: The CDF issued a Notification on Jon Sobrino dated 26 Nov 2006 (published March 2007, signed Levada and Amato, approved Benedict XVI) flagging 'erroneous or dangerous' christological propositions in Jesus the Liberator (1991) and Christ the Liberator (1999), chiefly over-emphasis on Jesus' humanity and 'the church of the poor' as a christological locus.
s: CDF Notification on the works of Fr. Jon Sobrino, 26 Nov 2006, vatican.va; NCR coverage 2007. Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: The 'preferential option for the poor,' born at Medellin, was assimilated into ordinary magisterium: John Paul II affirmed it by name in Sollicitudo Rei Socialis (1987, par. 42) as 'a special form of primacy in the exercise of Christian charity' (glossing it as 'love of preference for the poor'), Benedict XVI called it 'not ideological but born from the Gospel,' and Francis made it a leitmotif.
s: John Paul II, Sollicitudo Rei Socialis, 30 Dec 1987, par. 42; Benedict XVI and Francis catechesis via vatican.va. Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: Pope Francis came not from Gutierrez's school but from its Argentine cousin, the teologia del pueblo (Gera, Tello, Scannone, who taught Bergoglio), which is anti-Marxist, reads 'the people' through popular religiosity rather than class struggle, and prioritizes unity over conflict, which is why it could embody the option for the poor without the Marxist vulnerability that sank Boff.
s: J.C. Scannone, 'Pope Francis and the Theology of the People,' Theological Studies; Cushwa Center, Notre Dame. Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: Under Francis, Gutierrez was welcomed back (meeting Francis in 2013 and 2014, praised in L'Osservatore Romano, and in 2015 co-authoring On the Side of the Poor with the sitting CDF prefect Cardinal Gerhard Muller) and died 22 Oct 2024 at 96, partly rehabilitated by the institution that once shadowed him.
s: Gutierrez & Muller, On the Side of the Poor (Orbis, 2015); NCR, 'Liberation theology finds new welcome...'; obituaries Oct 2024. Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: Oscar Romero, archbishop of San Salvador assassinated at the altar on 24 March 1980 by a right-wing death squad and long viewed in Rome as a liberationist embarrassment, was declared a martyr (Feb 2015), beatified (23 May 2015), and canonized (14 Oct 2018) by Pope Francis.
s: Britannica, 'St. Oscar Romero'; America Magazine and Catholic press, 2015 & 2018. Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: The movement's energy migrated into integral ecology (Francis's Laudato Si', 2015, binding care for the poor and the planet, with Boff a credited forerunner) and indigenous theology (the 2019 Amazon Synod and Querida Amazonia, 2 Feb 2020), transposing Medellin's reading 'from the underside' from class onto ecology and ethnicity.
s: Francis, Laudato Si' (2015) and Querida Amazonia (2 Feb 2020), vatican.va; America Magazine, 'a second look' (Jan 2024). Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: Brazil's base ecclesial communities, numbered in the tens of thousands at their 1980s peak, entered continuous decline from the 1990s and are now estimated at around 20,000 with an aging membership, with only modest Francis-era revival.
s: Catholic Outlook, 'basic ecclesial communities in Brazil show signs of revival'; wisdomlib (Archives de sciences sociales des religions). Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: The conservative-empirical critique holds that liberation theology redirected the Church's best pastoral agents into politics while Pentecostalism won the poor; Recio Huetos ('Bleeding Catholicism,' Religions 2023) ties LT's post-1989 retreat to Catholic 'bleeding,' citing Latinobarometro figures of Catholics falling from 80.3% (1995) to 60.4% (2020) and Protestants rising from 6% to 12.8%.
s: Javier Recio Huetos, 'Bleeding Catholicism,' Religions 14:11 (2023): 1354 (MDPI). Accessed via abstract/index 2026-06-25.

claims.t: The liberationist rebuttal, at full strength, holds the decline was active suppression from above (conservative episcopal appointments, defunded base communities, disciplined leaders) that cleared the field for Pentecostalism rather than a fair loss, and that the outcome is absorption not defeat: the option for the poor is now magisterial, the martyr a saint, the instinct alive in eco/indigenous theology and a Latin American papacy.
s: The Alleged Decline of Liberation Theology,' Religions 13:12 (2022): 1181; 'The Solved Conflict,' Int. J. Latin Am. Religions (Springer, 2021). Accessed via abstract 2026-06-25.

claims.t: Benedict XVI sustained the official critique into his papacy, warning in a December 2009 ad limina address to Brazilian bishops that the consequences of liberation theology ('rebellion, division, dissent, offenses, anarchy') were 'still being felt' and calling certain of its principles 'deceitful.
s: Religion News Service, 'Pope warns of deceitful aspects of liberation theology,' Dec 2009; CNA/EWTN News. Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: The Sodalitium Christianae Vitae and its four affiliated branches were formally suppressed by Pope Francis, the dissolution decree signed 14 April 2025 after a Vatican investigation found the movement had 'no authentic charism' and documented sadistic abuse by founder Luis Fernando Figari.
s: OSV News, 'Peru-based Catholic movement formally suppressed by the Vatican'; NCRegister/CNA, 'Sodality of Christian Life Signs Its Official Dissolution Decree' (14 April 2025); America, 21 Jan 2025; a

claims.t: Francis's motu proprio Ad Charisma Tuendum (22 July 2022) ended the practice of ordaining Opus Dei's prelate a bishop, moved oversight from the Dicastery for Bishops to the Dicastery for the Clergy, and changed reporting to annual; the prelate now receives the honorary title of protonotary apostolic.
s: CNA/EWTN, 'To guard the charism: in new decree, Pope Francis makes changes to Opus Dei,' 22 July 2022; Opus Dei, 'Ad charisma tuendum: Questions and Answers'; accessed 2026-06-25

claims.t: Opus Dei submitted its revised statutes to the Holy See on 11 June 2025, but as of 16 February 2026 Leo XIV had not approved them, telling the prelate the process 'continues in its study phase' with no foreseeable publication date — a live, unresolved restructuring.
s: ZENIT, 'Nine Questions and Answers Regarding the Process of Adapting Opus Dei's Statutes,' 23 June 2025; EWTN Vatican/NCRegister, 'Pope Leo XIV Tells Opus Dei No Decision Yet on Revised Statutes,' Feb

claims.t: The Legionaries of Christ, founded by serial abuser Marcial Maciel (≥60 victims), were placed under a Vatican papal delegate in May 2010 after a 2009–10 apostolic visitation, and survive in rehabilitated form with 1,327 members at the end of 2025 (3 bishops, 1,049 priests, 203 in formation, 72 novices).
s: EWTN Vatican, 'Legionaries Leader on Renewal After Maciel Scandal'; Legionaries of Christ, 'Statistics' (end-2025: 1,327 members); accessed 2026-06-25

claims.t: The Society of Jesus, the Church's largest male order and Francis's own, has fallen from a 1965 peak of ~36,038 to about 13,995 at the end of 2023 (a ~13,800–14,000 band), with 2023 seeing only 314 novices enter worldwide against 319 deaths and Africa the only growth region.
s: Catholic World Report, 'Prominent Jesuit: The Society of Jesus is in profound decline,' 24 May 2024; CNA, 'Halving of Jesuit numbers is a lesson in humility'; accessed 2026-06-25

claims.t: Professed religious sisters worldwide fell from 599,228 (end-2022) to 589,423 (end-2023), a 1.6% drop driven by deaths among an aging population, with North America (−3.6%) and South America (−3%) declining while Africa grew (+2.2% 2022–23, +2.6% 2024).
s: Vatican News, 'New Church statistics reveal growing Catholic population, fewer pastoral workers,' 20 March 2025; Global Sisters Report, 'Population of sisters'; accessed 2026-06-25

claims.t: US religious sisters fell from nearly 80,000 in 2000 to around 35,000 by 2025 (per Georgetown's CARA), with roughly eight in ten aged 70 or older and a 2019 LCWR estimate that as many as 300 of ~420 US women's institutes are in their last decades.
s: OSV News, 'As numbers decline, communities age, women religious urged to discern their emerging future,' Aug 2025; NCR, 'Studies chart diminishment of US sisters' numbers'; accessed 2026-06-25

claims.t: As the orders shrank, leadership of Catholic institutions passed from religious to laity: US Catholic hospital CEOs went from 196 religious / 420 lay (1988) to 45 religious / 525 lay (1996) to zero sister CEOs by 2019, with congregations creating 'public juridic persons' to preserve Catholic identity after the founders are gone.
s: Catholic Health Association / Health Progress, chausa.org; Global Sisters Report, 'As fewer sisters serve in health care'; accessed 2026-06-25

claims.t: Vatican officials themselves identify the new movements as structurally abuse-prone for reasons cutting across the left–right axis — both tight 'authoritarian' movements that exclude critics and loosely 'fluid' ones lacking accountability — with canonist Linda Ghisoni noting that bodies 'waving the banner of orthodoxy' are now under abuse investigation.
s: NCR, 'Purging silence: Vatican expands abuse prevention to lay movements'; NCR, 'Reform or suppression'; accessed 2026-06-25

claims.t: The Neocatechumenal Way (founded 1964 by Kiko Argüello and Carmen Hernández) claims about one million members in roughly 40,000 communities, holds Benedict XVI's definitive 11 May 2008 approval as a 'diocesan form of Christian initiation,' and remains a going concern with recurrent Vatican corrections of its distinctive liturgical practices.
s: Vatican.va, Decree of approval of the Statutes of the Neocatechumenal Way; CNA coverage; neocatechumenaleiter.org; accessed 2026-06-25

claims.t: Communion and Liberation saw Fr. Julián Carrón resign the presidency on 15 November 2021 (succeeded by lay president Davide Prosperi under new term-limit rules), with the Holy See appointing a special delegate over its Memores Domini branch in September 2021 and Francis repeatedly urging it to 'preserve the unity.
s: NCR/CNA, 'Fr. Julián Carrón resigns as president of Communion and Liberation'; CNA, 'Pope Francis to Communion and Liberation: Preserve the unity'; accessed 2026-06-25

claims.t: The Community of Sant'Egidio (founded 1968 by Andrea Riccardi) functions as a non-state diplomatic actor, having mediated the General Peace Agreement that ended Mozambique's civil war (signed in Rome 4 October 1992), and remained active in Mozambican diplomacy and refugee 'Humanitarian Corridors' in 2024–2025.
s: Community of Sant'Egidio, santegidio.org; Britannica 'Community of Sant'Egidio'; accessed 2026-06-25

claims.t: The Catholic Charismatic Renewal, by its own reckoning touching more than 120 million Catholics, is now served by CHARIS (instituted 8 December 2018, statutes in force 9 June 2019), a single international 'service' rather than an association; Leo XIV received its members on 30 May 2026.
s: Vatican News, 'CHARIS: a new service for the Catholic Charismatic Renewal,' 2019; Vatican.va, Leo XIV 'To Members of the Catholic Charismatic Renewal,' 30 May 2026; accessed 2026-06-25

claims.t: The Focolare Movement (founded 1943 by Chiara Lubich) published its first abuse report on 31 March 2023 and an independent GCPS Consulting inquiry into a French case ('JMM') that found at least 26 victims over decades (1958–2020) with leadership failures, prompting new central and local safeguarding commissions under president Margaret Karram.
s: Focolare Movement, focolare.org, GCPS independent inquiry; NCR, 'Abuse report from global Catholic group Focolare leaves many questions unanswered'; accessed 2026-06-25

claims.t: The lived-religion field — centrally Robert Orsi, with Tweed and McGuire — reframes religion as embodied, material, relational practice ('a network of relationships between heaven and earth') rather than doctrine or affiliation, and explicitly criticizes privileging 'real'/textual over 'bogus'/popular religion — the exact bias this corpus's modality exhibits.
s: Orsi 2005 (Princeton UP, via author/publisher pages); Tweed 2006 (Harvard UP); McGuire 2008 (Oxford UP); accessed 2026-06-25

claims.t: The Vatican's 2001 Directory on Popular Piety and the Liturgy is an institutional theory of popular devotion — subordinating it to the liturgy ('summit and source'), measuring it against the Gospel, and forbidding magic/superstition — proving the lived/popular layer is recognized and governed by the institution, not invented by outside scholars.
s: Congregation for Divine Worship, Directory on Popular Piety and the Liturgy, 17 Dec 2001, vatican.va; accessed 2026-06-25

claims.t: Pope Francis, formed at Aparecida (2007), made popular piety central to Evangelii Gaudium (2013, §§122–126), calling it 'the people's mysticism' with 'an active evangelizing power' — the magisterium itself arguing the devotional layer is a primary, not subordinate, form of the faith.
s: Francis, Evangelii Gaudium (24 Nov 2013) §§122–126, vatican.va; accessed 2026-06-25

claims.t: Our Lady of Guadalupe (apparitions to Juan Diego, 1531, Tepeyac) functions as the foundational identity-marker of Mexican/Latin American Catholicism — a mestiza Virgin fusing Indigenous and European symbols — and her basilica is the most-visited Catholic shrine on earth at ~20 million pilgrims a year (~9 million around 12 December).
s: Britannica, 'Our Lady of Guadalupe'; guadalupeshrine.org; catholicsandcultures.org; accessed 2026-06-25

claims.t: Lourdes (~6m pilgrims/year; 1858; Vatican-commended with its own feast; ~70 healings declared miraculous since the 1860s by a deliberately skeptical medical bureau) operates as a healing shrine whose appeal is sociological more than medical, and Fatima (~4m/year; 1917) carries a distinctively political-prophetic charge.
s: America Magazine, 9 Feb 2022; Religions (MDPI) 2022, 13(11):1028; accessed 2026-06-25

claims.t: On 19 Sep 2024 the DDF (Fernández, approved by Francis) granted a nihil obstat to Medjugorje devotion, explicitly NOT declaring the apparitions supernatural but recognizing spiritual fruits — the first major application of the DDF's new 17 May 2024 six-category Norms, a juridical tool designed to bless popular devotion's fruits while withholding verdict on its truth claims.
s: DDF, 'The Queen of Peace' note (19 Sep 2024) and Norms (17 May 2024), vatican.va; Vatican News and USCCB 2024; accessed 2026-06-25

claims.t: On 7 September 2025, Pope Leo XIV canonized Carlo Acutis (1991–2006; died at 15 of leukemia; built a Eucharistic-miracles website; body displayed in Assisi in jeans/sneakers; 'God's influencer') as the first millennial saint, with Pier Giorgio Frassati (1901–1925; mountaineer, servant of the poor) — both absent from the corpus's current-state docs.
s: NPR, WaPo (both 7 Sep 2025); CNN (13 Jun 2025); USCCB 2025; Vatican News 2025; Britannica; accessed 2026-06-25

claims.t: The 2025 Jubilee ('Pilgrims of Hope,' 24 Dec 2024 – 6 Jan 2026) drew 33,475,369 pilgrims from 185 countries to Rome per the Dicastery for Evangelization, with the Jubilee of Youth alone recording ~13 million passages — the largest concentrated demonstration of lived/pilgrimage Catholicism in the corpus's window, and absent from the corpus.
s: Dicastery for Evangelization figures via Salesian Bulletin (8 Jan 2026) and 2025 Jubilee compilation; Euronews (24 Dec 2024) for projection; accessed 2026-06-25

claims.t: The US National Eucharistic Revival (2022–2024) and 10th National Eucharistic Congress (Indianapolis, 17–21 July 2024; ~50,000–60,000 attendees; first since 1941) represent the institution's deliberate top-down attempt to manufacture weekly/affective devotional intensity (adoration, procession) against secular drift and Pentecostal appeal.
s: Wikipedia, '10th National Eucharistic Congress'; Catholic News Agency, July 2024; accessed 2026-06-25

claims.t: Folk-Catholic syncretism — Día de los Muertos, Afro-Brazilian/Caribbean traditions, and especially the fast-growing, Vatican-condemned Santa Muerte cult — shows demand for embodied, personally-protective lived religion is strong enough that, where the institution won't supply it, the marginalized manufacture it outside and against the institution; Santa Muerte's scale (millions of devotees) is an estimate, direction not magnitude.
s: Religions (MDPI) 2021, 12(3):220; folk-Catholicism anthropology sources; accessed 2026-06-25

claims.t: The central payoff — that lived/devotional intensity, not survey affiliation, is the deeper predictor of Catholic resilience or erosion, and that the Global-South demographic shift moves the Church toward populations for whom the textual tradition is least central and the devotional most — is an interpretive synthesis on the corpus's own data (docs 05–07) plus the lived-religion literature, not a single sourced fact.
s: Synthesis of corpus docs 05–07 with McGuire 2008 and Orsi 2005; accessed 2026-06-25

claims.t: Document 07 frames the 23 Eastern Catholic churches as harmonious internal diversity and names the Syro-Malabar Church only as a membership figure and de-Latinization success, omitting that it has been split for decades by the Ernakulam-Angamaly liturgy dispute, one of contemporary Catholicism's most acute internal conflicts.
s: Corpus 07_Comparative_And_Adjacent.md §V; CathNews 2025-07-02; NCRonline. Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: In August 2021 the Syro-Malabar Synod decreed a uniform Qurbana (priest facing the people for the Liturgy of the Word, facing the altar for the Eucharistic Prayer), which a majority of Ernakulam-Angamaly clergy, long accustomed to facing the people throughout, refused.
s: NCRonline; The News Minute; Catholics & Cultures / liturgy history. Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: St. Mary's Cathedral Basilica, Ernakulam, was closed from 27 November 2022; on Christmas Eve 2022 factions fought inside, the altar was dragged across the sanctuary and vessels crashed to the floor, police cleared the church, and the basilica remained practically paralyzed for ~three years, reopening to public liturgy on 1 December 2025.
s: NCRonline; Onmanorama 2022-12-28; Infovaticana 2025-12-04. Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: Pope Francis appointed Cyril Vasiľ as pontifical delegate (Aug 2023), accepted Cardinal Alencherry's resignation (7 Dec 2023), oversaw a 10 Dec 2023 ultimatum threatening de facto laicization of non-compliant priests by 3 July 2024, and issued direct video appeals to the Ernakulam-Angamaly faithful; apostolic administrators including Bosco Puthur followed and failed.
s: The Pillar 2023-12-07; EWTN/Crux/Catholic World Report; NCRonline; Aleteia. Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: On 19 June 2025 Major Archbishop Raphael Thattil and Vicar Joseph Pamplany signed a Holy-See-approved compromise letting Ernakulam-Angamaly priests celebrate facing the people while requiring at least one uniform-rite Mass per parish on Sundays/feasts; canonical penalties were lifted for all but two cases and the contested curia replaced. It took effect 3 July 2025.
s: The Tablet; CathNews 2025-07-02; Aleteia 2025-07-08; Catholic World Report 2025-07-10. Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: On 7 July 2025 the Holy See announced that Pope Leo XIV had concluded Cyril Vasiľ's mandate as papal delegate, the formal Roman signal that the crisis was resolved; outlets framed it as Leo withdrawing the delegate after an agreement avoided schism.
s: Catholic World Report 2025-07-10; Catholic Culture; Doc 05 (papal transition). Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: On 10 December 2025, One Church One Qurbana supporters of the uniform rite occupied St. Mary's Basilica, locked it, obstructed the versus populum liturgies, and posted defamatory images of the major archbishop and vicar; the church condemned the protests and on 10 January 2026 issued a circular appealing for peace, showing the truce is fragile.
s: Outlook India / Metrovaartha (Dec 2025); The Pillar 2025-12-11. Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: Because the Syro-Malabar versus populum Mass was popularized post-Vatican II by Cardinal Joseph Parecattil (Ernakulam 1956-1984) and the ad orientem uniform rite is presented as a recovery of the authentic East Syriac form, the Western traditionalist/progressive axis inverts in Kerala: the synod's restoration is the contested innovation locally, and the people-facing Mass is the defended tradition.
s: NCRonline; Catholics & Cultures / restored-liturgy history. Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: The Syro-Malabar war operationalizes Doc 07's 'every mechanism of endurance is also a mechanism of pathology,' tests the limits of Roman authority over a sui iuris church, and answers Doc 03's Open Question #6 in India — the largest Eastern test case in the corpus's flagged growth zone.
s: Corpus docs 03, 05, 07; sources [1]-[15]. Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: Marko Ivan Rupnik (b. 1954, Slovenia), Jesuit priest and former director of Rome's Centro Aletti, made roughly 220-232 mosaic installations worldwide, including the Vatican's Redemptoris Mater chapel, Lourdes, Fatima, San Giovanni Rotondo, the St. John Paul II National Shrine in Washington, and Madrid's Almudena Cathedral.
s: EWTN/CNA 2025; Crux Oct 2025.

claims.t: Across 2022-2025 reporting Rupnik was accused by more than 20 (some accounts at least 40) overwhelmingly former or current consecrated women tied to the Loyola Community he co-founded in Slovenia, of spiritual, psychological, and sexual abuse from the mid-1980s to 2018.
s: Detroit Catholic 2025; America Sept 2023; RNS/GSR Mar 2025.

claims.t: After a 2019 complaint the CDF found Rupnik guilty of absolving in confession a woman with whom he had had sexual relations (canon 1378), declaring excommunication in May 2020 for an act dated 2015; it was lifted within the same month after his stated repentance.
s: RNS/America Dec 2022-Sept 2023; NCR/CNA.

claims.t: In Sept 2023 the Diocese of Rome under Cardinal Angelo De Donatis stated its review found gravely anomalous procedures around Rupnik's 2020 excommunication and its lifting, with well-founded doubts even about the excommunication request, and forwarded its report to Vatican authorities.
s: America Magazine Sept 19, 2023.

claims.t: The Vatican doctrine office first declined to open a case, invoking the statute of limitations for the abuse of adults; after public pressure Pope Francis personally waived it on Oct 27, 2023, enabling the DDF to prosecute.
s: Crux Oct 2025; RNS Oct 13, 2025; NCR/CNA.

claims.t: On June 15, 2023 Superior General Arturo Sosa dismissed Rupnik from the Society of Jesus for his stubborn refusal to observe the vow of obedience, not for abuse; Rupnik was then incardinated in 2023 into the Diocese of Koper, Slovenia, remaining a priest.
s: RNS Oct 2025; America Sept 2023; Crux Oct 2025.

claims.t: A tribunal of five judges (women and clerics external to the DDF and Roman Curia) was named Oct 9-13, 2025; Pope Leo XIV confirmed on Nov 7, 2025 the canonical trial had begun; as of March 2026 the victims' lawyer reported total silence; as of June 2026 Rupnik has not been laicized and remains a priest of Koper.
s: Vatican News Oct 2025; RNS Oct 2025; InfoVaticana Mar 24, 2026.

claims.t: With no Vatican-wide directive custodians diverged: Lourdes announced on March 31, 2025 it would cover the mosaics on the Basilica of the Rosary doors, and Washington's JPII Shrine and the Knights of Columbus moved to cover theirs, while Fatima decided not to remove its mosaics (suspending only promotional use) on the view that the art belongs to the church not the artist.
s: CNA Mar 2025; CNA/EWTN Apr 2, 2025.

claims.t: Catholic Social Teaching is a cumulative, self-referential body of doctrine taught chiefly through papal encyclicals at the level of the ordinary (authoritative but largely non-infallible) magisterium, running from Rerum Novarum (1891) through a chain of anniversary encyclicals to Fratelli Tutti (2020) and Magnifica Humanitas (2026).
s: Pontifical Council for Justice and Peace, Compendium of the Social Doctrine of the Church (Vatican, presented 2 April 2004), https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/pontifical_councils/justpeace/documents/

claims.t: CST's principles are a short, stable list — human dignity (the architectonic foundation), the common good, subsidiarity, solidarity, the universal destination of goods, the dignity of work, and the preferential option for the poor — each crystallized in a particular encyclical (e.g., subsidiarity formally introduced in Quadragesimo Anno 1931; dignity-of-work / labor-over-capital in Laborem Exercens 1981).
s: Compendium of the Social Doctrine of the Church (2004); Cambridge University Press, Catholic Social Teaching, ch. 17 'Subsidiarity'; Seton Hall, 'Principles of Catholic Social Teaching.' Accessed 2026

claims.t: Subsidiarity is structurally double — it both forbids higher bodies from supplanting lower ones (the right's anti-statist reading) and requires higher bodies to assist when lower ones cannot secure the common good (the left's interventionist reading) — so the doctrine's seizability from both sides is a structural feature, not merely partisan opportunism.
s: Pius XI, Quadragesimo Anno (1931); Cambridge University Press, Catholic Social Teaching, ch. 17; Seton Hall and Virginia Catholic Conference principle summaries. Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: The 'preferential option for the poor' originated not in a papal encyclical but in the Latin American Church — its components at CELAM Medellin (1968), the full phrase as a section title at Puebla (1979), and its theological articulation by Gustavo Gutierrez in A Theology of Liberation (1971) — then migrated upward into the universal magisterium with the liberationist political program stripped out.
s: CELAM Medellin (1968) and Puebla (1979) documents via NCReporter and America Magazine; Gustavo Gutierrez, A Theology of Liberation (1971). https://www.ncronline.org/blogs/road-peace/gustavo-gutierrez-

claims.t: The 1991 fight over whether John Paul II's Centesimus Annus endorsed capitalism — the Novak/Weigel/Neuhaus 'neoconservative' reading (a guarded endorsement of the free economy) vs. the Catholic-left rejoinder that the pope 'didn't and couldn't have written' such an endorsement — is the worked template for the ongoing contest in which the same CST text is claimed by both political camps.
s: Acton Institute (M. Novak); Church Life Journal (Notre Dame), 'Catholic Social Doctrine Isn't a Surrogate for Capitalism'; NCRegister, 'Hidden Lessons of Centesimus Annus.' Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: A live, organized strand — Adrian Vermeule's 'common good constitutionalism' (2020 Atlantic essay 'Beyond Originalism'; 2022 Polity book), within a wider Deneen–Ahmari–Pappin New Right and the earlier Tradinista provocation — transposes CST's central term 'the common good' out of its postconciliar liberty-friendly register into an explicitly anti-liberal one, against the liberal-democratic settlement the postconciliar Church had largely accepted.
s: Adrian Vermeule, 'Beyond Originalism,' The Atlantic, March 2020; Common Good Constitutionalism (Polity, 2022); NCReporter Steubenville 'Restoring a Nation' coverage (Oct 2022); critiques in The Americ

claims.t: Pope Leo XIV (Robert Prevost, elected 8 May 2025) chose his name as a deliberate echo of Leo XIII and Rerum Novarum, and his first encyclical Magnifica Humanitas — signed 15 May 2026 (the 135th anniversary of Rerum Novarum), presented 25 May 2026 — is a substantial CST document on AI and the dignity of work that explicitly claims the Rerum Novarum lineage, constituting the clearest deliberate doctrinal re-centering on social teaching by a pope in a generation.
s: Leo XIV, Magnifica Humanitas (signed 15 May 2026), https://www.vatican.va/content/leo-xiv/en/encyclicals/documents/20260515-magnifica-humanitas.html; Vatican News and NCR reporting, May–June 2026; cro

claims.t: The Church's geopolitical activity asserted in doc 08 (Driver 8) is its social teaching externalized: development and debt advocacy speaks Populorum Progressio / Caritas in Veritate; migration speaks Fratelli Tutti; climate speaks Laudato Si'; AI-and-labor speaks Magnifica Humanitas — so whether CST coheres or fractures by 2050 directly determines whether the Church speaks geopolitically with one accent or several.
s: Synthesis across Populorum Progressio (1967), Fratelli Tutti (2020), Laudato Si' (2015), Magnifica Humanitas (2026), and corpus doc 08 (Drivers 5, 7, 8). Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: By 2050 CST will function as a partially-unifying common language whose core (dignity, the poor, development, work) coheres across a Global-South-majority Church that reads CST through development/debt/colonialism, while its application to contested Western questions (the market, the state, the meaning of 'the common good,' life-adjacent issues) remains an axis of the traditionalist–progressive polarization the corpus centers on.
s: Synthesis of corpus doc 08 (Drivers 1, 5, 8) with Populorum Progressio development lineage and the Medellin/Puebla/Gutierrez option-for-the-poor genealogy. Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: Cardinal Joseph Bernardin's 'consistent ethic of life' / 'seamless garment' (December 1983 Fordham address) was a deliberate attempt to hold the Church's life concerns — abortion, nuclear war, capital punishment, euthanasia, poverty — as one indivisible fabric, and its fraying under polarization (each camp keeping its half) is a leading indicator for whether CST's both/and structure survives.
s: Fordham University materials; Chicago Catholic (2018); America Magazine (2017); CHA (2008) on Bernardin's consistent ethic of life. Accessed 2026-06-25.

claims.t: Amazon launched what is generally credited as the first modern retail media network in 2012, beginning with sponsored-product search ads against its own first-party shopper data.
Amazon reported approximately $56 billion in advertising revenue in 2024, up ~18% year-over-year, and ~$17.3B in advertising services revenue in Q4 2025.
eMarketer projected Amazon's U.S. retail media ad revenue would pass $60.6 billion in 2025 and climb to ~$69.7 billion in 2026.
Google reversed its plan to deprecate third-party cookies in Chrome on April 22, 2025, after repeated delays; Chrome continues to allow third-party cookies unless users disable them.

Dramatic figures circulating for Google's October 2025 Privacy Sandbox API sunset (e.g., 85% attribution inaccuracy, 42-67% reduction in advertiser spend) trace to a single analytical blog and are not corroborated by Tier 1-3 sources.

Linear TV's share of time U.S. viewers spent watching video on a TV screen fell from 72.2% in 2020 to a forecast ~56.5% by the end of 2024, and streaming surpassed broadcast+cable combined (43.7%) by February 2025.

U.S. CTV ad spend rose to $23.6 billion in 2024, up 16% year-over-year per IAB, reaching ~$26.6B in 2025 (IAB advertiser-reported); eMarketer's broader measure puts 2025 at $33.35B, forecast to surpass linear TV ad spend around 2028 at ~$46.9B.

By Q2 2025 ad-supported content captured 73.6% of total U.S. TV viewing time; as of Q1 2024, 38% of premium VOD subscriptions were ad-supported (up from 31% in Q2 2023); FAST reaches more than one-third of the U.S. population.
Both Disney/Hulu's self-service ad tool and Roku Ads Manager publish a $500 minimum to launch a campaign, the entry point that converted national TV from an agency product into an SMB product.
Disney's self-service advertising platform (anchored by Hulu Ad Manager) grew roughly nine-fold, with over 75,000 businesses signed up, and is expanding to Disney+ and ESPN+ inventory.

MNTN, a performance-CTV platform whose customer base is ~96% SMBs, IPO'd on the NYSE on May 22, 2025 at $16/share (closing +27% day one); client count grew ~89% YoY in Q1 2025 and Q3 2025 revenue was ~$70M (+31%). MNTN estimated a $60B-$120B serviceable market.
Vibe.co was founded in August 2021, launched September 2022, reached a $100M revenue run rate in under two years, and raised a $50M Series B led by Hedosophia at a $410M valuation in September 2025.

Vibe.co reported 5,000+ brands as of its September 2025 Series B; Walmart's June 23, 2026 acquisition release cites 10,000+ advertisers — consistent with growth, but both are company-reported figures.

CTV advertising historically could report exposure (impressions, reach, completion, modeled ROAS) but not incrementality — whether the ad caused a sale — and as of 2026 only ~15% of advertisers said they strongly trusted their retail-media measurement.

Walmart's CTV closed-loop measurement claims surfaced at NewFronts 2026 (44% median viewing on successful campaigns; 65% of surveyed customers say CTV ads aided discovery) and a Scintilla CPG case study (2.97% sales lift, 72% win-back) are Walmart-reported and vendor-favorable, not independently audited; Digiday separately flags a remaining incrementality hurdle.

Walmart Connect generated $6.4 billion in advertising revenue in FY2026, up 46% year-over-year; in Q4 FY26 advertising and membership income together were roughly one-third of operating profit; the business draws on first-party data from 150M+ weekly customers.
Walmart renamed its media business from 'Walmart Media Group' to 'Walmart Connect' on January 28, 2021, with a three-pillar strategy: owned properties, in-store screens, and first-party data offsite.

Walmart completed its $2.3 billion acquisition of VIZIO ($11.50/share) on December 3, 2024, acquiring the SmartCast TV operating system, ~18M active SmartCast accounts (of ~23M opted-in devices), and VIZIO's ACR (automatic content recognition) viewing data.

In late April 2026 Walmart Connect launched 'Connect Select,' a curated CTV marketplace inside the Walmart DSP with Magnite, PubMatic, FreeWheel and Index Exchange as SSPs and VIZIO/Paramount/Warner Bros. Discovery inventory; on May 28, 2026 it made first-party audiences available inside Yahoo DSP routed through Magnite's supply-side tech against VIZIO CTV inventory.

Walmart announced on June 23, 2026 it would acquire Vibe.co, reported at $1.4 billion (WSJ), structured per trade reporting as roughly $1.2B cash plus ~$180M founder/executive retention, with close expected by end of FY2027 subject to HSR antitrust waiting-period clearance; founders Arthur Querou (CEO) and Franck Tetzlaff (CTO) join Walmart Connect.
Vibe.co was co-founded by Arthur Querou (Co-Founder/CEO) and Franck Tetzlaff (Co-Founder/CTO); no source attests a founder named 'Stan Coignard,' which appears to be a brief error.

Tetzlaff co-founded Doctolib and was CTO of Frichti; Querou founded Appinest and MotionLead and was Chief Mobile Officer of Adikteev; together they previously built KMTX, sold to Seedtag in June 2022.
Vibe is HQ'd in New York (131 Varick St) with a primarily Europe-based technical team and US-based sales/operations/marketing — a deliberate dual French/NYC structure.
Vibe consistently positions itself as 'the Google Ads of streaming TV,' letting marketers run streaming TV 'the way they run paid social.
Users can register, target, drag-and-drop creative and go live 'within minutes' with budgets 'as low as $50/day,' per CEO Querou.
No source consulted supports a '$500 minimum' entry; all attest '$50/day.' The $500 figure in the brief is unconfirmed and flagged.
The platform unifies AI creative generation (Vibe Studio), an ML bidding engine (Vibe IQ2), an AI Assistant, and direct publisher access (Vibe Connect) in one self-serve interface.
Vibe self-reported ~10% of platform ads are AI-generated as of the Series B, projecting ~30% in 2026.

Vibe runs its own demand-side platform with direct integrations to most major streaming platforms (excluding Netflix, Hulu, YouTube initially) and nearly every large SSP — not a reseller skin on a third-party DSP.

In November 2025 Vibe launched 'Certified Supply,' restricting buyable inventory to direct publisher integrations and opt-in Deal-ID whitelists, dropping open-market resellers after a test ad triggered ~500 bid requests (vs 1-5 expected).
Vibe integrates mobile-attribution platforms AppsFlyer and Adjust for lower-funnel measurement and says it is distancing itself from data brokers.
Vibe self-reports reach across 120M+ US households and 500+ apps and channels.

Vibe's headline average ~250% ROAS (2.5x), '4x better than traditional TV,' and ~20% sales lift are company self-reported marketing averages with no disclosed methodology, control group, or third-party audit.

Dramatic per-client figures (Meshki 2,976% ROAS/week; ONEHOPE 13x/month; Sijo +17% AOV; cost-per-conversion $80→$15-20) are selected customer testimonials, the upper tail, not the average or verified.
Vibe raised a ~$7M (reported $7.5M elsewhere) seed in 2022 led by Elaia Partners and launched its platform that year.

Vibe raised a $22.5M Series A (announced late Feb/Mar 2024) led by Singular, with Elaia, Motier Ventures, Sequoia Scout Fund and ad-tech angels; 2,000+ clients and eight-figure 2023 revenue at the time.

Vibe raised a $50M (€42M) Series B announced ~Sept 30/Oct 1 2025, led by Hedosophia at a $410M post-money valuation, with Singular, Elaia, QuantumLight, Illusian and angels Carolyn Everson and Nirav Tolia (board).
Vibe had raised ~$79.5M total by the Series B and stated it expected to be profitable by end of 2025.

Vibe self-reports a ~$100M revenue run-rate reached in under two years; a run-rate annualizes a recent period and differs from trailing revenue, with aggregators (GetLatka) listing ~$33.3M actual revenue — a gap material to the deal multiple.

Walmart announced on June 23, 2026 an agreement to acquire Vibe.co; terms were officially undisclosed but WSJ and The Information reported ~$1.4B including a ~$180M executive-retention payment; HSR clearance required, close expected by end of FY2027.

The ~$1.4B price is ~3.4x the $410M Series B valuation set ~9 months earlier and ~12.6x the ~$100M run-rate (far above public peer MNTN at ~1x revenue); effective multiple is higher if trailing revenue is nearer $33M.
Walmart describes Vibe as serving 10,000+ SME/mid-market advertisers at acquisition (up from 5,000+ brands at Series B); the founders and broader team are expected to join Walmart Connect post-close.
On January 28, 2021, Walmart renamed its media business from Walmart Media Group to Walmart Connect, stating an ambition to become one of the top ten US advertising platforms.

At the 2021 rebrand Walmart cited 150 million weekly US customers, nearly 170,000 in-store digital screens across 4,500+ stores, a planned DSP launch for the 2021 holiday season, and a Trade Desk partnership.
Walmart's Vibe purchase continues a pattern of buying ad-tech rather than building it: Polymorph Labs (2019), Thunder (2021), VIZIO (2024), Vibe (2026).
Walmart's global advertising revenue was approximately $6.4 billion in FY26 (year ended Jan 31, 2026), up 46% year over year, a figure that includes VIZIO.
Walmart Connect US (the domestic retail media arm specifically) grew 41% year over year in Q4 FY26 (quarter ended Jan 31, 2026).
In Q4 FY26, Walmart reported global advertising growth of 37% including VIZIO, with Walmart Connect US at 41% within that.
In Q1 FY26 (quarter ended ~April 2025), Walmart global advertising grew ~50% YoY while Walmart Connect US grew 31%, with early VIZIO gains lifting the blended line.
Walmart's prior-year (FY25) advertising sales were roughly $3.4 billion, framing the steepness of the FY26 jump to ~$6.4B.
Advertising and membership fees together accounted for roughly one-third of Walmart's operating income in Q4 FY26.
VIZIO-facilitated digital advertising has been estimated to carry margins near 70%.
Walmart CFO John David Rainey told analysts the ad business still has 'long ways to go' to reach best-in-class competitors, framing runway over current scale.
VIZIO inventory has appeared in Walmart Connect Ad Center's display beta tab in 2026, signaling self-serve integration of VIZIO supply.

Sam's Club rebranded its advertising business as the Member Access Platform (MAP) in June 2022, tying omnichannel ad campaigns to actual member purchases in-app and in-club using decades of first-party data.
Walmart agreed to acquire VIZIO on February 20, 2024 at $11.50/share in cash, approximately $2.3 billion fully-diluted equity value.
Walmart completed the VIZIO acquisition on December 3, 2024; VIZIO became a wholly-owned subsidiary and its Class A stock was delisted from the NYSE the same day.
At acquisition, VIZIO's SmartCast operating system had over 19 million active accounts (18M+ at agreement, 19.1M for Q3 2024), growing ~400% since 2018, with 5.8 billion streaming hours in Q3 2024.

VIZIO's automatic content recognition (ACR) identifies what is on-screen by sampling picture/audio, enabling targeting (what a household watches) and measurement (whether a household saw an ad), and is the signal Walmart fuses with purchase data to close the loop.
At acquisition VIZIO's Platform+ segment (advertising/data) accounted for a majority of company gross profit and held over 500 direct advertiser relationships including many Fortune 500.
As of March 24, 2026, VIZIO reached ~92 million households and the VIZIO operating system covered roughly 25-30% of US households; Walmart Connect touches 150 million weekly US customers.
Walmart rolled out a unified login across VIZIO and onn. (Walmart house-brand) TVs to track how streaming engagement maps to retail purchases.
In its first year inside Walmart, VIZIO delivered triple-digit advertising-revenue growth in Q4 FY26 (quarter ended Jan 31, 2026), from a comparatively small base.
Walmart stated VIZIO and Walmart Connect would operate separately for the foreseeable future, with founder William Wang continuing as VIZIO CEO reporting to Walmart US leadership.

Walmart Connect launched Connect Select, a curated programmatic CTV marketplace inside Walmart DSP combining premium streaming inventory with Walmart first-party data and closed-loop measurement, on April 27, 2026.
Connect Select's SSP (supply-side platform) partners are Magnite, PubMatic, FreeWheel, and Index Exchange.
Connect Select's publisher partners include VIZIO, Paramount, and Warner Bros. Discovery.

Connect Select targets mid-sized and smaller advertisers and integrates with campaign-management tools Pacvue and Skai, reducing complexity that historically concentrated CTV among large programmatic teams.
Walmart CTV campaigns delivered a median of 44% new-to-brand buyers in FY26, verified against actual Walmart purchase data.

On May 28, 2026, Walmart Connect made its first-party audiences and closed-loop measurement available inside Yahoo DSP, routed through Magnite's supply-side technology, covering VIZIO CTV inventory, initially as a closed proof-of-concept.
Magnite's supply-side decisioning is designed to reduce signal loss and improve audience match rates, and to extend Walmart's data-enablement model across multiple DSPs.
Adam Roodman (GM, Yahoo DSP) and Sean Buckley (President of Revenue and Market Strategy, Magnite) are quoted in the May 28, 2026 Walmart Connect data-access announcement.

Google Display & Video 360 (DV360), Google's enterprise DSP, is named alongside Yahoo DSP and Magnite in Walmart's June 2026 description of its growing media ecosystem, indicating a multi-DSP strategy.
Best Buy named Magnite its exclusive SSP/curation partner in September 2025 using a structurally similar retail-data-into-programmatic-CTV model, indicating an industry pattern.
Vibe.co is a self-serve CTV platform letting advertisers run streaming campaigns 'the way they run paid social: measurable, fast to launch, and optimized for better outcomes' (CEO Arthur Querou).

Per the acquisition announcement, Vibe brings self-serve activation, direct supply-partner integrations, proprietary ad technology, performance-driven optimization, more than 10,000 advertisers, and AI targeting/measurement.
The Walmart-Vibe combination is expected to support CTV adoption among SMB and mid-market advertisers including Walmart's third-party marketplace sellers.

Ryan Mayward, GM and Senior Vice President of Walmart Connect U.S., is the named Walmart executive in the June 23, 2026 Vibe announcement, framing the deal as making commerce media more accessible for advertisers of all sizes.
Walmart Marketplace has roughly 160,000-200,000 active third-party sellers (one cited figure: 160,000+ active, up ~40% YoY), a captive on-platform advertiser population.

Only about 25% of CTV campaigns currently carry lower-funnel (performance) objectives, and SMB streaming performance budgets remain small relative to search and social, indicating a largely unconverted long-tail TAM.
Walmart and VIZIO leadership have publicly described the strategy as a 'brand flywheel' connecting media, engagement, and commerce (Nyma Quidwai, Walmart).
John Furner became President and CEO of Walmart Inc. on February 1, 2026, succeeding Doug McMillon who retired January 31, 2026; the transition was announced November 14, 2025.
Furner started at Walmart as an hourly associate in 1993 and ran Sam's Club U.S. and then Walmart U.S. (since 2019) before becoming CEO.

Amazon's 2025 advertising business (~$60.6B retail media; >$68B all-in) is roughly 10x Walmart's $6.4B and commands ~79.7% US retail-media share versus Walmart's ~8.0%, with the two together absorbing over 84% of US retail-media budgets.

Walmart completed its $2.3 billion acquisition of VIZIO on December 3, 2024 at $11.50/share, bringing in the SmartCast operating system (~19M+ active accounts) and its ACR data, the owned-screen layer of the full-funnel stack.

Walmart completed its $2.3B acquisition of VIZIO on 2024-12-03 ($11.50/share), gaining SmartCast OS (~19M+ active accounts) and Inscape ACR data (currency-grade data from 24M+ opted-in TVs, ~79M viewers); VIZIO operates as a wholly owned subsidiary.

The Trade Desk's effective take is ~20% of gross spend ($2.4B revenue on ~$12B platform spend, 2024) while Amazon DSP charges ~1–2% on third-party media and ~0% on owned/O&O supply, capturing margin upstream as publisher/retailer.

By owning the OS (VIZIO), the data (Walmart Connect), and the self-serve front-end (Vibe), Walmart can collapse brand→DSP→SSP→publisher hops and capture publisher-side, data-fee, and buy-side margin — but only on the VIZIO-owned, Walmart-data slice; for most CTV impressions Walmart remains a toll-paying buyer.

Amazon Ads and Roku announced an exclusive partnership (2025-06-16) creating the largest authenticated US CTV footprint — ~80M households (~80%+ of US CTV homes per Comscore) accessible via Amazon DSP, fully available Q4 2025 — directly fortifying the SMB-CTV ground Walmart is buying into.

Walmart's Vibe.co acquisition is worth about $1.4 billion — roughly $1.2 billion in cash plus about $180 million in retention payments tied to top executives staying at Walmart for four years after close.
Walmart's official June 23, 2026 announcement disclosed no financial terms, stating only that the deal is subject to a Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period and expected to close by end of FY27.

At a ~$100M run rate the reported $1.4B price implies roughly 12.6x revenue, against the only public comparable, MNTN, trading at about 2.1x trailing sales (~$623M market cap / ~$299M TTM revenue) and down ~65% from its May 2025 IPO as of mid-June 2026.
Vibe raised a $50M Series B at a $410M valuation in September 2025; the reported $1.4B price is a ~3.4x markup in under nine months with no intervening financing event to reprice it.

Vibe is a buying layer, not a publisher: every impression runs through 100% direct publisher deals with Hulu, Disney+, Paramount+, Peacock, Tubi and 500+ apps, none of which Walmart owns; VIZIO supplies only a fraction of total CTV impressions.

Several streamers Vibe depends on for reach — Disney, Comcast/Peacock, Paramount, Fox/Tubi, Roku, Amazon — compete with Walmart in advertising or retail media, creating an incentive to restrict or worsen terms for a buying tool now owned by a retail rival.

Walmart Connect's CTV business runs on third-party DSPs (Magnite, Yahoo DSP, Google DV360); acquiring Vibe makes Walmart simultaneously a customer and competitor to those partners, who may deprioritize Walmart integrations or restrict inventory.

Folding a fast-moving French/NYC startup (founders Arthur Querou and Franck Tetzlaff) into Bentonville retail-corporate carries high base-rate failure risk; the direct analogue is Microsoft's 2019 PromoteIQ retail-media acquisition, which lost key execs and clients and was quietly sunset toward Criteo around 2024-2025.

Co-founders Arthur Querou (CEO) and Franck Tetzlaff (CTO) and the broader team are expected to join Walmart Connect post-close; Vibe states the platform 'operates unchanged' with its no-minimum self-serve entry point until the expected end-FY27 close.

Vibe's value rests on 10,000+ SMB/mid-market advertisers — the highest-churn, most support-intensive segment in advertising — implying ~$10,000 average revenue per advertiser; no public Vibe churn or net-retention figure exists, so durability of the ~$100M run rate is unproven.

Roughly $180M — about an eighth of the ~$1.4B consideration — is exec retention vesting over four years, signaling that much of the value lives in the founders/team rather than the code, and creating vest-and-rest and second-layer-talent-flight risk.

In February 2017 VIZIO agreed to pay $2.2M ($1.5M FTC + $1M New Jersey, $300K suspended) to settle charges it used default-on ACR software to collect second-by-second viewing data from 11 million smart TVs without consent — 100B+ data points/day, demographic appends sold to third parties — and the consent order required affirmative opt-in consent going forward.

Walmart's 2024 $2.3B VIZIO acquisition drew advocacy calls for FTC/DOJ scrutiny over concentration and data hoarding, received an FTC second request (with an HSR withdraw-and-refile in March 2024), and closed December 3, 2024 after the waiting period expired without a block or public consent decree — a scrutiny-then-clearance precedent for the Vibe HSR review.

2026 is widely characterized as the year U.S. privacy law shifts from creation to enforcement: ~20 state comprehensive laws, three new ones (Indiana, Kentucky, Rhode Island) effective Jan 1 2026, expanded CCPA/CPRA regulations the same day, a CPPA $1.35M penalty in late 2025, and sensitive-data opt-in regimes bearing on linking viewing and shopping data.

Walmart's global ad business did ~$6.4B in FY26 (+46%), ~1% of total revenue and roughly one-tenth the size of Amazon's ad business; Amazon's advertising-services revenue was $56.2B in 2024 and ~$68.6B in 2025 (+22%).

The standard 'cookie deprecation boosts first-party retail data' tailwind is muddier than claimed: Google reversed Chrome third-party-cookie deprecation in April 2025 but deprecated its remaining Privacy Sandbox APIs in October 2025, leaving a fragmented measurement environment with degraded attribution accuracy — a headwind for the closed-loop ROAS proof Vibe's SMB retention depends on.

Vibe's self-serve entry point is $50/day with no minimum campaign budget (first charge at $100 accumulated spend, then billed at $500 balance or every 30 days); the $500 minimum cited in the broader self-serve-CTV narrative applies to Roku Ads Manager, Disney Campaign Manager and Paramount Ads Manager, not to Vibe.

Pinterest disclosed no terms for tvScientific; the only figure in the public record is an unnamed-source estimate of '$300-to-$350 million' reported by Digiday, and the deal cleared only the FTC's $126.4M HSR reporting floor — so the corpus's '~$350M' must be relabeled as the top of an unverified estimate, not a fact.

Meta's CTV move is an audience-extension build (plugging Meta demand/targeting into third-party streaming via SSPs/OEMs, 'FAN for the living room'), not an acquisition; talks began early 2025, no product is announced, and prominent reporting landed April 2026 — so it cannot stand as evidence of an acquisition sprint.

Magnite acquired streamr.ai — an AI tool letting SMBs generate a video ad and launch it on CTV 'in less than 2 minutes' — on September 9, 2025 (terms undisclosed), three months before Pinterest's tvScientific deal; it is the cleanest evidence that incumbents are buying SMB self-serve CTV demand tools and should anchor the rewritten bear-case sentence.

Across 2025-2026, players both acquired CTV demand/measurement assets (Pinterest/tvScientific, Magnite/streamr.ai, Walmart/Vibe, Viant/TVision, Cadent/VuePlanner, Mediaocean/Innovid) and built self-serve CTV access organically (Roku Ads Manager+API, Comcast Universal Ads, The Trade Desk Ventura, Meta's exploration) — a consolidation-plus-platformization wave, which supports a strategic-scarcity reading without the 'everyone is buying demand tools' overstatement.

Fox and Roku publicly committed to keeping Roku 'open and partner-friendly,' but as a deal-announcement statement of intent this is not a binding guarantee; post-close Roku is a competitor-owned asset rather than a neutral CTV supply/OS layer, so its availability as neutral supply for Vibe/Walmart is contingent on a competitor's goodwill.

In the ANA's July 2024 survey, only ~10% of marketers said their retail-media funding was 'somewhat or completely incremental,' with the rest reallocated from existing budgets and ~36% drawn from media ad budgets — meaning most RMN 'growth' is shifted, not new, advertising demand.

An IAB study (Sept 2023, 200 RMN buyers + 30+ interviews) found 52% of RMN advertisers reallocating funds from digital platforms (social/search/digital video/CTV) and ~36% from traditional media — corroborating, from the seller-facing side, that retail-media spend is largely shifted rather than incremental.

The ANA's Jan 2023 report found 88% of brands felt 'somewhat or heavily influenced' by retailers to buy RMN advertising and framed marketers as 'reluctant buyers' treating RMNs as a 'have to buy,' supporting the 'tax on suppliers' critique that RMN dollars are coerced trade spend re-labeled as advertising.

Bain & Company found only 6% of advertisers fully trust retailers' reported media metrics, quantifying the 'grading their own homework' conflict of interest at the heart of the seller-graded-measurement critique.

The skeptic tradition holds that retailer-run lift studies carry the same conflict of interest as the attribution they replace — 'incrementality measurement sold by the media seller is last-click attribution in new packaging' — with named practitioners (OptiMine, Dagger, Merkle) noting retailers 'always take 100% attribution' and 'grade their own homework.

The IAB and MRC released draft Retail Media Measurement Guidelines (Sept 13, 2023) and a final version (Jan 29, 2024) with an IAB/BCG Executive Playbook — explicitly covering incrementality, transparency and cross-retailer comparability — evidence that the industry formally agrees seller-graded ROAS is insufficient.

Retail media is maturing and decelerating — eMarketer cut its U.S. retail-media CAGR forecast from 24.1% to 17.2% (2024–28) and projects global growth easing from ~15.4% (2026) to ~10.2% (2029) — softening the 'ever-compounding' tailwind the bull docs imply, though it remains among the fastest-growing ad channels.

The 200-plus RMNs are consolidating toward roughly ten that matter (Amazon and Walmart alone capturing ~89% of incremental U.S. dollars in 2026), with ~50% of advertisers planning to consolidate to a select few and sub-scale networks forced to partner, license, or retreat.

The same consolidation is hitting the self-serve CTV buying layer Walmart bought: a crowded field (Vibe, MNTN, Roku, tvScientific, Amazon, streamr.ai, Universal Ads) is consolidating — Pinterest closed its tvScientific acquisition Feb 17 2026 and MNTN trades down ~65% from its 2025 IPO — which is bullish for owning a scaled onramp but bearish for the standalone-economics case behind the $1.4B price.

The 'tax on suppliers' incrementality critique is fundamentally a CPG-versus-big-retailer dynamic; the SMB long tail Vibe targets has no trade-spend, slotting or co-op pool to recycle, so its CTV dollar is the most genuinely incremental slice of the whole category — the one place the incrementality critique works in Walmart's favor (though that same dollar is also the most discretionary and churn-prone).

claims.t: A hashed email (HEM) is a one-way hash of a login/purchase email; despite the term, HEMs are reversible in practice by re-identification services and fragile (exact-match only, non-persistent), making them an imperfect identity spine.
