claims.t: A MAID (IDFA on iOS, GAID on Android) is a resettable per-device advertising ID — one person may hold several — and its iOS supply was gutted by ATT, relegating it to a mobile-to-household crosswalk role.
s: GSDSI, 'Identity Graphs 101' (Tier 5). Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: The IP address functions as a de facto household identifier in CTV matching; LiveRamp uses IP as a replacement for a hashed email to match CTV device IDs, discards it after matching, and recommends IPv4 because IPv6 in most cases will not match.
s: AdExchanger, 'How LiveRamp Connects The Many Dots Of Identity On TV' (Tier 5); LiveRamp CTV Targeting docs (Tier 1/5). Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: The CTV ID is a household-scoped identifier derived from ACR or a streaming SDK that represents the TV, not the viewer — connecting it to an individual requires a household-resolution crosswalk to a MAID or HEM.
s: GSDSI, 'Identity Graphs 101' (Tier 5). Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Automatic content recognition (ACR) is smart-TV software that captures a compressed fingerprint of the on-screen frame every few seconds (roughly 15s LG to 60s Samsung), matches it against a content database, and logs viewing including HDMI inputs — feeding both targeting and exposure measurement.
s: Samsung ACR support doc (Tier 1); smarttvs.org / versus.com / Wikipedia ACR explainers (Tier 5/7, mechanic only). Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: As of 2026 sources, all six major smart-TV brands — Samsung, LG, Vizio, Sony, TCL, Amazon — ship with ACR enabled by default with an opt-out.
s: smarttvs.org, 'How to Disable ACR Tracking' (2026, Tier 5); Samsung ACR support doc (Tier 1). Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Identity graphs resolve signals via deterministic matching (shared authentication, ~0.95+ confidence) and probabilistic matching (shared IP/device co-occurrence/postal, ~0.4–0.7 confidence), then a household-resolution layer rolls persons up to one household ID.
s: GSDSI, 'Identity Graphs 101' (Tier 5); LiveRamp Identity/RampID docs (Tier 1/5). Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: LiveRamp's RampID resolves fragmented touchpoints to a single person/household pseudonymous identifier that is tokenized and partner-specific — two companies referencing the same person see different RampID encodings — preventing the token from becoming a universal tracking key.
s: LiveRamp, 'Identity and Identifier Terms and Concepts' docs (Tier 1/5, vendor). Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: The data clean room — a neutral environment where two parties match audiences and exposure-to-conversion data without seeing each other's raw user-level records — is the mechanism that makes social-to-CTV legally and commercially possible (brand loads customer list, publisher loads exposure logs, room returns only aggregated overlap/reach/incremental conversions).
s: eMarketer clean-room FAQ + LiveRamp use-cases (Tier 5); IAB Tech Lab OPJA spec (Tier 1); Amazon Ads LinkedIn-CTV newsroom (Tier 1). Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: The independent clean-room field consolidated — LiveRamp acquired Habu (2024) and WPP/GroupM acquired InfoSum (2025) — and AdExchanger argues the standalone category effectively dissolved into cloud/walled-garden infrastructure by 2025, with incumbents capturing most of the value.
s: eMarketer/AdMonsters (Tier 5) for acquisitions; AdExchanger, 'Why 2025 Marked The End Of The Data Clean Room Era' (Tier 5, analysis). Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Amazon Marketing Cloud (AMC), Amazon's clean-room analytics environment built on AWS Clean Rooms, was expanded to all sponsored-ads advertisers at no cost, announced September 2025, lowering the cost barrier that had confined clean rooms to large advertisers.
s: Amazon Ads, 'Sponsored ads advertisers can now access AMC' (Sept 2025, Tier 1); AWS Blog, AMC on AWS Clean Rooms GA (Tier 1). Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: LinkedIn CTV Ads became available through Amazon DSP on May 7, 2026, activating LinkedIn's first-party professional signals (job title, industry, seniority; 1B+ members) on streaming inventory via Microsoft Monetize, matched against Amazon's hashed identity graph without LinkedIn selling raw data; Amazon was LinkedIn's second programmatic CTV DSP partner after The Trade Desk earlier in 2026.
s: Amazon Ads, 'LinkedIn CTV Ads now available through Amazon DSP' (2026-05-07, Tier 1); Marketing Dive; eMarketer (Tier 4/5). Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Match rates vary sharply by authentication: authenticated PII-rich matches (Google/Meta) run 60–80%; blind CRM-to-publisher overlaps in neutral clean rooms average ~50% (20–40% at the low end); LiveRamp cites 40–70% for unauthenticated CTV matching via IP.
s: Digiday multiplier-effect piece + growthjockey (Tier 5); AdExchanger LiveRamp interview (Tier 5). Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Retargeting audiences decay fast (browse-intent half-life of hours, weekly cohort churn) requiring weekly graph refresh; and reported match rates are partly inflated by third-party identity-bridge multipliers (e.g. InfoSum/Acxiom Match Multiplier claiming ~40% incremental lift), which blend direct overlap with projection.
s: GSDSI + Taboola (Tier 5) for decay; Digiday, 'Multiplier effect' (Tier 5) for inflation. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Because the social platform targets an individual but the CTV ID is household-scoped, ads intended for one person reach whoever is on the couch, and household exposures are attributed to individual conversions via error-prone crosswalks — a precision ceiling inherent in using a household screen to reach an individual.
s: GSDSI, 'Identity Graphs 101' (Tier 5); tvScientific + StackMatix CTV guides (Tier 5). Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: CTV has no click: viewers see an ad on TV then convert elsewhere and later, so last-touch/last-click attribution collapses, and the gap is filled by view-through (directional only), incrementality tests (causal, needs holdouts), and MMM (aggregate, coarse).
s: Prescient AI, fusepoint, tvScientific incrementality guides (Tier 5). Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Self-attribution creates circularity: in walled-garden/clean-room settings platforms grade their own homework, one conversion can be claimed by two or three platforms at once, CTV data sits in publisher-specific silos with proprietary methods, and there is no neutral arbiter — sharpest where one walled garden supplies audience, impression, and measurement together.
s: eMarketer walled-garden measurement + AI Digital + VideoWeek (Tier 5). Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: The practical retargeting flow — pixel/engagement capture, audience definition, graph resolution/onboarding, clean-room match, DSP activation, ACR/log exposure measurement — begins at an individual (a social login) and ends at a household (a TV screen), with the largest drop-offs at onboarding and the overlap match and the largest distortion at non-click measurement.
s: tvScientific CTV retargeting guide (Tier 5); LiveRamp docs (Tier 1/5); Amazon Ads newsroom (Tier 1); composite with sources 14–18. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: LinkedIn's CTV Ads product reached general availability across the United States and Canada (English-language only) in spring 2026, after a 2025 beta.
s: LinkedIn Marketing Solutions Help, 'CTV Ads' (a5966603), accessed 2026-06-30; AdExchanger, 2026.

claims.t: CTV Select is LinkedIn's premium curated CTV solution running Paramount+ and NBCUniversal inventory, available only to LinkedIn managed accounts with a dedicated representative.
s: LinkedIn Marketing Solutions Help (a5966603), accessed 2026-06-30; AdExchanger, 2026.

claims.t: On May 7, 2026, Amazon Ads and LinkedIn announced LinkedIn CTV Ads are available through Amazon DSP, bringing LinkedIn first-party signals (job title, industry, seniority) from 1B+ members to streaming TV via Microsoft Monetize, deal-based, US-only, activatable alongside Amazon audiences in one campaign.
s: Amazon Ads newsroom, 'LinkedIn CTV Ads are now available through Amazon DSP,' 2026-05-07; Marketing Dive; eMarketer; MediaPost, all 2026.

claims.t: The Trade Desk, announced March 18, 2026, was LinkedIn's first demand-side platform partner for connected-TV ads; Amazon DSP was the second (May 7 2026) and Microsoft Advertising a third route (~May 14 2026).
s: The Trade Desk press room, 2026-03-18; ppc.land, 'Microsoft Monetize fuses LinkedIn profile data into CTV via three DSPs,' 2026.

claims.t: Every LinkedIn-CTV deal flows through Microsoft Monetize on the supply side regardless of which DSP executes the buy; the DSP is interchangeable, the SSP is not.
s: ppc.land, 'Microsoft Monetize fuses LinkedIn profile data into CTV via three DSPs,' 2026; Amazon Ads newsroom, 2026-05-07 (Monetize for Amazon route).

claims.t: Microsoft acquired Xandr from AT&T in June 2022 (inheriting the Invest DSP and Monetize SSP) and shut down the Invest buy-side platform on February 28, 2026, leaving Monetize without captive demand.
s: ppc.land, 'Microsoft Monetize's survival bet: LinkedIn data on Amazon DSP CTV,' 2026.

claims.t: LinkedIn builds audience segments from declared professional facets, creates PMP deals in Microsoft Curate encoding LinkedIn audience + CTV inventory, and routes Deal IDs to buyer DSPs; targeting relies on member declarations, NOT IP-based household graphs or third-party cookies, and buyers never access individual member data.
s: ppc.land, 'Microsoft Monetize fuses LinkedIn profile data into CTV via three DSPs,' 2026.

claims.t: External-DSP routes reportedly require a $50,000 minimum spend over 30 days, a minimum audience of one million members, and up to five business days to generate a Deal ID; DSP routes are US-only while the direct Campaign Manager route adds Canada.
s: ppc.land, 'Microsoft Monetize fuses LinkedIn profile data into CTV via three DSPs,' 2026.

claims.t: LinkedIn reports Salesforce's CTV Ads reached 4x the on-target impressions of linear TV, achieved over 70% unique reach (audiences not reached by linear, measured by iSpot), and were 11x more cost-effective at reaching key audiences than linear.
s: AdExchanger, 2026; iSpot.tv case study, 'Salesforce Achieves Over 70% Unique Reach With LinkedIn's CTV Ads,' 2026.

claims.t: LinkedIn reports ServiceNow saw a 19% lift in awareness among audiences at large companies and a 45% improvement in lead submission rates (brand lift measured via Kantar).
s: AdExchanger, 2026; LinkedIn Business / Kantar ServiceNow case study, 2026.

claims.t: A CTV impression is delivered to a household while LinkedIn targeting is an individual professional; because LinkedIn uses member declarations rather than deterministic household graphs, reaching a specific decision-maker on their TV is probabilistic rather than deterministic — a structural limit on the 'reach the CFO on their smart TV' claim.
s: ppc.land, 2026; Demandbase, 'Understanding CTV in B2B advertising,' 2026.

claims.t: Amazon reported ~$17.2B in Q1 2026 advertising revenue (+22% YoY), and trade coverage frames the LinkedIn deal as reflecting Amazon's ambition to expand its own B2B advertising capabilities — a latent competitive threat to LinkedIn's supplier position.
s: MediaPost, 'Amazon, LinkedIn Team For B2B Inventory Ahead Of Upfront,' 2026-05-08; Marketing Dive, 2026.

claims.t: LinkedIn's DSP-route documentation confirms company-category as a facet but does not confirm support for true named-account-list ABM targeting; measurement, pricing, and attributes beyond title/industry/seniority are also under-specified.
s: ppc.land, 'Microsoft Monetize fuses LinkedIn profile data into CTV via three DSPs,' 2026.

claims.t: LinkedIn cites a Magna Media Trials study finding 98% of LinkedIn users watch CTV in a given week vs. 83% who watch linear TV, supporting the argument that professionals have migrated to streaming.
s: AdExchanger, 2026 (citing Magna Media Trials).

claims.t: Pinterest is repositioning from an upper-funnel discovery platform to a lower-funnel performance-marketing channel, and the tvScientific acquisition extends that performance model onto off-platform CTV inventory.
s: Pinterest Newsroom, 11 Dec 2025; AdExchanger, 11 Dec 2025; Digiday, 16 Dec 2025; RockWater, 19 Dec 2025. Accessed 30 Jun 2026.

claims.t: Performance+ is Pinterest's AI/automation performance-ad suite, and tvScientific's outcome-based CTV engine integrates directly into it.
s: Pinterest Newsroom & tvScientific press release, 11 Dec 2025; AdExchanger, 11 Dec 2025. Accessed 30 Jun 2026.

claims.t: Pinterest agreed to acquire tvScientific on 11 December 2025 and closed the deal on 17 February 2026.
s: Pinterest Newsroom, 11 Dec 2025; Pinterest Form 8-K via StockTitan & Globe and Mail, Feb 2026. Accessed 30 Jun 2026.

claims.t: Pinterest did not disclose the deal price; trade consensus is $300-350M (~3-3.5x revenue on ~$100M tvScientific revenue), while one secondary financial outlet reported $465.1M that does not appear in Pinterest's SEC filing.
s: Digiday, 16 Dec 2025; RockWater, 19 Dec 2025; TipRanks, Feb 2026; Pinterest 8-K via StockTitan, Feb 2026. Accessed 30 Jun 2026.

claims.t: After the close, Pinterest raised its Q1 2026 guidance to $958-978M revenue and $163-183M Adjusted EBITDA, reflecting a partial-quarter tvScientific contribution (no standalone tvScientific revenue disclosed).
s: Pinterest Form 8-K, Feb 2026, via StockTitan, Globe and Mail, TipRanks. Accessed 30 Jun 2026.

claims.t: tvScientific is a self-serve, cost-per-outcome CTV performance platform using deterministic ID matching to tie TV exposure to conversions, claiming reach of ~95% of ad-supported video-on-demand audiences.
s: tvScientific press release & Pinterest Newsroom, 11 Dec 2025; AdExchanger, 11 Dec 2025. Accessed 30 Jun 2026.

claims.t: On 27 April 2026, tvScientific by Pinterest launched CTV Audiences, letting advertisers reach Pinterest first-party high-intent audiences OFF Pinterest on CTV for the first time.
s: Pinterest Newsroom 'Introducing tvScientific by Pinterest,' ~27 Apr 2026; VideoWeek/Digiday/eMarketer/MediaPost, 27 Apr 2026. Accessed 30 Jun 2026.

claims.t: CTV Audiences is an audience-extension play: a walled-garden first-party audience activated on third-party CTV inventory Pinterest does not own, combining deterministic and probabilistic matching.
s: Digiday, 27 Apr 2026; AdExchanger, 11 Dec 2025. Accessed 30 Jun 2026.

claims.t: Pinterest/tvScientific report a +27% lift in outcomes per $100 spent and +65% in purchases when tvScientific's AI is enriched with Pinterest high-intent signals; these are vendor-reported and unaudited.
s: Pinterest Newsroom, ~27 Apr 2026; Digiday/VideoWeek/eMarketer/MediaPost, 27 Apr 2026. Accessed 30 Jun 2026.

claims.t: In a named LG case study, adding Pinterest audiences drove a +73% increase in unique households reached and a +24% lift in net-new customers; vendor-reported, single case, no disclosed control.
s: Pinterest Newsroom, ~27 Apr 2026; VideoWeek & MediaPost, 27 Apr 2026. Accessed 30 Jun 2026.

claims.t: Named analysts raised at launch that Pinterest's individual-level intent may not fully survive resolution to a shared household CTV ID, and that the attribution model producing the lift figures — crediting any household device after one exposure — is 'blunt'; reach/inventory ceilings may also cap scale.
s: Trey Titone, Ad Tech Explained, 12 Dec 2025; Digiday (Inghelbrecht), 16 Dec 2025; AdExchanger, 11 Dec 2025. Accessed 30 Jun 2026.

claims.t: tvScientific by Pinterest competes in the performance-CTV challenger tier (peers MNTN, Vibe), beneath the large brand-DSPs (The Trade Desk, DV360); its differentiator is proprietary first-party intent data, its handicap is not owning CTV inventory.
s: Digiday, 16 Dec 2025 & 27 Apr 2026; RockWater, 19 Dec 2025; AdExchanger, 11 Dec 2025. Accessed 30 Jun 2026.

claims.t: The current tvScientific-powered CTV advertising play is a distinct product from the old 'Pinterest TV' live-shopping creator feature launched 8 November 2021.
s: TechCrunch, 1 Nov 2021; Pinterest Newsroom, Nov 2021; Variety, 1 Nov 2021. Accessed 30 Jun 2026.

claims.t: The original daily live-shopping-show format of 'Pinterest TV' appears largely wound down and to have evolved into streaming content partnerships, but no formal dated discontinuation could be sourced.
s: Pinterest Newsroom items and trade coverage (Retail Dive, TechCrunch), 2021-2026; search of Pinterest newsroom/help, accessed 30 Jun 2026.

claims.t: Reddit reported Q1 2026 total revenue of $663M (+69% YoY), advertising revenue of $625M (+74% YoY, ~94% of revenue), net income $204M, and 126.8M daily active uniques (+17%) — an on-platform first-party-audience business.
s: Reddit Inc. Form 8-K Q1 2026, SEC EDGAR, filed 2026; ALM Corp 2026; Mobile Dev Memo (Seufert) 2026. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Reddit attributes its ad acceleration to on-platform mechanics (Reddit Max campaigns, search-led traffic +30% YoY, Dynamic Product Ads, +75% advertiser count) with no CTV or off-platform extension mentioned in its Q1 2026 disclosure.
s: Reddit Q1 2026 8-K; ALM Corp 2026; Mobile Dev Memo 2026. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Reddit's Interactive Ads format (Paramount's Running Man 'Dodge the Drones' game, built by KarmaLab + Hi From the Future, late 2025) is an on-platform in-feed unit in the Reddit feed, not a CTV format or off-platform inventory.
s: Adweek 2025; Digiday 2026. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: The Digiday piece grouping 'Amazon, Disney and Reddit' as expanding interactive ad formats is a trend paragraph — Amazon/Disney have CTV formats while Reddit's cited unit is in-feed — not a description of a Reddit CTV product or partnership.
s: Digiday, 'Dedicated interactive and localized ad formats…', 2026. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Reddit is deliberately building a walled garden — launching Dual Attribution first-party measurement (beta May 20, 2026), partnering with Anonym so advertiser first-party data never leaves, and shopping for ad-tech acquisitions to reduce external reliance — the strategic antithesis of audience extension.
s: MediaPost 2026-05-20; ppc.land 2026; Portada 2026. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Reddit's 'Other revenue' ($39M Q1 2026, +15%) is AI-training data licensing (Google ~$60M/yr from Feb 2024, OpenAI ~$70M/yr); no Reddit–Amazon advertising data partnership activating Reddit audiences in Amazon DSP for CTV was confirmed.
s: CBS News 2024; CJR 2025; Bloomberg 2025-09-17; Reddit Q1 2026 8-K. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: TikTok launched a CTV app in 2021 (Fire TV first, later Samsung/LG/Vizio/Google/Apple) that failed to gain traction due to poor formatting/UI porting vertical mobile onto a horizontal lean-back screen.
s: eMarketer 2026; Tech-ish 2025; Axios 2025-02-08. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: The TikTok US TV app was removed from US smart-TV app stores in early 2025 as ban-law (PAFACA) compliance, and the service was discontinued globally on June 15, 2025 — both traction weakness and regulatory compliance are causes, with the US removal driven by the latter.
s: Axios 2025-02-08; Tech-ish 2025-05-16; Sony Canada support notice 2025. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: As of 2026, TikTok's Global Head of Creator Marketing Marisa Hammonds said a TV app is 'not on the roadmap right now. Never say never' — a step-back, contrasting Instagram's December 2025 Reels CTV app launch.
s: Mike Shields Substack 2026; eMarketer 2026. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: The live 'TikTok on CTV' thesis is vertical-video-as-entry-point, operated by streamers embedding short-clip discovery feeds (Disney+ 'Verts' Mar 2026; Netflix vertical test; Peacock/Tubi feeds) to route viewers into long-form — borrowing TikTok's grammar, not using TikTok's audience graph.
s: eMarketer 2026; Paramount Ads Manager 2026. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Renewed big-screen interest is driven by a mobile-engagement plateau (Meta DAU +6% YoY Q1 2025 vs +7% prior; YouTube Shorts 200B+ daily views), but for TikTok this manifests off-platform — the plateau pressure is real yet TikTok chose not to build the surface.
s: eMarketer 2026; Digital Information World 2026-03 (single-vendor, directional). Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: TikTok's US business closed into 'TikTok USDS Joint Venture LLC' on January 22, 2026 — Oracle/Silver Lake/MGX ~15% each, ByteDance <20%, Adam Presser CEO, Oracle as security partner re-training a US algorithm — a first-year restructuring that biases toward protecting the core ~$14–17B US mobile ad machine over speculative CTV bets.
s: ContentGrip 2026; Variety 2025; Bloomberg 2026-01-23; eMarketer/WARC 2026. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Brands run TikTok-style creative into CTV via third-party tooling with no TikTok involvement — Rollo reformatted vertical social creative for CTV via Spaceback + Roku Ads Manager (~700K households, sub-$0.01/day/household, ~$182 AOV); Uproxx pitches publisher-owned 'TikTok-ready shows' — both repurpose the vertical grammar, not the TikTok audience.
s: Demand Gen Report 2026; Adweek 2026; AdExchanger 2026. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Meta launched Instagram for TV, an app streaming Reels to the television, into test on Amazon Fire TV in the US on December 16, 2025.
s: Meta Newsroom, 'Watch Reels on the Big Screen With Instagram for TV,' about.fb.com, 2025-12-16; TechCrunch 2025-12-16. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Instagram for TV is framed by Meta as an engagement/content product; its launch materials contain no advertising or monetization language and no CTV ad product has been announced.
s: Meta Newsroom 2025-12-16; TechCrunch 2025-12-16. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: As of June 2026 Instagram for TV is US-only, having expanded from Fire TV (Dec 2025) to Google TV (Feb 24 2026) to Samsung smart TVs (June 2026) — the three largest US CTV platforms.
s: TechCrunch 2026-02-24; The Next Web June 2026; Deadline June 2026. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Meta is expanding Instagram for TV beyond short-form Reels: an episodic-series feature launched on mobile June 2 2026, and the TV app is testing a horizontal-video hub and 'Live on TV.
s: The Next Web, 'Instagram is coming for your living room with episodic series and live TV on Samsung,' June 2026. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Since early 2025, Meta has reportedly held exploratory meetings with SSPs Magnite and Comcast-owned FreeWheel, plus TV OEMs and publishers, to push its ad demand into third-party CTV — but has announced no product and declined to comment.
s: Digiday, 'Meta eyes CTV expansion...,' 2026-04-27; ExchangeWire digest 2026-04-28. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Analysts expect a Meta CTV ad product to take the form of an 'Audience Network for CTV' — extending Meta's demand and targeting into third-party CTV inventory via SSPs and TV OEMs, not building or acquiring supply.
s: Digiday 2026-04-27; Brainlabs 2026-06-02. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: A central obstacle is whether Meta's performance algorithm can find a conversion signal on CTV inventory at ~$20-$40 CPM against Meta's typical ~$6-$9 range, or whether Meta would need to steer spend.
s: Brainlabs 2026-06-02. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Meta acquired video SSP LiveRail in July 2014 to power Facebook Audience Network video ads; it was written down amid fraud and poor supply quality and the ad server was sunset — cited as why any current Meta CTV move is expected to be partnership-led rather than build/buy-the-supply.
s: AdExchanger 'As LiveRail Sunsets Its Ad Server...'; Digiday 2026-04-27. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: New Instagram for TV (Reels on the big screen, 2025-) is distinct from IGTV — a standalone long-form vertical-video mobile app launched June 2018 as a YouTube competitor, peaking at ~7M downloads and discontinued February 2022.
s: TechCrunch, 'Instagram is shutting down its standalone IGTV app,' 2022-02-28. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Meta reported ~$196.2B in FY2025 ad revenue (of ~$201.0B total) with 3.58B Family daily active people (Dec 2025); Zuckerberg said in Q3 2025 that Reels alone has a >$50B annual revenue run-rate, larger than YouTube's ~$46B total ad revenue.
s: Meta 'Q4 and Full Year 2025 Results' 2026; Tubefilter/Motley Fool transcript 2025-10-29/30. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: US CTV ad spending reached ~$33.35B in 2025 and is forecast to grow to ~$46.9B by 2028, surpassing linear TV (~$45.1B) for the first time.
s: eMarketer forecasts (via MNTN Research summary and eMarketer content), 2025-2026. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Meta cut ~10% of its global workforce (~8,000 workers) and closed ~6,000 open positions, a constraint cited as reinforcing a plug-and-play partnership approach to CTV over building owned infrastructure.
s: AdExchanger 2026-04-28. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: As of May 7, 2026 LinkedIn CTV Ads are available through Amazon DSP, routing LinkedIn's 1B+ member professional signals (job title, industry, seniority) to US premium streaming via Microsoft Monetize on a deal-based basis.
s: Amazon Ads Newsroom, May 7 2026, advertising.amazon.com/library/news/linkedin-ctv-ads-amazon-dsp; Marketing Dive 2026 (accessed 2026-06-30)

claims.t: The Trade Desk was named LinkedIn's first programmatic CTV DSP partner (announced ~March 2026), initially in a test phase with a small group of brands, making Amazon DSP the second rail.
s: The Trade Desk press room / thekeyword.co, Mar 2026 (accessed 2026-06-30)

claims.t: Pinterest announced acquisition of CTV ad platform tvScientific on Dec 11 2025 and closed it in February 2026, launching CTV Audiences; tvScientific reaches ~95% of AVOD audiences via deterministic IDs and runs cost-per-outcome campaigns integrated into Performance+.
s: Pinterest Newsroom Dec 11 2025; VideoWeek Apr 27 2026 (accessed 2026-06-30)

claims.t: Amazon's ad business grew 24% YoY to $17.2B in Q1 2026 (>$70B TTM); Amazon DSP holds ~14% DSP share, is the fastest-growing top-five DSP (~24% YoY), and has direct CTV deals with Netflix, Roku (80M+ households), Disney, Samsung, Tubi and Comcast.
s: AdStatus/Storyboard18 2026; Marketing Dive 2026 (accessed 2026-06-30)

claims.t: The Trade Desk's effective take rate is about 21%, comprising a mid-teens buy-side platform fee, a 4.5% publisher fee on OpenPath supply, and a Predictive Clearing bid-shading fee embedded in CPMs; WPP and Dentsu exited OpenPath over economics/opacity concerns.
s: AdExchanger, 'Why Amazon Is Gaining Ground In CTV...', 2026 (accessed 2026-06-30)

claims.t: In an audience-extension buy, DSP platform fees run ~15-20% of media spend, third-party data segments add $0.50-$3.00 CPM (B2B $2-$5), and the all-in tech tax (DSP + data + verification) can reach 40-60% on top of raw media CPM.
s: Stackmatix, 'Programmatic Advertising Costs', 2026; AdExchanger 2026 (accessed 2026-06-30)

claims.t: Walmart Connect and Disney (2024) let advertisers match Walmart purchase data to Disney's Audience Graph via clean-room technology using synthetic household IDs for closed-loop attribution across Hulu/Disney+, with Disney also in Walmart's Partner Lab (Roku, NBCU, TalkShopLive, TikTok).
s: Disney Advertising Press 2024; AdExchanger 2024 (accessed 2026-06-30)

claims.t: Mobile-advertising-ID (MAID) match rates are declining industry-wide due to Apple ATT and consumer ID-reset behavior, pushing matching to household/neighborhood precision; cookies carry a 90-day lookback often cut to 30 days at destinations, structurally eroding the addressable social-to-CTV overlap.
s: LiveRamp Match Rates docs + Clean Room pages (accessed 2026-06-30)

claims.t: Meta has held exploratory CTV audience-extension meetings since early 2025 with Magnite, Comcast/FreeWheel, TV OEMs and publishers and progressed to requesting inventory-availability data, but has no CTV activation product today; its 2025 revenue (~$201B) is overwhelmingly mobile and DAU growth slowed to ~6% YoY in Q1 2025.
s: Digiday, 'Meta eyes CTV expansion...', 2026 (accessed 2026-06-30)

claims.t: TikTok previously launched a CTV app that failed to gain traction (attributed to poor formatting and UI), faces a vertical-vs-horizontal format mismatch, and is hiring a CTV product leader; its US app has split from the global business amid ownership uncertainty.
s: eMarketer 2026; Ad Age 2026; ExchangeWire Jan 2026 (accessed 2026-06-30)

claims.t: Reddit reported Q1 2026 revenue of $663M (+69% YoY) and ad revenue of $625M (+74% YoY) but has disclosed no CTV activation product and relies on weaker logged-out identity, leaving data-licensing as its plausible CTV path.
s: Reddit Q1 2026 8-K (SEC EDGAR); CNBC Apr 30 2026 (accessed 2026-06-30)

claims.t: Pinterest reports its tvScientific integration delivers a 27% uplift in outcomes per $100 spent and a 65% uplift in purchases, but these are vendor-reported, un-audited figures.
s: VideoWeek, Apr 27 2026 (accessed 2026-06-30)

claims.t: Open programmatic CTV carries material fraud/invalid-traffic risk: Pixalate reported ~18-19% CTV IVT through 2025 and 38% malformed/fraudulent CTV app bundle IDs in Q2 2025; DoubleVerify found >1 in 4 CTV impressions would fail criteria without protection and detected 140% more CTV fraud schemes in Q1 2026 vs Q1 2025.
s: Pixalate 2025 (via DV/AI Digital coverage); DoubleVerify Newsroom 2026 (accessed 2026-06-30)

claims.t: LinkedIn CTV Ads reached general availability across the US and Canada (June 2025), with CTV Select premium inventory spanning Paramount and NBCUniversal (NBCU partnership preceding Paramount by ~a year).
s: StreamTV Insider June 2025; TheDesk June 2025 (accessed 2026-06-30)

claims.t: Ranked by credible CTV extension through 2029: (1) LinkedIn, (2) Pinterest, (3) Meta, (4) Reddit, (5) TikTok, driven by weighting distribution mechanism, organizational commitment, and signal uniqueness over raw reach.
s: Author synthesis of sources [1]-[24], 2026-06-30

claims.t: Snapchat is a demand-side social walled garden with a large authenticated logged-in base (483M DAU, 956M MAU as of Q1 2026), meeting the corpus's subject-population definition.
s: Snap Inc. Q1 2026 Financial Results 8-K, May 6, 2026, sec.gov / investor.snap.com (accessed 2026-06-30)

claims.t: Apple's ATT cost Snap an estimated ~$546M in 2022 ad revenue, placing it in the same signal-loss casualty cohort as the ranked platforms.
s: Lotame ATT impact study 2022, as cited in 01_Origins.md line 53

claims.t: Snap has no CTV audience-extension product, no smart-TV/big-screen app, no DSP (Trade Desk/Amazon) CTV partnership, and no disclosed CTV pilot as of mid-2026.
s: Snap Q1 2026 8-K (sec.gov); Snapchat 2026 ad roadmap (Social Media Today / Snap for Business), accessed 2026-06-30

claims.t: Snap's hardware bet for the post-phone era is standalone true-AR Specs glasses (preorders 2026, fall shipping), a lean-in personal single-user surface structurally opposed to the shared lean-back CTV screen.
s: Snap Newsroom 'Introducing SPECS' 2026; TechCrunch Apr 10 2026; UploadVR 2026 (accessed 2026-06-30)

claims.t: Snap's Snowflake clean-room / Conversions-API integration is built to measure on-Snapchat conversions and sharpen mobile-DR targeting (inbound signal recovery), not to push Snap audiences out onto CTV inventory.
s: Digiday, 'Snowflake and Snap partner to integrate clean rooms with conversions API,' 2024 (accessed 2026-06-30)

claims.t: Snap's one off-platform audience-extension attempt, the Snap Audience Network (announced 2019, tested early 2020), extended its ad format into third-party mobile apps only — never CTV — and never scaled.
s: Marketing Dive, 'Report: Snapchat tests audience network to place ads outside its app,' Mar 5 2020 (accessed 2026-06-30)

claims.t: Snap generated roughly $5.9B revenue in FY2025 versus Meta's ~$201B, making Snap on the order of 3% of Meta's size — so the 'needs a new surface' logic applied to Meta barely applies to Snap.
s: Snap FY2025 quarterly 8-Ks (investor.snap.com); Meta 2025 revenue per 06_Meta chapter / Digiday (accessed 2026-06-30)

claims.t: Direct response contributes ~75% of Snap's ad revenue (first crossed in Q1 2025), a mobile-app-install/lower-funnel mix whose value the shared household CTV screen degrades most — giving Snap the least natural reason to want CTV delivery.
s: Snap for Business 'DR Improvements' + Snap Q1 2025 results (accessed 2026-06-30)

claims.t: Scored on the market map's six dimensions Snapchat lands at or below TikTok — zero on distribution mechanism and organizational commitment to CTV — so it is correctly excluded from the credible-extension ranking, by argument rather than silence.
s: This chapter's synthesis of sources [1]-[10]; scorecard rubric from 07_Market_Structure

claims.t: YouTube was the largest single distributor of US television by total viewing time in March 2026 at 13.5%, ahead of Disney (10.5%) and Netflix (8.2%), and held the top spot for a run of consecutive months.
s: Nielsen Media Distributor Gauge via TheWrap (Mar 2026) and Nielsen.com (Jul 2025, Jan 2026), accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Television surpassed mobile as the primary device for YouTube viewing in the US by watch time as of late 2024, with more than one billion hours of YouTube content watched on TV screens daily.
s: Neal Mohan, Think with Google annual letter, Feb 11 2025; TV Technology coverage, accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Google owns all four layers of the social-to-CTV stack (identity match, DSP, CTV inventory, measurement) that LinkedIn and Pinterest assemble from external vendors: Customer Match/PAIR identity, DV360, YouTube inventory, and Ads Data Hub.
s: Google DV360 Customer Match Help + PAIR blog, accessed 2026-06-30; corpus chapters 02, 07.

claims.t: Advertisers can upload hashed first-party customer lists to DV360, match them to signed-in Google accounts on YouTube, and retarget those users on connected TV inventory, with lists persisting up to 540 days.
s: Google, 'Customer Match for YouTube & partners line items,' DV360 Help, accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: YouTube generated $9.88 billion in ad revenue in Q1 2026 (+10.7% YoY) and exceeded $60 billion across ads and subscriptions for full-year 2025 — larger than the entire US CTV ad market the five renters are entering.
s: Alphabet Q1 2026 results via Hollywood Reporter/Variety, Apr 2026; corpus chapter 01.

claims.t: YouTube Select CTV is a productized premium big-screen ad buy with curated brand-safe lineups, the direct analogue of LinkedIn's CTV Select except built on YouTube's own inventory rather than rented broadcaster supply.
s: Search Engine Land + Google blog on YouTube Select, 2025-2026; corpus chapter 07.

claims.t: YouTube's integrated model demonstrates that the neutral activation layer (Amazon DSP / The Trade Desk) the corpus builds its market structure around is a feature of a fragmented market that a fully integrated inventory-plus-DSP-plus-identity owner does not need.
s: This chapter's synthesis of sources [1][3][4][8] against corpus chapter 07.

claims.t: A federal court found in April 2025 that Google illegally monopolized the ad-exchange and publisher-ad-server markets, and the DOJ sought divestitures (remedy phase resolving in 2026), but the remedy targets the open-web ad-tech stack, not directly YouTube inventory or DV360's buy-side integration.
s: TechPolicy.Press, AdExchanger, Adweek coverage of DOJ v. Google ad-tech case, 2025.

claims.t: The VPPA (18 U.S.C. § 2710) prohibits a video tape service provider from knowingly disclosing personally identifiable information concerning a consumer's video-viewing, and provides liquidated damages of not less than $2,500 per violation plus attorneys' fees.
s: 18 U.S.C. § 2710, Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School, https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/18/2710, accessed 2026-06-30

claims.t: VPPA class-action filings surged from 2022, targeting streamers, sports leagues, and publishers whose Meta Pixel transmits a logged-in user's video-viewing plus a Facebook identifier to Meta, generating a caseload in the thousands driven by the $2,500-per-violation math.
s: Privacy World, '2025 VPPA Litigation Year in Review,' Dec 2025; WilmerHale, '2024 Year in Review: VPPA Litigation Trends,' Feb 12 2025

claims.t: In Salazar v. NBA (2d Cir. Oct 15 2024), the Second Circuit held that a VPPA 'consumer' includes a subscriber to any of a provider's goods or services — audiovisual or not — so that exchanging an email for a free newsletter suffices for standing.
s: Salazar v. National Basketball Association, No. 23-1147 (2d Cir. Oct 15 2024), law.justia.com; Holland & Knight, Dec 2024

claims.t: A circuit split on 'consumer' (Second/Seventh Circuit broad vs. Sixth Circuit Salazar v. Paramount 133 F.4th 642 (Apr 3 2025) and D.C. Circuit Pileggi narrow) led the Supreme Court to grant certiorari in Salazar v. Paramount Global, No. 25-459, on January 26, 2026.
s: Salazar v. Paramount Global, No. 25-459 (U.S., cert. granted Jan 26 2026), supremecourt.gov/qp/25-00459qp.pdf; SCOTUSblog; 133 F.4th 642 (6th Cir. 2025)

claims.t: In Solomon v. Flipps Media, 136 F.4th 41 (2d Cir. May 2025), the Second Circuit adopted the 'ordinary person' standard, holding that a Facebook ID and the coded strings a Meta Pixel transmits — and by implication a bare IP address — are not VPPA PII because an ordinary person cannot identify a viewer from them, effectively shutting the door on the standard pixel-VPPA claim in the circuit.
s: Solomon v. Flipps Media, Inc., 136 F.4th 41 (2d Cir. May 2025); Morgan Lewis, July 2025; Privacy World, Dec 2025

claims.t: California's CCPA defines personal information to include online identifiers reasonably capable of being linked to a particular consumer OR household, so a persistent or combined IP address that resolves a household is regulated personal information.
s: IAPP, 'Are IP addresses personal information under CCPA?'; California Lawyers Association, 'What Is Personal Information Under the CCPA?

claims.t: Under the CPRA, transferring identifiers to a third party for cross-context behavioral advertising is a 'share' that requires no money to change hands and that a consumer can refuse via opt-out or a Global Privacy Control signal — reaching the clean-room match even though it is not a 'sale' of raw data.
s: California Lawyers Association (Business Law), CPRA/CCBA analysis; IAB via Orrick, 'Data Clean Rooms: A U.S. State Privacy Law Perspective,' Apr 2025

claims.t: On February 11, 2026, the California AG announced a record $2.75M CCPA settlement with Disney for failing to honor opt-outs (including GPC signals) across devices and services, specifically citing connected-TV apps that routed users to external webforms so data-sharing from the CTV app persisted; the remedy requires a single logged-in opt-out to propagate across every service tied to the account.
s: California AG press release, Feb 11 2026, oag.ca.gov; WilmerHale, Mar 9 2026; Lowenstein Sandler client alert

claims.t: On December 16, 2025, the Texas AG sued Samsung, LG, Sony, Hisense, and TCL under the Texas DTPA over ACR that captures viewing every 500 milliseconds and monetizes it without informed consent, obtaining temporary restraining orders against Samsung and Hisense and seeking penalties up to $10,000 per violation.
s: Texas OAG press release, Dec 16 2025, texasattorneygeneral.gov; IAPP, 'Automated content recognition technology takes privacy enforcement spotlight

claims.t: In February 2017 the FTC and New Jersey AG settled with Vizio for $2.2 million over collecting second-by-second viewing histories from 11 million smart TVs without consent and appending demographic data — the precedent for the current ACR enforcement wave.
s: FTC press release, 'VIZIO to Pay $2.2 Million…,' Feb 6 2017, ftc.gov

claims.t: On August 1, 2025, a Northern District of California jury found Meta violated CIPA by using an embedded SDK to intercept sensitive reproductive-health data from Flo app users for targeted advertising without consent; CIPA carries $5,000 per violation and Meta acknowledged potential exposure in the billions.
s: Bloomberg Law, 'Meta's Health Privacy Trial Loss…'; CompliancePoint, Aug 2025 (Frasco v. Flo Health, N.D. Cal.)

claims.t: The CIPA pixel-as-wiretap/pen-register theory is volatile: it survived early motions (Greenley v. Kochava) but was narrowed in Doe v. Eating Recovery Center (N.D. Cal. Oct 2025, judge calling CIPA 'a total mess'), checked by an April 2026 class-cert denial, and faces pending SB 690 (passed CA Senate June 3 2025) that would exclude commercial-business-purpose devices subject to opt-out.
s: Privacy World, Dec 2025; Duane Morris, Oct 21 2025; Holland & Knight, Apr 2026; Traverse Legal

claims.t: Legal exposure is uneven across the five platforms: LinkedIn–Amazon (logged-in first party, clean-room match, no third-party pixel, propagated opt-out) is least exposed; Reddit, TikTok, and Pinterest/tvScientific — leaning on a retargeting pixel and/or IP-based household resolution — are most exposed; Meta bears the highest gross exposure as the pixel/SDK defendant of record but is partly insulated on the VPPA axis by the 'ordinary person' shielding of its own hashed identifier.
s: Synthesis of sources [1]-[29] applied to platform mechanics in corpus chapters 02-06

claims.t: As of 2026, twenty U.S. states have comprehensive consumer-privacy laws in effect (including CA, CO, CT, TX, OR), with Texas's TDPSA applying without revenue/volume thresholds and a growing group requiring recognition of universal opt-out signals as of January 2026.
s: MultiState, '20 State Privacy Laws in Effect in 2026,' Feb 4 2026; Bloomberg Law State Privacy Legislation Tracker

claims.t: The Disney Audience Graph, Disney Select, and DRAX remain live branded products in 2026, with Disney Select offering roughly 1,800 first-party audience segments built from 100,000+ attributes and sold programmatically through the Disney Real-Time Ad Exchange across Disney+, Hulu, and ESPN.
s: Disney Advertising Press fact sheet (Tier 1); AdExchanger 'Inside Disney's Plan To Automate Half Its Ad Business' (Tier 5); Marketing Dive (Tier 5). Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: In June 2025 Disney integrated DRAX with Amazon DSP across Disney+, ESPN, and Hulu, letting advertisers match Disney's audience data with Amazon browsing/streaming/purchase insights via Amazon Publisher Cloud and Disney Compass.
s: ETCentric, 'Disney Integrates Real-Time Ad Exchange with Amazon DSP,' June 2025 (Tier 5). Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: NBCUniversal's One Platform (launched 2020) is backed by NBCU ID, a first-party identity graph of roughly 150 million person-level and 50 million household identifiers spanning its entertainment brands, OTT, Peacock, and Universal Parks, with a clean room (Audience Insights Hub) for matching advertiser data.
s: AdExchanger, 'NBCUniversal Built A First-Party Data Platform Stocked With 150 Million IDs' (Tier 5); NBCUniversal Newsroom CES 2026 launch, Dec 17 2025 (Tier 1). Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Netflix launched its own proprietary ad server (Netflix Ads Suite, April 2025 US, global by mid-2025), ending its Microsoft ad-tech dependency, and now sells native first-party targeting including 100+ interest segments across 17 categories plus mood-based and postal-code segmentation, and shipped its own conversion API in early 2026.
s: StreamTV Insider (Tier 5); ppc.land 'Netflix Ads gets Amazon audiences, Yahoo signals, and its own conversion API' (Tier 5); ALM Corp analysis (Tier 5). Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Netflix simultaneously sells its own interest segments and imports third-party audience data — Amazon Audiences (into Netflix Q2 2026, US first, via Amazon DSP programmatic access from Sept 2025) and deterministic Yahoo DSP segments (partnership from Oct 2025) — indicating viewing data alone does not yet satisfy performance advertisers.
s: ppc.land; thekeyword.co 'Netflix adds Amazon and Yahoo audience data'; Marketing Dive (all Tier 5). Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Roku surpassed 100 million global streaming households (April 2026) and runs Roku Data Cloud (launched Jan 6, 2025) built on ACR plus opt-in first-party sign-up/purchase signals — but explicitly declines the data-seller role ('We don't want to be selling data for CPMs'), routing exclusively through agency, measurement, and DSP partners rather than selling segments directly.
s: Roku Newsroom '100 Million Streaming Households' Apr 2026 (Tier 1); AdExchanger 'Roku's Clean Room Evolves Into Its New Form' (Tier 5); Roku Data Cloud collaboration-suite page (Tier 1). Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Samsung Ads sells 600+ ready-to-buy first-party ACR-derived segments (plus a Data+ data-as-a-service offering) and LG Ad Solutions sells deterministic ACR-informed household segments from webOS TVs across 30-40+ countries — both capturing cross-app, all-input viewing at the glass that no single streamer can see.
s: Samsung Ads solutions pages (Tier 1); AdExchanger Samsung AVOD-planning coverage (Tier 5); LG Ad Solutions technology pages (Tier 1); AI Digital smart-TV guide (Tier 5). Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Walmart's ~$2.3B acquisition of Vizio fused Inscape ACR viewing data (25M+ opted-in TVs, all inputs; ~19M active SmartCast accounts) with Walmart's verified retail purchase data, enabling target-by-Walmart-purchase-history and closed-loop exposure-to-sale attribution — a product superior to a social platform's intent proxy on measurable-sales goals.
s: AdExchanger 'Walmart Buys Smart TV Manufacturer Vizio' (Tier 5); Digilant, Kepler, TheMeasure analyses (Tier 5). Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Amazon is simultaneously the DSP rail social platforms rent, a retail-media data seller (~$56.7B projected 2026 US retail-media spend, ~10x Walmart), and a streamer with its own first-party audience (Prime Video, Fire TV), giving it a native full-funnel purchase-plus-viewing loop that positions it to observe, replicate, and disintermediate substitutable social segments.
s: eMarketer 'FAQ on Amazon advertising' (Tier 5); Amazon Ads DSP product page (Tier 1); Skai/Tinuiti/MNTN (Tier 5). Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Of the five social platforms' core signals, only LinkedIn's verified declared professional identity (job title, seniority, employer, function) is genuinely non-substitutable from viewing/registration/commerce data, because viewers do not declare professional attributes to a television; Pinterest intent, Reddit affinity, TikTok engagement, and most Meta segments are substantially reconstructable from streamer/OS data.
s: Synthesis across sources 1-21; consistent with corpus 03_LinkedIn (declared vs inferred signal) and 07 Market Structure §2.3 durability test. Compiled 2026-06-30.

claims.t: On the 2029 horizon the streamers' audience businesses are years ahead of the social entrants for the substitutable segments — Disney Select productized since 2021, NBCU One Platform since 2020, Netflix ad-server independence and Roku Data Cloud since 2025 — versus Meta (no product), Reddit/TikTok (no owned screen), and Pinterest/LinkedIn (live only in 2026); the comparison inverts only for LinkedIn's non-substitutable segment, where streamers are absent.
s: Synthesis across sources 1-21 and corpus 06_Meta, 07_Market_Structure; match-rate-decay mechanism per LiveRamp docs cited in 07. Compiled 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Roughly 36% of advertisers increasing 2026 CTV budgets are reallocating that money out of social, and eMarketer frames CTV as the channel marketers flee to because they have hit a performance ceiling on social — a demand to escape social, not to activate social audiences on CTV.
s: IAB via eMarketer/StreamTV Insider 2026 [2]; eMarketer 'CTV becomes the new performance engine…' 2026 [4]; Premion/Advertiser Perceptions 2026 [1]. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: The buyer-side survey data behind the 2026 'unify social and CTV' narrative describes creative and planning coordination (78.4% run both channels; 55.2% reuse core creative with format tweaks), not activation of a social platform's first-party audience against streaming inventory.
s: eMarketer, 'Marketers rush to unify social, CTV strategies,' 2026 [3]. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: In 2025-26 the three largest agency holding companies each acquired an owned identity/data asset — Omnicom absorbed IPG's Acxiom (merger closed Nov 26, 2025), Publicis agreed to buy LiveRamp for $2.2B (announced May 18, 2026), and WPP folded InfoSum into GroupM — giving each a structural preference to activate its own graph over renting a social platform's segment.
s: SEC 8-K + The Drum 2025 [5]; bestmediainfo 2025 [6]; Digiday 2026 [7]; AdExchanger/Marketing Dive 2025 [8]. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Publicis CEO Arthur Sadoun framed the $2.2B LiveRamp acquisition as owning the identity/intelligence layer outright rather than partnering — 'Identity is the qualifier for AI. If you don't have the identity, you just don't win' — evidencing a holdco structural preference for its own graph over a walled garden's licensed segments.
s: Digiday, 'Identity is the qualifier for AI: Publicis' $2.2 billion LiveRamp deal…,' 2026 [7]. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Dentsu and WPP quietly exited The Trade Desk's OpenPath in early 2026 over undisclosed fees and loss of transparency about where ads run — a revealed preference by the largest buyers to remove intermediary tolls, directly hostile to adding a new social-data-licensing layer.
s: Adweek exclusive 2026 [9]; Campaign US 2026. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: The ANA's log-level programmatic transparency study found roughly 36 cents of every programmatic dollar reaches working media (up to ~50 cents with best practices), making any additional intermediary data-licensing layer — a social-data fee atop a DSP atop an SSP — a hard sell to a CFO.
s: ANA Programmatic Media Supply Chain Transparency Study, Dec 2023 [10]; AdExchanger. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: Legacy B2B intent providers (Bombora, ZoomInfo, Demandbase) are account-level and cannot easily activate as individual CTV audiences because ad platforms target individuals not companies, leaving LinkedIn's declared, verified, individual-level professional graph with a genuinely thin substitution set and the clearest fundable buyer demand.
s: getuntitled.ai 2026 [11]; 6sense/ZoomInfo comparison pages 2026 [12]. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: The top buyer-cited reasons for raising CTV spend in 2026 are reaching engaged/opt-in audiences (44%) and combining TV branding with digital precision (40%) — the buyer wants the precision, agnostic about whether a social platform supplies it, so social-audience-on-CTV competes against every other precision source.
s: Premion/Advertiser Perceptions, '2026 CTV/OTT Advertiser Survey,' 2026 [1]. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: There is no shipped Meta audience-on-CTV product to buy; documented buyer 'buy-in' is for Meta's automated ad tools on Meta's own surfaces (per eMarketer's Willens), and whether that transfers to Meta's audience on someone else's streaming inventory is untested — making Meta-audience-on-CTV a forecast, not funded demand.
s: Digiday, 'Meta eyes CTV expansion…' 2026, incl. Willens commentary [15]. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: The holdco-owns-identity thesis is qualified by skepticism that Acxiom (a data broker) is a genuine proprietary first-party spine, which means holdcos will still rent truly non-substitutable signals (e.g. verified job title) — the specific crack through which LinkedIn's demand survives.
s: Digiday, 'The Acxiom data dilemma behind Omnicom's… IPG acquisition,' 2025 [14]. Accessed 2026-06-30.

claims.t: As of mid-2026 no social-to-CTV audience-extension product operates outside North America: every live product (LinkedIn CTV Ads, tvScientific by Pinterest, Instagram for TV) is US-first, with Canada the only annex, and none has an announced ex-US launch.
s: LinkedIn Marketing Solutions Help, 'CTV Ads,' accessed 2026-06-30, linkedin.com/help/lms/answer/a5966603; Pinterest Newsroom + tvScientific, Dec 2025; Meta 'Introducing Instagram for TV,' Dec 2025 + Deadline Jun 2026

claims.t: Europe is the world's second-largest CTV advertising market — roughly €14 billion in 2025 on IAB Europe's framing, with CTV reaching ~46% of EU ad views — making a US-only reading of 'credible extension through 2029' materially incomplete.
s: IAB Europe CTV Knowledge Hub; TVREV, 'Europe's CTV Market Is Growing Fast,' 2025

claims.t: Under EU law a dynamic IP address is personal data where the holder has legal means reasonably likely to identify the person (CJEU, Breyer, C-582/14, 2016), so the corpus's IP-as-household-key resolution is regulated personal-data processing in the EU, not a free technical choice.
s: CJEU, Case C-582/14 Breyer, 19 Oct 2016, via GDPRhub and Inside Privacy (Covington)

claims.t: Under the ePrivacy Directive Article 5(3), accessing information on terminal equipment — which the EDPB's Guidelines 2/2023 expressly extend to connected TVs — requires prior opt-IN consent, the mirror image of the US opt-out regime under which all six TV brands ship ACR on by default.
s: ePrivacy Directive 2002/58/EC Art. 5(3); EDPB Guidelines 2/2023 on technical scope of Art. 5(3), 2024

claims.t: The EU designated Alphabet (incl. YouTube, Google Ads), Amazon (incl. Amazon Ads), Meta (incl. Instagram, Meta Ads), ByteDance (TikTok), and Microsoft (LinkedIn) as DMA gatekeepers whose core platform services are barred from cross-surface personal-data combination without freely-given consent (Article 5(2)).
s: European Commission, 'Commission designates six gatekeepers under the DMA,' 6 Sep 2023, and DMA gatekeepers portal

claims.t: On 23 April 2025 the European Commission fined Meta €200 million because its 'pay-or-consent' model did not secure freely-given consent for combining personal data across services under DMA Article 5(2) — concrete proof the cross-surface data-joining the US bridge assumes is gated and enforced in the EU.
s: European Commission DMA decision, 23 Apr 2025, via Taylor Wessing and Hunton Andrews Kurth

claims.t: GDPR contains no B2B or employee-data exemption: professional attributes (job title, seniority, employer, work email) are personal data with no special professional-context relief — so LinkedIn's professional-data moat, its US strength, is maximally exposed in the EU.
s: Troutman Pepper Locke; GDPR Local, analyses of GDPR B2B/professional data, 2024-2025

claims.t: On 22 October 2024 the Irish Data Protection Commission fined LinkedIn Ireland €310 million, finding no valid lawful basis on any of three grounds (consent not freely given/informed/specific; contractual necessity inapplicable; legitimate interest overridden by data-subject rights) for behavioural analysis and targeted advertising — the exact activity underlying its CTV moat.
s: Irish Data Protection Commission press release, 24 Oct 2024; IAPP and Goodwin coverage of procedure and appeal

claims.t: Scored for the EU rather than the US, the credible-extension ranking inverts: LinkedIn falls (professional-data moat becomes GDPR liability + gatekeeper + €310M precedent), Meta/YouTube acquire DMA drag, and non-gatekeeper Pinterest becomes the least legally encumbered front-runner — a reversal invisible to the US scorecard.
s: Analysis in this chapter grounded in EC gatekeeper designations, DPC decision, and GDPR B2B analyses

claims.t: Post-Brexit the UK has diverged toward a lighter storage-and-access regime — the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 (Royal Assent 19 Jun 2025) added PECR consent exemptions — while keeping EU adequacy (renewed 19 Dec 2025 to 2031), making the English-language UK the probable first ex-US landing for any social-to-CTV bridge.
s: ICO storage-and-access guidance; Addleshaw Goddard on Data (Use and Access) Act 2025; EU adequacy renewal Dec 2025

claims.t: The retail-media/clean-room template that seeded the US bridge exists in Europe (Tesco/Nectar360, Carrefour Links/Unlimitail, Ahold Delhaize, InfoSum integrations, growing CTV, ~22% growth toward ~€31bn by 2028), but the social-platform extension of it onto CTV does not yet exist there.
s: eMarketer clean-rooms FAQ; Retail Media Age UK RMN guide; Kevel/IAB Europe retail-media takeaways 2025

claims.t: US ACR practice is drifting toward the EU opt-in posture — Samsung's Feb 2026 Texas AG settlement to require explicit consent and Kentucky HB692 (Mar 2026) mandating opt-in ACR — which narrows the transatlantic gap by tightening the US rather than loosening the EU.
s: Consumer Reports, 'How to Turn Off Smart TV Snooping Features,' and ACR-privacy coverage, 2026

claims.t: Comcast acquired FreeWheel for approximately $320 million, announced March 1, 2014.
Magnite acquired SpotX from RTL Group for $1.17 billion ($560M cash + ~14M shares), announced February 5, 2021.
Magnite acquired SpringServe for approximately $31 million net, announced July 1, 2021, via an option negotiated as part of the SpotX deal.
IAS acquired Publica for $220 million in cash and stock, announced August 2021, roughly two months after IAS's own IPO.

Nexxen was formed through a multi-year roll-up (Taptica to Tremor International 2019, Unruly 2020, Spearad 2021 for $14.7M, Amobee 2022 for $239M), rebranding as Nexxen in June 2023 with the parent legally renamed Nexxen International in January 2024.
Equativ and Sharethrough merged June 12, 2024, with the deal reportedly valuing Sharethrough between $100M and $125M, fully unifying under the Equativ brand in June 2025.

Netflix began in-housing its ad server away from Microsoft starting with 2024 Canada testing, launching Netflix Ads Suite in the US in April 2025, with Microsoft remaining only a programmatic partner alongside The Trade Desk, Google DV360, Magnite, and (from June 2025) Yahoo DSP.

As of Comcast's June 29, 2026 announcement of the NBCUniversal/Sky spin-off, FreeWheel and Universal Ads are expected to remain with Comcast's connectivity/technology business, but FreeWheel's precise commercial relationship to NBCUniversal post-separation is undisclosed.

A 2020 ISBA/PwC programmatic transparency study found only 51% of advertiser spend reached the publisher as working media; a December 2023 ANA study found 36 cents of every dollar, with transaction costs eating 29% of spend.
FreeWheel data indicates 68% of CTV ad spend runs through direct insertion orders, 25% through programmatic guaranteed, and only 7% through auction-based open exchange/PMP deals.

OpenRTB originated from a November 2010 industry consortium, extended to video via a 2011 subcommittee including Adap.tv and BrightRoll working with DataXu and ContextWeb, producing OpenRTB 2.0 in June 2011; the IAB Tech Lab was established in 2014.

Invidi (founded ~2003) and Canoe Ventures (launched 2008, jointly owned by Comcast/Charter/Cox) built set-top-box-based addressable TV ad insertion that predates internet-video programmatic infrastructure and shares its architectural logic with later SSAI-based CTV monetization.

CTV never adopted client-side header bidding at open-web scale primarily because streaming apps on smart-TV operating systems generally cannot execute the browser-based JavaScript client-side header bidding requires, pushing the industry toward server-side alternatives like Prebid Server.
Magnite's CTV contribution ex-TAC reached $82.3M in Q1 2026, up 30% YoY, crossing 51% of total company contribution ex-TAC for the first time (vs 43% a year earlier).

Nexxen's Q1 2026 adjusted EBITDA fell 30% YoY to $16.3M and the company swung to a $5.3M net loss (IFRS) from a $1.6M profit a year earlier, even as revenue grew.

Pixalate's Q4 2025 CTV Seller Trust Index found Nexxen's measured CTV inventory to be 100% arbitraged (non-authorized-direct) across all three CTV platforms scored.

Yahoo shut down its supply-side platform and video exchange in 2023 and has not re-entered the SSP business as of mid-2026; Backstage is a DSP-side initiative that bypasses SSPs rather than operating one.
Viant Technology is a demand-side platform; its only sell-side relevance is TVision Insights, acquired for $40M, closing May 5, 2026.
Kargo's self-reported CTV business grew 96% in 2024, with no dollar base disclosed; Kargo operates a closed, invitation-only marketplace rather than an open SSP.

Equativ (with Sharethrough fully absorbed as of June 2025) claims combined net recurring revenue above $200M, but third-party estimators diverge sharply (roughly $74M to over $200M), leaving no confident CTV-specific figure derivable.

By the ANA's Q3 2025 Programmatic Transparency Benchmark, only about 47.1% of programmatic ad spend reached the publisher, up 11 points since 2023, with $13.6B in working media value reclaimed that quarter.
The ANA's Q2 2025 benchmark found the median number of SSPs used per advertiser fell from 19 to 17 in a single quarter, and active domains bought against fell from 53,799 to 28,958.
Jounce Media data cited by AdExchanger found a median direct-authorized CTV CPM floor of $14 versus $19.50 through an SSP reseller path — a 39% average markup for the same underlying impression.

A curation-focused executive stated some curators charge 30%+ for repackaging existing SSP inventory into exclusive deal lists, with curator fees frequently layered on top of SSP costs and obscured by non-disclosed revenue-sharing agreements.

A March 2024 Adalytics forensic investigation found Magnite, PubMatic, Sharethrough, OpenX, Nexxen, Index Exchange and TripleLift all still serving ads on identified made-for-advertising sites despite public pledges; PubMatic was found to have transacted for over 7,500 brands on the sampled MFA sites.
By the ANA's Q4 2025 benchmark, private marketplace deals accounted for more than 92% of median spend across formats and effectively 100% of CTV transactions specifically.

The UK's ISBA/PwC study found unattributable advertiser spend fell from 15% (2020) to 3% (January 2023), with impression-match rate rising from 12% to 58% — the most rigorous independent audited transparency exercise identified, with no confirmed third edition for 2025-2026.
Magnite's Disney relationship was renewed in October 2024 on a two-year term, meaning it is due for renewal around October 2026 — inside the forecast horizon.

Comcast will split into two public companies, spinning off NBCUniversal and Sky, while retaining FreeWheel inside the broadband/wireless Comcast entity; announced June 29, 2026, expected to close roughly a year later.

Fox Corporation and Roku signed a definitive agreement on June 15, 2026 for Fox to acquire Roku for approximately $22 billion; board-approved but still requires shareholder and regulatory approval, expected close H1 2027.

Amazon's Roku data partnership gives Amazon DSP exclusive third-party access to Roku's logged-in identity signal at the OS level, covering roughly 80 million US CTV households (~80% of the market), rolled out to all US Amazon DSP advertisers by Q4 2025.

Amazon DSP holds roughly 14% of global DSP spend versus Google DV360's ~32% and The Trade Desk's ~19%, while simultaneously owning major CTV supply — a structural buy-side/sell-side overlap unmatched by other major CTV sellers.

Netflix completed its transition to a fully in-house Netflix Ads Suite by 2025, and told investors programmatic buying was on track to exceed 50% of its non-live advertising business, with programmatic inventory volume up more than a third heading into Q2 2026.
Amazon's Freevee was shut down as a standalone app in August 2025 and folded into Prime Video.

Samsung's ACR footprint declined from roughly 88 million TVs in late 2024 to roughly 77 million in early 2026, and Samsung settled a case with the Texas Attorney General over ACR data-collection practices in February 2026.

TCL and Hisense's US television lineups largely run Roku TV or Google TV rather than their own operating systems, so their US ad inventory flows through Roku's or Google's stacks; VIDAA is a genuine separate ad platform mainly outside North America.

Disney's DRAX programmatic ad exchange is on pace to exceed its earlier goal of 50% of ad revenue sold programmatically and now targets roughly 75%, while deliberately preserving independent SSP access alongside DRAX Direct DSP integrations.

YouTube leads US CTV/TV viewing share (~12.7% per Nielsen's Gauge, Q1 2026) and sells its inventory almost entirely through Google's own ad-serving stack, with third-party SSP/publisher access historically limited to a small set of partners.
TVision measures attention via cameras in an opt-in, Census-weighted panel of roughly 5,000 U.S. households, capturing person-level, second-by-second gaze and presence data.
Adelaide's AU is a 0-100 modeled/predictive score (not a direct panel observation) built from contextual signals and trained against outcome data, refreshed quarterly.
CTV ad impressions routinely clear 90%+ and approach 100% viewability because the format is unskippable and full-screen, making viewability a near-useless quality discriminator for CTV specifically.

OpenX and TVision launched what they billed as the first supply-side attention pre-bid targeting solution for CTV in March 2026, combining TVision's predictive attention models with OpenX real-time bidstream signals.
Index Exchange embedded xpln.ai attention signals, calibrated against eye-tracking data, directly into its SSP for pre-bid optimization in February 2026.
TripleLift's guaranteed-AU-score CTV deal with Adelaide, launched September 2023, remains part of TripleLift's current CTV measurement offering as of 2026.
Viant Technology agreed to acquire TVision for $40 million ($22.5M cash, $17.5M stock), announced in early 2026, folding an independent attention-measurement vendor into a DSP.
The IAB and MRC finalized Version 1.0 Attention Measurement Guidelines in November 2025, explicitly intended as the basis for future MRC accreditation audits of attention measurement services.

As of mid-2026, no vendor has secured MRC accreditation for a CTV-specific attention metric; DoubleVerify's Authentic Attention accreditation covers desktop/mobile, while its CTV accreditations are scoped to viewability and brand suitability, not attention.
The ARF's Phase 3 Attention Measurement Validation Initiative (June 2026) found attention measures align reasonably at the broad channel level but diverge more at the platform and placement level.

Byron Sharp and the Ehrenberg-Bass Institute argue attention scores do not reliably predict advertising effectiveness, that ads work via fleeting low-attention exposure for familiar brands, and that chasing attention trades off against maximizing reach.
Sharp explicitly warns that claims from parties selling attention measurement or high-attention media may exaggerate attention's importance.
Adelaide's 2026 Outcomes Guide claims attention-powered campaigns saw a 33% average upper-funnel lift and 53% lower-funnel lift in 2025, based on 60 vendor-selected case studies.

IAB/MRC guidelines define attention as a complementary signal to, not a replacement for, viewability/CTR/conversion metrics, and note attention data is validated primarily against brand recall and lift rather than sales.

Attention vendors (TVision, Adelaide, Realeyes, Lumen) use incompatible units and scales with no industry-agreed common measure, and there is active trade-press argument against forcing standardization.

CTV already scores at or near the top of cross-channel attention leaderboards (Adelaide CTV score rising 57.55 to 69.53; TVision finding CTV ~13% higher attention index than linear), which weakens attention's power to discriminate quality within CTV specifically.

Karen Nelson-Field's finding that ~75% of paid digital impressions deliver little value is as much an indictment of low-quality programmatic supply broadly as a specific case for attention, and does not itself establish that higher attention scores convert to more sales.

Performance CTV requires three things: identity resolution linking TV exposure to downstream action, incrementality proof the action wouldn't have happened anyway, and a seller pricing mechanism for its own funnel-risk exposure.

US CTV ad spend is on pace for roughly $37.95 billion in 2026, up 14-15% YoY; the IAB's 2026 Digital Video Ad Spend & Strategy report (July 14, 2026) shows new customer acquisition as the top buyer objective (54%) and cross-platform measurement priority rising from 64% to 72%.
Self-serve CTV minimums have collapsed to SMB-accessible levels: Roku Ads Manager's floor is $500 total spend, and Amazon removed its self-serve minimum for Streaming TV entirely as of unBoxed 2025.

Walmart agreed in June 2026 to acquire Vibe.co, a self-serve CTV platform, for $1.4 billion, adding to its December 2024 $2.2 billion Vizio acquisition, to build a closed-loop retail-data-to-CTV ad stack.

MNTN's FY2025 10-K reports $290M revenue (29% growth), ~$24M operating income, and 23% adjusted EBITDA margin on a pure self-serve, ROAS-optimized CTV model — but MNTN is a single, self-interested data point, not proof legacy premium sellers can replicate the economics.

In a CPA/cost-per-outcome deal, the platform (not the advertiser) absorbs the cost of every non-converting impression and is paid only on completed events, which is why publishers have historically resisted pure CPA structures.

No public SSP or performance-CTV platform discloses what percentage of guaranteed-outcome campaigns miss their target, the average shortfall cost, or the margin cushion built into quoted CPOs — a significant, unaddressed disclosure gap.
s: synthesis

claims.t: Most CTV incrementality tests fail in practice due to underpowered samples, contaminated control groups, and short test windows, even as 52% of marketers report already using incrementality testing.

Last-touch attribution systematically under-credits TV (a delayed-conversion channel) while loosely-controlled 'lift' studies systematically over-credit it via selection bias — both errors can coexist across different advertisers simultaneously.

Nielsen retired Panel-Only ratings for national TV currency effective September 1, 2025, moving fully to Big Data + Panel, with Panel-Only ACM removed from transactional systems January 1, 2026, and further currency-metric adjustments in mid-2026.

CTV CPMs ($20-40) run three to ten times Meta's placements ($6-9), and Google/Meta's AI-optimized ecosystems reportedly deliver 18-22% more conversions, meaning performance-CTV positioning pulls premium inventory into a cost fight against walled gardens it structurally cannot win on price.

Ehrenberg-Bass mental/physical availability research and Binet & Field's 60:40 framework constitute direct, institutionally-weighted counter-evidence that performance-CTV optimization erodes the brand equity that lowers future acquisition costs.

MRC accreditation activity in 2024-2026 has concentrated on viewability and auction transparency rather than the causal-outcome claims behind guaranteed-outcome products, suggesting outcome claims are harder to independently verify than delivery claims.

Retail-media data (Amazon Marketing Cloud open access + Prime Video signals; Walmart/Vizio/Vibe.co) moved structurally onto the sell side during 2025-2026, making outcome measurement a native curation capability rather than a licensed third-party add-on.

claims.t: Bolivia's 1985 hyperinflation did not fall to single digits within a year — annual inflation was still ~276% in 1986, reaching the mid-teens only by 1987
s: Independent correction of an overstated original claim

claims.t: Poland's 1989–90 Balcerowicz Plan stabilized inflation and the economy grew through the 1990s
s: PBS Commanding Heights; secondary aggregation (T4/T5)

claims.t: The SIME/DIME negative-income-tax experiment (1968–82, ~4,800 households) found modest labor-supply reductions and a disputed link to higher marital dissolution, contributing to Congress dropping NIT proposals
s: HHS/ASPE; Boston Fed (T2)

claims.t: Lucas's rational expectations (1972) and the Lucas Critique (1976) reshaped macroeconomics toward DSGE modeling
s: U Chicago News; BFI working paper (T1/T2)

claims.t: DSGE macro's lack of a financial sector is widely blamed for the profession's failure to foresee the 2008 crisis
s: Academic literature review (T2)

claims.t: OECD union density fell from ~46% (1980) to ~40% (mid-1990s), linked by sociological research to rising inequality
s: SAGE/American Sociological Review (T2)

claims.t: Eucken's Freiburg School formed in deliberate reaction to both Depression-era laissez-faire failure and Nazi economic planning
s: eucken.de (T2); Acton Institute (T5)

claims.t: Erhard's 20 June 1948 currency reform plus simultaneous price-control abolition triggered the Wirtschaftswunder (~8%/yr GDP growth through the 1950s)
s: Econlib/Britannica/LSE working paper (T2/T4/T5)

claims.t: The Wirtschaftswunder's attribution to ordoliberalism alone is contested against Marshall Plan aid, an undervalued exchange rate, refugee labor, and ordinary catch-up growth
s: Carlin/LSE (T2)

claims.t: The Bundesbank's 1957 independence and inflation-averse culture are rooted partly in Weimar hyperinflation trauma, though how much is genuine memory vs. myth is itself debated
s: Bundesbank; EH.net (T2)

claims.t: Ordoliberal thinking shaped EU competition law (Treaty of Rome Articles 101/102) via the German delegation, though this causal chain is itself contested by some legal scholars

claims.t: The Eurozone-crisis austerity debate genuinely divides serious economists — the ordoliberal-sympathetic case (Sinn, Feld) against the critical case (Krugman and others)
s: T2/T4/T5/T6 mixed, both sides at full strength

claims.t: Bundesbank president Jens Weidmann was the sole ECB Governing Council dissenter against the OMT ("whatever it takes") program and testified against it before Germany's Constitutional Court, softening his stance only around 2019
s: Bloomberg; independently corroborated via Euronews, Irish Times, PIIE

claims.t: Veblen's *The Theory of the Leisure Class* (1899) introduced conspicuous consumption and an evolutionary, anti-equilibrium approach to economics
s: Veblen primary text (T1)

claims.t: Commons's transaction-based institutionalism influenced Wisconsin-era policy (workers' compensation, an early lineage into Social Security)
s: Britannica Money; New World Encyclopedia (T4/T5)

s: WEA Economic Thought journal (T2)

claims.t: Coase's 1937 transaction-cost theory of the firm won the 1991 Nobel; North's institutions-and-growth thesis won in 1993; Williamson's governance/hold-up theory won in 2009
s: Primary excerpts; Nobel press releases (T1/T2)

claims.t: MMT traces its roots through Knapp's chartalism (1905) and Lerner's functional finance to Kelton's modern synthesis

claims.t: Krugman and Summers each raised specific, sourced objections to MMT's core claims
s: Bloomberg/Yahoo Finance/The Week (T3/T4)

claims.t: MMT has real political association (Sanders, AOC) but no enacted US legislation is officially labeled MMT; Kelton held an interim dean role at Stony Brook as of September 2025
s: Sanders press office; Stony Brook (T1)
